The opening up of the e-file is of no help to White, since his king has nowhere to go; in view of the threat of mate he is forced to play 26. f5, on which 26... Ne5 wins.
zh: 如果23. Qe4，则23... Qxa2! 24. Bd6 Kd7，黑方在保持多一兵的同时，也使王的位置稳固下来。23. Qc2 Qh3+ 24. Ke4 f5+ 25. exf6 gxf6也很有意思。打开e线对白方没有帮助，因为白王无处可去；面对将杀威胁，他被迫走26. f5，而26... Ne5后黑方获胜。

text: To engineer a possible escape for the king via d2 White would have to give up his h-pawn; moreover, there would also be a permanent danger of the exchange of queens. For this reason he prefers to embark on new adventures.
zh: 白方若想安排王经d2逃走，就必须放弃h兵；此外，还会始终面临兑后的危险。因此，他宁可开始新的冒险。

caption_zh: 白方走完25. Kd5后的局面

text: This position caused amazement among some of the spectators, who attempted to get the manager of the tournament to intervene, since it was clear that White's piece on d5 was his queen and that on b1 his king! The position is, of course, a strange one; what is also unusual is that within seven moves the white king has reached a1. Clearly, it is helped in this by Black, who checks unnecessarily instead of building up a mating net. Black played 25... Qg2+?, when the correct move was 25... Rc8!. In that case White's king would get into trouble on the c-file, which it would have to cross to extract itself from the scrape it has got into. The following variations illustrate the strength of the rook move and are at the same time instructive as regards play against an exposed king: 25... Rc8! and now:
zh: 一些观众看到这个局面十分惊讶，甚至想请赛事负责人出面干预，因为在他们看来，白方d5上的显然应该是后，b1上的才应该是王！这个局面当然很奇特；更奇特的是，仅仅七步之后，白王便到了a1。黑方显然帮了它的忙：他没有织杀网，却不断作出不必要的将军。黑方走了25... Qg2+?，正确的却是25... Rc8!。这样一来，白王想脱身就必须穿过c线，并会在那里遇到麻烦。下面这些变化既说明了这步动车的力量，也展示了怎样对付暴露的王。25... Rc8!之后：

text: 1) White carries out a counterattack with his queen: 26. Qxb7 Qg2+ 27. Kc5 Ne7+ 28. Kb6 Rc6+ 29. Ka7 Qf2+ 30. Ka8 O-O+ 31. Bb8 Rb6 and Black wins.
zh: 1）白方用后反击：26. Qxb7 Qg2+ 27. Kc5 Ne7+ 28. Kb6 Rc6+ 29. Ka7 Qf2+ 30. Ka8 O-O+ 31. Bb8 Rb6，黑方获胜。

text: 2) The white king tries to force its way through to the a1-corner; this gives rise to the most interesting point in the analysis. After 26. Kc4 Black does not try any checking moves, but instead first consolidates his own position by 26... g6!!, having observed that White has no good move to make. If 27. Rc2 or 27. Qc2, then 27... b5+ 28. Kb3 Nd4+, while if 27. Rcd1, then 27... Nd4+; if 27. Red1 or 27. Rf1, the ring is tightened by 27... Qe3, and if 27. Qb6, then 27... Na5+ 28. Kd5 (or 28. Kb4 Qxh2!) 28... Qg2+ 29. Ke6 Qxa2+ 30. Kf6 (or 30. c4 Nxc4, etc.) 30... Rc6 31. Qa7 Rf8+ 32. Kg7 Rc7+! 33. Bxc7 Rg8+ 34. Kf6 Qf7+ 35. Kg5 Qe7+ and mates.¹
zh: 2）白王试图闯到a1角落，这带出了分析中最有趣的一点。26. Kc4之后，黑方不急于将军，而是先用26... g6!!巩固自身局面，因为他已经看出白方没有好棋可走。如果27. Rc2或27. Qc2，则27... b5+ 28. Kb3 Nd4+；如果27. Rcd1，则27... Nd4+；如果27. Red1或27. Rf1，则用27... Qe3进一步收紧包围圈；如果27. Qb6，则27... Na5+ 28. Kd5（或28. Kb4 Qxh2!）28... Qg2+ 29. Ke6 Qxa2+ 30. Kf6（或30. c4 Nxc4等）30... Rc6 31. Qa7 Rf8+ 32. Kg7 Rc7+! 33. Bxc7 Rg8+ 34. Kf6 Qf7+ 35. Kg5 Qe7+，随后将杀。¹

text: The possibility of 27. Kb3 still remains. There is admittedly no mating net then, but with 27... Qxh2 Black obtains a material advantage and goes on to threaten both 28... Qxf4 and 28... Na5+ followed by ...Nc4.
zh: 白方还可以27. Kb3。诚然，这样没有现成的杀网，但黑方用27... Qxh2获得子力优势，随后同时威胁28... Qxf4，以及28... Na5+后接...Nc4。

text: 3) The white king tries to defy the danger of mate by advancing to b6. Black then has a number of continuations, the simplest of which seems to be 26. Kc5 Qxh2 27. Kb6 Qxf4 28. Kxb7 (if 28. Qb3, then 28... Qf2+ 29. Bc5 Qxc5+ 30. Kxc5 Na5+ with a won ending) 28... Qc4 29. Kxc8 Nb4+ 30. Kb7 Qb5+ 31. Ka7 Nc6+ followed by 32... Kd7+ and mates.
zh: 3）白王试图走到b6，迎着将杀的危险继续前进。黑方有多种后续手段，最简单的似乎是26. Kc5 Qxh2 27. Kb6 Qxf4 28. Kxb7（如果28. Qb3，则28... Qf2+ 29. Bc5 Qxc5+ 30. Kxc5 Na5+，进入胜势残局）28... Qc4 29. Kxc8 Nb4+ 30. Kb7 Qb5+ 31. Ka7 Nc6+，随后32... Kd7+并将杀。

text: ¹ In this line Vuković fails to take his own advice and gives too many checks, which actually allow White to escape by 34. Kh6! Qxh2+ 35. Kg5 Qg3+ 36. Kf6, etc. The correct continuation is 32... Qe6! and there is no way to meet the threat of 33... Rg8+ 34. Kh6 g5+.
zh: ¹ 在这个变化中，武科维奇没有遵循自己的建议，给出了太多将军，实际上让白方可以通过34. Kh6! Qxh2+ 35. Kg5 Qg3+ 36. Kf6等手段逃脱。正确的后续手段是32... Qe6!，白方无法应付33... Rg8+ 34. Kh6 g5+的威胁。

text: The actual game took the following course:
zh: 实战则这样进行：

caption_zh: 黑方走完29... Rc8后的局面

text: White obviously cannot play 30. Qxf5 since then 30... Na5+ leads to mate; instead, he gives up his f-pawn and then by retreating his king quickly to a1 safeguards his position.
zh: 白方显然不能30. Qxf5，因为30... Na5+后会被将杀。他放弃f兵，再迅速把王退到a1，保障自身局面的安全。

text: A further mistake; he could still have fought for a draw by 32... Qf3!. The square c4 is naturally more suitable for the knight.
zh: 又一次失误；32... Qf3!本来仍可争取和棋。c4格自然更适合马来占据。

text: After 33... Rc6 34. Qd1 Nb7 35. Be5 Black cannot play 35... Rxe6 because of 36. Bxg7 Rg8 37. Rxe6+ and White wins.
zh: 33... Rc6 34. Qd1 Nb7 35. Be5之后，黑方不能35... Rxe6，因为36. Bxg7 Rg8 37. Rxe6+，白方获胜。

text: A terrible move; he should have played 34... Rd8.
zh: 糟糕的一步；应当走34... Rd8。

text: Since if 36... Rxg7, then 37. Qxh5+ followed by 38. Qh8+ and White forces mate.
zh: 因为如果36... Rxg7，则37. Qxh5+后接38. Qh8+，白方强制将杀。

text: In addition to this strange game, I shall extract from the treasury of chess curiosities three more encounters which have particular relevance to the theme of a king's successful wandering. The series opens with a game between Hamppe and Meitner, in which the pursued king seeks asylum among the enemy pawns and is successful to the extent that the opponent cannot obtain anything beyond perpetual check.
zh: 除了这盘奇特的对局，我还要从国际象棋的奇闻宝库中选出三局，它们尤其切合王游走后成功脱险的主题。首先是汉佩对迈特纳一局：被追赶的王跑到敌方兵群中寻求庇护，使对手最多只能取得长将。

text:
Hamppe – Meitner
Vienna, 1872
Vienna Game
zh:
汉佩—迈特纳
1872年，维也纳
维也纳开局

text: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Bc5 3. Na4
zh: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Bc5 3. Na4

text: 3. Nf3, which was often played by Anderssen, is the soundest answer to 2... Bc5. Hamppe's move is of doubtful value because of the bishop sacrifice on f2.
zh: 安德森经常采用的3. Nf3，是对2... Bc5最稳健的应对。由于黑方可以在f2弃象，汉佩这步棋的价值值得怀疑。

text: In return for the bishop, Black obtains a promising attack on the king, which is deprived of the right to castle.
zh: 黑方以一象为代价，使白王失去易位权利，并获得有希望的进攻。

text: 4. Kxf2 Qh4+ 5. Ke3
zh: 4. Kxf2 Qh4+ 5. Ke3

text: If 5. g3 then 5... Qxe4 6. Qe2 Qxa4 (not 6... Qxh1 because of 7. Nf3 and 8. Bg2) 7. Qxe5+ Ne7 8. Qxg7 Rg8 9. Qxh7 d6 and Black has the better position.
zh: 如果5. g3，则5... Qxe4 6. Qe2 Qxa4（不能6... Qxh1，因为7. Nf3后接8. Bg2）7. Qxe5+ Ne7 8. Qxg7 Rg8 9. Qxh7 d6，黑方局面较好。

caption_zh: 黑方走完6... d5后的局面

text: 7. Kc3
zh: 7. Kc3

text: White plans b3 and Kb2. If 7. Nc3, then 7... Nf6! 8. Qe1 (or 8. Qf3 dxe4+ 9. Nxe4 Bf5, etc.¹) 8... dxe4+ 9. Kc4 whereupon Black should not continue with 9... Be6+ 10. Kb4 e3+ 11. Ka3 Nc6 since White replies with 12. b3 followed by Kb2, but rather with 9... e3+! 10. Kb3 Nc6 11. a3 Be6+ and wins. This illustrates the method of countering a king's planned withdrawal to safety.
zh: 白方计划b3后接Kb2。如果7. Nc3，则7... Nf6! 8. Qe1（或8. Qf3 dxe4+ 9. Nxe4 Bf5等¹）8... dxe4+ 9. Kc4，此时黑方不应继续9... Be6+ 10. Kb4 e3+ 11. Ka3 Nc6，因为白方可以12. b3后接Kb2；正确的是9... e3+! 10. Kb3 Nc6 11. a3 Be6+，黑方获胜。这说明了怎样阻止王按计划退到安全地带。

text: ¹ This line is only equal after 10. Qxf4 exf4 11. Ke2! Nxe4 12. d3 followed by Bxf4, restoring the material balance.
zh: ¹ 10. Qxf4 exf4 11. Ke2! Nxe4 12. d3后接Bxf4，白方恢复子力平衡，这个变化只是均势。

text: If 8. d4 then 8... Nc6 9. Bb5 (or 9. b3) 9... exd4+ and Black has three pawns for his bishop as well as good prospects for a continuing attack on White's king or, indeed, his knight on a4.
zh: 如果8. d4，则8... Nc6 9. Bb5（或9. b3）9... exd4+，黑方以一象换得三兵，而且有望继续攻击白王，甚至攻击a4上的白马。

caption_zh: 白方走完9. a3后的局面

text: 9. c4? would be weak because of 9... b5!. Similarly, 9. Bxa6 bxa6 10. c3 Qxg2 11. Qf3 (or 11. Ne2 Bg4 12. Re1 Ne7!) 11... Qh3! is bad for White.² This is a typical example of an attack against a displaced king being deferred on the grounds that further action would only help the consolidation of the king's position. Thus, for example, after 9. Bxa6 bxa6 10. c3, 10... Rb8+ would enable White to prepare a new home for his king on b2 by 11. Ka3 and b3. Instead, Black directs his attack against the other flank and, while mowing down some pawns, tries to exploit the general lack of development of White's position.
zh: 9. c4?较弱，因为9... b5!。同样，9. Bxa6 bxa6 10. c3 Qxg2 11. Qf3（或11. Ne2 Bg4 12. Re1 Ne7!）11... Qh3!对白方不利。² 这是推迟攻击暴露的王的典型例子：继续追击只会帮助王稳固位置。例如9. Bxa6 bxa6 10. c3之后，10... Rb8+会让白方通过11. Ka3和b3，在b2为王安排一个新家。黑方因此转向另一侧进攻，一边扫荡白兵，一边设法利用白方整体出子不足。

text: ² This is highly disputable after 12. Qg3 Qxh1 13. Qxe5+ Kf8 14. Nxh3, and White could quickly develop a strong initiative.
zh: ² 12. Qg3 Qxh1 13. Qxe5+ Kf8 14. Nxh3之后，上述判断很值得商榷；白方可以很快取得强劲的主动权。

text: Effective, and probably necessary, although it gives no more than a draw. If 9... Be6 White would reply 10. d4! exd4 11. Bxa6 bxa6 12. Nf3 with the better prospects. Bilguer's Handbuch answers 9... Be6 with 10. d3? d4+ 11. c4 dxc3+ 12. Kxc3 and considers that White retains the advantage. However, after 12... Qd4+ 13. Kd2 Nf6! 14. Qc2 (if he stops 14... Ne4+ by 14. Nc3, then 14... Nc5!) 14... O-O-O 15. Nf3 Qf2+ 16. Kd1 Ng4 Black has excellent chances based on ...e4 and ...Ne3+.
zh: 有力，而且很可能是必需的一步，虽然最多只能取得和棋。如果9... Be6，白方可以10. d4! exd4 11. Bxa6 bxa6 12. Nf3，前景较好。比尔格的《开局谱》给9... Be6的应对是10. d3? d4+ 11. c4 dxc3+ 12. Kxc3，并认为白方仍有优势。然而12... Qd4+ 13. Kd2 Nf6! 14. Qc2（如果14. Nc3阻止14... Ne4+，则14... Nc5!）14... O-O-O 15. Nf3 Qf2+ 16. Kd1 Ng4之后，黑方以...e4和...Ne3+为基础，机会很好。

text: 10. Kxa4 Nc5+ 11. Kb4¹ a5+ 12. Kxc5
zh: 10. Kxa4 Nc5+ 11. Kb4¹ a5+ 12. Kxc5

text: If 12. Kc3? then 12... d4+ 13. Kc4 b6 14. Kd5 f6 15. Kc6 Kd8, and the mating net is complete.²
zh: 如果12. Kc3?，则12... d4+ 13. Kc4 b6 14. Kd5 f6 15. Kc6 Kd8，杀网已经织成。²

text: ¹ In his book Draw!, Wolfgang Heidenfeld offered some rather convincing analysis to prove that White could have won by 11. Kb5!.
zh: ¹ 沃尔夫冈·海登费尔德在《和棋！》中给出了颇有说服力的分析，证明白方可以通过11. Kb5!获胜。

text: ² Heidenfeld pointed out that this line can be improved by 14. Qf3 Be6+ 15. Qd5 Ne7 16. Qxe6 fxe6 with an unclear position.
zh: ² 海登费尔德指出，这个变化可以改进为14. Qf3 Be6+ 15. Qd5 Ne7 16. Qxe6 fxe6，局面不明朗。

caption_zh: 白方走完14. Bc6后的局面

text: The only reply!
zh: 唯一的应对！

text: Against 16. c3? or 16. Ka4?, 16... Nd4 is decisive.
zh: 对16. c3?或16. Ka4?，16... Nd4都是决定性的。

text: He must not capture! If 17. Kxb7? then 17... Kd7 18. Qg4+ Kd6 and White has no defence against 19... Rhb8#.
zh: 不能吃象！如果17. Kxb7?，则17... Kd7 18. Qg4+ Kd6，白方无法防住19... Rhb8#。

text: Black keeps up perpetual check with the bishop on b7 and a6. White's king must not venture to a4 because of ...Bc4 and then ...b5#. An original ending to a king hunt!
zh: 黑象在b7和a6之间往返，形成长将。白王不能冒险走到a4，因为黑方有...Bc4后接...b5#。一场追王竟以如此独特的方式结束！

text: The next game abounds in dramatic features and gives us an opportunity for some more remarks on the subject of attacking a king that has lost the right to castle.
zh: 下一盘棋充满戏剧性，也给了我们进一步讨论如何攻击失去易位权利的王的机会。

text:
Morphy – Barnes
Simultaneous Display against Five Masters, London 1859
Petroff Defence
zh:
墨菲—巴恩斯
1859年，伦敦，对五位大师的车轮战
俄罗斯防御

text: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Bc4
zh: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Bc4

text: Morphy regularly employed this against the Petroff; it does no more than leave the position evenly balanced.
zh: 墨菲经常用这步棋应对俄罗斯防御；这步只能维持均势，并不能带来优势。

text: A dubious gambit originating from Kieseritzky.
zh: 这是基塞里茨基提出的一种可疑的弃兵。

text: 4... Nxc3 5. dxc3 f6!
zh: 4... Nxc3 5. dxc3 f6!

text: A good, as well as necessary, move in this position.
zh: 在这个局面中，这既是好棋，也是必要的一步。

text: 6. O-O Qe7?!
zh: 6. O-O Qe7?!

text: After this White has approximately equal chances. Correct was 6... Nc6! 7. Nh4 g6 8. f4 f5! with advantage to Black.
zh: 这之后白方大致可以保持均势。正确的是6... Nc6! 7. Nh4 g6 8. f4 f5!，黑方有利。

text: 7. Nh4 d6 8. Qh5+ Kd8 9. f4
zh: 7. Nh4 d6 8. Qh5+ Kd8 9. f4

text: 9. Ng6? fails against 9... Qe8.
zh: 9. Ng6?会被9... Qe8反驳。

text: 9... Be6 10. Bxe6 Qxe6 11. fxe5 dxe5 12. Ng6
zh: 9... Be6 10. Bxe6 Qxe6 11. fxe5 dxe5 12. Ng6

text: White regains the pawn, since if 12... Qe8?, then 13. Qd1+! unpins the knight with gain of tempo.
zh: 白方吃回一兵，因为如果12... Qe8?，则13. Qd1+!带着先手解除马的牵制。

text: A positional mistake, since he forfeits the chance of c4, without which his pawn attack is ineffective. 16. a4 was correct.
zh: 这是局面棋方面的错误，因为白方放弃了c4的机会；没有这步冲兵，兵的攻击就缺乏力量。正确的是16. a4。

text: Threatening ...Nf8.
zh: 威胁...Nf8。

text: 18. Qg4 Qe6 19. Qe4 Nb6! (D)
zh: 18. Qg4 Qe6 19. Qe4 Nb6!（见图）
caption_zh: 黑方走完19... Nb6后的局面

text: Owing to the weakness on c4, White's position has lost its sting. Morphy now decides to compromise his game still further by sacrificing his knight; there is probably nothing better.
zh: 由于c4的弱点，白方的局面已经失去锋芒。墨菲现在决定弃马，使自己的局面进一步恶化；大概也没有更好的办法。

text: 20. Qxb7 Qg4 21. a4 Rc8 22. Rad1 Qxg6 23. Be3 Nc4 24. Qc6 Qf7
zh: 20. Qxb7 Qg4 21. a4 Rc8 22. Rad1 Qxg6 23. Be3 Nc4 24. Qc6 Qf7

text: Clearly not 24... Nxe3 because of 25. Rxd6+ Ke7 26. Rd7+ Kf8 27. Qc5+.
zh: 显然不能24... Nxe3，因为25. Rxd6+ Ke7 26. Rd7+ Kf8 27. Qc5+。

text: 25. Bxa7 e4
zh: 25. Bxa7 e4

text: 25... Ke7 would also have been good, followed by ...Kf8 (“delayed artificial castling”).
zh: 25... Ke7也很好，随后...Kf8，完成“姗姗来迟的人工易位”。

text: 26. Rd4 Qh5
zh: 26. Rd4 Qh5

text: Black begins to have his threats. 27. h3 is obviously met by 27... Qe5, while if 27. g3, then 27... Rh8 28. h4 Qe2, threatening mate by either 29... Qxf1+ or 29... Rxh4+. Morphy now finds the one reply which still offers resistance.
zh: 黑方开始制造威胁。27. h3显然可以用27... Qe5应对；如果27. g3，则27... Rh8 28. h4 Qe2，威胁通过29... Qxf1+或29... Rxh4+将杀。墨菲找到了唯一仍能抵抗的应对。

caption_zh: 黑方走完28... e2后的局面

text: 28... Qh4 was probably even stronger.
zh: 28... Qh4很可能更强。

text: Black has drawn his opponent's king out of position but now, when he is faced with the task of producing a mating attack, he stumbles. 31... f5? only appears to tighten the net (that is, by the threat of 32... Qf1+ 33. Rxf1 Rxh2#); in fact it allows the king to escape via g5. 31... Qf1+ 32. Rxf1 Rxh2+ 33. Kg4 Ne5+ would also have been unsound, since after 34. Kg3! Nxc6+ White can liquidate by interpolating 35. Rxd6+ cxd6 36. Bb6+ and only then 37. Kxh2.
zh: 黑方已经把对手的王引了出来，但在需要发动将杀进攻时却失误了。31... f5?只是表面上收紧杀网——威胁32... Qf1+ 33. Rxf1 Rxh2#；实际上却让白王可以经g5逃脱。31... Qf1+ 32. Rxf1 Rxh2+ 33. Kg4 Ne5+也不成立，因为34. Kg3! Nxc6+之后，白方可以插入35. Rxd6+ cxd6 36. Bb6+，然后才37. Kxh2，通过兑换化解局面。

text: 31... Qxc3+ 32. Rd3 (forced) 32... Qe5 33. Qf3 Ke7, etc. was one line which led to victory.
zh: 31... Qxc3+ 32. Rd3（被迫）32... Qe5 33. Qf3 Ke7等，是一条可以取胜的变化。

text: 32. Qxc4! Qf1+ 33. Kh4 Rxh2+ 34. Kg5 Qg2+?
zh: 32. Qxc4! Qf1+ 33. Kh4 Rxh2+ 34. Kg5 Qg2+?

text: After this fresh mistake Black ought to have lost. 34... Qg1+ 35. Rg4 Qe3+ might still have resulted in a win.¹
zh: 又犯了这个错误后，黑方本该输棋。34... Qg1+ 35. Rg4 Qe3+则仍有可能取胜。¹

text: ¹ In fact, it wins rather easily after 36. Kg6 Qh6+ 37. Kxf5 Qxh5+ 38. Rg5 Rf2+ 39. Rf4 Rxf4+ 40. Qxf4 Qf7+. It follows that White should have played 32. Rxc4! instead of 32. Qxc4?, when the position would indeed have been unclear.
zh: ¹ 实际上，36. Kg6 Qh6+ 37. Kxf5 Qxh5+ 38. Rg5 Rf2+ 39. Rf4 Rxf4+ 40. Qxf4 Qf7+后，黑方取胜相当容易。由此可见，白方应该走32. Rxc4!，而不是32. Qxc4?；那样局面才真正不明朗。

caption_zh: 白方走完35. Rg4后的局面

text: By sacrificing his rook White succeeds in blocking the g-file and thus obtaining a respite for his king in the comparative safety of g5. Naturally, the king is only secure there for one or two moves, but in the present position that is enough, for White also has some threats at his disposal.
zh: 白方弃车，成功堵住g线，让王在相对安全的g5获得喘息。当然，王在那里只能安全地待上一两步，但在当前局面中已经足够，因为白方也有一些可以制造的威胁。

text: The initiative now passes to White, and he should win quickly. The creation of a “makeshift shelter” for one or two moves is often extremely important when the king is being pursued, always on the assumption, of course, that the counterattack made possible by the gain of time promises to be successful.
zh: 主动权现在转到白方手中，他应当很快获胜。王被追赶时，为它安排一个能停留一两步的“临时避难所”，往往极其重要。当然，前提始终是：利用赢得的时间发动反击，必须有成功的希望。

text: Fortune smiled on him earlier, but now he loses the game which he could have won, e.g. 36. Rxd6+ cxd6 37. Qg8+ Ke7 (if 37... Kc7 or 37... Kd7, then 38. Qf7+ Kc6 39. b5#) 38. Qxg7+ Ke8 (or 38... Ke6 39. Qf6+ Kd5 40. Qf7+! mating next move) 39. Qg6+ Ke7 (if 39... Kd7 then 40. Qf7+ Kd8 41. Bb6+ Rc7 42. Qxc7+ Ke8 43. Qd8+ Kf7 44. Qf6+ Kg8 45. Qg6+ Kf8 46. Qxd6+, etc.) 40. Qf6+ Ke8 41. Qe6+ Kd8 42. Bb6+ Rc7 43. Qxd6+, etc.
zh: 之前幸运之神曾眷顾白方，现在他却输掉了本来可以获胜的对局。例如36. Rxd6+ cxd6 37. Qg8+ Ke7（如果37... Kc7或37... Kd7，则38. Qf7+ Kc6 39. b5#）38. Qxg7+ Ke8（或38... Ke6 39. Qf6+ Kd5 40. Qf7+!，下一步将杀）39. Qg6+ Ke7（如果39... Kd7，则40. Qf7+ Kd8 41. Bb6+ Rc7 42. Qxc7+ Ke8 43. Qd8+ Kf7 44. Qf6+ Kg8 45. Qg6+ Kf8 46. Qxd6+等）40. Qf6+ Ke8 41. Qe6+ Kd8 42. Bb6+ Rc7 43. Qxd6+等。

text: If 37. Qf8+ then 37... Qe8 38. Rxd6+ cxd6 39. Qxd6+ Qd7 40. Bb6+ Ke8 41. Qxh2 Qe7+ and Black captures the bishop by further checking.
zh: 如果37. Qf8+，则37... Qe8 38. Rxd6+ cxd6 39. Qxd6+ Qd7 40. Bb6+ Ke8 41. Qxh2 Qe7+，黑方继续将军，随后吃掉白象。

text: Barnes played a number of games against Morphy; with his distinctive positional style, he was the most successful of all the British masters against that combinative genius.
zh: 巴恩斯与墨菲下过多盘棋；凭借独特的局面棋风格，他在所有英国大师中，对这位组合战术天才取得了最好的战绩。

text: Now comes the third and last example from the collection of curiosities – the game between Michelet and Kieseritzky, in which the hunted white king is not only saved but goes on actively to participate in the attack on his black colleague. The key to this success is the confinement of Black's queen in a most unusual “cage”.
zh: 接下来是这组奇闻中的第三个、也是最后一个例子：米舍莱对基塞里茨基一局。被追赶的白王不仅获救，还积极参与了对黑王的进攻。成功的关键，是把黑后关进了一个极不寻常的“笼子”。

text:
Michelet – Kieseritzky
Paris, 1845
King's Gambit Accepted
zh:
米舍莱—基塞里茨基
1845年，巴黎
王翼弃兵接受弃兵变例

text: 1. e4 e5 2. f4 exf4 3. Nf3 g5 4. Bc4 g4 5. Ne5
zh: 1. e4 e5 2. f4 exf4 3. Nf3 g5 4. Bc4 g4 5. Ne5

text: Today the Muzio Gambit 5. O-O is considered more promising.
zh: 在作者写作时，5. O-O的穆齐奥弃兵被认为更有希望。

text: The so-called Cochrane Gambit, which is favourable for Black.
zh: 这就是所谓的科克伦弃兵，对黑方有利。

text: 7. d4 Nf6 8. Nc3 Bg7
zh: 7. d4 Nf6 8. Nc3 Bg7

text: 8... fxg2+ is also good.
zh: 8... fxg2+也很好。

text: 9. g3 Qh3+ 10. Kf2 d6 11. Nxf7 Rf8 12. Ng5 Qg2+ 13. Ke3 (D)
zh: 9. g3 Qh3+ 10. Kf2 d6 11. Nxf7 Rf8 12. Ng5 Qg2+ 13. Ke3（见图）
caption_zh: 白方走完13. Ke3后的局面

text: An unsound idea, since White can obviously counter it by Kd3, after which the bishop will have done nothing but lose control of the long diagonal. 13... Nc6 was correct, and if 14. a3 then 14... Ke7 threatening 15... h6.
zh: 这个构想不成立，因为白方显然可以Kd3应对，黑象除了失去对长斜线的控制之外，什么也没有做到。正确的是13... Nc6，如果14. a3，则14... Ke7，威胁15... h6。

text: 14. Kd3 Nc6 15. a3 Bxg5 16. Bxg5 Nxe4
zh: 14. Kd3 Nc6 15. a3 Bxg5 16. Bxg5 Nxe4

text: This sacrifice is incorrect, but Black's position was already inferior as a result of his mistake on the 13th move. White's king is quite happy on d3.
zh: 这次弃子不正确，但黑方第13步的错误已经使局面变差。白王在d3相当舒适。

text: 17. Qe1 Bf5 18. Nxe4 f2 19. Qe3 Kd7 20. Bd5 Rae8 21. Raf1!
zh: 17. Qe1 Bf5 18. Nxe4 f2 19. Qe3 Kd7 20. Bd5 Rae8 21. Raf1!

text: White actually encourages Black to carry out his threat to win the queen, producing an original riposte to it.
zh: 白方实际上鼓励黑方执行得后的威胁，并为此准备了独特的反击。

text: 21... Bxe4+ 22. Bxe4 Rf3 23. Qxf3! gxf3 24. Bf5+
zh: 21... Bxe4+ 22. Bxe4 Rf3 23. Qxf3! gxf3 24. Bf5+

text: White now wins the other rook, leaving the black queen boxed in at g2. White conducts the ending with what is in effect an extra piece and, logically enough, takes his king into battle as well.
zh: 白方现在要吃掉另一只黑车，而黑后被困在g2。白方进入残局后，实际上相当于多一子；他顺理成章地也把王投入了战斗。

text: 24... Re6 25. d5 Ne5+ 26. Ke4 h5 27. dxe6+ Ke8 28. Bf6 h4 29. Bxe5 dxe5 30. Kxe5 hxg3 31. Kf6 1-0
zh: 24... Re6 25. d5 Ne5+ 26. Ke4 h5 27. dxe6+ Ke8 28. Bf6 h4 29. Bxe5 dxe5 30. Kxe5 hxg3 31. Kf6 1-0

text: The final position deserves a diagram.
zh: 最后的局面值得用一张图展示。
caption_zh: 白方走完31. Kf6后的局面

text: Black is lost, since he has no proper defence against Bg6+ followed by e7+ and e8=Q, etc. Black's play throughout this game is an example of how not to conduct an attack on a wandering king.
zh: 黑方已经输了，因为他无法有效防住Bg6+后接e7+、e8=Q等手段。黑方在整盘棋中的表现，为如何进攻游走的王提供了一个反面教材。

text: 3 On castling and attacking the castled position in general
zh: 第三章　易位与攻击王城的一般问题

text: The origin of castling
zh: 易位的起源

text: Castling, the most distinctive move in the whole of chess, affects the nature of mating attacks in various ways and because of its importance in this connection, the general significance of the move is worth examining.
zh: 易位是国际象棋中最独特的走法，它从多个方面影响着将杀进攻的性质。正因为它在这方面十分重要，有必要先考察易位的一般意义。

text: Castling is not of any great antiquity. It is also obvious that such a complex and distinctive operation as the modern castling move was not born in a day, but rather developed gradually from century to century with the evolution of the rules of the game themselves.
zh: 易位并不是自古就有的。显然，现代易位这样复杂而独特的走法，也不是一天之内产生的，而是随着国际象棋规则的演变，经过几个世纪逐渐形成的。

text: In the Indian game of chaturanga (pre-chess) there is no trace of the move, nor can it be found in the Arab shatranj. The first traces of any unusual or exceptional movement being made by the king, out of which the castling move evolved, are to be found in mediaeval European chess, which in its first stages can be described as the first and not very significant revision of shatranj towards providing the pieces with greater mobility. A historical source attesting to this first revision is a work by the Lombard monk Jacobus de Cessolis, in which are recorded the rules governing the movements of the individual chess pieces at the time. There it is stated that king, queen, and pawns have the right to make an initial move of two squares as well as the normal one. From this early reform the double opening step taken by the pawn survives to this day, while in the case of the queen it became obsolete when the piece was given its present powers of movement during the great reform of the game at the end of the fifteenth century. In the case of the king it was further developed and altered until it eventually took its present-day shape as castling.
zh: 在印度的恰图兰加——国际象棋的前身——中，找不到易位的踪迹；阿拉伯的沙特兰兹中也没有。后来演变成易位的王的特殊走法，最早见于中世纪欧洲国际象棋。其早期形态可以说是对沙特兰兹的第一次小幅改造，目的是提高棋子的活动能力。伦巴第修士雅各布斯·德·切索利斯的一部著作，为这次改造提供了史料依据：书中记载了当时各棋子的走法，指出王、后和兵在第一次移动时，除了正常走法，还可以走两格。这次早期改革中，兵初次移动可走两格的规则保留至今；后在十五世纪末的大改革中获得现代走法后，原有的特殊走法便被淘汰了。王的特殊走法则继续变化、发展，最终形成今天的易位。

text: There is extensive confirmation of the introduction of the king's move from other sources after Cessolis, though the particular conditions governing the move vary. The form most frequently recorded is that where the king moves like a knight (“Freudensprung”), with the limitation that it is not allowed to go beyond the second rank. The next form, which made its appearance in Italy in the sixteenth century, already included a movement by the rook in the same move – a step nearer to the castling of today. The king's use of the knight's jump disappears at this point and the rules state that the king is free to move from e1 to g1 or h1 and the rook from h1 to f1 or e1. This type of “free castling” or “Italian castling” persisted in Italy right up to the nineteenth century, when it was superseded by the present rules, which were introduced in France during the eighteenth century.
zh: 切索利斯之后的许多史料也证实了王的这种特殊走法，不过具体条件各不相同。记载最常见的形式，是王可以像马一样跳跃，称为“Freudensprung”，但不能越过己方第二横线。十六世纪意大利出现的下一种形式，已经允许王和车在同一步中同时移动，离现代易位又近了一步。此时王不再采用马的跳跃方式，而是可以自由选择从e1走到g1或h1，车则从h1走到f1或e1。这种“自由易位”或“意大利式易位”，在意大利一直沿用到十九世纪，后来才被现代规则取代；现代易位规则于十八世纪在法国采用。

text: This short survey of the historical evolution of castling is a good illustration of the gradual development of the rules of chess and it makes it particularly clear that these rules have been changed and perfected with the desire of enriching the game; the general tendency towards giving the pieces more dynamic movement reflects the increased animation of social movements in Europe from the Middle Ages onwards.
zh: 这段简短的易位史，清楚展示了国际象棋规则如何逐步发展，也尤其表明：规则的改变和完善，是为了丰富棋艺。棋子走法总体上变得更加活跃，反映出欧洲自中世纪以来社会运动日益活跃的趋势。

text: In addition to this general line of development in the laws of chess, we also owe the introduction and eventual adoption of the castling move to the indirect influence of the great reform of the fifteenth century. This reform created a powerful queen out of the fers (which moved one square) and the modern bishop out of the alfil (which moved exactly two squares). In this new type of chess, with three long-range pieces, the fighting ability of the king declined; once in the days of pre-chess it had been the strongest piece of all. The king now became a hindrance with its slow movement, and its position in the centre of the back rank stood out immediately as a fault in the game's structure. On the one hand, it had to be safeguarded against the formidable new forces, and on the other it had to be removed from the centre so as not to hamper them. For this reason it was necessary for the king to get away from the centre as quickly as possible, and it was to this end that the king's double move was built on and transformed into the full castling move.
zh: 除了规则发展的总体趋势，易位的产生和最终确立，也受到十五世纪大改革的间接推动。这场改革把只能走一格的fers变成威力强大的后，把只能跳两格的alfil变成现代的象。在这种拥有三个远程棋子的新式国际象棋中，王的战斗力相对下降了；在古代的前身棋种中，王曾是最强的棋子。现在，王移动缓慢，反而成了障碍；它位于底线中央，立刻显露为棋局结构上的一个缺陷。一方面，必须保护王，使其免受新生强大子力的攻击；另一方面，又必须让它离开中心，以免妨碍这些子力。王因此需要尽快撤离中心，原有的初次走两格的规则便逐步发展成完整的易位走法。

text: Therefore, not only the development of this most distinctive move can be traced through the history of chess but also its logic: it exists as the necessary complement to the reform of the other pieces' movements. We start a game of chess today with the pieces placed in the ancient order which derives from chaturanga, and then we switch over by castling to a new position, which is better suited to the alterations made in the game's rules.
zh: 因此，沿着国际象棋的历史，我们不仅能追溯这步独特走法的演变，也能理解它的内在逻辑：易位是其他棋子走法改革所必需的补充。今天开局时，棋子仍按源自恰图兰加的古老次序摆放；随后通过易位，我们转入一个更适合新规则的阵形。

text: The dynamic and positional significance of castling
zh: 易位的动态意义与局面棋意义

text: Chess moves in general can be looked at from the dynamic or the positional point of view, depending on whether we are considering them as part of an active combination or as static features.
zh: 一般来说，可以从动态或局面棋的角度考察走法，取决于我们把它看作具体组合战术的一部分，还是看作局面的静态特征。

text: The castling move without doubt powerfully increases the dynamic potential of a position. A player who has castled at once obtains a whole range of possibilities which he did not have before. He has increased the influence of the rook, cleared the square e1 for a possible attack along the e-file, and on top of this he has prepared the ground for the quick establishment of “communication between the rooks”, i.e. the entire clearing of the back rank, as a result of which the rooks cover each other or can combine together in attacks.
zh: 易位无疑能大幅增强局面的动态潜力。完成易位的一方，立即获得原先没有的一系列机会：车的作用扩大了，e1腾空了，可以准备沿e线进攻；此外，易位还为迅速“接通两车”创造了条件，也就是把底线完全清空，让两车互相保护，或联手参与进攻。

text: On the other hand, castling is also a positional move, and one which provides a particular element of permanency to the position. For it is unique and irrevocable; it can only be carried out once in a game, which means that the king will as a rule stay on the side on which it has castled. In special cases it can, it is true, travel with a greater or lesser degree of difficulty from its castled position to various parts of the board. Thus castling is only relatively irrevocable (unlike a pawn's move, which is absolutely so) but for practical purposes the king's position after castling is, at least until the arrival of the endgame, fairly definitely a permanent positional feature. Before castling, the king has three possible courses of action: to remain in the middle or to castle either to right or left. Once it has castled it no longer has any choice; it then has a definite shelter, a “permanent address”, a fact which the opponent naturally takes into account. It is certainly safer against attack, but it has at the same time committed itself positionally to one particular area of the board; thus the undoubted advantages of castling are offset by certain disadvantages.
zh: 另一方面，易位也是局面棋走法，为局面带来一种持久特征。易位只能进行一次，而且不可撤销；通常，王会留在它易位到的那一侧。当然，在特殊情况下，王也能克服不同程度的困难，从王城走到棋盘的其他区域。因此，易位只是相对不可逆，不像兵的移动那样绝对不可逆。但从实战角度看，至少在残局到来之前，易位后的王位便构成了局面中的一个持久特征。易位前，王有三种选择：留在中央，向右易位，或向左易位。一旦易位，就不再有同样的选择；它有了确定的庇护处，一个“固定住址”，对手自然会把这一点考虑进去。王固然更能抵御进攻，却也把自身的位置限定在棋盘的某一区域。所以，易位确实带来的好处，也伴随着一定的不利之处。

text: Artificial castling
zh: 人工易位

text: Chess also contains the term “artificial castling”, which involves a player creating a position the same as or similar to that reached after genuine castling. It is attained not by a single castling move but a series of moves by the king and the rook. In the continuation from the following diagram we shall encounter the simplest example of “artificial castling”.
zh: 国际象棋还有“人工易位”这个说法，指的是通过调动，形成与真正易位后相同或相似的阵形。它不是用一步易位完成的，而是靠王和车连续移动几步实现的。下图的后续手段，就是最简单的人工易位例子。

text: Black, to move, played:
zh: 轮到黑方行棋，他走了：

text: White's best would now be 2. Nxe4 d5 3. Bd3 dxe4 4. Bxe4, in which case the prospects would remain even. However, before taking the knight on e4 White decides to use his bishop to prevent his opponent from castling – an idea which, in this position, is faulty.
zh: 白方现在最好走2. Nxe4 d5 3. Bd3 dxe4 4. Bxe4，双方仍然均势。但白方决定先用象阻止对手易位，再吃e4马；在这个局面中，这个构想是错误的。

text: 2. Bxf7+ Kxf7 3. Nxe4
zh: 2. Bxf7+ Kxf7 3. Nxe4

text: At first sight White's plan appears to have succeeded, since, as well as maintaining the material balance, he has prevented Black from castling. However, the further play shows that Black can carry out “artificial castling” without difficulty and has made a clear gain in that he is left with strong pawns in the centre.
zh: 乍看之下，白方的计划似乎成功了：子力仍然平衡，而且黑方已不能易位。但后续走法表明，黑方可以轻松完成人工易位，并且留下了强大的中心兵，获得了实实在在的好处。

text: Now the superiority of Black's position is quite obvious, and one can easily appreciate the part played by “artificial castling”; Black has admittedly expended three moves on it, but White has derived no advantage from this fact, since he has made three moves of even less value, i.e. Bxf7+, Nxe4, and Ng3. In a sense, Black was castling while White was transferring his knight from c3 to g3.
zh: 黑方的局面优势现在相当明显，人工易位的作用也很容易看出来。黑方固然为此用了三步，但白方并没有占到便宜，因为他自己的三步——Bxf7+、Nxe4和Ng3——价值更低。某种意义上，白方把马从c3调到g3的同时，黑方完成了易位。

text: The correct moment for castling
zh: 易位的正确时机

text: Beginners are often advised to castle as quickly as possible. This is a useful and sensible piece of advice in the majority of instances. Certainly, less experienced players offend against this general precept extremely often, postponing castling unnecessarily and as a result suddenly finding themselves in an awkward situation, by which time it is far too late to castle. The present writer once made a statistical survey of late castling using a number of simultaneous games and came to the conclusion that a common characteristic of so-called “simultaneous massacres” (when the master wins all, or nearly all, of the games) was precisely the lateness of castling.
zh: 初学者常被建议尽快易位。在大多数情况下，这条建议既有用，也合理。经验不足的棋手却经常违背这条一般准则，无端拖延易位，结果突然陷入窘境，此时再想易位已为时太晚。我曾统计过一些车轮战中的迟易位现象，发现所谓“车轮战大屠杀”——大师赢下全部或几乎全部对局——的一个共同特征，正是对手易位太迟。

text: Around the twelfth move of one such simultaneous display the situation was as follows: the master had castled on eighteen of the boards and not yet on two, while his opponents had castled on three boards but not on the rest. The result: 2O-O to the master – a real massacre! This is a typical example which indicates the disadvantages resulting from a delay in castling. In other simultaneous displays, where masters had a harder task and poorer results, the statistics on castling, taken around the twelfth to fifteenth moves, on the whole showed smaller discrepancies.
zh: 在其中一场车轮战的大约第12回合，大师已经在18盘棋中完成易位，仅有2盘尚未易位；他的对手却只有3人易位，其余都没有。结果是大师以20比0全胜，真正的一边倒！这个典型例子说明了拖延易位的不利影响。而在其他大师下得更艰难、成绩更差的车轮战中，第12至15回合左右的易位统计，总体上显示双方的差距较小。

text: The general rule that one should castle as soon as possible is therefore quite in order, though it must at once be emphasized that there are also many exceptions to it. Every chess player of greater experience is well acquainted with those particular situations when it is correct to postpone castling or when it is altogether unnecessary. To make the matter clearer, I shall set out some situations of this kind and support them with examples:
zh: 因此，尽快易位这条一般规则是合理的；但也必须立即强调，它有许多例外。经验丰富的棋手都熟悉一些特殊局面：推迟易位是正确的，或者根本不需要易位。为了说得更清楚，下面列举几种情况，并用例子说明。

text: 1) Castling is postponed or not carried out at all, because some other action is more useful. This might be quite simply the capture of an opponent's piece, the spoiling of his position, or, indeed, an attack. If such an attack is sufficiently strong and profitable, the attacker often never castles, because he is victorious first. This kind of situation needs no particular examples.
zh: 1）因为其他行动更有用，所以推迟易位，甚至完全不易位。这可能只是吃掉对手一个子、破坏对手的局面，也可能是发动进攻。如果进攻足够有力、收益足够大，进攻方往往还没易位就已经获胜。这种情况不需要专门举例。

text: 2) Castling is postponed, because for the time being it is still dangerous. It is better to prepare it by removing the danger first, e.g. by exchanging the opponent's threatening pieces or by some other manoeuvre.
zh: 2）因为眼下易位仍有危险，所以推迟。最好先消除危险，为易位做好准备，例如兑掉对手具有威胁的棋子，或采用其他调动手段。

text: As an example of the dangers of castling too early, let us take the following variation of the Giuoco Piano.
zh: 下面这个意大利开局的变化，可以说明过早易位的危险。

text: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. d3 Nf6 5. Bg5 h6 6. Bh4 d6 7. O-O?
zh: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. d3 Nf6 5. Bg5 h6 6. Bh4 d6 7. O-O?

text: At this point castling is premature and incorrect. There is a danger of Black's replying ...g5 and following up with a pawn attack against White's castled position; this danger ought to be averted first. 7. Nc3 is a step in this direction; if Black continues with 7... O-O? 8. Nd5 g5, then White can reply 9. Nxg5! Nxd5 10. Qh5 hxg5 11. Bxg5 with an overwhelming attack. Moreover, if Black answers 7. Nc3 with 7... g5 8. Bg3 and then ...Bg4 or ...h5!?, the situation is less dangerous because White has not yet castled and can therefore prepare to castle on the queenside, which is not threatened.
zh: 此时易位为时过早，也是不正确的。黑方可能应以...g5，随后用兵攻击白方王城；白方应当先防止这种危险。7. Nc3正是朝这个方向努力：如果黑方继续7... O-O? 8. Nd5 g5，则白方可以9. Nxg5! Nxd5 10. Qh5 hxg5 11. Bxg5，获得势不可挡的进攻。此外，如果7. Nc3 g5 8. Bg3后，黑方继续...Bg4或...h5!?，危险也较小，因为白方尚未易位，可以准备在没有受到威胁的后翼长易位。

caption_zh: 黑方走完9... h4后的局面

text: Black does not worry about the consequences of Nxf7 but continues his attack consistently. In fact, he gives up his queen for the bishop on g3; this would not be a good exchange if White had not castled, but against the castled position the attack is decisive.
zh: 黑方不担心Nxf7的后果，而是坚持进攻。实际上，他以自己的后换掉g3象；如果白方尚未易位，这样的交换就不好，但白方已经易位，黑方就能发动制胜进攻。

text: 10. Nxf7 hxg3 11. Nxd8
zh: 10. Nxf7 hxg3 11. Nxd8

text: If 11. hxg3, then 11... Qe7 12. Nxh8 Qh7 followed by ...Ng4, with a decisive attack.
zh: 如果11. hxg3，则11... Qe7 12. Nxh8 Qh7，随后...Ng4，黑方获得决定性的进攻。

text: 11... Bg4 12. Nf7 Rxh2! 13. Qd2 Nd4 14. Nc3 Nf3+ 15. gxf3 Bxf3 16. Qh6 Rg2+ 17. Kh1 Rxf2+ 18. Kg1 Rg2+ 19. Kh1 Rg1#
zh: 11... Bg4 12. Nf7 Rxh2! 13. Qd2 Nd4 14. Nc3 Nf3+ 15. gxf3 Bxf3 16. Qh6 Rg2+ 17. Kh1 Rxf2+ 18. Kg1 Rg2+ 19. Kh1 Rg1#

text: 3) The player does not castle at once because, although he is able to castle on one side, he actually wishes to castle on the other side and needs to make further preparations. Alternatively, he delays until his opponent castles, and only then decides which side to castle. If he is aiming for an attack, he may decide to castle on the opposite side to his opponent; if he is aiming to forestall an attack, then he will more likely castle on the same side as his opponent.
zh: 3）虽然已经可以向一侧易位，但棋手实际上想向另一侧易位，还需要进一步准备，因此没有立即易位。另一种情况是，他等对手先易位，然后才决定自己向哪一侧易位。如果想进攻，他可能选择与对手异向易位；如果想防止进攻，则更可能选择同向易位。

text: There are many examples in the games of the masters of this kind of pause before castling. It is assumed, of course, that this pause does not entail any dangers. In open positions such dangers are more frequent than in closed ones.
zh: 大师对局中有许多这样暂缓易位的例子。当然，前提是这种等待不会带来危险。在开放局面中，这类危险比封闭局面更常见。

text: The following situation will serve as an example of this pause before castling.
zh: 下面的局面可以说明这种暂缓易位的做法。

text: It is White's move and he may, if he wishes, castle short immediately. But he calculates as follows: after 1. O-O Black will play ...O-O, and then how can I attack him? The pieces by themselves can achieve nothing in this blocked position; h3 and g4 still need to be played and must be prepared by Qd2. But in the meantime Black will consolidate his position on the kingside (e.g. by means of ...g6 and ...Rf8-f7-g7) after which the attack will have lost its power.
zh: 轮到白方行棋，如果愿意，他可以立即短易位。但他这样考虑：1. O-O之后，黑方会...O-O，届时怎样进攻呢？在这个封闭局面中，单靠棋子无法有所作为；还必须走h3和g4，而这些冲兵又需要先用Qd2准备。与此同时，黑方却会巩固王翼，例如通过...g6和...Rf8-f7-g7；等黑方站稳，进攻便失去力量了。

text: There is no doubt that for an attack based on g4, White's king is not well placed at g1, and it is better for that purpose to castle on the queenside and then deploy the rooks on the g- and h-files. However, if White chooses 1. Qd2 and then 2. O-O-O, Black can play 2... O-O-O, whereupon the attack with g4 no longer applies; White will have to play a hasty b4, in which case it will be quickly seen that his king is badly placed on c1. Consequently, he must put off castling and wait. White therefore plays 1. Qe2, and if 1... O-O, then 2. O-O-O, while if 1... O-O-O, then 2. O-O. He castles on the opposite side from Black in order to get the maximum freedom for carrying out his attack.
zh: 若要以g4为基础发动进攻，白王放在g1显然并不理想；为此最好长易位，再把两车部署到g线和h线。但如果白方选择1. Qd2后接2. O-O-O，黑方也可以2... O-O-O，此时g4进攻就不适用了。白方将不得不仓促冲起b4，很快便会发现c1的王位置不好。因此，他必须暂缓易位，等一等。于是白方走1. Qe2：如果1... O-O，就2. O-O-O；如果1... O-O-O，就2. O-O。他选择与黑方异向易位，让自己的进攻获得最大的行动自由。

text: 4) Castling may be postponed, and perhaps forgone forever, in certain positions where the centre is permanently blocked.
zh: 4）在中心长期封闭的某些局面中，可以推迟易位，甚至始终不易位。

text: The reason for being able to postpone castling in such positions is, of course, that the pawns form an obstruction in the centre and so make it impossible to open the central files and diagonals without painful sacrifices. With the centre blocked, the kings are also safer in the middle, at least for some time. The logical course of attack in such cases tends to be on the unblocked flanks, and there are times when the king is more exposed by being in a castled position on the wing than in the middle, where it is protected by the blocked pawns.
zh: 之所以可以推迟易位，当然是因为中心的兵形成屏障；不付出沉重的弃子代价，就无法打开中心的纵线和斜线。中心封闭时，王留在中央也较安全，至少在一段时间内如此。这类局面中，合理的进攻方向往往是尚未封闭的两翼。有时王易位到侧翼后反而更暴露，还不如留在中央，受到相互堵住的兵的保护。

text: A convenient example to illustrate this can be obtained by re-examining the above diagram, which we ought to do anyway because we left White's move 1. Qe2 unanswered. Black's best reply also consists of a postponement of castling, e.g. 1... a6 or 1... Nd8. The postponement of castling is feasible for both sides in this position, and for a very obvious reason: the pronounced blockade in the centre. Attacks can only take place down the flanks and as a result the kings are at the moment relatively safe in the middle. Play from this position might develop as follows:
zh: 重新考察上图，便能方便地说明这一点；我们本来也应该再看一看，因为还没有回答白方1. Qe2之后黑方怎么办。黑方最佳的应对同样是推迟易位，例如1... a6或1... Nd8。双方在这个局面中都可以暂缓易位，原因很明显：中心牢固地封闭着。进攻只能在两翼展开，因此两王眼下留在中央相对安全。对局可能这样发展：

text: 1. Qe2 Nd8 2. h3 Nf7 3. Qd2 O-O-O
zh: 1. Qe2 Nd8 2. h3 Nf7 3. Qd2 O-O-O

text: It is less dangerous for Black to castle on the queenside now; if White plays 4. O-O, Black replies 4... Rdg8, threatening ...g5, while after 4. O-O-O the danger of an attack on the flank disappears and Black can relax.
zh: 黑方现在长易位，危险已经较小。如果白方4. O-O，黑方应以4... Rdg8，威胁...g5；如果白方4. O-O-O，受到侧翼进攻的危险便消失了，黑方可以安心。

text: In this case the preliminary skirmish has in fact ended with castling, but there are blocked positions where castling does not occur at all and the kings stay permanently in the middle. Even in the above position White has the alternative of not castling and instead co-ordinating his rooks by Kf2; later on he can even take his king up to e3.
zh: 这个例子中的前期交锋最终还是以易位告一段落，但某些封闭局面中，双方根本不会易位，两王始终留在中央。即使在上面的局面中，白方也可以不易位，而是用Kf2接通两车；以后甚至可以把王走到e3。

text: 5) Castling is unnecessary, because the endgame is already not far off, in which case the king is well placed in the middle of the board.
zh: 5）残局已经不远，王留在棋盘中央位置很好，因此不需要易位。

text: These cases too are not infrequent in master chess; we shall select two examples from opening theory, where the white king forfeits the right to castle as a result of the exchange of queens.
zh: 这种情况在大师对局中也不少见。我们从开局理论中选出两个例子，白王都因兑后而失去易位权利。

text: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Nbd7 5. e3 Be7 6. Nf3 O-O 7. Rc1 c6 8. Bd3 dxc4 9. Bxc4 Nd5 (D)
zh: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Nbd7 5. e3 Be7 6. Nf3 O-O 7. Rc1 c6 8. Bd3 dxc4 9. Bxc4 Nd5（见图）
caption_zh: 黑方走完9... Nd5后的局面

text: Capablanca's freeing manoeuvre in the Orthodox Defence to the Queen's Gambit.
zh: 这是后翼弃兵正统防御中，卡帕布兰卡用来解放局面的调动手段。

text: 10. Bxe7 Qxe7 11. Ne4 Qb4+ 12. Qd2 Qxd2+ 13. Kxd2
zh: 10. Bxe7 Qxe7 11. Ne4 Qb4+ 12. Qd2 Qxd2+ 13. Kxd2

text: This variation was played in a number of games from the 1927 World Championship Match between Capablanca and Alekhine. White does not worry about castling, as the position is approaching an endgame and the king is fairly safe in the middle of the board.
zh: 1927年卡帕布兰卡与阿廖欣的世界冠军赛中，多盘棋出现过这个变化。白方不必担心易位，因为局面已接近残局，王在棋盘中央相当安全。

text: A second example is supplied by my analysis of a variation of the Slav Defence.
zh: 第二个例子来自我对斯拉夫防御一个变化的分析。

text: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nc3 dxc4 4. e4 e5 5. dxe5!
zh: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nc3 dxc4 4. e4 e5 5. dxe5!

text: In my Modern Opening Theory I suggested that this was better than 5. Bxc4.
zh: 我在《现代开局理论》中提出，这步比5. Bxc4更好。
5... Qxd1+ 6. Kxd1!（见图）
caption_zh: 白方走完6. Kxd1后的局面

text: White could have retained his right to castle by playing 6. Nxd1; however, it is better to use the king since castling is no longer necessary in this position, and it is more important that the knight should remain on c3. For example, after 6. Nxd1 b5 7. a4 Black is not obliged to continue with ...b4, whereas after 6. Kxd1 b5 7. a4 he has nothing better than 7... b4, whereupon White obtains the advantage by 8. Nb1 Ba6 9. Nd2.
zh: 白方本可以6. Nxd1保留易位权利，但用王吃后更好，因为这个局面中已经不需要易位，保持马在c3反而更重要。例如6. Nxd1 b5 7. a4之后，黑方不必继续...b4；而6. Kxd1 b5 7. a4之后，黑方除了7... b4没有更好的选择，白方随后8. Nb1 Ba6 9. Nd2取得优势。

text: In this instance White, in playing Kxd1, does not gain the “centralizing tempo” which he did on the thirteenth move in the previous example, but he prefers to lose his chance to castle just to keep his knight on c3.
zh: 这个例子中，白方走Kxd1，并不像上一例第13步那样，顺便省下王向中心移动的一步；他宁可失去易位机会，只为把马留在c3。

text: Many occasions for renouncing castling in this way arise in practice, but one should avoid taking the king too far afield. This comment applies to so-called “queenless middlegames” and not to true endgames, in which the king is nearly always better placed in the centre. One should keep one's eyes open and weigh up the opponent's opportunities for an attack on one's king, for they can easily develop in “queenless middlegames”. Safety from attack and a genuine prospect of making further piece exchanges – these are the two important criteria affecting a decision on the forfeiture of the right to castle.
zh: 实战中有许多这样放弃易位的机会，但应当避免让王走得过远。这条提醒适用于所谓的“无后中局”，不适用于真正的残局；真正的残局中，王几乎总是在中心更好。无后中局仍很容易出现针对王的进攻，所以必须保持警觉，衡量对手的机会。王能否免受进攻，以及是否确实有望进一步兑换子力，是决定是否放弃易位权利的两项重要标准。

text: The cases I have mentioned in which castling can be justifiably postponed or dispensed with are meant to induce the reader to think about the problem more deeply, for every rule in chess should be applied flexibly. To make a correct decision on exactly when to castle one needs considerable knowledge and experience.
zh: 我列举这些可以合理推迟或放弃易位的情况，是希望读者对这个问题作更深入的思考，因为国际象棋的每一条规则都应灵活运用。要正确决定究竟何时易位，需要相当的知识和经验。

text: Finally, one more hint: even in cases where there is justification for a delay in castling, it is still a good thing to have the opportunity to castle quickly on one side at least. When the pieces have been moved out on one side of the back rank, we have an opportunity to castle “at hand”, and this castling will cost just one tempo. However, if there is one piece which has still not left the back rank then obviously castling will cost us two tempi. Now there is a big difference between one tempo and two, if one's opponent can discover some concealed means for a sudden attack on the king before it has reached its castled residence! For this reason it is good policy to get ready to castle as soon as possible, and then consider whether it can still be put off for a while.
zh: 最后再提醒一点：即使有理由推迟易位，至少把一侧迅速易位的条件准备好，仍是好事。当底线一侧的棋子已经出动，就可以随时易位，只需花一步。如果还有一个子没有离开底线，完成易位显然就要花两步。如果对手发现了隐蔽手段，能在王进入王城前突然发动进攻，那么只需一步与需要两步的时间差别就十分关键了！因此，最好尽快做好易位准备，然后再考虑是否可以继续稍等。

text: The basic elements of the attack on the castled king
zh: 攻击已经易位的王的基本要素

text: The attack on the castled king is a particular type of mating attack, but in practice it is the most important, since castling takes place in the majority of games.
zh: 攻击已经易位的王，是将杀进攻的一种特殊类型；但在实战中，它最为重要，因为大多数对局都会出现易位。

text: In considering an attack of this kind, we must begin with a general survey of the action involved, acquainting ourselves, on the one hand, with the basic characteristics of the actual castled position itself and, on the other, with the good and bad aspects of an attack on that position.
zh: 考察这类进攻时，首先必须总体了解所涉及的行动：一方面认识王城本身的基本特征，另一方面认识对王城发动进攻的有利与不利之处。

text: The castled position consists of the castled king and the protective pawns and also to a certain extent the pieces which are in the vicinity or in some other way connected with the formation.
zh: 王城由易位后的王和保护它的兵组成；在一定程度上，也包括附近的棋子，或以其他方式与这一阵形发生联系的棋子。

text: This structure should be regarded as a positional formation, i.e. a group of pieces having one or more fairly permanent features. One could also go further and say that castled positions are, as a rule, passive rather than active positional formations, i.e. their more permanent feature stems ultimately from a certain immobility of the pieces, and not in their mobility, as is the case when the pieces are in strong positions. (This is, of course, the general rule, but in practice the castled position may also contain a piece in a strong position, for example a fianchettoed bishop.)
zh: 这种结构应看作一种局面棋阵形，即一组具有一个或几个相当持久特征的棋子。进一步说，王城通常是被动而非主动的阵形：它的持久性，归根结底来自某些棋子不能轻易移动，而不是来自子力占据强大位置时所具有的活动能力。当然，这只是一般规律；实战中的王城也可能包含位置强大的棋子，例如侧翼出动的象。

text: The passive nature of the castled position results from the lack of mobility of the king, and this is indirectly transferred to the other pieces in the position as well; the first to be affected are the pawns, which “may not be moved, if the castled position is not to be weakened”, and which are as a result made indirectly immobile. If they in fact move from their initial squares and so create weaknesses in the castled position, these weaknesses result from the reduced options entailed by the advance. (A pawn at h2 controls the square g3 and also has it in its power, by advancing, to govern g4, g5, g6, etc. If it moves to h3, then, out of its total number of actual or potential areas of control, it loses that over g3, and so loses part of its active potential.)
zh: 王城的被动性质，来自王的活动能力不足，并间接传递给阵形中的其他棋子。首先受影响的是兵：“如果不想削弱王城，就不能轻易动这些兵”，因此它们也间接变得难以移动。兵离开原位后若造成王城弱点，根源就在于冲兵减少了它的选择。例如，h2兵控制g3，也可以通过冲兵控制g4、g5、g6等格。如果冲起h3，它在所有实际或潜在的控制范围中，就失去了对g3的控制，因此丧失了一部分活动潜力。

text: Even the pieces associated with the castled position are affected to a certain extent by the general immobility of the formation, whether functionally because of the need for a certain square to be defended or spatially because of the difficulty involved in their centralization.
zh: 连与王城有关的其他棋子，也会在一定程度上受到整个阵形不易移动的影响：从作用上说，它们可能必须守住某个格；从空间上说，它们可能难以向中心调动。

text: The structure and the degree of weakness of the opponent's castled position also influence the way in which the attacker employs his pieces in a mating attack. The variety here is extremely wide, ranging from lightning assaults to purely positional manoeuvres and from uncompromising charges to cautious preparations, in which the player really only flirts with an attack on the king in order to restrict his opponent's options. More will be said on these and similar points later on.
zh: 对手王城的结构和薄弱程度，也影响进攻方在将杀进攻中怎样运用子力。这里的方式变化极多：从闪电般的突袭，到纯粹的局面棋调动；从毫不妥协的猛攻，到谨慎的准备——有时棋手实际上只是佯示杀王，用来限制对手的选择。后文会进一步讨论这些问题。

text: However, the basic weaknesses of the castled position which I have described also contain one positive feature which becomes apparent when an attempt is made to exploit them. This positive feature derives from the fact that the castled position is always a decentralized one, so that as a rule any attack on it demands a greater or lesser decentralization of the attacker's pieces. This factor is particularly important in that the main positional rule for normal play is that pieces should be centralized. There is, then, a basic contradiction between consistent centralization and an attack on the castled king, and it is here that the principal risk of such an attack lies. If the attack does not succeed, the fact that some of the attacker's pieces are out of position as a rule tells against the attacker.
zh: 不过，我刚才描述的王城基本弱点，也包含一个有利因素；一旦有人试图利用这些弱点，它就会显现出来。这源于王城始终偏离中心，因此对王城的进攻，通常也要求进攻方的子力不同程度地离开中心。这一点尤其重要，因为正常行棋的一条主要局面棋原则，是让子力向中心集中。因此，坚持子力中心化与攻击已经易位的王之间，存在一个基本矛盾，这正是此类进攻的主要风险所在。如果进攻不成功，进攻方一些棋子偏离了理想位置，通常就会反过来对自己不利。

text: The reader will come to understand the deeper significance of this argument in the final chapters of this book.
zh: 在本书最后几章，读者将理解这段论述更深层的意义。

text: To understand the attack on the castled king we shall start with the basic factors involved, spatial, material and temporal (the method I applied in my Introduction to Chess and School of Combinations). It is true that in every action which takes place on the chessboard all these three factors can be observed together, since each move has its own spatial, material and temporal significance; however, the emphasis of one's actual observation may be in one case on the spatial, in another on the material, and in a third on the temporal, aspect. For this reason, the separation of the different factors is the most effective and the clearest method for teaching purposes.
zh: 要理解对已经易位的王的进攻，我们先从其中的基本因素入手：空间、子力和时间。这也是我在《国际象棋入门》和《组合教程》中采用的方法。的确，棋盘上的每个行动都同时涉及这三个因素，因为每一步都具有空间、子力和时间上的意义；但实际观察时，有时重点在空间，有时在子力，有时在时间。因此，出于教学目的，把不同因素分别讨论，是最有效、最清楚的方法。

text: The attack on the castled king in the past
zh: 攻击已经易位的王的历史

text: At the time when modern chess was in its infancy, i.e. after the reforms of the rules in the last quarter of the fifteenth century, the attack on the castled king did not yet exist, or at any rate there was no trace of it in the games recorded. The castling move itself was at that time only in the process of being created (some were still using the mediaeval king's jump, while others were castling but in two moves – i.e. first Rh1-f1, and then on the next move Ke1-g1, etc.) and combinative technique – especially with the “new pieces”, the queen and the knight – was still fairly primitive, so that the decision in a game was usually reached by cruder methods than by attacking the castled king, e.g. by capturing on f7 before castling had taken place or simply by winning material.
zh: 现代国际象棋刚刚起步时，也就是十五世纪最后四分之一时期的规则改革之后，攻击已经易位的王尚未出现，至少留存的对局记录中没有它的踪迹。当时易位本身还在形成过程中：有人仍采用中世纪的王跳跃，也有人分两步易位，例如先把车从h1移到f1，下一步再把王从e1移到g1。组合技术仍相当原始，尤其是运用这些“新棋子”——后和马——的技术。因此，对局通常通过比攻击王城更粗糙的办法分出胜负，例如趁对手尚未易位吃f7，或只是取得子力优势。

text: The first recorded instance of an attack on the castled king occurs in the so-called Paris MS., which originated about 1500, a more mature and fuller development of Lucena's work of 1497, the oldest printed book on modern chess. In the course of analysing an opening (one later given the name of Philidor Defence) the author arrives at the position at the top of the following page. Black, to move, plays:
zh: 最早有记录的王城进攻，见于约1500年形成的所谓《巴黎手稿》。它是在卢塞纳1497年著作的基础上，更成熟、更完整的发展；卢塞纳的那部书是最早印行的现代国际象棋书。作者在分析一种后来被称为菲利道尔防御的开局时，得到了下图局面。轮到黑方行棋，他走了：

text: He uses his pawns to carry out an attack on the king, a plan suited to this position as it takes advantage of White's weakness on h3.
zh: 黑方用兵攻击王，这个计划适合当前局面，因为它利用了白方h3的弱点。

text: A mistake, which Lucena makes “in accordance with the thought of his times”. White could have defended himself satisfactorily if he had immediately played 3. b5!.
zh: 这是卢塞纳“按照那个时代的思维方式”犯下的错误。白方如果立即3. b5!，本来可以有效防守。

text: A further mistake. White should at once have played 5. bxc6 Nxc6 6. Qd5 Qd7 7. Ba3, when Black, pinned down at c6 and g8, would have had to refrain from going straight ahead with ...g4 and consolidate his position first.
zh: 又一个错误。白方应当立即5. bxc6 Nxc6 6. Qd5 Qd7 7. Ba3。这样黑方在c6和g8受到牵制，就不能径直...g4，而必须先巩固自身局面。

text: 5... g4 6. fxg4 hxg4 7. Nxg4?
zh: 5... g4 6. fxg4 hxg4 7. Nxg4?

text: Poor defensive technique! After 7. Kh1 Black would have had a difficult task, for 7... gxh3 would not do any good because of 8. Qh5+ followed by Qxh3.
zh: 防守技术欠佳！7. Kh1会让黑方不容易进攻，因为7... gxh3毫无益处，白方有8. Qh5+后接Qxh3。

text: 7... Nxg4 8. hxg4 Rxg4 9. bxc6 Nxc6 10. Nd5 Bd8 (D)
zh: 7... Nxg4 8. hxg4 Rxg4 9. bxc6 Nxc6 10. Nd5 Bd8（见图）

text: White could have put up more resistance by 11. Ra3. No real advantage would come of 11. Qc4 because of 11... Kd7. Naturally, 11. c4? is very weak and quite inappropriate, since it does nothing to help the defence and only obstructs the diagonal for the white queen.
zh: 白方用11. Ra3可以作出更顽强的抵抗。11. Qc4也不能带来实际好处，因为黑方有11... Kd7。11. c4?自然很弱，也完全不合时宜：它对防守毫无帮助，只会堵住白后的斜线。

text: Black's technique is poor too. After 13... Rgh4 14. Rf1 Qg6!, White would be caught in a mating net.
zh: 黑方的技术也欠佳。13... Rgh4 14. Rf1 Qg6!之后，白方就会落入杀网。

text: 14. Kf1 Qh5 15. Qf3 Qg6 16. Qd3 Rh1+?
zh: 14. Kf1 Qh5 15. Qf3 Qg6 16. Qd3 Rh1+?

text: The manuscript follows on from here with 17. Ke2 Rxa1 18. Bxa1 Rxg2 and concludes: “Black has the better prospects”. To all appearances the author was mainly concerned with the win of a pawn, forgetting that the primary aim of an attack on the castled king is mate! By 16... Rg3 17. Qc2 Qg4 18. Ke1 Ba5+ the matter could have been brought to an end considerably more quickly.
zh: 手稿接着给出17. Ke2 Rxa1 18. Bxa1 Rxg2，并得出结论：“黑方前景更好。”看起来作者主要关心的是如何得一兵，却忘了攻击王城的首要目标是将杀！16... Rg3 17. Qc2 Qg4 18. Ke1 Ba5+本来可以快得多地结束战斗。

text: The advance in technique in attacking the castled king was extremely slow throughout the sixteenth century, and it was only at the beginning of the seventeenth that Greco in his manual indicated some combinations which, though new then, now strike modern minds as nothing more than elementary tricks. As an example of the technical level reached by Greco, let us look at a continuation from his book.
zh: 整个十六世纪，攻击王城的技术进步极其缓慢。直到十七世纪初，格雷科才在自己的手册中给出一些组合战术；它们在当时是新发现，在现代棋手看来却只是基本技巧。下面看他书中的一个后续手段，以了解他达到的技术水平。

text: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. O-O Nf6 5. Re1 O-O 6. c3 Qe7?
zh: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. O-O Nf6 5. Re1 O-O 6. c3 Qe7?

text: Greco had not yet realized the importance of keeping control of the centre and gives Black this weak move instead of the correct 6... d6.
zh: 格雷科还没有认识到保持中心控制的重要性，给黑方安排了这步软着，而不是正确的6... d6。

text: This is even stronger than 8. cxd4.¹
zh: 这甚至比8. cxd4更强。¹

text: ¹ As we shall see, this comment is incorrect. After 8. cxd4 White has a clear advantage, since Black has no compensation for White's central control. The move 8. e5 is a mistake which gives Black at least equality.
zh: ¹ 正如后面将看到的，这个评注不正确。8. cxd4之后，白方明显有利，因为黑方没有足够的补偿来抵消白方的中心控制。8. e5是错误，至少让黑方取得均势。

caption_zh: 黑方走完8... Ng4后的局面

text: 9. cxd4?
zh: 9. cxd4?

text: Weakly played. By 9. Bg5 (an intermediate move!) 9... Qe8 10. cxd4 White would have obtained a winning position. (Greco and other authors right up to the middle of the nineteenth century did not see the intermediate move 9. Bg5, so that 8. e5 came to be regarded in the textbooks as a mistake!¹)
zh: 这步走得弱。9. Bg5——一记过渡着！——9... Qe8 10. cxd4本来可以使白方获得胜势。（格雷科以及此后直到十九世纪中叶的其他作者，都没有看到9. Bg5这记过渡着，因此教科书反而把8. e5视为错误！¹）

text: ¹ Black should meet 9. Bg5 by 9... dxc3!. After 10. Bxe7 Bxf2+ 11. Kf1 cxb2 12. Nc3 (12. Na3 Bxe1 also favours Black) 12... Bxe1 (12... bxa1=Q 13. Qxa1 Bxe1 14. Nd5 is unclear) 13. Nd5 Nxe7 14. Nxe7+ Kh8 Black has a clear advantage in view of the threats of 15... bxa1=Q and 15... Ne3+. White's strongest move is 9. b4!, but an analysis of the resulting complications (which lead to a roughly equal position) would take us too far afield. Perhaps those old analysts knew a thing or two after all!
zh: ¹ 黑方应以9... dxc3!应对9. Bg5。10. Bxe7 Bxf2+ 11. Kf1 cxb2 12. Nc3（12. Na3 Bxe1也对黑方有利）12... Bxe1（12... bxa1=Q 13. Qxa1 Bxe1 14. Nd5不明朗）13. Nd5 Nxe7 14. Nxe7+ Kh8之后，由于威胁15... bxa1=Q和15... Ne3+，黑方明显有利。白方最强的是9. b4!，但分析由此产生的复杂变化——其结果大致均势——会离题太远。也许那些老分析家终究还是有些真本事！

text: 9... Nxd4! 10. Nxd4 Qh4
zh: 9... Nxd4! 10. Nxd4 Qh4

text: This is Greco's trick. White has two exposed spots, at h2 and f2.
zh: 这就是格雷科的技巧。白方有两个暴露的点：h2和f2。

text: Greco naturally also gives the continuation 11. Nf3 Qxf2+ followed by 12... Qg1+ and a smothered mate by the knight at f2.
zh: 格雷科自然也给出11. Nf3 Qxf2+，随后12... Qg1+，由马在f2完成闷杀的后续手段。

text: In carrying his attack further Greco does not notice all the finesses. 12... Nxe3+ followed by ...d6 would have been better here.²
zh: 继续进攻时，格雷科没有注意到所有细节。这里12... Nxe3+后接...d6本来更好。²

text: ² A baffling comment, as after 12... Nxe3+ 13. fxe3 d6 14. Nf3 White starts to consolidate his extra material. Greco's continuation appears best to me.
zh: ² 这个评注令人费解，因为12... Nxe3+ 13. fxe3 d6 14. Nf3之后，白方开始巩固自己的子力优势。我认为格雷科的后续手段反而最好。

text: 13. Ke2 Qxg2 14. Rg1 Nxe3 15. Kxe3?
zh: 13. Ke2 Qxg2 14. Rg1 Nxe3 15. Kxe3?

text: This way White loses two valuable pawns, and Greco concludes his analysis with 15... Bxd4+ 16. Kxd4 Qxf2+ 17. Kc3 Qe3+ 18. Bd3 Qxe5+, with advantage to Black.
zh: 这样白方丢掉两个重要的兵。格雷科以15... Bxd4+ 16. Kxd4 Qxf2+ 17. Kc3 Qe3+ 18. Bd3 Qxe5+结束分析，黑方有利。

text: Instead of 15. Kxe3?, the correct continuation is 15. Rxg2 Nxd1 16. Nf5, when Black must find the reply 16... d5! 17. Nxg7 Bh3!, if he is to retain the better prospects (though even here there is still some uncertainty after 18. Rg3 Bxf2 19. Rxh3 dxc4 20. Nd2, etc.). If he played 16... Nxb2 17. Nh6+ Kh8 18. Nxf7+, he would have to consent to a draw, since 18... Rxf7 is probably not a good idea.³
zh: 白方不应15. Kxe3?，正确的后续手段是15. Rxg2 Nxd1 16. Nf5。黑方若想保持较好的前景，必须找到16... d5! 17. Nxg7 Bh3!这个应对；不过即使如此，18. Rg3 Bxf2 19. Rxh3 dxc4 20. Nd2等之后，局面仍有些不确定。如果黑方16... Nxb2 17. Nh6+ Kh8 18. Nxf7+，就不得不接受和棋，因为18... Rxf7很可能并非好主意。³

text: ³ After 18... Rxf7 19. Bxf7 b6!, followed by ...Ba6+ and developing the rook, Black is virtually winning – three pawns for the exchange and a pair of active bishops is surely too much.
zh: ³ 18... Rxf7 19. Bxf7 b6!之后，再接...Ba6+并出动车，黑方实际上已经是胜势：以半子为代价换得三兵，再加上活跃的双象，补偿显然十分充足。

text: In step with the general advance in chess skill there can also be seen an advance in the technique of attacking the castled king, first with Philidor and then, particularly, with Morphy. The romantic reaction which followed led to the development of a number of particular types of sacrificial attacks, but without in general reaching Morphy's level. Steinitz was concerned with perfecting defensive technique, and his influence on the style of the period was slowly beginning to make the attack on the castled king fade from master chess. Lasker, too, the new World Champion, was even in his youth already turning away from forcing such attacks, preferring to aim at perfection in the endgame.
zh: 随着整体棋艺的提高，攻击王城的技术也在进步，先是菲利道尔，后来尤其是墨菲。随后浪漫派棋风再度兴起，推动了多种特定类型的弃子进攻的发展，但总体上没有达到墨菲的水平。斯坦尼茨致力于完善防守技术；他对时代棋风的影响，逐渐使王城进攻在大师对局中淡出。新任世界冠军拉斯克甚至在年轻时，就已不再执意强行发动这种进攻，而更倾向于追求残局中的精确。

text: At the end of the century, however, there were three great masters who defended the thesis of attacking chess and who in doing so clearly showed themselves to be supporters of the attack on the castled king. These were Chigorin, Tarrasch and Pillsbury, each of whom in his own way helped to enrich the technique of attack. Chigorin illustrated particularly the power of the positional sacrifice in his games; Tarrasch's thesis was that the rapid development of the pieces and a strong centre were the basic requisites for an attack on the castled king; while Pillsbury created a kind of synthesis of the attacking style and the positional and endgame play of Steinitz and Lasker. In other words, the American grandmaster showed how a rapid switch can be made from attack to a simplification which gives the better ending.
zh: 然而，十九世纪末有三位大棋手坚持进攻型国际象棋的主张，并明确支持攻击王城。他们是齐果林、塔拉什和皮尔斯伯里，各自以不同方式丰富了进攻技术。齐果林的对局尤其展示了局面棋弃子的威力；塔拉什认为，迅速出子和强大的中心，是攻击王城的基本条件；皮尔斯伯里则把进攻棋风，与斯坦尼茨、拉斯克的局面棋和残局技巧融为一体。换句话说，这位美国大棋手展示了怎样从进攻迅速转入简化，并获得更好的残局。

text: In this way all the basic elements of a perfected technique for attacking the castled king were set out, and after a short period of stagnation in the first two decades of the present century there followed the real blossoming of the dynamic style with the arrival of Capablanca and Alekhine. This development is still relevant to the theme of the attack on the castled king today, and more will be said about it at the end of the book.
zh: 至此，完善的王城进攻技术所需的各项基本要素都已具备。二十世纪头二十年经历短暂的停滞后，随着卡帕布兰卡和阿廖欣的到来，动态棋风真正繁荣起来。这种发展，在作者写作时仍与攻击王城的主题密切相关；本书末尾还将进一步讨论。

text: 4 Mating patterns
zh: 第四章　将杀模式

text: Spatial relationships in a mating attack can be observed by examining mating patterns, focal-points, and the roles played by the ranks, files, and diagonals. In this chapter we shall be concerned with mating patterns. This choice has a practical justification in that mating patterns can be more easily remembered than the ways leading up to mate. For this reason mating patterns, even though they occur only at the very end of a mating attack, are fundamental for practical purposes because of the excellent mnemonic assistance which they provide to the player.
zh: 通过考察将杀模式、杀王焦点，以及横线、纵线和斜线的作用，可以认识将杀进攻中的空间关系。本章讨论将杀模式。这样安排有实际理由：与通往将杀的具体走法相比，将杀模式更容易记住。因此，虽然将杀模式只在进攻的最后阶段出现，但它能为棋手提供极好的记忆线索，在实战中具有基础性的重要意义。

text: Our first concern is for the most common mating patterns; these hardly ever occur in the middle of the board, but they are very frequent in the castling area, i.e. near the king's position on the edge of the board.
zh: 我们先讨论最常见的将杀模式。它们很少出现在棋盘中央，却经常出现在王城区域，也就是靠近棋盘边缘的王的位置附近。

text: Typical mates without enemy pieces
zh: 没有其他敌方子力的典型将杀

text: There are a very large number of typical mates of this kind and most of them are elementary, so we shall consider only a few examples. (For the sake of greater clarity the diagrams are shown without the white king.)
zh: 这类典型将杀很多，大多属于基本知识，因此只看几个例子。为了让图示更清楚，图中省去了白王。

text: In the first position White, to move, has a choice between two typical mates:
zh: 第一个局面中，轮到白方行棋，他可以选择两种典型将杀：

text: In this position there are again two possible mates, depending on how Black replies.
zh: 这个局面同样有两种将杀，取决于黑方怎样应对。

text: If **1. Nf6+ Kh8**, then **2. Rh7#** (the so-called Arab mate, because it is recorded in Arabic manuscripts of the ninth century). If **1. Nf6+ Kf8**, then there follows **2. Rf7#**, a mating pattern which is worth remembering.
zh: 如果**1. Nf6+ Kh8**，则**2. Rh7#**。这就是所谓的阿拉伯杀，因为九世纪的阿拉伯手稿中已经记载了它。如果**1. Nf6+ Kf8**，则**2. Rf7#**；这个将杀模式也值得记住。

text: Another mate which should be known is this one with two knights, but if there are no other pieces on the board then it cannot be forced.
zh: 另一个应该熟悉的将杀，是这个双马将杀；但如果棋盘上没有其他子力，就无法强制实现。

text: Typical mates with enemy pieces
zh: 有其他敌方子力的典型将杀

text: The so-called back-row mate by the rook (or queen) is one of the most typical mating patterns.
zh: 由车或后完成的所谓底线杀，是最典型的将杀模式之一。

text: Of the fairly large number of typical mates with queen and pawn this one is given first.
zh: 后与兵配合的典型将杀有很多，这里先看这一种。

text: Black is to move; he cannot escape mate, since he is threatened by **1. Qh6** and **2. Qg7#**. If he plays 1... Kh7, then **2. Qh4+** and **3. Qh6**, etc. If Black had a pawn on h7 he would have the defence 1... Kh8 2. Qh6 Rg8.
zh: 轮到黑方行棋，但他无法逃脱将杀，因为白方威胁**1. Qh6**后接**2. Qg7#**。如果1... Kh7，则**2. Qh4+**后接**3. Qh6**等。如果黑方在h7还有一个兵，就可以用1... Kh8 2. Qh6 Rg8防守。

text: Damiano's Mate
zh: 达米亚诺杀

text: This is a position from the book (1512) by Damiano, a Portuguese apothecary, one of the first authors in the literature of European chess. White mates in five moves.
zh: 这个局面出自葡萄牙药剂师达米亚诺1512年的著作。他是欧洲国际象棋文献最早的一批作者之一。白方有五步杀。

text: 1. Rh8+ Kxh8 2. Rh1+ Kg8 3. Rh8+ Kxh8 4. Qh1+ Kg8 5. Qh7#
zh: 1. Rh8+ Kxh8 2. Rh1+ Kg8 3. Rh8+ Kxh8 4. Qh1+ Kg8 5. Qh7#

text: The rook sacrifices were naturally introduced to make the essential point clear: the queen must reach the h-file with gain of tempo.
zh: 安排这两次弃车，自然是为了突出关键：后必须带着先手进入h线。

text: The pattern of Damiano's mate can be seen more clearly in the following examples.
zh: 下面的例子可以更清楚地展示达米亚诺杀的模式。

text: 1. Qh5 Be7 2. Qh7+ Kf8 3. Qh8#
zh: 1. Qh5 Be7 2. Qh7+ Kf8 3. Qh8#

text: In this case a bishop has been placed on f8 and also a pawn on d6, with the result that the bishop can only move to e7, where it blocks the king's escape. The general theme of Damiano's mate, the pattern of which is characterized by a black pawn on g7 and a white pawn or bishop on g6, can be subjected to numerous variations.
zh: 这个例子中，f8放了一只象，d6还放了一个兵；因此黑象只能走到e7，在那里堵住黑王的退路。达米亚诺杀的一般主题，以g7黑兵和g6白兵或白象为特征，可以形成许多不同的变化。

text: The following diagram serves as a memory aid for mates with queen and rook:
zh: 下图可以帮助记忆后与车配合的将杀：

text: Black, to move, cannot avoid mate; if he plays 1... Kg7, then **2. Qh6+** and **3. Qh7#** or **3. Qh8#**, while if 1... f6, then **2. Qh7#**. If Black has another pawn on g7 he can save himself from immediate mate by 1... f6, while if he has one on g6 he can extricate himself by 1... Kg7.
zh: 轮到黑方行棋，但他无法避免将杀。如果1... Kg7，则**2. Qh6+**后接**3. Qh7#**或**3. Qh8#**；如果1... f6，则**2. Qh7#**。如果黑方在g7还有一个兵，可以用1... f6避免立即被杀；如果在g6有一个兵，则可以1... Kg7脱身。

text: Of the mates with queen and bishop this position is worth remembering.
zh: 在后与象配合的将杀中，这个局面值得记住。

text: Black cannot save himself from mate, but if he plays 1... g6, White does not reply 2. Bxg6+ (which is answered by 2... Kg7, and Black's king slips away) but 2. Qh6, in which case there is no remedy against mate.
zh: 黑方无法避免将杀，但如果他1... g6，白方不应2. Bxg6+，因为2... Kg7后黑王会逃走；应当2. Qh6，这样黑方就无法防住将杀。

text: Smothered Mate
zh: 闷杀

text: The smothered mate with queen and knight is a celebrated one: **1. Nf7+ Kg8 2. Nh6+ Kh8** (or 2... Kf8 3. Qf7#) **3. Qg8+! Rxg8** (or 3... Nxg8) **4. Nf7#**.
zh: 后与马配合的闷杀十分著名：**1. Nf7+ Kg8 2. Nh6+ Kh8**（或2... Kf8 3. Qf7#）**3. Qg8+! Rxg8**（或3... Nxg8）**4. Nf7#**。

text: This position falls into the category of typical mates, and it is useful to know the mating patterns which arise if Black tries to parry the threat of Qh7#, e.g. with **1... Rb8**.
zh: 这个局面也属于典型将杀。黑方如果设法应付Qh7#的威胁，例如走**1... Rb8**，熟悉随后可能出现的将杀模式很有用。

text: If there is a black pawn on e7 or if the square is otherwise occupied by Black, then there follows **2. Qh7+ Kf8 3. Qh8#**; if this is not so, mate can be achieved, for example, by **2. Qxf7+ Kh8 3. Ne6 Rg8 4. Qh5#**.
zh: 如果e7有一个黑兵，或被其他黑子占据，就有**2. Qh7+ Kf8 3. Qh8#**；如果不是这样，也能将杀，例如**2. Qxf7+ Kh8 3. Ne6 Rg8 4. Qh5#**。

text: Of the various attacking positions with queen and knight this scheme is also well worth remembering.
zh: 在后与马配合的各种进攻阵形中，这种阵形也很值得记住。

text: On **1. Nf6+**, Black replies 1... Kh8 and if 2. Nh5+, then 2... f6. If **1... Kg7**, White has a double check with **2. Ne8+** (in some cases, depending on the arrangement of the other pieces, 2. Nh5+ may be stronger) and after 2... Kh6 **3. Qf4+** g5 **4. Qf6+** Kh5 **5. Ng7+** White only needs a pawn on g2 or h2 to force mate.
zh: 对**1. Nf6+**，黑方应以1... Kh8；如果2. Nh5+，则2... f6。如果**1... Kg7**，白方可以**2. Ne8+**双将；在某些局面中，根据其他子力的配置，2. Nh5+可能更强。随后2... Kh6 **3. Qf4+** g5 **4. Qf6+** Kh5 **5. Ng7+**，白方只需在g2或h2有一个兵，就能强制将杀。

text: Greco's Mate
zh: 格雷科杀

text: This position is also worth knowing; Black is forced to play **1... h6**, after which he is mated by **2. Bxf7+ Kh8 3. Qg6! hxg5 4. Qh5#**.
zh: 这个局面也值得熟悉。黑方被迫走**1... h6**，随后**2. Bxf7+ Kh8 3. Qg6! hxg5 4. Qh5#**，白方将杀。

text: In the case of mating patterns with rook and bishop one should first of all get to know the above position.
zh: 研究车与象配合的将杀模式，首先应熟悉这个局面。

text: It is Black's move and he must try to parry Rg5#; this cannot be achieved by 1... h6, because of 2. Rxh6, which leaves him with no way out. So **1... Rc8 2. Rg5+ Kf8 3. Rg7!**, and now too mate is unavoidable, for Black is unable to free the square d7 in time to provide the king with an escape square. If he did not have, for instance, the pawn on c6, he could play 3... Bc6 4. Rxh7 Ke8 and then 5. Rh8+ could be met by 5... Kd7. One could replace Black's bishop and c6-pawn by a white pawn on c6 and a black one on c7; mate would still be unavoidable.¹
zh: 轮到黑方行棋，他必须设法防住Rg5#。1... h6做不到，因为2. Rxh6后仍无路可逃。因此**1... Rc8 2. Rg5+ Kf8 3. Rg7!**，但将杀依旧无法避免：黑方不能及时腾出d7，为王提供逃脱格。例如，如果没有c6兵，他就能3... Bc6 4. Rxh7 Ke8，再以5... Kd7应对5. Rh8+。也可以把黑象和c6黑兵换成c6白兵和c7黑兵；将杀仍然不可避免。¹

text: ¹ In the diagram position, Black can avoid mate by 1... Ra8 2. Rg5+ Kf8 3. Rg7 Ra4 4. Rxh7 Rg4. It is true to say that this defence is not often available in practical situations, but it is worth bearing in mind the idea of “defending from behind” because it is often overlooked.
zh: ¹ 在图中局面，黑方可以用1... Ra8 2. Rg5+ Kf8 3. Rg7 Ra4 4. Rxh7 Rg4避免将杀。实战中确实不常有这种防守，但值得记住“从后方防守”的思路，因为它经常被忽略。

text: Morphy's Mate
zh: 墨菲杀

text: The pattern of this mate with rook and bishop becomes clear in its final stage.
zh: 这种车象将杀的模式，在最后阶段便清楚地显现出来。

text: 1. Qxf6 gxf6 2. Rg1+ Kh8 3. Bxf6#
zh: 1. Qxf6 gxf6 2. Rg1+ Kh8 3. Bxf6#

text: Morphy's Concealed Mate
zh: 隐蔽的墨菲杀

text: A similar mating pattern occurs in this diagram: **1. Rxg7+ Kh8 2. Rxf7+** (not 2. Rg1+ because of 2... f6) **2... Kg8 3. Rg7+ Kh8 4. Rg1+ Rf6 5. Bxf6#**.
zh: 这个图中出现了类似的将杀模式：**1. Rxg7+ Kh8 2. Rxf7+**（不能2. Rg1+，因为2... f6）**2... Kg8 3. Rg7+ Kh8 4. Rg1+ Rf6 5. Bxf6#**。

text: **1. Rd8+ Kf7** (or 1... Kh7 2. Rh8#) **2. Rf8#** is a typical mating pattern well worth remembering.
zh: **1. Rd8+ Kf7**（或1... Kh7 2. Rh8#）**2. Rf8#**，是一个很值得记住的典型将杀模式。

text: Anastasia's Mate
zh: 阿纳斯塔西娅杀

text: 1. Ne7+ Kh8 2. Rxh7+ Kxh7 3. Rh5#
zh: 1. Ne7+ Kh8 2. Rxh7+ Kxh7 3. Rh5#

text: (The name comes from W. Heinse's novel Anastasia and chess (1803), in which this mate is recorded.)
zh: 这个名称来自W.海因泽1803年的小说《阿纳斯塔西娅与国际象棋》，书中记载了这种将杀。

text: Here the continuation ends with a typical mating pattern with a rook and pawn.
zh: 这里的后续手段，最终形成车与兵配合的典型将杀模式。

text: 1. Qg5 Kh8 2. Qh6 Rg8 3. Qxh7+ Kxh7 4. Rh1#
zh: 1. Qg5 Kh8 2. Qh6 Rg8 3. Qxh7+ Kxh7 4. Rh1#

text: “Blind swine”
zh: “盲猪”

text: If it is White's move, he mates with **1. Rg7+**, **2. Rh7+**, and **3. Rbg7#**. If Black is to move and plays **1... Rfd8**, White can neither force mate nor even win. That is to say, after 2. Rg7+ Kh8 3. Rh7+ Kg8 4. Rbg7+ Kf8 5. Rb7, Black simply plays 5... Kg8, “questioning” the white rook and countering the threat of mate.
zh: 如果轮到白方，他可以**1. Rg7+**、**2. Rh7+**、**3. Rbg7#**将杀。如果轮到黑方，且他走**1... Rfd8**，白方不仅无法强制将杀，甚至不能获胜。也就是说，2. Rg7+ Kh8 3. Rh7+ Kg8 4. Rbg7+ Kf8 5. Rb7之后，黑方只需5... Kg8，攻击白车，同时应付将杀威胁。

text: (It depends of course on the distribution of the other pieces whether White can in fact win. In this position he can easily mate if he has a pawn on h4, for he plays 6. h5 followed by 7. h6, 8. Rbg7+, and 9. Rh8# – a mate which is worth remembering. In this line Black's pawn on f6 is actually a help to White. If it were not there, Black could get a draw after 6. h5 by playing 6... Ra6!.)
zh: 当然，白方究竟能否取胜，还取决于其他子力的配置。在这个局面中，如果白方在h4有一个兵，就能轻松将杀：6. h5后接7. h6、8. Rbg7+和9. Rh8#，这是值得记住的将杀。这个变化中，黑方的f6兵实际上帮了白方的忙；如果没有它，6. h5之后黑方可以6... Ra6!取得和棋。

text: The pair of rooks which “grunt out check” on the seventh rank but cannot get a sight of mate were once nicknamed “blind swine” by Janowski.
zh: 两只车在第七横线上哼哼着不断将军，却看不到将杀的机会，雅诺夫斯基曾给它们起了个绰号：“盲猪”。

text: An acquaintance with typical mating patterns is extremely useful when making a quick survey of the board in an actual game. The addition of further material to the position can be especially useful, for then one can see which changes help to prevent mate and which enrich the mating patterns in new situations.
zh: 实战中快速审视棋盘时，熟悉典型将杀模式极其有用。在这些局面中加入其他子力，尤其有助于学习：这样可以看清，哪些变化有助于防止将杀，哪些变化又会在新局面中丰富将杀模式。

text: Less usual mating patterns
zh: 不太常见的将杀模式

text: Of the large number of less usual, and even exotic, mating patterns, I have chosen ones which bear some nickname or which can easily be given one.
zh: 不太常见、甚至十分奇异的将杀模式很多。我选出了一些已经有绰号，或很容易起绰号的模式。

text: Epaulette Mate
zh: 肩章杀

text: The epaulettes are, of course, the two black rooks on the king's shoulders. The next mate also gets its name from its outward appearance.
zh: 所谓肩章，当然就是王两肩上的那两只黑车。下一个将杀也根据外形得名。

text: “Swallow's tail”
zh: “燕尾杀”

text: Pawn Mate
zh: 兵杀

text: **1. g6 Bg8 2. g7#**. On 1. g6 Kg8 2. Qxh7+ Kf8 we get yet another mating pattern with 3. g7+ Kf7 4. g8=Q# (mate with two queens).
zh: **1. g6 Bg8 2. g7#**。如果1. g6 Kg8 2. Qxh7+ Kf8，则3. g7+ Kf7 4. g8=Q#，又得到另一种将杀模式——双后将杀。

text: Mate with Two Bishops
zh: 双象将杀

text: **1. Be6** d4 **2. Bh2** and **3. Be5#**. This could also be called Rubinstein's mate, after the famous game Rotlewi–Rubinstein, in which mate with two bishops was the basic motif of the attack.
zh: **1. Be6** d4 **2. Bh2**，随后**3. Be5#**。这种将杀也可以称为鲁宾斯坦杀：著名的罗特莱维对鲁宾斯坦一局中，双象将杀正是进攻的基本主题。

text: Boden's Mate
zh: 博登杀
caption_zh: 舒尔德（白）对博登（黑），黑方行棋

text: This position is from the game Schulder–Boden, London 1853¹, in which the following mate with two bishops was recorded for the first time; it is not uncommon after castling queenside. Black plays: **1... Qxc3+! 2. bxc3 Ba3#**.
zh: 这是1853年在伦敦的舒尔德对博登一局中的局面¹，也是这种双象将杀第一次见诸记录；长易位后，这种将杀并不少见。黑方走：**1... Qxc3+! 2. bxc3 Ba3#**。

text: ¹ In the original book this example was incorrectly given as Macdonell–Boden, 1869 and Black's rook on e8 was missing.
zh: ¹ 原著误把这个例子写成1869年的麦克唐纳对博登，而且漏掉了e8的黑车。

text: Pillsbury's Mate
zh: 皮尔斯伯里杀

text: **1. Rxg7+ Kh8 2. Rg8+! Kxg8 3. Rg1+** and mate. This is really a variation on Morphy's mate, contrived in such a way that it is the rook which mates and not the bishop, which is under attack from Black's rook.
zh: **1. Rxg7+ Kh8 2. Rg8+! Kxg8 3. Rg1+**，随后将杀。这实际上是墨菲杀的一种变化：由于白象受到黑车攻击，安排成由车而非象来完成将杀。

text: Legall's Mate
zh: 莱加尔杀

text: Legall was Philidor's teacher and this position arose in the game Legall–St Brie, Paris 1750. The moves leading up to the diagram were **1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 d6 3. Bc4 Bg4 4. Nc3 g6?** and Legall now played:
zh: 莱加尔是菲利道尔的老师。这个局面出现在1750年巴黎的莱加尔对圣布里一局中。图前走法是**1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 d6 3. Bc4 Bg4 4. Nc3 g6?**，随后莱加尔走了：
caption_zh: 黑方走完4... g6后的局面

text: **5. Nxe5! Bxd1?** (5... Be6 would have been better) **6. Bxf7+ Ke7 7. Nd5#**. (This is of course a case of an attack before castling, but the example is given here for purely practical reasons.)
zh: **5. Nxe5! Bxd1?**（5... Be6更好）**6. Bxf7+ Ke7 7. Nd5#**。当然，这是易位前的进攻，但出于实用考虑，仍在这里列出。

text: The next mate is similar to Greco's, but differs in that the attacker (here Black) opens the h-file not only for his opponent but also for himself. It arose in the game Anderssen–Max Lange, Breslau 1859 after **1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Nd4 4. Nxd4 exd4 5. Bc4 Nf6 6. e5 d5 7. Bb3 Bg4 8. f3 Ne4 9. O-O d3 10. fxg4?**¹ (D).
zh: 下一种将杀与格雷科杀相似，区别在于进攻方——这里是黑方——打开h线时，不仅让对手能使用这条线，自己也能使用它。这种将杀出现在1859年布雷斯劳的安德森对马克斯·朗格一局中，经过**1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Nd4 4. Nxd4 exd4 5. Bc4 Nf6 6. e5 d5 7. Bb3 Bg4 8. f3 Ne4 9. O-O d3 10. fxg4?**¹后，得到下图。
caption_zh: 白方走完10. fxg4后的局面

text: Max Lange's Mate
zh: 马克斯·朗格杀

text: ¹ 10. Qe1! would have favoured White.
zh: ¹ 10. Qe1!本来可以使白方有利。

text: Play proceeded as follows: **10... Bc5+ 11. Kh1 Ng3+ 12. hxg3 Qg5 13. Rf5 h5!** and now if 14. Rxg5, then 14... hxg4+ and mate; in the game White played **14. gxh5** but resigned after **14... Qxf5 15. g4 Qf2 0-1**.
zh: 对局接着这样进行：**10... Bc5+ 11. Kh1 Ng3+ 12. hxg3 Qg5 13. Rf5 h5!**。现在如果14. Rxg5，则14... hxg4+后将杀。实战中白方走**14. gxh5**，但在**14... Qxf5 15. g4 Qf2 0-1**之后认输。

text: The next position arose in the game Réti–Tartakower, Vienna 1910 after the moves **1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nf6 5. Qd3 e5 6. dxe5 Qa5+ 7. Bd2 Qxe5 8. O-O-O Nxe4** (D).
zh: 下一局面来自1910年在维也纳的列蒂对塔塔科维尔一局。经过**1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nf6 5. Qd3 e5 6. dxe5 Qa5+ 7. Bd2 Qxe5 8. O-O-O Nxe4**后，得到下图。
caption_zh: 黑方走完8... Nxe4后的局面

text: Réti's Mate
zh: 列蒂杀

text: The game concluded: **9. Qd8+! Kxd8 10. Bg5+ Kc7** (or 10... Ke8 11. Rd8#) **11. Bd8#**.
Blackburne's Mate
zh: 布莱克本杀

text: For this mate the attacker needs three minor pieces (two bishops and a knight) and usually a queen as well, which is sacrificed.
zh: 实现这种将杀，进攻方需要三个轻子——双象和一马——通常还需要一个后，用来弃掉。

text: **1. Qh1 h5 2. Qxh5! gxh5 3. Bh7#**. This mating pattern is named after Blackburne, who was the first to mate in this way.
zh: **1. Qh1 h5 2. Qxh5! gxh5 3. Bh7#**。这种将杀模式以首先采用它完成将杀的布莱克本命名。

text: 5 Focal-points
zh: 第五章　杀王焦点

text: The series of examples examined in the chapter on mating patterns has given us a good idea of the difficulties a defender encounters when his forces (especially the pawns in front of his castled king) are poorly placed and when the attacker's one aim is to fill the various 'holes and cracks' in the weakened enemy defences with his own pieces and thus obtain an even tighter grip. It follows from this that the squares in the immediate vicinity of the king, where the drama of the mating attack usually reaches its climax, play a special role. If the attacker threatens mate or actually mates on these squares, they are mating focal-points, but if he only harries the king from them or uses them as points from which to break into the castled position, they are called strategic or auxiliary focal-points. It may be that there is more than one mating focal-point, and in that case we speak of compound focal-points. If there are many focal-points (both mating and strategic) on squares of the same colour, we speak of a network of weak squares.
zh: 上一章关于将杀模式的一系列例子，已经让我们充分认识到：当防守方的子力，尤其是王城前的兵，位置不佳，而进攻方一心用自己的棋子填入对方防线中的各种“孔洞与裂缝”，不断加强控制时，防守方会遇到怎样的困难。因此，紧邻王的那些格子具有特殊作用；杀王的战斗通常就在这里达到高潮。如果进攻方威胁在这些格子上将杀，或者实际在这里将杀，它们就是将杀焦点；如果进攻方只是从这里骚扰王，或以此为突破王城的据点，它们就称为战略焦点或辅助焦点。有时将杀焦点不止一个，我们便称之为复合焦点。如果同一颜色的格子上存在许多焦点，无论是将杀焦点还是战略焦点，我们便称之为弱格网络。

text: Generally speaking, every focal-point is a weak square in the defender's territory and a potentially strong one for the attacker. In addition to the focal-points there are also other squares in the castling area which have a specific function, e.g. blocked squares, particularly those occupied by the defender's pawns, and also any weak squares on which the attacker can safely post his pieces.
zh: 一般而言，每一个焦点都是防守方阵地中的弱格，对进攻方则可能成为强格。王城区域中除焦点外，还有一些格子具有特定作用，例如被堵住的格子，尤其是防守方的兵占据的格子；还有一些弱格，进攻方可以安全地把棋子安置在那里。

text: As an illustration of this, take the following position (which we have already seen earlier). Here we have the following scheme:
zh: 以下局面前面已经出现过，我们用它来说明上述概念。各格的作用如下：

将杀格：g8、f8；
将杀焦点：h7、h8；
辅助焦点：h7（黑方用...Be7应对将杀威胁之后）；
进攻方的强格：f7、g6、h7；
被堵住的格子：g7，以及稍后的e7。

text: The focal-point at g7
zh: g7焦点

text: As usual, when referring to specific squares we assume that White is the attacker. It is understood that if Black is the attacker, then the discussion applies equally to the square g2.
zh: 和往常一样，讨论具体格子时，我们假定白方是进攻方。如果黑方发动进攻，下文的讨论同样适用于g2格。

text: The most important focal-points where castling kingside is concerned are g7 and h7, since these squares are more accessible to the attacker than the others in the castling area. Of the two, h7 is the more frequent object of attack (since it comes under fire from the bishop operating from d3, a natural point of development, while the king's knight can reach g5, for example, more easily than f5 or h5). However, attacks against g7 are the more dangerous. The reasons for this are very simple: the queen can mate more easily from g7 than h7 (owing to the king's ability to flee to f8), but as well as this, a weakness on g7 usually brings with it two more on f6 and h6, while one on h7 generally only entails a single extra one at g6. Every player of any experience is well acquainted with this fact and knows that ...g6 involves a greater weakening than ...h6. On the other hand, h7 is usually harder to defend than g7, which the king's bishop can support in two ways (from f8 or f6).
