zh: 从本局及其评注可以看出，开放直线可以具有不同程度的意义。首先是白方开放的g线：缺少其他方面的支持，它就无效；但评注也指出，只要白兵推进到e5，这条线就会有价值。接着是黑方开放b线、c线的调动：先在评注中提出，随后在实战关键阶段真正实施。一旦通过弃兵打开c线，双车在线上的强大威力最终便为进攻方带来胜利。

text: The attack along the h-file
zh: 沿h线的进攻

text: Using a rook to control an open h-file is one of the classic methods of attack after castling kingside, and so a number of examples will be devoted to it.
zh: 短易位后，用车控制开放h线是一种经典进攻方法，因此我们将用若干实例专门讨论。

text: Firstly, we have an instance of a rook exercising control from h3, in front of the h2-pawn.
zh: 首先看一个车在h2兵前方、从h3格施加控制的例子。
caption_zh: 勒德尔—塞米什，斯维讷明德，1931年；白先。

text: This diagram comes from Rödl-Sämisch, Swinemünde 1931. White plays:
zh: 此图出自勒德尔—塞米什，斯维讷明德，1931年。白方走：

text: A sacrifice of the bishop which might be termed 'semi-classic', this draws the king out to h7 so that the rook can get to h3 with gain of tempo; at the same time defence by ...h6 is excluded. It could also be put like this: the temporal factor here requires that the operation of 'clearing' h7 be carried out before posting the rook on the h-file.
zh: 这种弃象可以称为“半古典式”：它把王引到h7，让车能带先手来到h3；同时排除了...h6的防守。也可以这样说：这里的时间因素要求先“清理”h7，再把车部署到h线上。

text: White removes the bishop from f6 to allow his queen to move immediately to h4.
zh: 白方消灭f6象，使后能立即到h4。

text: Since the f-pawn is blocked, this is the only possible way of averting mate.
zh: 由于f兵被堵住，这是避免将杀的唯一办法。

text: **6. Qxh5 f6 7. g5 Qxd5**
zh: **6. Qxh5 f6 7. g5 Qxd5**

text: To stop the fatal thrust g6. If 7... Rfe8, the quickest results are attained by 8. gxf6.
zh: 阻止致命的g6突破。若7... Rfe8，8. gxf6最快见效。

text: If 9... Ke7 10. Qxg7+ Rf7 11. Rxf7+ Qxf7, then 12. Re3+ is decisive.
zh: 若9... Ke7 10. Qxg7+ Rf7 11. Rxf7+ Qxf7，则12. Re3+决定胜负。

text: Next we have an example of a complex sacrificial combination based on an explosive opening of the h-file.
zh: 接下来是一个复杂的弃子组合，以猛然打开h线为基础。
caption_zh: P.施密特—K.里希特；白先。

text: White (P. Schmidt) mated Black (K. Richter) in spectacular style:
zh: 白方P.施密特以华丽的方式将杀黑方K.里希特：

text: Drawing the king into the fire of the battery of rook and h-pawn. If 1. hxg6, Black would relieve his position by exchanging queens.
zh: 把王引到车与h兵的叠子火力之下。若1. hxg6，黑方可以兑后缓解局面。

text: Discovered check, or 'a salvo from the battery of rook and pawn', or, lastly, the pawn on h5 as a kind of outpost — three names for the same thing.
zh: 闪将，或“车兵叠子的一次齐射”，也可以把h5兵视作一种前哨——三种说法，指的是同一回事。

text: With this sacrifice White lures the king into the fire of a new battery — bishop and pawn!
zh: 白方借此弃车，把王诱入一组新的叠子火力之中——象与兵！

text: **3... Kxh5 4. f4+ Nxe2 5. Nf6+ Kh6 6. Rh1+ Kg7 7. Ne8+ Rxe8 8. Rh7+ Kf6 9. Rxf7#**
zh: **3... Kxh5 4. f4+ Nxe2 5. Nf6+ Kh6 6. Rh1+ Kg7 7. Ne8+ Rxe8 8. Rh7+ Kf6 9. Rxf7#**

text: This is also an instructive example with reference to weaving the mating net: White is the master of the h-file, but he still needs to deprive the black king of squares on the g-file. The most difficult to deal with is g5, but White solves that problem with his third and fourth moves.
zh: 这也是一个编织杀网的好例子：白方控制着h线，但还须剥夺黑王在g线上的逃生格。其中最难处理的是g5；白方通过第三、第四步解决了这一问题。
caption_zh: 托特—西盖蒂，布达佩斯，1946年；白先。

text: This example, from the game Toth-Szigeti, Budapest 1946, shows us an execution of Anastasia's mate on the h-file.
zh: 此例出自托特—西盖蒂，布达佩斯，1946年，展示了在h线上实现阿纳斯塔西娅将杀。

text: **1. Bxh7+ Kxh7 2. Rh3+ Kg8 3. Qh5 Qh6**
zh: **1. Bxh7+ Kxh7 2. Rh3+ Kg8 3. Qh5 Qh6**

text: To all appearances Black has parried the attack on the h-file, but now comes the unexpected point.
zh: 表面上黑方已经挡住h线进攻，但此时出现了出人意料的关键着。

text: **4. Nf5! Qxh5 5. Ne7+ Kh7 6. Rxh5#**
zh: **4. Nf5! Qxh5 5. Ne7+ Kh7 6. Rxh5#**

text: One of the most important types of attack along the h-file is that which involves the doubling of the heavy pieces on the file, threatening mate at h8. If the enemy king's flight squares on the second rank are occupied by its own pawns, then the attacker must concentrate his effort on doubling his heavy pieces as rapidly as possible and mate his opponent at the focal-point h8. However, if the king has a square to escape to or there is a threat to get one by moving the g-pawn or f-pawn, attention must be turned to this possible means of defence. The most economical formation against this, as far as the use of attacking material is concerned, is one with an assault pawn at g6 and a defending one at g7. The continuations from the following diagram are devoted to this typical formation (with colours reversed).
zh: 沿h线进攻最重要的类型之一，是将重子叠在线上，威胁在h8将杀。如果敌王在第二横线上的逃生格被自己的兵占据，进攻方就应集中力量，尽快叠重子，在h8焦点将杀对方。但如果王已有逃生格，或可能通过移动g兵、f兵获得逃生格，就必须注意这种潜在防守。就投入的攻击子力而言，最经济的应对配置是：进攻兵在g6，防守兵在g7。下图的变化专门说明这一典型配置，只是双方颜色相反。

text: In this example Black is the attacker. He has already sacrificed his queen in order to reach this position, his intention being to mate White's king with a rook on h1. Doubling rooks is not a problem for Black in this position, but he is involved in a struggle for f2, which is important as a flight square for the white king. There are two methods of handling this: the king can be allowed to get out and a mating net then woven round it, or the formation with the pawn at g3 and doubled rooks can be set up. Both courses lead to success in this position, and both do so in two ways, so that in all Black has four lines which lead to victory. Here they are:
zh: 本例中黑方是进攻者。为了达到这个局面，他已经弃后，打算用车在h1将杀白王。在此局面中叠车并不困难，但黑方必须争夺f2，因为它是白王的重要逃生格。处理办法有两种：允许王逃出来，再在周围编织杀网；或建立g3兵与双车叠线的配置。两种办法在这里都能奏效，每种又各有两条途径，所以黑方共有四个获胜变化，如下：

text:
A) 1... Rah8 2. f4
The only reply; if 2. g3, White is mated by the rooks; if 2. f3, then 2... g3.
2...Rh1+
This is the 'mating net' method; 2... g3 allows White to reply 3. Qxh5.
3. Kf2 Nxe4+ 4. Ke1 Rxf1+ 5. Kxf1 Rh1+ 6. Bg1 Rxg1+ 7. Kxg1 Nf3+ 8. Kf1 Ng3#.
zh:
A）1... Rah8 2. f4
唯一应手；若2. g3，双车将杀白王；若2. f3，则2... g3。
2...Rh1+
这是“杀网”法；2... g3会让白方有3. Qxh5。
3. Kf2 Nxe4+ 4. Ke1 Rxf1+ 5. Kxf1 Rh1+ 6. Bg1 Rxg1+ 7. Kxg1 Nf3+ 8. Kf1 Ng3#。

text: In this variation the doubled rooks have disappeared, but the 'doubled knights' are not to be overlooked.
zh: 这个变化中，叠车已经消失，但不可忽视“双马联手”的作用。

text:
B) 1... Ne2+ 2. Qxe2 Rah8 3. f4 g3 4. Qxh5 Bxe3+ 5. Rf2
Some players are more hurt by forced moves of this kind than by mate itself.
5...Nxh5 6. Kf1 gxf2 7. Ke2 f1=Q+ 8. Kxf1 Ng3+ 9. Ke1 Rh1#.
zh:
B）1... Ne2+ 2. Qxe2 Rah8 3. f4 g3 4. Qxh5 Bxe3+ 5. Rf2
对有些棋手而言，被迫走这种着法，比遭到将杀本身更难受。
5...Nxh5 6. Kf1 gxf2 7. Ke2 f1=Q+ 8. Kxf1 Ng3+ 9. Ke1 Rh1#。

text: Let us now look at the two continuations which use the method based on the ...g3 formation.
zh: 再看以...g3配置为基础的两种续着。

text:
C) 1... Ne2+ 2. Qxe2 Rah8 3. f4 Bxe3+ 4. Qxe3 Nxe4!
This controls f2 and draws the queen away from the defence of g3.
5. Qxe4 g3
zh:
C）1... Ne2+ 2. Qxe2 Rah8 3. f4 Bxe3+ 4. Qxe3 Nxe4!
控制f2，并把后引离g3的防守。
5. Qxe4 g3

text: By means of a series of diversions Black has now established the necessary conditions for the success of the pure formation of doubled rooks plus pawn on g3 against pawn on g2. To avoid mate White would now have to give up nearly all his material: 6. Qe7+ Kxe7 7. Re1+ Kd7 8. Kf1 Rh1+ 9. Ke2 Re8+, after which 10... Rexe1 leads to a further harvest on the back rank.
zh: 经过一系列引离，黑方建立了双车加g3兵对付g2兵这一纯粹配置的获胜条件。白方若想避免将杀，就几乎须交出全部子力：6. Qe7+ Kxe7 7. Re1+ Kd7 8. Kf1 Rh1+ 9. Ke2 Re8+，随后10... Rexe1，继续在底线上收割。
D）1... Rh7（见下图）

text: Finally, there is also the possibility of the rook retiring from h5 so that the queen cannot take it after ...g3.
zh: 最后还可以把h5车退开，使它在...g3之后不会被后吃掉。

text:
2. f4
If 2. g3, we get the following entertaining variation: 2... Nf3+ 3. Qxf3 gxf3 4. Bg5 Nxe4 5. Bh4 Nxg3! 6. Bxg3 Rah8 mating. An example of 'clearing up' on the h-file.¹
2...g3 3. Rf3
Or 3. Qe1 Ne2+ 4. Qxe2 Rah8, etc.
3...Rah8 4. Rxg3 Rh1+ 5. Kf2 Nxe4#
zh:
2. f4
若2. g3，会出现如下有趣变化：2... Nf3+ 3. Qxf3 gxf3 4. Bg5 Nxe4 5. Bh4 Nxg3! 6. Bxg3 Rah8，将杀。这是在h线上“清理线路”的一例。¹
2...g3 3. Rf3
或3. Qe1 Ne2+ 4. Qxe2 Rah8，等等。
3...Rah8 4. Rxg3 Rh1+ 5. Kf2 Nxe4#。

text: In the above diagram doubling rooks was an easy task, but the crux lay in controlling the squares which the king might use for its escape. However, there are cases where the problem lies in actually doubling the rooks on the intended file. As a rule a necessary condition for this is that the attacker's back rank should be clear of other pieces so that the rooks can be moved at will. When the rooks on a given rank cover each other, they are said to be 'united'. Naturally, being 'united' can also apply to a queen and rook. The continuation from the following diagram is instructive in this context.
zh: 上图中叠车很容易，关键在于控制王可能逃往的格子。但也有一些局面，难点恰恰就是把双车叠到预定直线上。通常，必要条件是进攻方的底线没有其他棋子挡路，使车可以自由调动。当双车在同一横线上互相保护时，我们称之为“连通”。当然，后车也可以“连通”。下一图的续着在这方面很有启发性。

text: ¹ There is no argument about Vuković's first three lines, but in variation 'D' White can play 2. Bxd4 Rah8 (after 2... Bxd4 3. Re1 Rah8 4. Kf1 the king slips out) 3. Qxg4+! Kc7 4. Qh3 Rxh3 5. gxh3 Bxd4 6. Nc3, escaping into an ending in which he is only slightly worse.
zh: ¹ 纳恩注：武科维奇的前三个变化没有问题，但在D变化中，白方可以2. Bxd4 Rah8（若2... Bxd4 3. Re1 Rah8 4. Kf1，王就逃出来了）3. Qxg4+! Kc7 4. Qh3 Rxh3 5. gxh3 Bxd4 6. Nc3，脱身转入仅略差的残局。
caption_zh: 克罗吉乌斯—涅梅莱，洛维萨，1934年；白先。

text: The diagram represents a critical stage in the game Krogius-Niemelä, Lovisa 1934.
zh: 此图是克罗吉乌斯—涅梅莱，洛维萨，1934年一局的关键时刻。

text: White is in a precarious position, even though his pawn formation is sound and he has an open h-file. If he withdraws his bishop to c2, Black has the strong reply 1... d4, while 1... Bxg5 is also worth considering. If 1. Qg4 cxd3 2. Qh4 (2. Qh3 h5 3. gxh6 {3. g4 Bc8!} 3... d4! is in Black's favour) 2... h5 3. g4, Black plays 3... Kg7! 4. gxh5 Rh8 5. h6+ Kh7, and White's attack is beaten back. Black's defensive plan against the idea of using the white g-pawn to break open the h-file is worth remembering, since there are often opportunities for such play in practice.
zh: 白方虽有稳健的兵形和开放h线，局面却岌岌可危。若将象退到c2，黑方有强手1... d4，1... Bxg5也值得考虑。若1. Qg4 cxd3 2. Qh4（2. Qh3 h5 3. gxh6〔3. g4 Bc8!〕3... d4!对黑有利）2... h5 3. g4，黑方就3... Kg7! 4. gxh5 Rh8 5. h6+ Kh7，击退白方攻势。白方打算利用g兵冲开h线，而黑方的这种防守计划值得牢记，因为实战中常有机会采用。

text: Taking into account all the difficulties described, White decided to strike immediately with his rook at h7; Black failed to discover the correct reply.
zh: 考虑到上述困难，白方决定立即用车在h7出击；黑方没有找到正确应手。

text: It is true that Black could not take the rook because of 2. Qh5+ Kg8 3. Qh6 cxd3 4. Kf2, after which he has no satisfactory defence against Rh1. However, it was also not a good idea to take the bishop; the precious tempo should have been expended on breaking up White's pawn formation, which is in fact the decisive factor in White's success on the h-file. Thus 1... Bxg5! would have been correct. In that case two of White's pieces are threatened and if 2. Kf2, then Black can play 2... Kxh7; 2. Rh3 can be met by 2... Bc8 and then ...Bh4+, while if 2. fxg5, then either 2... Qxg5 or 2... Kxh7. By sacrificing on g5 Black eliminates White's control of h6, and in some variations he captures with his queen on e5, thereby covering the square h8 in the manner of a fianchettoed bishop.
zh: 黑方确实不能吃车，因为2. Qh5+ Kg8 3. Qh6 cxd3 4. Kf2之后，对Rh1没有满意的防守。但吃象同样不好；宝贵的一拍应当用于破坏白方兵形，因为兵形实际上是白方h线进攻得手的决定性因素。因此正确的是1... Bxg5!。这时白方两子受攻；若2. Kf2，黑方可以2... Kxh7；2. Rh3可应2... Bc8，再...Bh4+；若2. fxg5，则2... Qxg5或2... Kxh7均可。通过在g5弃象，黑方消除了白方对h6的控制；在某些变化中，黑后还可吃到e5，像侧翼象一样守住h8。

caption_zh: 克罗吉乌斯—涅梅莱；2. Kf2后。

text: Uniting the rooks on the back rank above all else! In fact, the chief value of this kind of move derives from the characteristic dual control which it provides. That is, by playing 2. Kf2! White opens up the square h1 both for the queen and the a1-rook, whereas after, for example, 2. Qg4? only the queen would be brought into action and the a1-rook would be left behind. The inadequacy of 2. Qg4? is shown by the following continuation: 2... Kxh7 3. Qh4+ Kg8 4. Kf2 f6! 5. e6 (if 5. exf6, Black plays 5... Bxf6, enabling his king to wriggle out via f7) 5... fxg5 6. Qh6 Bf6 and Black has defended himself; e.g. if 7. Qxg6+ Bg7 8. Rh1, then 8... Rf6, while if 7. Rh1, then 7... Qe7 8. Qxg6+ Qg7, etc.
zh: 首先要在底线上连通双车！其实，这类着法的主要价值，在于它特有的双重作用：2. Kf2!同时为后和a1车让出h1；而若2. Qg4?，就只有后投入战斗，a1车仍被抛在后面。以下变化说明2. Qg4?的不足：2... Kxh7 3. Qh4+ Kg8 4. Kf2 f6! 5. e6（若5. exf6，黑方5... Bxf6，让王有机会经f7钻出去）5... fxg5 6. Qh6 Bf6，黑方守住了。例如7. Qxg6+ Bg7 8. Rh1，则8... Rf6；若7. Rh1，则7... Qe7 8. Qxg6+ Qg7，等等。

text: If 2... Kxh7, then 3. Qh1+ Kg8 4. Qh6 leaves Black without a defence against 5. Rh1 (for 4... f6 is no good on account of 5. Qxg6+). The white queen must be brought to h6, and it makes no difference whether it goes via h1 or h4 (as both Qg4-h4-h6 and Kf2, Qh1-h6 take three tempi), but in the case of the a1-rook, the continuation 2. Kf2! is better than 2. Qg4?, which does nothing to bring it into action.
zh: 若2... Kxh7，则3. Qh1+ Kg8 4. Qh6，黑方无法防住5. Rh1（4... f6也因5. Qxg6+而不行）。白后必须到h6，经h1还是h4并无区别，因为Qg4-h4-h6与Kf2、Qh1-h6都用三拍；但就a1车而言，2. Kf2!优于2. Qg4?，后者丝毫没有帮助它投入战斗。

text: Finally, it should be mentioned that a delayed sacrifice at g5 is also of no avail, e.g. 2... Bxg5 3. Qh1 Bf6 (or 3... f5 4. e6! Bf6 5. Qh6 Qe8 6. Rh1 and 7. Rh8+) 4. Qh6! followed by 5. Rh1 and 6. Rh8+.
zh: 最后还应指出，现在才在g5弃象也无济于事。例如2... Bxg5 3. Qh1 Bf6（或3... f5 4. e6! Bf6 5. Qh6 Qe8 6. Rh1再7. Rh8+）4. Qh6!，接5. Rh1和6. Rh8+。

text: For if 3... Qe8 or 3... fxe5, then 4. Qh6 is decisive.
zh: 因为无论3... Qe8还是3... fxe5，4. Qh6都决定胜负。

text: The formation with rook on h1 and pawn on h4
zh: 车在h1、兵在h4的配置

text: Of the various formations on the h-file the most important in practice is undoubtedly that with a rook on h1 and pawn on h4. It is a good representative example of battery attacks with rook and pawn which are created when the pawn captures an opposing piece and thereby opens up the file for the rook. This situation is often engineered by placing another attacking piece on the square covered by the pawn, creating threats which induce or oblige the opponent to take it. There are two other methods of exploiting the formation of rook and pawn — one is to simply advance the pawn, the other involves switching the rook on to another file (e.g. with rook on h1 and pawns at h4 and g2, moving the rook to h3 and then to g3).
zh: h线的各种配置中，实战最重要的无疑是车在h1、兵在h4。它是车兵叠子攻击的典型：兵吃掉敌子，从而为车开放直线。这种局面往往这样促成：把另一枚进攻棋子放到兵保护的格子上，制造威胁，诱使或迫使对方吃它。车兵配置还有另外两种利用方式：一是直接推进这个兵，二是把车转到另一条直线；例如车在h1、兵在h4和g2时，车先到h3，再转g3。

text: Here are a few examples of these ideas.
zh: 下面用几个实例说明这些构思。

text: In this position we see a formation in which preparations have already been made for the opening of the h-file after the capture of the knight at g5. It is true that White, to move, currently has no very sharp threats, but he reckons correctly that he can quickly strengthen his position; in the meantime, he puts his trust in the efficacy of hxg5 if Black takes the knight.
zh: 此局面已经做好准备：黑方吃g5马后，白方即可打开h线。轮白方走，他目前固然没有十分尖锐的威胁，但他正确地判断自己能迅速加强局面；在此期间，若黑方吃马，他相信hxg5会有威力。

text: We shall examine this weak move in order to get to know the various typical combinations which occur when the h-file is opened in such circumstances. Correct was 1... a5!, stopping b4. White would then probably play 2. g4 to exclude the possibility of ...Nf6-h5-g3. Thus, the game could go on for a few more moves with the knight on g5 en prise, until the critical moment came to decide on the exact significance of the knight's position: either White's attack would break through, or Black would take the knight without any ill-effects to himself, or thirdly White might simply withdraw the knight from g5.
zh: 我们分析这一弱着，是为了认识在这种情况下开放h线后产生的各种典型组合。正确的是1... a5!，阻止b4。白方随后可能2. g4，排除...Nf6-h5-g3的可能。因此，g5马虽受攻，对局仍可以再进行几步，直到关键时刻，才判定这匹马的位置究竟意味着什么：或者白方突破得手，或者黑方吃马而不受惩罚，或者白方干脆把马从g5撤走。

text: **2. hxg5 Nxd5 3. Bxd5 Be6**
zh: **2. hxg5 Nxd5 3. Bxd5 Be6**

text: If 3... g6, then 4. Ke2! (a characteristically quiet move by the king to unite the heavy pieces on the back rank) 4... Kg7 5. Rh7+! Kxh7 6. Qh1+ Kg8 7. Qh6 Ne7 8. Bd2 Nxd5 9. Rh1 followed by mate.
zh: 若3... g6，则4. Ke2!（典型的安静王步，在底线上连通重子）4... Kg7 5. Rh7+! Kxh7 6. Qh1+ Kg8 7. Qh6 Ne7 8. Bd2 Nxd5 9. Rh1，接着将杀。

text: This seems to provide the most resistance. If 4... g6, then 5. f5 Bxd5 6. f6 Be6 7. Qf3 and White can easily organize a mating attack.
zh: 这似乎抵抗最强。若4... g6，则5. f5 Bxd5 6. f6 Be6 7. Qf3，白方很容易组织将杀进攻。

text: **5. Qh5 Kf8 6. Bxe6 Rxe6**
zh: **5. Qh5 Kf8 6. Bxe6 Rxe6**

text: Or 6... fxe6 7. g6 Ne7 8. f5 exf5 9. Bg5, etc.¹
zh: 或6... fxe6 7. g6 Ne7 8. f5 exf5 9. Bg5，等等。¹

text: **7. f5 Re8 8. g6 Ke7 9. Bg5+** and Black either loses his queen or is mated, e.g. 9... f6 10. Bxf6+ gxf6 11. Qh7+ Kf8 12. Qf7#.
zh: **7. f5 Re8 8. g6 Ke7 9. Bg5+**，黑方不是丢后就是被杀。例如9... f6 10. Bxf6+ gxf6 11. Qh7+ Kf8 12. Qf7#。
caption_zh: 博登—伯德，伦敦，1869年；白先。

text: This position arose in the game Boden-Bird, London 1869. White played a move which made clear his ardent wish that Black should take the bishop on g5.
zh: 此局面出自博登—伯德，伦敦，1869年。白方下一着清楚表明，他热切希望黑方吃掉g5象。

text: Black takes the bishop, even though there is no danger at the moment. He could have played, for example, 1... a6 2. Ncd5 b5 3. h5, after which there is a real threat of Ng6+. This can be parried by 3... h6, and if 4. Ng6+, then 4... Kh7.²
zh: 当前并无危险，黑方却吃了象。他本可走例如1... a6 2. Ncd5 b5 3. h5，此后才真正有Ng6+的威胁。可用3... h6应对；若4. Ng6+，则4... Kh7。²

text: A typical method of 'clearing' the file before the battery opens fire with hxg5.
zh: 在以hxg5打开叠子火力之前，先“清理”直线的一种典型方法。

text: **2... hxg6 3. hxg5+ Nh6 4. gxh6 Bg5+ 5. Kb1 Bxh6**
zh: **2... hxg6 3. hxg5+ Nh6 4. gxh6 Bg5+ 5. Kb1 Bxh6**

text: If 5... gxh6, then 6. Ne4 Kg7 (or 6... Kg8 7. Rxh6 Bxh6 8. Qxg6+ Bg7 9. Qf7+ mating) 7. Rxh6! Kxh6 8. Nxg5! Qxg5 (or 8... Kg7 9. Ne4) 9. Rh1+ Qh5 10. Qxg6#.
zh: 若5... gxh6，则6. Ne4 Kg7（或6... Kg8 7. Rxh6 Bxh6 8. Qxg6+ Bg7 9. Qf7+，将杀）7. Rxh6! Kxh6 8. Nxg5! Qxg5（或8... Kg7 9. Ne4）9. Rh1+ Qh5 10. Qxg6#。

text: **6. Qxg6 Re7 7. f6 Qe8 8. f7 Qf8 9. Rxh6+ gxh6 10. Rh1 Rxe6 11. Qxe6 Kh7 12. Ne4 Rc7 13. Ng5+** and mates.
zh: **6. Qxg6 Re7 7. f6 Qe8 8. f7 Qf8 9. Rxh6+ gxh6 10. Rh1 Rxe6 11. Qxe6 Kh7 12. Ne4 Rc7 13. Ng5+**，接着将杀。

text: ¹ In this line, Black can still resist with 7... Ke7, so White should prefer 7. Qh8+ Kf7 8. g6+ Kxg6 9. Qh5+ Kf6 10. fxe5+, winning immediately.
zh: ¹ 纳恩注：此变化中，黑方仍可7... Ke7抵抗，所以白方应选7. Qh8+ Kf7 8. g6+ Kxg6 9. Qh5+ Kf6 10. fxe5+，立即获胜。

text: ² Although White then wins easily by 5. Ngxe7 Nxe7 6. Bxf6 gxf6 7. Nxf6+ Kh8 8. Qf4 Ng8 9. Nxg8 Kxg8 10. f6.
zh: ² 纳恩注：不过白方此时可5. Ngxe7 Nxe7 6. Bxf6 gxf6 7. Nxf6+ Kh8 8. Qf4 Ng8 9. Nxg8 Kxg8 10. f6，轻松获胜。

text: The diverse character of the formation with rook on h1 and pawn on h4 is well illustrated by the following examples where the rook is switched from the h- to the g-file. In this case the rook is potentially active on two files at the same time and develops great power as a result.
zh: 车在h1、兵在h4的配置具有多样性，以下把车从h线转到g线的例子很好地说明了这一点。这时车同时拥有在两条直线上活动的潜力，因而威力巨大。
caption_zh: 武科维奇—瓦伊达博士，德布勒森，1925年；白先。

text: The above position arose in the game Vuković-Dr Vajda, Debrecen 1925. Black had just threatened White's bishop by ...h6, and White replied:
zh: 上图出自武科维奇—瓦伊达博士，德布勒森，1925年。黑方刚以...h6攻击白象，白方应：

text: If Black accepts the sacrifice, then after 1... hxg5 2. hxg5 g6 3. gxf6 Nxf6 4. Ne5 White obtains an attacking position without having to surrender any material.
zh: 若黑方接受弃子，则1... hxg5 2. hxg5 g6 3. gxf6 Nxf6 4. Ne5，白方无须付出任何子力，就得到攻击局面。

text: Consistently refusing the gift offered him on g5, Black hopes to persuade the bishop eventually to retreat. However, he is in any case in a poor position, as a result of his premature advance ...c4 earlier in the game. With his pawn on c5 Black would still have some say in the centre, and a central action is usually a valuable antidote against an attack on the castled king. With the pawn on c4, Black is only able to undertake slow operations on the queenside, and they are not sufficient to counterbalance White's attack.
zh: 黑方始终拒收g5上的礼物，希望最终迫使白象退走。然而，他此前过早推进...c4，局面无论如何都不好。兵若在c5，黑方在中心还有发言权；中心行动通常是应对杀王进攻的有效药方。兵到了c4，黑方就只能在后翼缓慢行动，不足以抗衡白方的进攻。

text: A manoeuvre designed to bring the rook into the game as quickly as possible; it is characteristic of the formation with rook on h1 and pawn on h4.
zh: 尽快让车投入战斗的调动，是车在h1、兵在h4配置的典型手段。

text: Black lacks a good answer to the threat of Bxh6. After 3... Bxg2 4. Rg3 his situation deteriorates still further, while if 3... Kf8, then 4. Bxh6 gxh6 5. Nxf7 Kxf7 6. Qg6+ Kf8 7. Qxh6+ Kf7 8. Bg6+ Kg8 9. Rg3 leads to mate.
zh: 黑方对Bxh6的威胁没有好办法。3... Bxg2 4. Rg3会使局面进一步恶化；若3... Kf8，则4. Bxh6 gxh6 5. Nxf7 Kxf7 6. Qg6+ Kf8 7. Qxh6+ Kf7 8. Bg6+ Kg8 9. Rg3，形成将杀。

caption_zh: 武科维奇—瓦伊达博士；4. Bxh6后。

text: If 4... gxh6, then 5. Rg3+ soon decides the issue.
zh: 若4... gxh6，则5. Rg3+很快决定胜负。

text: Or 5... Bxg2 6. Qxh5 g6 7. Rg3, etc.
zh: 或5... Bxg2 6. Qxh5 g6 7. Rg3，等等。

text: Black gives up a second pawn, but he can do nothing to save his position. After **8. hxg6 Bxe5 9. gxf7+ Kxf7 10. dxe5 Qa5** White played **11. e4** and won in ten more moves, but the finish might have been even more abrupt with 11. Bxg7 Kxg7 12. g5 followed by Qh5.
zh: 黑方再弃一兵，但已无力挽救局面。**8. hxg6 Bxe5 9. gxf7+ Kxf7 10. dxe5 Qa5**后，白方走**11. e4**，再过十步获胜；不过11. Bxg7 Kxg7 12. g5再Qh5，结束得还会更快。

text: The h-file in connection with the classic bishop sacrifice
zh: h线与古典弃象的结合

text: The analysis of the classic bishop sacrifice, to which we devoted particular attention in an earlier chapter, must now be supplemented by cases where such a sacrifice is combined with an attack along the h-file. This arises when White has a rook on h1 and pawn on h4, the pawn acting as a support for the knight on g5. We shall examine two examples from master chess in which the h-file is opened up.
zh: 前一章详细分析了古典弃象，现在须补充弃象与h线进攻结合的情况。这通常发生在白车位于h1、白兵位于h4时，h兵为g5马提供支持。我们来研究两个大师实战中打开h线的例子。

text: The following position comes from the game Steinitz-Golmayo, Havana 1888, and arose after the moves:
zh: 下图出自斯坦尼茨—戈尔马约，哈瓦那，1888年，由以下着法形成：

text: **1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. e5 Nfd7 5. f4 c5 6. dxc5 Bxc5 7. Nf3 O-O 8. Bd3 Nc6? (D)**
zh: **1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. e5 Nfd7 5. f4 c5 6. dxc5 Bxc5 7. Nf3 O-O 8. Bd3 Nc6?（见下图）**
caption_zh: 斯坦尼茨—戈尔马约；8... Nc6后。

text: Steinitz at this point played:
zh: 斯坦尼茨此时走：

text: White could have played immediately 9. Bxh7+ Kxh7 10. Ng5+ Kg6 11. Qd3+ f5 and then 12. Qg3 Qe8 (against other queen moves, 13. Qh4 is decisive) 13. Nxe6+ Kf7 14. Nc7¹ Qd8 15. Nxa8 when White has the upper hand.
zh: 白方本可立即9. Bxh7+ Kxh7 10. Ng5+ Kg6 11. Qd3+ f5，然后12. Qg3 Qe8（若后走其他地方，13. Qh4决定胜负）13. Nxe6+ Kf7 14. Nc7¹ Qd8 15. Nxa8，白方占优。

text: ¹ In this line 14. Nxg7! Rg8 15. Nxe8 Rxg3 16. e6+ is decisive.
zh: ¹ 纳恩注：此变化中14. Nxg7! Rg8 15. Nxe8 Rxg3 16. e6+可决定胜负。

text: Steinitz rejected the idea of the sacrifice because on the twelfth move he had reckoned only on 12. Nxe6? Qa5 13. Nxf8+ Nxf8 14. Qxd5 Be6, which would indeed have been favourable for Black.
zh: 斯坦尼茨放弃弃象构思，是因为第十二步只考虑了12. Nxe6? Qa5 13. Nxf8+ Nxf8 14. Qxd5 Be6，那确实对黑方有利。

text: White would have had a harder task after 9... h6, although even then he could have gained the advantage by 10. Ng5. Given that this is a typical continuation, let us examine a few variations:
zh: 9... h6会使白方的任务更艰巨，不过即便如此，10. Ng5仍可取得优势。由于这是典型续着，我们考察几个变化：

text:
1) 10... hxg5 11. Bh7+! Kxh7 12. Qh5+ Kg8 13. hxg5 f5 14. g6 and mate.
2) 10... Ndxe5 11. fxe5 Nxe5 12. Bh7+ Kh8 13. Bf4 Ng6 14. Bd2 and White is the better placed.¹
3) 10... Nb4 11. Bh7+ Kh8 12. Qh5 Qe7 13. Bd2 f5 (if 13... Re8 then 14. Bg6 while against 13... Nc6 or other such moves White plays 14. O-O-O) 14. Qg6 Nxc2+ (also in White's favour is 14... Qe8 15. Nxe6, etc.) 15. Kd1 Nxa1 16. Bg8! followed by mate with the queen on h7.²
zh:
1）10... hxg5 11. Bh7+! Kxh7 12. Qh5+ Kg8 13. hxg5 f5 14. g6，接着将杀。
2）10... Ndxe5 11. fxe5 Nxe5 12. Bh7+ Kh8 13. Bf4 Ng6 14. Bd2，白方局面更佳。¹
3）10... Nb4 11. Bh7+ Kh8 12. Qh5 Qe7 13. Bd2 f5（若13... Re8，则14. Bg6；若13... Nc6或类似着法，白方14. O-O-O）14. Qg6 Nxc2+（14... Qe8 15. Nxe6等也对白方有利）15. Kd1 Nxa1 16. Bg8!，接着后在h7将杀。²

text: ¹ This contention seems highly dubious. After 13... Nc4, attacking b2 and threatening 14... e5, White is clearly worse. Black has two central pawns for the piece, White's king is trapped in the centre and his pieces are hopelessly tangled up on the kingside. Therefore White should prefer 12. Nf3, with a double-edged position.
zh: ¹ 纳恩注：这一判断非常可疑。13... Nc4攻击b2并威胁14... e5之后，白方明显较差。黑方以两个中心兵补偿所弃的一子，白王困在中心，子力也在王翼乱成一团。因此白方应选12. Nf3，局面双方均有机会。

text: ² There is also a fair degree of wishful thinking in this line, for example after 14... Qe8 15. Nxe6 Nxc2+ 16. Kd1 (16. Ke2 Qxe6!) 16... Qxg6 17. Bxg6 Nxa1 the queens are exchanged and White is a whole rook down. He can regain the exchange easily enough, but rounding up the a1-knight is far from easy — the assessment must be that Black is better. All these lines illustrate the point that Vuković himself makes: launching an attack without first completing your development is a risky business.
zh: ² 纳恩注：这个变化也有相当一部分是一厢情愿。例如14... Qe8 15. Nxe6 Nxc2+ 16. Kd1（16. Ke2 Qxe6!）16... Qxg6 17. Bxg6 Nxa1，双方兑后，白方净少一车。收回一个交换固然容易，但围捕a1马远非易事，评价必须是黑方更好。这些变化恰恰说明武科维奇自己提出的道理：尚未完成出子便发动进攻，是危险的事。
**10. Ng5! fxg5（见下图）**
caption_zh: 斯坦尼茨—戈尔马约；10... fxg5后。

text: The sacrifice is both correct and necessary; after 11. hxg5 Black would have the reply 11... g6 12. Rxh7 Ndxe5 13. fxe5 Bf2+, etc.
zh: 弃象既正确又必要；若11. hxg5，黑方有11... g6 12. Rxh7 Ndxe5 13. fxe5 Bf2+等应手。

text: The fact that the knight is sacrificed on g5 first and then the bishop on h7 makes no difference to the actual structure of the combination; the order of moves is conditioned by temporal factors.
zh: 先在g5弃马，再在h7弃象，并不改变组合的实际结构；着法次序由时间因素决定。

caption_zh: 斯坦尼茨—戈尔马约；13. Qh5后。

text: Otherwise 14. g6 is decisive.¹
zh: 否则14. g6决定胜负。¹

text: ¹ Here Black misses 13... Ncxe5! 14. fxe5 Qc7!, when it is hard to see how White can continue his attack.
zh: ¹ 纳恩注：黑方在这里错过了13... Ncxe5! 14. fxe5 Qc7!，此后很难看出白方如何继续进攻。

text: **14. fxe5 Rf5¹ 15. g4 Rxe5+ 16. Kd1 Be3**
zh: **14. fxe5 Rf5¹ 15. g4 Rxe5+ 16. Kd1 Be3**

text: If 16... Bd7, then 17. Qh8+ Kf7 18. Rf1+ Ke7 19. Qxg7+ Kd6 20. Nb5#, while if 16... Bf8, then 17. Bf4.

zh: **17. Bxe3 Rxe3 18. Nb5!（见下图）**
caption_zh: 斯坦尼茨—戈尔马约；18. Nb5后。

text: In the preceding note we gave a line ending with Nb5#; now the same move serves to tighten the mating net, which Black had attempted to cut through by 16... Be3 (freeing the c5-square for the king's escape!).
zh: 上一条评注给出一个以Nb5#结束的变化；现在同一着法又用来收紧杀网。黑方原想借16... Be3突围，腾出c5供王逃生！

text: The alternatives were 18... Kf8 19. Qh8+ Kf7 20. Rf1+ followed by mate and 18... Re5 19. Qh7+ Kf8 20. Rf1+, etc.
zh: 其他选择是18... Kf8 19. Qh8+ Kf7 20. Rf1+接着将杀，或18... Re5 19. Qh7+ Kf8 20. Rf1+等。

text: It is the formation with pawn on g6 against pawn on g7 (which has already been discussed) that is finally decisive. The part played by the knight on b5 is evident in several variations, as well as in the final position, e.g. if 19... Kf8, then 20. Qh8+ and 21. Qxg7+, etc.
zh: 最终决定胜负的，正是此前讨论过的g6兵对g7兵配置。b5马的作用，在几个变化以及最后局面中都很明显，例如19... Kf8后，20. Qh8+再21. Qxg7+等。

text: ¹ In this position 14... Qc7 is less effective, as 15. Bf4! Rxf4 16. Qh8+ Kf7 17. g6+! Ke7 18. Qxg7+ gives White a very dangerous attack — Black needs a defensive knight on d7.
zh: ¹ 纳恩注：此局面中14... Qc7不那么有效，因为15. Bf4! Rxf4 16. Qh8+ Kf7 17. g6+! Ke7 18. Qxg7+使白方获得非常危险的攻势；黑方需要一匹马在d7防守。

text:
Alekhine – Asgeirsson
Reykjavik Simultaneous Display, 1931
French Defence
zh:
阿廖欣—阿斯盖尔松
雷克雅未克车轮战，1931年
法兰西防御

text: **1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. Bxf6 Bxf6 6. Nf3 O-O 7. Bd3 Re8?!**
zh: **1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. Bxf6 Bxf6 6. Nf3 O-O 7. Bd3 Re8?!**

text: An unnecessary loss of time; correct is 7... c5 at once.
zh: 不必要地浪费时间；应立即7... c5。

caption_zh: 阿廖欣—阿斯盖尔松；9... c5后。

text: White has prepared for the sacrifice of his bishop on h7 by 9. h4, and the reply 9... c5 does nothing to stop it. Relatively best was 9... f5! 10. exf6 (after 10. Ne2 c5 11. c3 White is the better placed, but his attack is delayed and Black is not without counterplay) 10... Bxf6. The situation is then easier for Black, for as a result of the exchange on f6 an extremely important attacking unit has disappeared, namely White's pawn on e5. Sacrifices in this position are therefore not worthwhile; after 11. Bxh7+ Kxh7 12. Ng5+ Kg8 13. Qh5 Black has an adequate defence in 13... Qd7, while if 11. Ng5, he can play 11... Bxg5 12. hxg5 Qxg5! 13. Bxh7+ Kf8, and White's attack is not worth much owing to his weakness in the centre and the activity of Black's queen, especially on the dark squares.¹
zh: 白方9. h4准备在h7弃象，9... c5却丝毫没有阻止这一点。相对最好的是9... f5! 10. exf6（若10. Ne2 c5 11. c3，白方局面更佳，但攻势被延缓，黑方也并非没有反击）10... Bxf6。这样黑方比较容易应付，因为f6上的兑换消灭了一枚极其重要的攻击单位，即白方e5兵。因此，此局面中的弃子并不值得：11. Bxh7+ Kxh7 12. Ng5+ Kg8 13. Qh5后，黑方13... Qd7足以防守；若11. Ng5，可11... Bxg5 12. hxg5 Qxg5! 13. Bxh7+ Kf8，由于白方中心薄弱，加上黑后活跃、尤其在黑格上活跃，白方攻势价值不大。¹

text: The last continuation can also be brought about by a different series of moves: 11. Ng5 Bxg5 12. Bxh7+, when Black should not play 12... Kxh7 (in which case 13. hxg5+ and 14. Qh5 is extremely strong) but 12... Kf8! 13. hxg5 Qxg5, ending with the position described above. These possibilities are worth getting to know well, since we are dealing with a typical position. Particularly important is the significance of Black's ...f5 in this kind of position: if White does not take the pawn at once en passant, the sacrifice on h7 is prevented directly; while if he takes it, then it is indirectly thwarted or at any rate made weaker, since White's pawn has disappeared from e5.
zh: 最后一个变化也可由不同次序形成：11. Ng5 Bxg5 12. Bxh7+，此时黑方不应12... Kxh7（那样13. hxg5+接14. Qh5极强），而应12... Kf8! 13. hxg5 Qxg5，得到上述局面。这是典型局面，这些可能性值得熟悉。尤其应注意黑方...f5的意义：白方若不立即吃过路兵，h7弃象就被直接阻止；若吃过路兵，由于e5兵消失，弃象也会被间接化解，或至少减弱。

text: It is also worth noting that to avert the sacrifice entirely by ...h6 or ...g6 is not a good thing in this position. If 9... h6, White plays 10. Ne2 followed by c3 and attacks in a different way (e.g. by means of Bb1 and Qd3 he forces a weakening of the square g6 or, alternatively, he plays g4, etc.); in this connection it is important to note that ...f5, if played later on, would create a new weakness on g6. If 9... g6, White can immediately play 10. h5, but still better is first 10. Ne2, etc.
zh: 还应注意，此时以...h6或...g6彻底避免弃象，并不好。若9... h6，白方10. Ne2，接c3，改用其他方式进攻，例如Bb1、Qd3迫使g6格变弱，或走g4等。这里须注意，黑方如果后来才走...f5，又会在g6造成新弱点。若9... g6，白方可立即10. h5，但先10. Ne2等还更好。

text: ¹ This is not so. After 14. Qf3+ Ke7 (14... Qf6 15. Bg6) 15. Rh5 Qf6 16. Qg3 Qxd4 (or else 17. O-O-O, with a massive lead in development without any sacrifice by White) 17. Rd1 Qf6 18. Bg6 Rf8 19. Rf5 Black's queen is trapped.
zh: ¹ 纳恩注：并非如此。14. Qf3+ Ke7（14... Qf6 15. Bg6）15. Rh5 Qf6 16. Qg3 Qxd4（否则17. O-O-O，白方无须弃子，便有巨大的出子优势）17. Rd1 Qf6 18. Bg6 Rf8 19. Rf5，黑后被困。

text: The sacrifice is correct, even though it demands extremely precise and high-quality play from the attacker.
zh: 这个弃象是正确的，尽管要求进攻者走得极其精确、水平很高。

text: 11... Kg6 would be hopeless here; the formation comprising rook on h1 and pawns on h4 and e5 is a formidable weapon against it, e.g. 11... Kg6 12. Qd3+ f5 13. h5+ Kxg5 14. Qg3+ and 15. Qg6#.
zh: 这里11... Kg6毫无希望；h1车与h4、e5双兵的配置是对付它的强大武器。例如11... Kg6 12. Qd3+ f5 13. h5+ Kxg5 14. Qg3+，接15. Qg6#。

text: He must!
zh: 非走不可！

text: This move puts a spoke in Black's defensive plans. He would lose quickly after 14... fxg6 15. Qxg6, while if 14... cxd4, White can win either by 15. gxf7 or 15. Qh8+ Ke7 16. Qxg7 Rf8 17. Qf6+ Kd7 18. g7 Rg8 19. Rh8 Qe8 20. Nxd5 Nc6 21. Qh6.
zh: 这一着打乱了黑方防守计划。14... fxg6 15. Qxg6会迅速输棋；若14... cxd4，白方既可15. gxf7，也可15. Qh8+ Ke7 16. Qxg7 Rf8 17. Qf6+ Kd7 18. g7 Rg8 19. Rh8 Qe8 20. Nxd5 Nc6 21. Qh6获胜。

caption_zh: 阿廖欣—阿斯盖尔松；15... Rf8后。
阿廖欣—阿斯盖尔松；16. O-O-O后。

text: Alekhine the player and Alekhine the commentator failed to see that Black could have saved himself after this move. 16. dxc5! was both necessary and good in order to prevent Black from taking the initiative in the centre. This is underlined by the following variations:
zh: 无论作为棋手还是评注者，阿廖欣都没有看出，此着之后黑方本可自救。为了阻止黑方在中心取得主动，16. dxc5!既必要又好。以下变化说明了这一点：

text: 1) 16... Nd7 17. O-O-O Qa5 (if 17... Rxf7 White wins by 18. Nxd5+ and 19. e6, while if 17... Nxc5, then 18. b4) 18. Qg5+ Kxf7 19. Rh7 Rg8 20. Nxd5! Qxa2 (if 20... exd5 then 21. e6+ Kxe6 22. Qxd5+ and 23. Qxg8 wins, while if 20... Qxc5, then 21. Qh5+ Kf8 22. Nf4 wins) 21. Qe7+ Kg6 22. Qxe6+ Nf6 23. Rxg7+ mating.
zh: 1）16... Nd7 17. O-O-O Qa5（若17... Rxf7，白方18. Nxd5+接19. e6获胜；若17... Nxc5，则18. b4）18. Qg5+ Kxf7 19. Rh7 Rg8 20. Nxd5! Qxa2（若20... exd5，则21. e6+ Kxe6 22. Qxd5+接23. Qxg8获胜；若20... Qxc5，则21. Qh5+ Kf8 22. Nf4获胜）21. Qe7+ Kg6 22. Qxe6+ Nf6 23. Rxg7+，将杀。

text: 2) 16... Nc6 17. O-O-O Qa5 (or 17... Rxf7 18. Qg5+ Kd7 19. Qg6 Nxe5 {19... Qe7 transposes to line 3} 20. Rxd5+ exd5 21. Qd6+ and 22. Rh8+, etc.) 18. Qg5+ Kxf7 19. Rh7 Rg8 20. Qf6+ Ke8 21. Qg6+ Ke7 (if 21... Kf8, then 22. Rh4 wins, while if 21... Kd8, then 22. Nxd5) 22. Rxg7+ Rxg7 23. Qxg7+ Ke8 24. Rh1! Ne7 25. Rh7 Qxc5 26. Na4! Qc7 (or 26... Qb4 27. Qf7+ Kd8 28. c3!) 27. Qf7+ Kd8 28. Qf8+ mating.

3) 16... Rxf7 17. Qg5+ Kd7 18. Qg6 Qe7 (defending the rook and parrying the threat of Nxd5) 19. O-O-O Nc6 (if 19... Kc7, then 20. Nb5+ and 21. Nd6, while if 19... Kc6, then 20. Rxd5) 20. Qg4! Kc7 21. Nb5+ Kb8 22. Nd6 Rf8 23. Rh7 Nxe5 (if 23... Rg8, then 24. Rdh1 followed by Rh8, etc.) 24. Qg3 Qf6 25. Rxg7 Qf4+ (should Black attempt to free himself with 25... Bd7, White wins by 26. Qxe5 and 27. Rxd7) 26. Qxf4 Rxf4 27. Rh1 Rf8 28. Rhh7 and mate on b7.
zh: 3）16... Rxf7 17. Qg5+ Kd7 18. Qg6 Qe7（保车并抵挡Nxd5的威胁）19. O-O-O Nc6（若19... Kc7，则20. Nb5+接21. Nd6；若19... Kc6，则20. Rxd5）20. Qg4! Kc7 21. Nb5+ Kb8 22. Nd6 Rf8 23. Rh7 Nxe5（若23... Rg8，则24. Rdh1，再Rh8等）24. Qg3 Qf6 25. Rxg7 Qf4+（若黑方25... Bd7企图解围，白方26. Qxe5接27. Rxd7获胜）26. Qxf4 Rxf4 27. Rh1 Rf8 28. Rhh7，接着在b7将杀。

text: These variations do not exhaust the possibilities of the position, but they give a good illustration of the strength of White's game after 16. dxc5.
zh: 这些变化没有穷尽局面中的一切可能，但很好地说明了16. dxc5后白方局面的力量。

text: An example of the inadequacy of passive defence. 17. Nb5, which is what Black was afraid of, is by no means White's principal threat and is only effective in conjunction with a strong initiative. Alekhine is also at fault in his commentary when he claims that Nb5 represented a threat after 16. O-O-O.
zh: 这是消极防守不足以奏效的一例。黑方所担心的17. Nb5绝非白方的主要威胁，它只有与强烈主动配合才有效。阿廖欣在评注中声称16. O-O-O后存在Nb5的威胁，也不正确。

text: Instead of 16... a6? Black should have played 16... cxd4! and thus exploited the extra tempo in the centre, e.g.:
zh: 黑方应以16... cxd4!代替16... a6?，利用多出的一拍在中心行动，例如：

text:
1) 17. Nb5 Nc6 and now:
1a) 18. f4 Rxf7 19. Nd6 and now Black has a satisfactory defence in 19... Qf8!¹
1b) 18. Nd6 Nxe5 (this gives back material and at the same time eliminates White's threats) 19. Nxc8+ Rxc8 20. Qxe5 Qc7, and Black's position is in no way inferior.
1c) 18. Qg5+ Kd7 19. Qxg7 b6! 20. Nd6 Ba6 21. f4 d3 and Black obtains counterplay, e.g. if 22. c3 or 22. cxd3, then 22... Nd4, while Ne8 can always be answered by ...Ke7.
2) 17. Rxd4 Nc6 18. Rf4 (sacrifices at this point are insufficient to break through) 18... Kd7 19. Rg4 Qe7 20. Rxg7 b6 and against any further activity by White on the kingside Black has enough counterplay based on ...Nd4 and eventually ...Rac8 and ...Qc5.
zh:
1）17. Nb5 Nc6，此时：
1a）18. f4 Rxf7 19. Nd6，黑方现在有满意的防守19... Qf8!¹
1b）18. Nd6 Nxe5（交还子力，同时消除白方威胁）19. Nxc8+ Rxc8 20. Qxe5 Qc7，黑方局面丝毫不差。
1c）18. Qg5+ Kd7 19. Qxg7 b6! 20. Nd6 Ba6 21. f4 d3，黑方获得反击。例如22. c3或22. cxd3，都可应22... Nd4；Ne8则始终可以...Ke7应对。
2）17. Rxd4 Nc6 18. Rf4（此时弃子不足以突破）18... Kd7 19. Rg4 Qe7 20. Rxg7 b6，对白方王翼的进一步行动，黑方以...Nd4，以及随后的...Rac8、...Qc5为基础，拥有充分反击。

text: ¹ Not so, as White wins by 20. Qg5+ Kd7 21. Nxf7 Qxf7 22. Rh7 and the g7-pawn falls.
zh: ¹ 纳恩注：并非如此，白方20. Qg5+ Kd7 21. Nxf7 Qxf7 22. Rh7获胜，g7兵将被吃掉。

text: Now all is well again, and the position is won.
zh: 现在又一切顺利，白方已是胜势。

text: If 18... exd5 then 19. Nxd5+ Ke6 20. Nf4+ Ke7 21. e6! Nf6 22. Qe5 and mates.
zh: 若18... exd5，则19. Nxd5+ Ke6 20. Nf4+ Ke7 21. e6! Nf6 22. Qe5，将杀。

text: There are a number of 'subsidiary solutions' here, but 21. Rxd7+? Bxd7 22. Ne4 does not work because of 22... Qe1#.
zh: 这里有若干“次要解法”，但21. Rxd7+? Bxd7 22. Ne4行不通，因为22... Qe1#。

text: But now, of course, this way is all right!
zh: 当然，现在这样走就完全可以了！

caption_zh: 阿廖欣—阿斯盖尔松；24... Kf8后。

text: In the past commentators used to end their work on games like this by praising the winner, but does not the loser in some way deserve credit too? Is it not he who 'fulfils the ardent desires' of the attacker, as is done in this case by the good-natured matador from Ultima Thule...?
zh: 过去，评注者谈到这样的棋局，总以赞美胜者收尾；但败者难道不也应得到某种赞誉吗？正是他“满足了”进攻者的“热切愿望”，就像本局这位来自极北之地、性情温厚的斗牛士一样，不是吗……？

text: Diagonals in the attack on the castled king
zh: 斜线在攻击易位王时的作用

text: Tartakower thought it suitable to bestow epithets of the following kind on the files: a-file — positional; b — covetous; c — far-sighted; d — prosaic; e — dangerous; f — tempting; g — sacrificial; and h — contentious. He might also have invented something similar (even if he in fact did not) to apply to the ranks. But the diagonals? Well, they are all somehow equally 'elegant, subtle, far-sighted', etc. On the long diagonals (a1-h8 and a8-h1) more kings have already died than in the whole of the world's history; more tragedies have been played out on the classic diagonals (b1-h7 for White and b8-h2 for Black) than in all the world's theatres, and on the developing diagonals (a2-g8 and a7-g1 respectively) there have been more mistakes made than in a large library full of books. Now that we have started on nicknames and epithets, let us bestow on the diagonals a4-e8 and h4-d8 (from White's point of view; a5-e1 and h5-d1 from Black's) the name of pinning diagonals. The reader can think over for himself how much material he has already lost on them.
zh: 塔塔科维尔觉得可以给各条直线加上这样的称号：a线——局面棋型；b线——贪婪；c线——深谋远虑；d线——平淡；e线——危险；f线——诱惑；g线——弃子；h线——好斗。他或许也能为横线编出类似称号，即便实际上没有这样做。但斜线呢？它们似乎都同样“优雅、微妙、深谋远虑”等等。在长斜线a1-h8、a8-h1上倒下的王，比世界历史上死去的国王还多；在古典斜线——白方b1-h7、黑方b8-h2——上演出的悲剧，比全世界剧院里的悲剧还多；而在出子斜线a2-g8、a7-g1上犯下的错误，比一座大图书馆所有书里的错误还多。既然开始起绰号，我们就把a4-e8和h4-d8（从白方看；黑方则是a5-e1和h5-d1）称作“牵制斜线”。读者不妨想想，自己在这些斜线上已经丢过多少子力。

text: Just as the rook is the piece suited for play on open files and ranks, so the bishop is the master of the diagonals, indeed they are his raison d'être. At all stages of the game, and especially in an attack on the castled king, marshalling bishops on the diagonals demands great skill. A player's skill, in fact, is often demonstrated by his play on the diagonals, and the impression is then given that 'the slender bishop is subtler than the stout rook'. Putting facetiousness aside, let us now look at the relationship between the lines commanded by the rook and the bishop's diagonals.
zh: 车适合在开放直线和横线上作战，象则是斜线的主人；可以说，斜线就是象存在的理由。在棋局各阶段，尤其攻击易位王时，沿斜线部署象都需要高超技巧。棋手的本领往往就表现在斜线运用上，让人觉得“苗条的象比敦实的车更精巧”。玩笑到此为止，现在来看看车控制的线路与象的斜线之间的关系。

text: In the first place, it should be stressed that the fundamental difference does not lie in the number or importance of the squares on the files or diagonals, nor in the weight of operations on them. The differences arise only from the different values of rook and bishop and also from the part played by pawn moves in opening up or blocking a line.
zh: 首先须强调，根本区别不在直线或斜线上格子的数量或重要性，也不在沿线行动的分量。区别只来自车与象的不同价值，以及兵步在打开或封闭线路时所起的作用。

text: It is harder to sacrifice the more valuable rook than the bishop, and the order of value is even more relevant when it comes to pinning: exchanging a bishop for a pinned rook wins the exchange, while bishop for knight is tit-for-tat, but a rook can only gain from pinning a piece when it takes the queen. The other difference is still more explicit: it is comparatively easy to open up or close a diagonal by the normal advance of one's pawns, but achieving the same object on a file means that the pawn has to make a capture, and this naturally depends on the disposition of one's opponent's pieces; hence, there may be considerable difficulty in opening up a file. If, on the other hand, it has to be closed, an outpost as a rule has to be established; on the diagonals, however, outposts are the exception, since the 'open-shut' game is easily carried out by the pawns. It is in this, ultimately, that the whole 'subtlety and far-sightedness' of the diagonal lies. We shall open a series of examples with a case of pinning on a diagonal. The pinning here is in fact a temporary episode within the whole operation of 'clearing up' on the diagonal, and the end comes with the line being completely breached when the pinned piece is captured.
zh: 车更值钱，弃车比弃象更难；在牵制中，子力价值的高低就更加重要：象换掉被牵制的车是得交换，象换马则价值相当，而车通过牵制获利，只有吃到后才行。另一个区别更明显：通常推进己方兵，就比较容易打开或封闭斜线；但要在直线上达到同样目的，兵必须吃子，自然就要取决于对方子力的配置，所以开放直线可能相当困难。反过来，要封闭直线，通常须建立前哨；斜线上的前哨却是例外，因为兵很容易完成“开关”动作。斜线全部的“微妙与深谋远虑”，归根结底就在这里。我们以斜线上的牵制开始这一组实例。这里的牵制其实只是清理整条斜线过程中的暂时环节，最后吃掉被牵制棋子，彻底打通线路。
caption_zh: 托卢什—伦特，爱沙尼亚锦标赛，1945年；白先。

text: This position comes from the game Tolush-Renter, Estonian Championship 1945. It is White to move.
zh: 此局面出自托卢什—伦特，爱沙尼亚锦标赛，1945年。白先。

text: This draws Black's king out to g7 and at the same time opens up the diagonal of the white bishop on b2.
zh: 把黑王引到g7，同时打开b2白象的斜线。

text: If 2... Qe6, then 3. f5.

In this way White wins the enemy bishop, but the correct method of exploiting the position would have been to aim consistently for a breakthrough on the square f6, e.g. 4. Qg5 Rc6 5. f5 Rg8 (or 5... Rd8 6. Re1 and if 6... Rdd6, then 7. Qh6 followed by Rf4 wins; otherwise the manoeuvre Rf4-g4 is at once decisive¹) 6. Qh6 Bc8 7. h4 b5 (Black has no better move; for example, ...Rg7 and ...Ne8 will not save him because of f6) 8. h5 a5 9. Rfd2 b4 (the combination which White has prepared by advancing his h-pawn to h5 is also decisive against other moves) 10. Rd6 Rxd6 11. Rxd6 Qxd6 12. Bxf6+ Qxf6 13. Qxf6+ Rg7 14. h6 and White mates.
zh: 这样白方可赢得对方一象，但利用局面的正确方法应当是始终瞄准f6突破。例如4. Qg5 Rc6 5. f5 Rg8（或5... Rd8 6. Re1，若6... Rdd6，则7. Qh6再Rf4获胜；否则Rf4-g4的调动立即决定胜负¹）6. Qh6 Bc8 7. h4 b5（黑方没有更好着法，例如...Rg7和...Ne8都挡不住f6）8. h5 a5 9. Rfd2 b4（白方通过h兵推进到h5所准备的组合，对其他着法也决定胜负）10. Rd6 Rxd6 11. Rxd6 Qxd6 12. Bxf6+ Qxf6 13. Qxf6+ Rg7 14. h6，白方将杀。

text: ¹ Black might defend by 6... Rdd6 7. Qh6 Qd8, and if 8. Rf4 then 8... Rd1. In view of the uncertainties of this approach, Tolush's method appears sounder.
zh: ¹ 纳恩注：黑方或可6... Rdd6 7. Qh6 Qd8防守；若8. Rf4，则8... Rd1。鉴于这种方案的不确定性，托卢什的处理看来更稳妥。

text: **4... Qe6 5. Qg5 Rc6 6. Rxb7** and White won in due course.
zh: **4... Qe6 5. Qg5 Rc6 6. Rxb7**，白方随后获胜。

text: An important point is that, in addition to 'clearing' one's opponent's pieces from a diagonal, cases also occur where one's own pieces prevent it being opened. It is extremely difficult to resuscitate a diagonal on which one has a blocked pawn of one's own. Structurally, it is a similar problem to that of opening a file where a pawn blocks the path of a rook, and it is usually solved in the same way, i.e. by sacrificing a piece on a square controlled by the pawn. Here is an example.
zh: 一个重要问题是：除了清除斜线上的敌子，也会有己方棋子妨碍斜线开放的情况。如果斜线上有己方被封锁的兵，要使它恢复活力就极其困难。在结构上，这与兵挡住车路、需要开放直线的问题相似；通常也用同样办法解决，即在这个兵控制的格子上弃子。下面是一个例子。
caption_zh: 亚历山大—萨博，希尔弗瑟姆，1947年；白先。

text: This position occurred in the game Alexander-Szabo, Hilversum 1947. White pitched his knight into f6 with check so as to bring the long diagonal back to life.
zh: 此局面出自亚历山大—萨博，希尔弗瑟姆，1947年。白方将马投到f6将军，使长斜线重获生机。

text: If 1... Kh8, then 2. Qh4 is very strong.¹
zh: 若1... Kh8，则2. Qh4很强。¹

text: **2. Qg3+ Kh8 3. exf6 Bxf6 4. Ne5!**
zh: **2. Qg3+ Kh8 3. exf6 Bxf6 4. Ne5!**

text: White threatens 5. Rxf6, 5. Nxf7+ and indeed 5. Qh4 (5... Bxh4 6. Nxf7+ and 7. Nh6#). Black no longer has any defence.
zh: 白方威胁5. Rxf6、5. Nxf7+，还有5. Qh4（5... Bxh4 6. Nxf7+，接7. Nh6#）。黑方已无防守。

text: Since if 6... Rxf6, 7. Bf1 is decisive.
zh: 因为若6... Rxf6，7. Bf1决定胜负。

text: The 'clearing' of the long diagonal was a victory for the bishop.
zh: 长斜线的“清理”，就是象的胜利。

text: ¹ 2. Qh4 allows the defence 2... Qxd3. Instead, 2. Qe4 is correct, when 2... gxf6 3. exf6 followed by Ng5 forces mate.
zh: ¹ 纳恩注：2. Qh4允许黑方2... Qxd3防守。正确的是2. Qe4，若2... gxf6 3. exf6，再Ng5，可强制将杀。

text: As far as play on the diagonals is concerned, the strength of the central squares on the given diagonals is particularly important. These squares can assist the attacker in setting up outposts, in transferring pieces, and in other operations. Thus one should, as a rule, aim to have such squares protected or even over-protected. This is one of the maxims of positional play, and we shall see in the next example how Black pays for ignoring this maxim and how the attack on the castled king suddenly erupts.
zh: 就斜线作战而言，相关斜线上的中心格是否强固，尤其重要。这些格子能帮助进攻者建立前哨、转移子力，以及执行其他行动。所以通常应设法保护、甚至超额保护它们。这是局面棋的一条格言；下一例将展示黑方忽视它所付出的代价，以及针对易位王的进攻如何突然爆发。
caption_zh: 施托尔茨—吉马尔德，格罗宁根，1946年；白先。

text: This position arose in Stoltz-Guimard, Groningen 1946. White played:
zh: 此局面出自施托尔茨—吉马尔德，格罗宁根，1946年。白方走：

text: **1. dxc5 Nxc5?**
zh: **1. dxc5 Nxc5?**

text: A mistake, since it surrenders to White control over the important central squares d4 and e5, which means that the long diagonal occupied by his bishop on b2 is already as good as opened up (considering the gain of tempo by Nb5, which White always has in hand). Black should have played either 1... bxc5 or 1... Bxc5.
zh: 错误，因为这把重要中心格d4、e5的控制权让给白方，也意味着b2象占据的长斜线几乎已经打开了；要知道白方始终可以Nb5带先手。黑方应走1... bxc5或1... Bxc5。

text: 2... Qb8 is not good here because of White's grip on e5, e.g. 3. Be5 Qa8 4. Nc7, and Black loses the exchange.
zh: 白方牢牢控制e5，因此2... Qb8不好，例如3. Be5 Qa8 4. Nc7，黑方丢交换。

text: Black will, it is true, win back the a-pawn, but White will have succeeded, without loss of time, in strengthening the position of his knight at b5 (...a6 is no longer possible).
zh: 黑方固然能吃回a兵，但白方已经不失时间地巩固了马在b5的位置，因为黑方再也不能...a6。

text: Suddenly the course of the game turns against Black's castled position; White threatens Bxf6 followed by mate on h7.
zh: 棋局突然转向攻击黑王城；白方威胁Bxf6，再在h7将杀。

text: Black should have consented to a further weakening of the diagonal by 6... g6, for that would have meant less trouble for him than the text move.¹
zh: 黑方本应接受6... g6对斜线的进一步削弱，因为这比实战着带来的麻烦小。¹

text: **7. Bxf6 hxg5 8. Be5**
zh: **7. Bxf6 hxg5 8. Be5**

text: By threatening Bc7, White installs his bishop with gain of tempo at e5, a square that is now firmly under his control. His next intention is to play Qb2, after which the bishop's whole manoeuvre takes on the purpose of clearing the diagonal.
zh: 借助Bc7的威胁，白方带先手把象安置到e5，这个格子如今牢牢控制在他手中。接下来打算Qb2；于是象的整个调动就成为清理斜线的行动。

text: If 9... f6, which the tournament book (by Euwe and Kmoch) considers correct, White wins a pawn: 10. Bd6 Re8 (or 10... Qd7 11. Bc7 Ra6 12. Bf3, etc.) 11. Bxe7 Rxe7 12. Nd6 Qc6 13. Nxb7 Rxb7 14. cxd5 exd5 15. Rxd5, and Black is in difficulties on a fresh diagonal (a2-g8).
zh: 若9...f6——尤伟和克莫赫编写的赛事专辑认为这是正确着——白方可以得兵：10. Bd6 Re8（或10... Qd7 11. Bc7 Ra6 12. Bf3等）11. Bxe7 Rxe7 12. Nd6 Qc6 13. Nxb7 Rxb7 14. cxd5 exd5 15. Rxd5，黑方又在另一条斜线a2-g8上遇到困难。

text: Not 10. Bxg7? because of 10... Qc6.
zh: 不能10. Bxg7?，因为10... Qc6。

caption_zh: 施托尔茨—吉马尔德；11. f3后。

text: The tournament book gives this a question mark and suggests 11... f6; however, after 12. Bd6 Rfe8 13. b4 Na4 14. Qb3 Kh8 15. Bxe7 Black loses his e-pawn.
zh: 赛事专辑给此着加问号，建议11... f6；但12. Bd6 Rfe8 13. b4 Na4 14. Qb3 Kh8 15. Bxe7后，黑方会丢e兵。

text: Making use of the other square Black surrendered with 1... Nxc5?. White has now created a battery consisting of queen and knight.
zh: 利用黑方1... Nxc5?让出的另一个格子。白方现在组成了后马叠子。

text: The various operations on the diagonal are concluded by a bishop sacrifice, the aim of which is to lure the king into the line of fire. Black did not submit to this and played 14... Rfa8, losing after a further sixteen moves. However, we are only interested in the continuation 14... Kxg7, which is followed by 15. Nxe6+ Kg6 16. Qg7+ Kf5 17. Nd4#. The plan also works with 15. Nf5+, in which case mate is achieved by 17. g4#.
zh: 斜线上的各种行动，以弃象收尾，目的是把王诱入火力线。黑方不愿就范，走了14... Rfa8，又过十六步输棋。我们这里只关注14... Kxg7，随后15. Nxe6+ Kg6 16. Qg7+ Kf5 17. Nd4#。15. Nf5+也能实现同样计划，那时17. g4#将杀。

text: ¹ 6... Nce4 is perhaps the most sensible. Black blocks the b1-h7 diagonal without creating a further weakness on the kingside.
zh: ¹ 纳恩注：6... Nce4也许最明智。黑方封闭b1-h7斜线，而不在王翼制造新弱点。

text: The next example is devoted to the problem of recognizing strong diagonals and combining their 'clearing' with an effective use of the bishop.
zh: 下一例讨论如何认出强大的斜线，并把“清理”斜线与有效运用象结合起来。
caption_zh: 伦丁—塔塔科维尔，格罗宁根，1946年；白先。

text: Here we have a position from the game Lundin-Tartakower, Groningen 1946. It is clear that White is the better placed, and that Black is weak on the a2-g8 diagonal, but it is less obvious that the white bishop will put in such a quick appearance on that diagonal and that the game will be decided on the b1-h7 diagonal. White won as follows:
zh: 此局面出自伦丁—塔塔科维尔，格罗宁根，1946年。白方局面更佳、黑方在a2-g8斜线上薄弱，这很明显；但白象会如此迅速地出现在那条斜线上，而且棋局最终会在b1-h7斜线上定胜负，就不那么显然了。白方如下获胜：

text: Otherwise e5 is too strong.
zh: 否则e5太强。

text: The bishop is on its way to c4, the knight on g5 is already casting glances in the direction of f7, and the threats on the e-file see to it that the initiative remains in White's hands.
zh: 象正要转到c4，g5马已经觊觎f7，而e线上的威胁保证主动权仍掌握在白方手里。

text: This opens the diagonal with gain of tempo (the threat is Qd5+ and then Qxb7).
zh: 带先手打开斜线，威胁Qd5+再Qxb7。

text: If 6... Bc6, then 7. Nf7+ Kg8 8. Qxc6! bxc6 9. Ne5+ Kh8 10. Nxg6+ hxg6 11. Rxe4 g5 12. Bxa6, etc.
zh: 若6... Bc6，则7. Nf7+ Kg8 8. Qxc6! bxc6 9. Ne5+ Kh8 10. Nxg6+ hxg6 11. Rxe4 g5 12. Bxa6等。

text: **7. Nf7+ Kh7 8. Ne5 Qe8 9. Qxe4+ Bf5 10. Qxb7 Nb8 11. Bf7 Qd8 12. Qf3 Qf6 13. g4 Bb1 14. Qd1!**
zh: **7. Nf7+ Kh7 8. Ne5 Qe8 9. Qxe4+ Bf5 10. Qxb7 Nb8 11. Bf7 Qd8 12. Qf3 Qf6 13. g4 Bb1 14. Qd1!**

text: Now Black's bishop does not have a single square left on the b1-h7 diagonal. Black lost the exchange and the game a few moves later.
zh: 现在黑象在b1-h7斜线上连一个可去的格子都没有了。黑方丢了交换，几步后输棋。

text: Here is an example showing the strength of two bishops working together.
zh: 下面一例展示双象合作的力量。

text: White offers a pawn in order to open up the long diagonal for his b2-bishop.
zh: 白方献出一兵，为b2象打开长斜线。

text: Black does not accept the sacrifice. After 1... exd5 2. Rxe8 Qxe8 3. Ng5 both 3... g6 4. Bxg6! fxg6 5. Qd4 and 3... h6 4. Bh7+ Kh8 5. Qh5 give White a decisive attack.
zh: 黑方不接受弃兵。1... exd5 2. Rxe8 Qxe8 3. Ng5后，无论3... g6 4. Bxg6! fxg6 5. Qd4，还是3... h6 4. Bh7+ Kh8 5. Qh5，白方都有决定性攻势。

text: **2. dxe6 Rxe6 3. Rxe6 fxe6 4. Qc2 Bxf3**
zh: **2. dxe6 Rxe6 3. Rxe6 fxe6 4. Qc2 Bxf3**

text: 4... g6 is met by 5. Qc3, while if 4... h6, then 5. Bh7+ Kh8 6. Nh4.
**5. Bxh7+ Kh8 6. gxf3**
zh: **5. Bxh7+ Kh8 6. gxf3**

text: Having gained a pawn and weakened Black's position, White won the game in ten more moves.
zh: 白方多了一兵，又削弱了黑方局面，再过十步便获胜。
caption_zh: 盖勒—科托夫，苏联锦标赛，莫斯科，1955年；16. b3前。

text: In this position, which arose in Geller-Kotov, USSR Championship (Moscow) 1955, White sacrificed a pawn to obtain control of the long diagonal and thereby gain the possibility to break through with a winning attack.
zh: 此局面出自盖勒—科托夫，苏联锦标赛，莫斯科，1955年。白方弃兵夺取长斜线，从而争取以致胜攻势突破的可能。

text: Black accepts the pawn sacrifice, a decision which not only costs him a series of tempi but also causes him to yield control of the long diagonal to White.
zh: 黑方接受弃兵，这一决定不仅让他损失一连串先手，也把长斜线的控制权交给白方。

text: **18. Bb2 Bb7 19. d5 c4 20. bxc4 bxc4 21. Bxe4 Rxe4 22. Ng5 Re7 23. Qh5 h6 24. Nf5! Rxe1+ 25. Rxe1 hxg5**
zh: **18. Bb2 Bb7 19. d5 c4 20. bxc4 bxc4 21. Bxe4 Rxe4 22. Ng5 Re7 23. Qh5 h6 24. Nf5! Rxe1+ 25. Rxe1 hxg5**

text: 25... g6 fails against 26. Qxh6! Bxh6 27. Nxh6+ Kf8 28. Nh7#. If 25... c3, White wins by 26. Re7! cxb2 27. Nxh6+.¹
zh: 25... g6挡不住26. Qxh6! Bxh6 27. Nxh6+ Kf8 28. Nh7#。若25... c3，白方26. Re7! cxb2 27. Nxh6+获胜。¹

text: There was a threat of 27. Rh3 f6 28. Qg6, etc. If 26... f6, then 27. Qg6! (not 27. Bxf6 because of 27... Qf7!) 27... g4 28. Nh6+ Kh8 29. Nxg4, etc. If 26... g4, then 27. Nh6+ gxh6 28. Qxg4+ with mate in three moves.
zh: 白方原来威胁27. Rh3 f6 28. Qg6等。若26... f6，则27. Qg6!（不能27. Bxf6，因为27... Qf7!）27... g4 28. Nh6+ Kh8 29. Nxg4等。若26... g4，则27. Nh6+ gxh6 28. Qxg4+，三步杀。

text: For 28... Bf8 is answered by 29. Rxf8+ and 30. Qh8#.
zh: 因为28... Bf8会被29. Rxf8+接30. Qh8#应对。

text: ¹ After 26. Re7, Black has the surprising defence 26... Bxd5!, when 27. Rxc7 cxb2 28. Qd1 Bxa2 promotes the pawn. Therefore, 26. Ne7+ Qxe7 27. Rxe7 Bxd5 28. Nxf7! is better, when White should win.
zh: ¹ 纳恩注：26. Re7后，黑方有意外的防守26... Bxd5!，若27. Rxc7 cxb2 28. Qd1 Bxa2，兵便升变。因此较好的是26. Ne7+ Qxe7 27. Rxe7 Bxd5 28. Nxf7!，白方应能获胜。

text: 8 Pieces and pawns in the attack on the castled king
zh: 第八章　攻击易位王时的棋子与兵

text: Our examination of the attack on the castled king has so far (in chapters 4-7) been mainly directed towards the spatial aspect of the attack, and it is now time to examine the parts played by particular pieces and the significance of material sacrifices. Some of these points have already been touched on, so in this chapter we shall concern ourselves only with certain themes where the material aspect is paramount and which have not yet been fully dealt with.
zh: 到目前为止，我们在第四至第七章研究攻击易位王，主要着眼于进攻的空间方面。现在该考察各个棋子的作用，以及弃子的意义了。有些问题前面已经涉及，所以本章只讨论那些以子力因素为主、尚未充分论述的主题。

text: The queen in the attack on the castled king
zh: 后在攻击易位王时的作用

text: The queen is undoubtedly the most important piece in the attack on the castled king, and indeed without it such an attack rarely comes into consideration. Admittedly, it is not impossible to undertake a direct attack without the queen, but the necessary conditions for it cannot easily be created.
zh: 后无疑是攻击易位王时最重要的棋子。实际上，没有后时，这种进攻很少进入考虑范围。诚然，无后也并非不能发动直接进攻，但所需条件不易创造。

text: The queen's great mobility, its main characteristic, is a useful factor in the attack on the castled king, but its effectiveness at short range is even more striking. If it is in occupation of the focal-point g7, the enemy king on g8 has every square taken from it; moreover, if it is protected on that focal-point and the focal-point itself has been cleared of the influence of the opposing pieces, then the king is mated. The queen is, as it were, 'made for focal-points', and particularly for play on compound focal-points. Therefore, the queen's chief strategy in an attack on the castled king consists in playing on the focal-points and discovering ways in which to attack as effectively as possible at close range. Thus the queen, which in an endgame on an open board feels such an aversion towards the opponent's king that it will not allow it nearer than two paces away, is filled in attack with some kind of dark desire and dreams only of how it can steal into the castled dwelling and there fold the king in a close and deadly embrace.
zh: 后机动性极强，这是它的主要特点，在攻击易位王时很有用；但它近距离作战的效力更加突出。如果后占据g7焦点，g8敌王的所有格子都会被剥夺；若后在该焦点受到保护，而且焦点本身已排除敌子的影响，王就被将杀了。可以说，后是“为焦点而生”的，尤其适合在复合焦点上行动。因此，后攻击易位王的主要战略，是围绕焦点运作，寻找最有效的近身攻击办法。后在空旷棋盘的残局中，对敌王如此嫌恶，总要让它保持两格之遥；进攻时却充满某种幽暗欲望，一心梦想潜入王城，把王紧紧抱住，给予致命的拥抱。

text: The reverse side of the queen's positive characteristics is its great material value; this means that the queen is not lightly sacrificed and is not as a rule given up for smaller gains, such as preventing castling or clearing a focal-point. However, there are a number of different kinds of queen sacrifice which occur in the attack on the castled king; these can be reduced in the main to two fairly sharply differentiated types: the case where the sacrifice forces mate, 'check upon check', as it were, and the case where it produces a great positional weakness on the opposing side.
zh: 后这些优点的另一面，是它极高的子力价值。因此不能轻易弃后，通常也不会为了阻止易位、清理一个焦点等较小收益而弃后。不过，攻击易位王时仍有多种弃后，大致可以归为区别鲜明的两类：一类通过接连不断的将军，强制将杀；另一类则在对方局面中造成巨大的弱点。

text: There are also unusual and curious queen sacrifices; we shall give three examples as variations on this theme, ranging over a period of 40 years.
zh: 也有一些不寻常而奇妙的弃后。下面给出三个围绕这一主题的变奏，年代跨度达四十年。
caption_zh: 福克斯—鲍尔，华盛顿，1901年；白先。

text: In this position, from the game Fox-Bauer, Washington 1901, White, to move, set his opponent a trap.
zh: 此局面出自福克斯—鲍尔，华盛顿，1901年。轮白方走，他给对手设了个陷阱。

text: **1. Ndc4 dxc4?**
zh: **1. Ndc4 dxc4?**

text: Black in his greed accepted the sacrifice, which he should have refused.
zh: 黑方贪心接受了本应拒绝的弃子。

text: A correct sacrifice of the queen, which forces the opening of either the h-file or the a2-g8 diagonal.
zh: 正确的弃后，强制打开h线或a2-g8斜线。

text: Or 2... fxg6 3. Bxc4+ Kf8 4. Nxg6+ and 5. Rh8#.
zh: 或2... fxg6 3. Bxc4+ Kf8 4. Nxg6+，接5. Rh8#。

text: **3. Nxg6 fxg6 4. Bxc4+ Kf8 5. Rh8#**
zh: **3. Nxg6 fxg6 4. Bxc4+ Kf8 5. Rh8#**
caption_zh: 列维茨基—马歇尔，布雷斯劳，1912年；黑先。

text: A position from the game Lewitzky-Marshall, Breslau 1912. Marshall won renown in the following way:
zh: 此局面出自列维茨基—马歇尔，布雷斯劳，1912年。马歇尔以下列方式赢得盛誉：

text: White saw that 3. gxh3 would not do because of 3... Nf3+ and intended, on 3... Qa3, to play 4. Rc7, etc.¹
zh: 白方看出3. gxh3不行，因为有3... Nf3+；他打算如3... Qa3，就4. Rc7等。¹

text: However, Black took him by surprise with:
zh: 然而，黑方出人意料地走出：

text: 4. hxg3 Ne2# and 4. fxg3 Ne2+ 5. Kh1 Rxf1# fail at once, while after 4. Qxg3 Ne2+ 5. Kh1 Nxg3+ 6. Kg1 Nxf1 7. gxh3 Nd2 White is left a knight down.
zh: 4. hxg3 Ne2#和4. fxg3 Ne2+ 5. Kh1 Rxf1#都会立即被杀；而4. Qxg3 Ne2+ 5. Kh1 Nxg3+ 6. Kg1 Nxf1 7. gxh3 Nd2后，白方净少一马。
caption_zh: 阿廖欣—苏皮科，特内里费，1945年，盲棋；白先。

text: This position is from a blindfold game of Alekhine's at Tenerife in 1945 (Alekhine-Supico) and acts as a counterpart to Marshall's combination above. Alekhine, in playing
zh: 此局面出自1945年阿廖欣在特内里费下的一盘盲棋（阿廖欣—苏皮科），恰与上面马歇尔的组合相映成趣。阿廖欣走出

text: forced Black to resign (1-0). If Black does not take the queen but plays instead 1... Rg8, White wins by 2. Qxh7+ and 3. Rh3#; if Black plays 1... hxg6 the rook mates immediately, while if 1... fxg6, then 2. Nxg6+, and again the rook mates on h3.
zh: 迫使黑方认输（1-0）。如果黑方不吃后而改走1... Rg8，白方2. Qxh7+接3. Rh3#获胜；若1... hxg6，车立即将杀；若1... fxg6，则2. Nxg6+，车仍在h3将杀。

text: Lovers of curiosities will have noticed the common square (g6 or g3) on which the queen is sacrificed on all three occasions. The curious side of these examples should not distract one from noticing what is typical in them: in all these cases the attacker has a number of other pieces at his disposal, all in the strongest aggressive positions, while only his queen is somehow 'underemployed'. As a result, it is given the task of breaking up the position by sacrificing itself. The situation is that although the pieces are in very aggressive positions, they cannot settle the issue by themselves since, if they are sacrificed, their aggressive formation also disappears. It is therefore left to a less committed piece to carry out the work of destruction, and in these cases this is none other than the queen. Usually, however, the reverse applies: the other pieces are sacrificed, while the queen reaps the harvest.
zh: 喜欢奇闻的读者会发现，三次弃后都发生在相应的同一个格子g6或g3。但这些例子的奇巧，不应掩盖其中的典型因素：进攻方都有许多其他棋子，全部处于最具攻击力的位置，只有后似乎“用武不足”。因此，它承担了弃掉自身、破坏敌阵的任务。其原因是：其他棋子虽然位置积极，却不能独力解决问题，因为若将它们弃掉，强大的进攻配置也随之消失。于是，破坏工作便留给一枚牵涉较少的棋子，而在这些例子中，它恰恰就是后。不过通常情形正相反：弃掉的是其他棋子，后负责收获成果。

text: ¹ Although even this fails after 4... Ne2+ 5. Kh1 Rxh2+ 6. Kxh2 Qd6+, etc.
zh: ¹ 纳恩注：不过即使这样也不行，因为4... Ne2+ 5. Kh1 Rxh2+ 6. Kxh2 Qd6+等。

text: The heavy pieces in the attack
zh: 进攻中的重子

text: The examples in chapters 4-7 have shown us various kinds of operations on the part of the rook, the bishop, and the knight on lines and focal-points, and no further illustrations of the use of these pieces in an attack on the castled king need be given. Only one special case remains to be dealt with, and that is the attack on the castled king carried out by the heavy pieces (queen and rooks) alone. The main feature of this kind of attack can be summed up as the task of overcoming the clumsiness of the rooks. The attacker must aim to make his own rooks active and force his opponent's into passivity. A rook's mobility depends essentially on its ability to switch its control suddenly from one file to another and, in particular, from a file to a rank. Or, in the terminology used in my Introduction to chess (2nd ed., p. 171), the rook must have corresponding strong squares at its disposal. Here are a few examples:
zh: 第四至第七章的实例，已展示车、象、马在各种线路和焦点上的行动，无须再举例说明它们在攻击易位王时的运用。现在只剩一种特殊情况：单用重子，即后和车，攻击易位王。这类进攻的主要特点，可以概括为克服车的笨拙。进攻方应设法活跃自己的车，迫使对方的车陷于被动。车的机动性，根本上取决于它能否把控制突然从一条直线转到另一条，尤其从直线转到横线。用我在《国际象棋入门》第二版第171页的术语来说，就是车必须拥有可用的对应强格。以下是几个例子：
caption_zh: 温特—卡帕布兰卡，拉姆斯盖特，1929年；黑先。

text: This position is from the game Winter-Capablanca, Ramsgate 1929. Black, to move, played:
zh: 此局面出自温特—卡帕布兰卡，拉姆斯盖特，1929年。轮黑方走，他走了：

text: Black threatens 2... g5, which would not have been good at once because of 2. Rg2. White is now obliged to weaken his pawn position by moving his h-pawn.
zh: 黑方威胁2... g5；立即走这步原本不好，因为有2. Rg2。白方现在被迫动h兵，削弱兵形。

text: **2. h4 Rh5 3. Rh2 Rhf5**
zh: **2. h4 Rh5 3. Rh2 Rhf5**

text: After 'feeling about' a little Black reverts to the former position.
zh: 稍作“试探”之后，黑方恢复原先的配置。

text: **4. Rhf2 Qd6 5. Qe3 Qd8 6. Qxe6**
zh: **4. Rhf2 Qd6 5. Qe3 Qd8 6. Qxe6**

text: A disagreeable exchange, but White has nothing better. If 6. Rh2, then 6... Qf6, while if 6. Qg3, then 6... Qf6 followed by ...c5.
zh: 这是不愉快的交换，但白方别无更好选择。若6. Rh2，则6... Qf6；若6. Qg3，则6... Qf6，再...c5。

text: On 7. Qe4, which would have provided better resistance, Black would have replied 7... Qg3+ followed by 8... Qxc3, but not 7... Rg5+? because of 8. fxg5 Qxe4 9. Rxf8+ and White mates.
zh: 7. Qe4抵抗较强，黑方可7... Qg3+再8... Qxc3；但不能7... Rg5+?，因为8. fxg5 Qxe4 9. Rxf8+，白方将杀。

text: It is patently clear that Black's rooks are active and White's passive.
zh: 显而易见，黑车活跃，白车被动。

text: White has no satisfactory defence. If he exchanges queens, he loses a pawn, while if 10. Rg3, then 10... Qh2+ followed by 11... Qxa2.
zh: 白方没有满意的防守。兑后会丢兵；若10. Rg3，则10... Qh2+，再11... Qxa2。

caption_zh: 鲁宾斯坦—阿廖欣，德累斯顿，1926年；黑先。

text: This position is from the game Rubinstein-Alekhine, Dresden 1926.¹ Black played:
zh: 此局面出自鲁宾斯坦—阿廖欣，德累斯顿，1926年。¹黑方走：

text: 2. exf4 is no better, since Black can continue 2... Qh4 with the double threat of 3... Rxg2+ and 3... Qxh3.
zh: 改走2. exf4也不会更好，因为黑方可2... Qh4，同时威胁3... Rxg2+和3... Qxh3。

text: Black compels the king to go to h1 so that he can play ...Qg3 with gain of tempo on the sixth move!
zh: 黑方迫使王去h1，以便在第六步带先手走...Qg3！

text: ¹ In the original book, this position was incorrectly given with Black's bishop on c8 instead of b7. The analysis has been modified to take account of this correction.
zh: ¹ 纳恩注：原版书错误地把黑象放在c8，而非b7。此处已相应修改分析。

text: **4. Kh1 Qg7 5. Qd4 Ba6! 6. Rf2 Qg3! 7. Rc2 Bxf1 8. Rxf1 Rac8**
zh: **4. Kh1 Qg7 5. Qd4 Ba6! 6. Rf2 Qg3! 7. Rc2 Bxf1 8. Rxf1 Rac8**

text: By threatening to break through at c4, Black gains a tempo for doubling rooks. Alekhine now uses his heavy pieces to force home the final attack.
zh: 借助在c4突破的威胁，黑方为叠车赢得一拍。阿廖欣现在用重子完成最后的进攻。
**9. b3 Rc7 10. Re2 Rcg7 11. Rf4 Rg6!（见下图）**
caption_zh: 鲁宾斯坦—阿廖欣；11... Rg6后。

text: Black threatens ...Rh6, ...Rxh3+ and ...Qg1#. If White plays 12. Rf1, the plan of 12... Rh6 followed by sacrificing at h3 is again in order, for the rook on f1 is unprotected; moreover, if it is moved (e.g. to a1) then 13... Rxh3+ still succeeds because the queen can follow up with a decisive check at f3.
zh: 黑方威胁...Rh6、...Rxh3+和...Qg1#。若白方12. Rf1，12... Rh6再在h3弃车的计划仍然成立，因为f1车无根；而若把它移走，例如到a1，13... Rxh3+仍能奏效，因为后可以随后在f3给予决定性将军。

text: In his book, My Best Games of Chess 1924-1937, Alekhine mentions another reply, 12. Qd1, and claims that 12... Rh6 leads to an original zugzwang position; this is not correct (because Black has the strong threat of 13... Qg7 14. Qd4 Rxh3+, etc.), but it is true inasmuch as White's rooks cannot move; they provide a perfect illustration of 'the rook's clumsiness'.
zh: 阿廖欣在《我的最佳对局1924—1937》中提到另一应手12. Qd1，并声称12... Rh6会形成一种别出心裁的楚茨文克局面。这并不准确，因为黑方有很强的威胁13... Qg7 14. Qd4 Rxh3+等；但就白车无法移动而言，这个说法又有道理。它们完美地说明了“车的笨拙”。

text: After 12. Qd1 Rh6 White would have to play 13. Qa1 (not 13. c4 because of 13... d4!), in which case the strongest reply is 13... a6! (creating another threat, i.e. ...b5-b4 followed by ...d4; if 13... Qg7, then 14. c4 is possible). Now White's front e-pawn is lost, but he can still offer some resistance by 14. Rf1. Black, however, must not take the e-pawn while White's queen is on a1; he does better with 14... b5 15. axb5 axb5, after which one can speak of a type of zugzwang position, since White cannot prevent the situation of his pawn on e5 from deteriorating still further. If 16. b4 (or 16. Qd1 or 16. Qe1), Black takes the pawn on e5, after which he should win.
zh: 12. Qd1 Rh6后，白方须13. Qa1（不能13. c4，因为13... d4!），黑方最强应手是13... a6!，制造另一个威胁...b5-b4再...d4；若13... Qg7，白方就可14. c4。现在白方前面的e兵要丢了，但14. Rf1仍能作些抵抗。不过白后在a1时，黑方不应吃e兵，较好的是14... b5 15. axb5 axb5；此后可以说是一种楚茨文克，因为白方无法防止e5兵的处境进一步恶化。若16. b4，或16. Qd1、16. Qe1，黑方吃掉e5兵，应能获胜。

text: In the actual game White gave up a pawn in a different way and lost as follows:
zh: 实战中白方用另一种方式丢兵，随后输棋：

caption_zh: 鲁宾斯坦—阿廖欣；13... Qg7后。

text: Stronger than the prosaic 13... Rxh4+. The black queen retires and at the same time creates the threat of ...Rg6, a typical case of a tripled formation with a rook in front of the queen. The reader should note the mobility of Black's heavy pieces, which allows such rapid and useful regroupings to be made. In the course of the game and its variations up to this point two pairs of corresponding strong squares for Black stand out, namely, g6 and h6 for the rook, and g3 and g7 for the queen.
zh: 比平淡的13... Rxh4+更强。黑后退回，同时制造...Rg6的威胁，是车在后前方、三枚重子叠线的典型配置。读者应注意黑方重子的机动性，正是它使这种迅速而有效的重组成为可能。到这里为止，实战及其变化已显出黑方两对对应强格：车的g6、h6，以及后的g3、g7。

text: After all the different formations on the squares described, here is yet another: the rook now tries out the square g3 and threatens ...Rh3+.
zh: 上述格子上已有那么多种配置，现在又来一种：车来到g3，威胁...Rh3+。

text: If 16. Kg1, Black had planned to play 16... d4! 17. exd4 e3 18. Qc2 Rh3, and White is helpless against 19... Qg3.
zh: 若16. Kg1，黑方计划16... d4! 17. exd4 e3 18. Qc2 Rh3，白方挡不住19... Qg3。

text: Alekhine won the Brilliancy Prize for this game. How light those heavy pieces were in his hands!
zh: 阿廖欣凭本局获得精彩对局奖。重子在他手里显得多么轻盈！

text: After these examples, which are typical of the style of the two world champions, here is a little light entertainment.
zh: 这两个例子典型地体现了两位世界冠军的风格，下面再来一点轻松的娱乐。
caption_zh: 伯恩施坦—科托夫，格罗宁根，1946年；白先。

text: It is the finish of the game Bernstein-Kotov, Groningen 1946. Black, having greedily and needlessly snapped up a pawn (he had just played ...Re4xb4 instead of the correct ...Rc4) lost as follows:
zh: 这是伯恩施坦—科托夫，格罗宁根，1946年一局的结尾。黑方贪心地吃了一兵，其实根本没有必要；他刚走了...Re4xb4，而正确的是...Rc4，随后以如下方式落败：

text: **1. Rcc8 Qe4 2. Rh8+ Kg6 3. f5+ exf5 4. Qxh6+! gxh6 5. Rag8#**
zh: **1. Rcc8 Qe4 2. Rh8+ Kg6 3. f5+ exf5 4. Qxh6+! gxh6 5. Rag8#**

text: The sacrifice in the attack on the castled king
zh: 攻击易位王时的弃子

text: Before we turn to the role of the pawns in the attack on the castled king, a few general remarks must be made about sacrifices in the castling area. Certain combinative elements are present in the case of every sacrifice, though these sacrifices may be of widely diverging types. However, the typical sacrifice in the castling area is the one which is closely influenced by the special characteristics of that area, namely the castled king and the pawns in front of it. The typical sacrifice either changes the structure of the pawns, or aims to draw the king on to a square where it can be attacked, or else helps to create a focal-point. We have already met examples of the last two types in the course of discussing focal-points, particularly in the case of the classic bishop sacrifice. Here our principal interest is the pawn structure and the possibility of altering it by means of a sacrifice. A sacrifice can either simply annihilate one of the pawns in front of the king, or it can deflect the pawn on to another file, or finally it can cause it to be blocked.
zh: 在转入兵的作用之前，须先对王城区域的弃子作几点一般说明。每种弃子都包含某些组合因素，尽管其类型可能相差极大。然而，王城区域的典型弃子，与该区域的特殊性质紧密相关，即易位王及其前方的兵。典型弃子或者改变兵形，或者把王引到可受攻击的格子，或者帮助创造焦点。讨论焦点、尤其古典弃象时，我们已经见过后两类例子。这里主要关注兵形，以及通过弃子改变兵形的可能。弃子可以直接消灭王前的一兵，可以把兵引到另一条直线上，也可以使这个兵被封锁。

text: The main use of the sacrifice in the attack on the castled king is to eliminate the pawns in the castling area, and a number of examples will be devoted to this. But first of all, let us examine two examples where the emphasis is on spoiling the pawn structure by deflecting or blocking the pawns.
zh: 攻击易位王时，弃子的主要用途是消灭王城区域的兵，我们将举若干例子说明。但首先看两个例子，重点在于通过引离或封锁兵来破坏兵形。
caption_zh: 卡帕布兰卡—尼姆佐维奇，巴特基辛根，1928年，分析局面；白先。

text: This position comes from an analysis of the game Capablanca-Nimzowitsch, Bad Kissingen, 1928. White mates as follows:
zh: 此局面出自卡帕布兰卡—尼姆佐维奇，巴特基辛根，1928年一局的分析。白方如下将杀：

text: **1. Nfg5! fxg5**
zh: **1. Nfg5! fxg5**

text: Deflecting the pawn from f6.
zh: 把兵从f6引开。

text: Blocking the f7-pawn.
zh: 封锁f7兵。

text: and Black has no way of stopping mate on h7.
zh: 黑方无法阻止在h7被将杀。

text: White here overcame the resistance of Black's f-pawn on the diagonal b1-h7 by making sacrifices which deflected one pawn and blocked the other.
zh: 白方通过弃子引开一个兵、封锁另一个兵，从而克服了黑方f兵在b1-h7斜线上的抵抗。
caption_zh: 斯坦尼茨—L.保尔森，巴登-巴登，1870年；白先。

text: This position arose in the game Steinitz-L. Paulsen, Baden-Baden 1870. It is White's move, and he is faced with the task of finding the most effective attacking plan against Black's castled position. To this end he played:
zh: 此局面出自斯坦尼茨—L.保尔森，巴登-巴登，1870年。轮白方走，他须找到攻击黑王城的最有效计划。为此他走：

text: White gives up a pawn in order to weaken Black's castled position and open up the a- and b-files. This kind of pawn sacrifice is instructive and typical. Its advantage lies in the fact that Black has no way of blocking the pawn structure but is forced to capture in order to avoid getting into worse difficulties.
zh: 白方弃一兵，削弱黑王城并打开a、b线。这类弃兵既典型，又有启发性。其优点在于，黑方无法封锁兵形，为避免更严重的困难，必须吃兵。

text: The castled position has been effectively weakened and the situation is ripe for the further thrust a5, that being the logical method of following up 1. b6!, but Steinitz sees that, before playing a5, he can strengthen his attack still further by sacrificing the exchange.
zh: 黑王城已被有效削弱，进一步a5冲击的时机成熟，这是1. b6!合乎逻辑的后续。但斯坦尼茨看出，在a5之前，先弃交换能进一步加强攻势。

text: Now the force of this move is even greater than before.
zh: 现在这步的力量比先前更大。

text: If 5... b5, then 6. a6 b6 (or 6... bxa6 7. Qa5 Qxd4+ 8. Bf2) 7. a7+ Kb7 8. Nxc7 Kxc7 (or 8... f5 9. Ne6) 9. Qc3+ Kb7 10. Bd7 with a decisive attack.
zh: 若5... b5，则6. a6 b6（或6... bxa6 7. Qa5 Qxd4+ 8. Bf2）7. a7+ Kb7 8. Nxc7 Kxc7（或8... f5 9. Ne6）9. Qc3+ Kb7 10. Bd7，攻势决定胜负。

text: If 5... c5, then White plays 6. axb6 Qxd4+ 7. Qxd4 cxd4 8. Nc7 followed by 9. Ra8#.
zh: 若5... c5，白方6. axb6 Qxd4+ 7. Qxd4 cxd4 8. Nc7，接9. Ra8#。

text: **6. axb6 cxb6 7. Nxb6 Ne7**
zh: **6. axb6 cxb6 7. Nxb6 Ne7**

text: Black must parry the threat of 8. Qc3.
zh: 黑方须应对8. Qc3的威胁。

text: Or 9... Qxf6 10. Qc3 Nc6 11. Ra8+ Kc7 12. Nd5#.
**10. c4 Na7 11. Qa2 Nb5 12. Nd5** and White won after **12... Qxd5 13. cxd5 Nxd4 14. Qa7+ Kc7 15. Rc1+ Nc6 16. Rxc6#**.
zh: **10. c4 Na7 11. Qa2 Nb5 12. Nd5**，白方在**12... Qxd5 13. cxd5 Nxd4 14. Qa7+ Kc7 15. Rc1+ Nc6 16. Rxc6#**后获胜。

text: One further remark must be made before passing on to the destructive sacrifice: a sacrifice and the operations following it must have the aim of creating a focal-point, especially if the opponent has some active counterplay at his disposal. The next diagram shows an example where the attacker wrecks his opponent's castled position and regains the material he has sacrificed, but is still unsuccessful because he cannot create a focal-point.
zh: 讨论破坏性弃子之前，还须补充一点：弃子及其后续行动，必须以创造焦点为目标，尤其当对手拥有积极反击时。下图中，进攻方摧毁了对方王城，也收回了所弃子力，却仍未成功，原因就是没能创造焦点。
caption_zh: 科勒—塔塔科维尔，宁多夫，1927年；白先。

text: This position is from the game Colle-Tartakower, Niendorf 1927. White is excellently placed here and ought to continue with 1. Nh3, but Colle, the lover of sacrifices, cannot resist the temptation and offers material in a position which is still insufficiently prepared.
zh: 此局面出自科勒—塔塔科维尔，宁多夫，1927年。白方配置极佳，应续1. Nh3。但酷爱弃子的科勒抵挡不住诱惑，在准备尚不充分的局面中献出了子力。

text: **1. Nexf7? Rxf7 2. Nxe6 Qc8 3. Bg6 Nf8 4. Bxf7+ Kxf7 5. Nxg7**
zh: **1. Nexf7? Rxf7 2. Nxe6 Qc8 3. Bg6 Nf8 4. Bxf7+ Kxf7 5. Nxg7**

text: All these captures have been made on different squares, none of which qualifies as a candidate for a focal-point. No wonder that Black develops a counterattack that ensures sufficient counterplay.
zh: 这些吃子发生在不同格子上，没有一格适合成为焦点。因此黑方展开反攻、得到充分反击，就不足为奇了。

text: **5... Ba6 6. c4 Qg4 7. Qxg4 Nxg4 8. Nf5 Bxc4 9. Rd1 h5**
zh: **5... Ba6 6. c4 Qg4 7. Qxg4 Nxg4 8. Nf5 Bxc4 9. Rd1 h5**

text: The position is balanced and the game ended in a draw after a further 17 moves.
zh: 局面均势，又过十七步成和。

text: The destructive sacrifice
zh: 破坏性弃子

text: We have already referred to the annihilation of the pawns in front of the castled king as the most important or at any rate predominant result of sacrificial operations. It would be more exact to say that the destruction of these pawns is the most common combinative element of sacrifices in the castling area. Most players tend to pay more attention to the material aspect than to the temporal one, but the most decisive consequence of the destruction of pawns is that the departed pawns can no longer affect the game. This is a permanent positional factor by means of which many combinations are sustained, even when all may not have been in order on the temporal side. It is very important to spot the opportunities for making a destructive sacrifice, and in many positions the attacker is shown the way by simply calculating what would happen if his opponent were not to have a certain pawn.
zh: 前面已经说过，消灭易位王前的兵，是弃子行动最重要、至少也是最主要的结果。更准确地说，消灭这些兵，是王城区域弃子中最常见的组合因素。多数棋手较重视子力因素，较少注意时间因素；但消灭兵最关键的后果，在于消失的兵再也不能影响棋局。这是一种永久的局面棋因素，即使时间方面未必一切妥当，许多组合仍能靠它成立。发现破坏性弃子的机会十分重要；在许多局面中，进攻者只须计算：如果对方少了某一个兵，会发生什么？答案便能指明方向。

text: We shall look at a number of examples which illustrate typical destructive sacrifices.
zh: 下面看几个典型的破坏性弃子实例。
caption_zh: 洛伊德—德尔马，1879年对抗赛；黑先。

text: This position arose in a match game between Loyd and Delmar in 1879. It is Black's move, and he must act quickly if White is not to break through by b6 or Rxa7. Various attempts like ...Rg5+ or ...Rh5 meet with resistance, and only the immediate capture of the pawn at h2 ensures mate.
zh: 此局面出自洛伊德与德尔马1879年的一盘对抗赛。轮黑方走，他必须迅速行动，否则白方就以b6或Rxa7突破。...Rg5+或...Rh5等尝试都会遇到抵抗，只有立即吃掉h2兵才能确保将杀。

text: **1... Bxh2+! 2. Nxh2 Rg5+ 3. Ng4 Rh5 4. Nh2 Qxh2+ 5. Kf1 Re5** and mate by ...Qh1# is unavoidable.
zh: **1... Bxh2+! 2. Nxh2 Rg5+ 3. Ng4 Rh5 4. Nh2 Qxh2+ 5. Kf1 Re5**，...Qh1#已无法避免。

text: The destructive sacrifice on g7 (or g2) is particularly dangerous, and we shall examine one out of the rich collection of this type.
zh: g7或g2上的破坏性弃子尤其危险。此类实例极多，我们选一个来研究。
caption_zh: 舒莫夫—耶尼施，圣彼得堡，1849年；黑先。

text: This position arose in the game Shumov-Jaenisch, St. Petersburg 1849. Black, to move, concluded the game as follows:
zh: 此局面出自舒莫夫—耶尼施，圣彼得堡，1849年。轮黑方走，他如下结束战斗：

text: **1... Rxg2+ 2. Kxg2 Qg6+ 3. Kh1 Bd5+ 4. f3 Bxf3+ 5. Rxf3 Qg1#**
zh: **1... Rxg2+ 2. Kxg2 Qg6+ 3. Kh1 Bd5+ 4. f3 Bxf3+ 5. Rxf3 Qg1#**

text: We shall now go on to look at cases of successive sacrifices, whereby two of the pawns in front of the castled king are eliminated. It is often easy to spot sacrifices of this kind if the position is looked at in the light of our thematic criterion: what would the situation be if the pawns were not there? Let us take the next diagram, for example.
zh: 现在来看连续弃子、消灭易位王前两个兵的情况。若按本节的主题性判据来观察——这些兵如果不存在，局面会怎样？——往往很容易发现此类弃子。以下图为例。
caption_zh: 凯勒—罗哈切克，维也纳，1937年；白先。

text: In this position, from the game Keller-Rohaczek, Vienna 1937, it is White's move, and he has an easy task if he imagines Black's position without the pawns on h7 and g7 and realizes that White then mates with his queen on h5 and rook on g1. The operation is then extremely simple.
zh: 此局面出自凯勒—罗哈切克，维也纳，1937年。轮白方走；如果想象黑方没有h7、g7双兵，并意识到白后在h5、车在g1即可将杀，任务就很容易了。行动也极为简单。

text: **1. Bxh7 Kxh7 2. Qh5+ Kg8 3. Rxg7+ Kxg7 4. Rg1+** and mates.
zh: **1. Bxh7 Kxh7 2. Qh5+ Kg8 3. Rxg7+ Kxg7 4. Rg1+**，接着将杀。
caption_zh: 卢普雷希特—舒尔茨，美国通信赛，1946年；白先。

text: This position is from a correspondence game between Luprecht and Schulz played in the United States in 1946. Here it is a question of removing Black's pawns on a7 and b7 from in front of the king. If these pawns did not exist, a build-up with a rook on b1 and a queen on e3 would give White an irresistible mating attack. The solution is therefore simple.
zh: 此局面出自卢普雷希特与舒尔茨1946年在美国进行的一盘通信棋。问题是清除黑王前的a7、b7双兵。如果它们不存在，白车在b1、后在e3的配置就能产生无法抵挡的将杀进攻。因此解法很简单。

text: First, the queen is brought nearer with gain of tempo and then the second pawn is annihilated.
zh: 先带先手把后调近，再消灭第二个兵。

text: Or 4... Kc8 5. Qa7, when either the queen mates at b7 or the rook at b8. Mate is also inevitable after 4... Ka8 5. Qb6.
zh: 或4... Kc8 5. Qa7，随后要么后在b7将杀，要么车在b8将杀。4... Ka8 5. Qb6后，将杀也不可避免。

caption_zh: 利林塔尔—纳道尔夫，萨尔特舍巴登区际赛，1948年；白先。

text: A more complex instance of a double destructive sacrifice is provided by the finish to the game Lilienthal-Najdorf, which was awarded the First Brilliancy Prize at the Saltsjöbaden Interzonal tournament in 1948. In the above position, White continued:
zh: 利林塔尔—纳道尔夫一局的结尾，是双重破坏性弃子的一个更复杂实例。这盘棋获得1948年萨尔特舍巴登区际赛的第一精彩对局奖。在上图中白方续走：

text: This eliminates the pawn on g7 (in this case the sacrifice does not take place on that square but indirectly at f4). Black accepts the sacrifice in order not to be left a pawn down.
zh: 消灭g7兵。在这里，弃子并不直接发生在g7，而是间接发生在f4。黑方为了避免少兵，接受弃子。

text: **1... Rxf4 2. Nxf4 exf4 3. Bxh7+!**
zh: **1... Rxf4 2. Nxf4 exf4 3. Bxh7+!**

text: Eliminating the pawn on h7 as well — by a direct sacrifice. Beyond that, in fact, there is no mate in sight. However, Black's weakness on the second rank and the power of the manoeuvre Rad1-d7, by which it must be exploited, are evident.
zh: 再以直接弃象消灭h7兵。事实上，往后还看不到将杀。但黑方第二横线的弱点，以及利用它的Rad1-d7调动的力量，已经十分明显。
**3... Kxh7 4. Qh5+ Kxg7 5. Rad1（见下图）**
caption_zh: 利林塔尔—纳道尔夫；5. Rad1后。

text: Black has three minor pieces for a rook and two pawns, but his knights are badly placed, whereas the position is just right for White's rooks.
zh: 黑方以三个轻子对车与双兵，但双马位置恶劣，白方双车却恰好如鱼得水。

text: With 5... Qf6, Black attempts to lessen the force of the attack by returning some material, but he is unsuccessful because his knights continue to find themselves on awkward squares. Other lines were no better, e.g.:
zh: 5... Qf6试图交还一些子力，减弱攻势，但未能成功，因为黑马仍然位置尴尬。其他变化也不好，例如：

text:
1) 5... Nd4 6. cxd4 cxd4 7. Rfe1! Nf6 8. Qe5 Kf7 9. Rxd4 and White wins.
2) 5... Nd6 6. Qg4+ Kf7 7. Rfe1 Bc8 8. Qxf4+ also wins.
3) 5... Qc8 (if 5... Qe7, then 6. Rfe1, while if 5... Qc7, then 6. Qg4+ and 7. Rd7) 6. Rfe1 Nf6 7. Qg5+ Kf7 8. Rd6 Qh8 9. Ree6 is also decisive.
zh:
1）5... Nd4 6. cxd4 cxd4 7. Rfe1! Nf6 8. Qe5 Kf7 9. Rxd4，白胜。
2）5... Nd6 6. Qg4+ Kf7 7. Rfe1 Bc8 8. Qxf4+也获胜。
3）5... Qc8（若5... Qe7，则6. Rfe1；若5... Qc7，则6. Qg4+再7. Rd7）6. Rfe1 Nf6 7. Qg5+ Kf7 8. Rd6 Qh8 9. Ree6，同样决定胜负。

text: **6. Rd7+ Kf8 7. Rxb7 Nd8**
zh: **6. Rd7+ Kf8 7. Rxb7 Nd8**

text: Or 7... Nd6 8. Rh7 Nf7 9. Rxf7+ Qxf7 10. Qh8+ Qg8 11. Qf6+ followed by 12. Qxc6 and White wins.
zh: 或7... Nd6 8. Rh7 Nf7 9. Rxf7+ Qxf7 10. Qh8+ Qg8 11. Qf6+，接12. Qxc6，白胜。

text: If 11... Ng5, then 12. h4 Nh3+ 13. gxh3 Qg6+ 14. Qg5 is decisive.
zh: 若11... Ng5，则12. h4 Nh3+ 13. gxh3 Qg6+ 14. Qg5决定胜负。

text: Of the various sacrificial devices to eliminate two pawns in front of the castled king, the sacrifice of both bishops on h7 and g7 is particularly worth noting. One of the oldest examples of this occurred in the game Lasker-Bauer, Amsterdam 1889. The opening moves were:
zh: 在消灭易位王前两个兵的各种弃子手段中，h7、g7上的双象弃子尤其值得注意。最早的实例之一，出现在拉斯克—鲍尔，阿姆斯特丹，1889年。开局着法如下：

text: **1. f4 d5 2. e3 Nf6 3. b3 e6 4. Bb2 Be7 5. Bd3 b6 6. Nc3 Bb7 7. Nf3 Nbd7 8. O-O O-O 9. Ne2 c5 10. Ng3 Qc7 11. Ne5 Nxe5 12. Bxe5 Qc6 13. Qe2 a6? (D)**
zh: **1. f4 d5 2. e3 Nf6 3. b3 e6 4. Bb2 Be7 5. Bd3 b6 6. Nc3 Bb7 7. Nf3 Nbd7 8. O-O O-O 9. Ne2 c5 10. Ng3 Qc7 11. Ne5 Nxe5 12. Bxe5 Qc6 13. Qe2 a6?（见下图）**
caption_zh: 拉斯克—鲍尔；13... a6后。

text: In this position, after Black's mistaken last move, Lasker worked out a combination which involved the sacrifice of both bishops; to this end he first of all forced the deflection of Black's knight.
zh: 黑方上一步出错后，拉斯克在此局面中算出了一个双象弃子的组合；为此，他首先强制引离黑马。

text: 14... c4 also results in a quick finish, e.g. 15. Nxf6+ Bxf6 (or 15... gxf6 16. Qg4+ Kh8 17. Qh4 cxd3 18. Bxf6+ Bxf6 19. Qxf6+ followed by Rf3-g3, etc.) 16. Bxh7+ Kxh7 17. Qh5+ Kg8 18. Bxf6 gxf6 19. Rf3 with a quick mate.
