zh: 14... c4也会很快结束，例如15. Nxf6+ Bxf6（或15... gxf6 16. Qg4+ Kh8 17. Qh4 cxd3 18. Bxf6+ Bxf6 19. Qxf6+，再Rf3-g3等）16. Bxh7+ Kxh7 17. Qh5+ Kg8 18. Bxf6 gxf6 19. Rf3，很快将杀。
**15. Bxh7+! Kxh7 16. Qxh5+ Kg8 17. Bxg7!（见下图）**
caption_zh: 拉斯克—鲍尔；17. Bxg7后。

text: The dark-squared bishop gives itself up just like its colleague on the light squares, and it is left to White's queen and rook to make use of the files thereby opened. If now 17... f6, then 18. Rf3 wins.
zh: 黑格象也像白格象一样献身，接下来由白后与车利用由此打开的直线。若此时17... f6，则18. Rf3获胜。

text: To prolong the game by sacrificing his queen; clearly, there is no other possibility.
zh: 打算弃后拖延战斗；显然已经没有其他办法。

text: **20. Rh3+ Qh6 21. Rxh6+ Kxh6 22. Qd7 Bf6 23. Qxb7** and White won the game in a few moves.
zh: **20. Rh3+ Qh6 21. Rxh6+ Kxh6 22. Qd7 Bf6 23. Qxb7**，白方几步后获胜。

text: Here are two more examples of this type.
zh: 再看两个同类例子。

text:
Nimzowitsch – Tarrasch
Preliminary event, St Petersburg 1914
Queen's Gambit Declined, Tarrasch Defence
zh:
尼姆佐维奇—塔拉什
圣彼得堡赛预赛，1914年
后翼弃兵拒弃兵变例，塔拉什防御

text: Correct here is 5. cxd5.
zh: 这里正确的是5. cxd5。

text: **5... Nc6 6. O-O Bd6 7. b3 O-O 8. Bb2 b6 9. Nbd2 Bb7 10. Rc1 Qe7 11. cxd5 exd5 12. Nh4 g6 13. Nhf3 Rad8 14. dxc5?**
zh: **5... Nc6 6. O-O Bd6 7. b3 O-O 8. Bb2 b6 9. Nbd2 Bb7 10. Rc1 Qe7 11. cxd5 exd5 12. Nh4 g6 13. Nhf3 Rad8 14. dxc5?**

text: Better is 14. Re1 and then Nf1.
zh: 较好的是14. Re1，再Nf1。

text: **14... bxc5 15. Bb5 Ne4 16. Bxc6 Bxc6 17. Qc2 Nxd2! 18. Nxd2 d4 19. exd4 (D)**
zh: **14... bxc5 15. Bb5 Ne4 16. Bxc6 Bxc6 17. Qc2 Nxd2! 18. Nxd2 d4 19. exd4（见下图）**
caption_zh: 尼姆佐维奇—塔拉什；19. exd4后。

text: The beginning of the sacrificial combination.
zh: 弃子组合的开始。

text: If White accepts the second sacrifice by 22. Kxg2, then 22... Qg4+ 23. Kh2 Rd5 is decisive.
zh: 若白方22. Kxg2接受第二次弃子，则22... Qg4+ 23. Kh2 Rd5决定胜负。

text: For if 32. Kd7, then 32... Bb5#.

Alekhine – Drewitt
Portsmouth, 1923
Sokolsky Opening
zh:
阿廖欣—德鲁伊特
朴次茅斯，1923年
索科尔斯基开局

text: **1. Nf3 d5 2. b4 e6 3. Bb2 Nf6 4. a3 c5 5. bxc5 Bxc5 6. e3 O-O 7. c4 Nc6 8. d4 Bb6 9. Nbd2 Qe7 10. Bd3 Rd8 11. O-O Bd7 12. Ne5! Be8 13. f4 Rac8 14. Rc1 Nd7 15. Nxc6 Rxc6 16. c5 Nxc5 17. dxc5 Bxc5 18. Rf3 Bxa3? 19. Rxc6 Bxc6 (D)**
zh: **1. Nf3 d5 2. b4 e6 3. Bb2 Nf6 4. a3 c5 5. bxc5 Bxc5 6. e3 O-O 7. c4 Nc6 8. d4 Bb6 9. Nbd2 Qe7 10. Bd3 Rd8 11. O-O Bd7 12. Ne5! Be8 13. f4 Rac8 14. Rc1 Nd7 15. Nxc6 Rxc6 16. c5 Nxc5 17. dxc5 Bxc5 18. Rf3 Bxa3? 19. Rxc6 Bxc6（见下图）**
caption_zh: 阿廖欣—德鲁伊特；19... Bxc6后。

text: The beginning of a well-prepared combination involving two bishop sacrifices.
zh: 准备充分的双象弃子组合由此开始。

text: If 22... Kxg7, then 23. Qg4+ and mate, while after 22... f6 23. Bh6 Kf7 24. Qh5+ Black's king cannot extricate itself from the mating net.
zh: 若22... Kxg7，则23. Qg4+，接着将杀；若22... f6 23. Bh6 Kf7 24. Qh5+，黑王也无法逃出杀网。

text: The pawns in the attack on the castled king
zh: 兵在攻击易位王时的作用

text: These examples of destructive sacrifices have shown us a procedure for dealing with the opponent's pawns, and now we shall examine the part played by the attacker's pawns in the attack on the castled king. The part is a very varied one, reflecting, as it does, the rich possibilities inherent in the pawn's movements. The pawns are, above all, the pieces which cost one the least to sacrifice in one's efforts to weaken the enemy position; they are also excellent at harrying one's opponent's pieces as well as helping to support one's own on focal-points or strong squares. In all these cases the positive characteristics of the pawn are to the fore. The other side to the use of pawns in an attack on the castled king is a logical consequence of their negative characteristics, namely their limited mobility and the impossibility of reversing their moves. The attacker's pawn needs, on average, three moves before it can have a direct effect on the opposing castling area itself; also, the attacker cannot transfer it from one file to another at will, but only when opposing units are so placed as to come into its line of fire. Equally inconvenient is the other aspect of the pawn's negative characteristics: in advancing, it weakens the squares which it leaves behind it, and if the attack does not succeed, serious positional weaknesses may become evident in the attacker's position. The irreversibility of pawn moves may also lead to a general blockade, which in turn produces a rigid position and complicates the attack. However, the pawn still has one more positive characteristic which can on some occasions help the attacker: the promotion of the pawn into a piece on the opponent's back rank may be the attacker's last trump at the critical stage of an attack.
zh: 这些破坏性弃子的例子，展示了处理敌兵的一种办法。现在我们来考察进攻方自己的兵在攻击易位王时所起的作用。兵的作用非常多样，反映了兵步本身所蕴含的丰富可能。首先，为了削弱敌阵而弃兵，代价最小；兵也很善于驱赶敌子，并协助支持己方棋子占据焦点或强格。这些都体现了兵的优点。使用兵进攻的另一面，则合乎逻辑地来自兵的缺点：机动性有限，而且不能后退。进攻方的兵通常平均要走三步，才能直接影响敌方王城；进攻者也不能随意把它从一条直线调到另一条，只能在敌子恰好进入其攻击范围时通过吃子转线。兵的另一个缺点同样不便：向前推进会削弱身后的格子；若进攻失败，进攻方局面中就可能显露严重弱点。兵步不可逆，还可能导致全面封锁，使局面僵硬，增加进攻难度。不过兵另有一种优点，有时能够帮助进攻者：在敌方底线升变成子，可能成为进攻关键阶段的最后王牌。

text: Thus all the different aspects of the pawn's special characteristics find their expression in an attack on the castled king, and the picture becomes still more varied when we fill in the spatial side of pawn operations in this kind of attack. Here is a brief summary of a pawn's role in the attack on the castled king.
zh: 因此，兵的各种特性都会在攻击易位王时体现出来；再加上此类进攻中兵行动的空间因素，情形就更加多样。下面简要归纳兵的作用。

text:
1) The attacker's pawn (with or without a sacrifice) forces the opponent to weaken his castled position.
2) It serves to create combinative elements in attack (e.g. by deflecting or attracting the opponent's pieces or opening up files).
3) It forms part of an attacking formation (e.g. in the formation with a rook on h1 and a pawn on h4 or as a support to a piece on a focal-point).
4) A particular example of such an attacking formation which should be mentioned is the pawn centre; as a rule, this serves either generally to confine the opponent or to provide the basis for an attack on the castled king.
5) The pawn advances independently on the flank in order to drive an enemy piece away or to take control of a square. An advance of this kind is usually called a bayonet attack.
6) Two or three attacking wing pawns advance against the opponent's castled position in a frontal formation (a pawn avalanche or roller).
7) The pawn moves up into the castling area as a straightforward attacking unit against the enemy king.
8) The pawn advances into the castling area (with or without an attack on the king) in order to be promoted, after which it can carry on the attack in its new role.
zh:
1）进攻方的兵，无论是否弃掉，迫使对手削弱王城。
2）制造进攻中的组合因素，例如引离或引入敌子，或开放直线。
3）组成攻击配置的一部分，例如h1车、h4兵的配置，或支持焦点上的棋子。
4）这种攻击配置中，一个值得单列的例子是兵中心；它通常总体限制对手，或为攻击易位王提供基础。
5）兵在侧翼独立推进，驱赶敌子或控制某格。这通常称为刺刀进攻。
6）两三个侧翼进攻兵组成正面阵列，向敌王城推进，即兵的雪崩或滚压。
7）兵进入王城区域，直接作为攻击单位对付敌王。
8）兵进入王城区域，争取升变；这一过程可以伴随对王的攻击，也可以没有。升变后，兵便能以新的身份继续进攻。

text: These various types of action are usually interrelated in practical play, and single moves often combine two or more such functions. Indeed, when the process is observed as a whole over the space of a few moves, the continuous transition from one type to another is virtually the rule, except in the case of point 4 (centre pawns). As an example of the kind of progressive changes which can take place in the role of a pawn attack let us look schematically at 'the career of an h-pawn', move by move.
zh: 这些行动类型在实战中通常互相关联，单步着法往往兼有两种以上功能。事实上，如果把几步之内的过程作为整体观察，除第4点中心兵外，从一种类型不断转变为另一种，几乎就是常态。为了说明兵进攻的作用如何逐步变化，我们逐步示意一下“一个h兵的生涯”。

h3：兵前进一步，驱赶g4敌子，可以称作“小刺刀”，参见第5点；
h4：与h1车形成固定配置，第3点；随后g4，便有了正面阵列，第6点；
h5：威胁吃g6敌兵、打开h线，潜在属于第2点；黑方于是...g5封锁，但由此削弱王前兵形，第1点；
h6：支持对g7焦点的进攻，第3点；
h7+：黑方挡住g7威胁，但兵现在转为直接攻击，第7点；
h8=Q：兵升后，继续进攻，第8点。

text: Every chess player will admit that such a career on the part of an h-pawn is in no way exceptional but is, on the contrary, a typical illustration of the many-sidedness of a pawn's role in an attack on the castled king.
zh: 每个棋手都会承认，h兵这样的生涯并非例外；恰恰相反，它典型地展示了兵在攻击易位王时作用的多面性。

text: Examples have already been given of the aspects of a pawn's activity listed under points 1-3 and 7-8, so we shall restrict ourselves in this chapter to a survey of those under points 4-6.
zh: 第1至3点和第7至8点的兵的活动，前面已经有实例，所以本章只讨论第4至6点。

text: The role of the pawn centre
zh: 兵中心的作用

text: The centre pawns have the task of controlling important squares and preventing the opposing forces from using them. As a result the pawn centre is the main weapon in the struggle for an advantage in development and space. However, in addition to the general positional function of restricting the opponent, the pawn centre also acts as a basis for an attack on the castled king. Firstly, the overall restriction imposed on the opponent makes it difficult for him to deploy his pieces and so indirectly assists the attacker's plans; in addition, each of the centre pawns directly controls the outer squares of the castled position. Thus, on e5, the e-pawn controls the important square f6, and on e6, the square f7; a similar control is exercised against the queenside castling position by the d-pawn (the squares c6 and c7).
zh: 中心兵的任务，是控制重要格子，不让敌子使用。因此，兵中心是争夺出子优势和空间优势的主要武器。但除了限制对手这一一般的局面棋作用，兵中心还为攻击易位王提供基础。首先，对对手的整体限制使其难以部署子力，间接帮助进攻者实施计划；其次，每一个中心兵都直接控制王城外围的格子。例如e兵在e5时控制重要的f6，在e6时控制f7；d兵对长易位阵地也发挥类似控制，涉及c6、c7格。

text: We have already seen a number of fine examples of the influence of a centre pawn in an attack on the castled king, and especially the part played by the pawn on e5 in the classic bishop sacrifice. In this section we shall examine the more general situation, where a central formation has the functions both of a restricting agent and also of a direct controller of squares in the castling area. From the profusion of practical examples of this kind we shall take one in which the attacker's centre is particularly dynamic.
zh: 我们已经见过若干精彩例子，说明中心兵对攻击易位王的影响，尤其e5兵在古典弃象中的作用。本节考察更一般的情况：中心兵阵同时承担限制对手和直接控制王城格子的功能。同类实战实例极多，我们选择一个进攻方中心格外富有活力的例子。

text:
Tarrasch – Alekhine
Bad Pistyan, 1922
Blumenfeld Counter-Gambit
zh:
塔拉什—阿廖欣
巴特皮斯蒂安，1922年
布卢门费尔德反弃兵

text: Preparing to accept the gambit offered by Black with 4... b5. Nowadays it is well known that it is not worth accepting this gambit and that it is best to play 5. Bg5, in order to maintain the centre pawn at d5.
zh: 准备接受黑方4... b5的弃兵。到本书写作时，人们已熟知接受这种弃兵并不值得，最好5. Bg5，以保持d5中心兵。

text: Black's great strength in the centre more than compensates for the minus pawn.
zh: 黑方强大的中心，对少一兵提供了充分有余的补偿。

text: **7. e3 Bd6 8. Nc3 O-O 9. Be2 Bb7 10. b3 Nbd7 11. Bb2 Qe7 12. O-O Rad8 13. Qc2 e5 14. Rfe1 (D)**
zh: **7. e3 Bd6 8. Nc3 O-O 9. Be2 Bb7 10. b3 Nbd7 11. Bb2 Qe7 12. O-O Rad8 13. Qc2 e5 14. Rfe1（见下图）**
caption_zh: 塔拉什—阿廖欣；14. Rfe1后。

text: White has no satisfactory defence against the growing threat of ...e4. If 14. e4, the strongest continuation is 14... d4 15. Bc4+ Kh8 16. Nd5 Bxd5 17. Bxd5 Nxd5 18. exd5, after which 18... e4 follows with even greater effect.
zh: 对日益增强的...e4威胁，白方没有满意防守。若14. e4，最强的是14... d4 15. Bc4+ Kh8 16. Nd5 Bxd5 17. Bxd5 Nxd5 18. exd5，随后18... e4的效果更强。

text: Now both aspects of the influence exerted by Black's pawn mass in the centre can be clearly seen: White is restricted, and at the same time the pawn on e4 deprives his knight of the square f3.
zh: 现在黑方中心兵群影响的两个方面都清楚可见：白方受到限制，同时e4兵又剥夺白马的f3格。

text: A laborious defence; this knight has to cover f2, while the other goes to f1 to defend h2.
zh: 艰难的防守：这匹马必须保护f2，另一匹则去f1守h2。

text: This move is aimed against the square g2; Black's plan is to advance the d-pawn and open the long diagonal for the b7-bishop.
zh: 此着针对g2格；黑方计划推进d兵，为b7象打开长斜线。

caption_zh: 塔拉什—阿廖欣；21. Nh2后。

text: Black's central mass makes another vigorous contribution to the attack. The d-pawn now advances to d3, where it controls White's support square e2. If 22. exd4 e3, both 23. fxe3 and 23. Rg1 are answered by 23... Qg3!.
zh: 黑方中心兵群又一次有力地支援进攻。d兵现在要前进到d3，控制白方的支撑格e2。若22. exd4 e3，无论23. fxe3还是23. Rg1，都可23... Qg3!应对。

text: Still better is 22... Ng3+ 23. Kg1 d3, for then 24. Qc4+ can be met without loss of tempo by 24... Bd5.
zh: 更好的是22... Ng3+ 23. Kg1 d3，因为此后24. Qc4+可由24... Bd5不失先手地应对。

text: **23. Qc4+ Kh8 24. Bb2 Ng3+ 25. Kg1 Bd5 26. Qa4 Ne2+ 27. Kh1 Rf7 28. Qa6 h5 29. b6 Ng3+ 30. Kg1 axb6 31. Qxb6 d2 32. Rf1 Nxf1 33. Nxf1 Be6 34. Kh1 Bxh3 35. gxh3 Rf3 36. Ng3 h4 37. Bf6 Qxf6 38. Nxe4 Rxh3+ 0-1.**
zh: **23. Qc4+ Kh8 24. Bb2 Ng3+ 25. Kg1 Bd5 26. Qa4 Ne2+ 27. Kh1 Rf7 28. Qa6 h5 29. b6 Ng3+ 30. Kg1 axb6 31. Qxb6 d2 32. Rf1 Nxf1 33. Nxf1 Be6 34. Kh1 Bxh3 35. gxh3 Rf3 36. Ng3 h4 37. Bf6 Qxf6 38. Nxe4 Rxh3+ 0-1。**

text: It is an irony of fate that the person to experience the might of the centre in this game should have been Tarrasch, a great devotee of the centre and a noted exponent of central pawn strategy. Such drastic examples of an action by the whole central mass in the attack on the castled king will not be found in contemporary master practice. The technique of playing against the centre has been so perfected that one can no longer succeed by the single expedient of following the pattern of the game above. Masters no longer accept gambits like the Blumenfeld; on all occasions they examine the extent of the compensation or the possibility of play against the centre, either by counterattacking it with pawns, or by exerting a restraining pressure on it with their pieces. The central formations which occur nowadays in master chess are not as a rule so uncompromisingly lethal as this one, but instead tend to be critical and sensitive formations, which demand an extremely precise use of the pieces if they are not to become weak and collapse. As a result of this characteristic sensitivity of central formations in the games of present-day masters, the temporal aspect of such actions has also altered, and nowadays one rarely sees a full pawn centre being maintained for many moves; it usually appears as a transitory feature, a phase of the game which is immediately followed either by an attack on the castled king or some other action. The following game provides an illustration of this kind of temporary, flexible centre and of a rapidly developed attack on the castled king.
zh: 命运真会开玩笑：本局亲身体验中心威力的，竟然是中心的忠实拥护者、中心兵战略的著名倡导者塔拉什。在本书写作时代的大师实战中，已经找不到整个中心兵群如此猛烈参与杀王的例子。对抗中心的技术已经十分完善，单纯照搬本局模式，不能再获成功。大师们不再轻易接受布卢门费尔德这类弃兵；他们总会衡量补偿是否充分，以及能否用兵反击中心，或以棋子施压、限制中心。因此，当时大师对局中的中心兵阵，通常不会像本局这样具有毫不妥协的杀伤力，而往往处于关键且敏感的状态；若不极其精确地运用棋子，就会变弱、崩溃。这种敏感性也改变了行动的时间特点：完整兵中心很少维持许多步，通常只是暂时现象，是紧接着攻击易位王或展开其他行动的一个阶段。下一局展示这种暂时而灵活的中心，以及迅速展开的杀王进攻。

text:
Keres – Fine
Ostend, 1937
Queen's Gambit Declined, Semi-Tarrasch Defence
zh:
凯列斯—法因
奥斯坦德，1937年
后翼弃兵拒弃兵变例，半塔拉什防御

text: **1. Nf3 d5 2. d4 Nf6 3. c4 e6 4. Nc3 c5 5. cxd5 Nxd5**
zh: **1. Nf3 d5 2. d4 Nf6 3. c4 e6 4. Nc3 c5 5. cxd5 Nxd5**

text: 5... exd5 would lead into the Tarrasch Defence proper. After the text move, the game develops along independent lines.
zh: 5... exd5会进入正统塔拉什防御。实战着之后，对局沿独立路线发展。

text: **6. e4 Nxc3 7. bxc3 cxd4 8. cxd4 Bb4+**
zh: **6. e4 Nxc3 7. bxc3 cxd4 8. cxd4 Bb4+**

text: Black's dark-squared bishop is exchanged in order to simplify the position further. Each exchange, as a rule, helps to diminish the power of the pawn centre and increases the significance of a queenside majority, which Black has here. Because of this, theory regards this position as approximately equal.
zh: 黑方打算兑换黑格象，进一步简化局面。一般说来，每一次兑换都有助于削弱兵中心的力量，并提高后翼多兵的意义，而黑方在这里恰有后翼多兵。因此，理论认为此局面大致均势。

text: **9. Bd2 Bxd2+ 10. Qxd2 O-O 11. Bc4 Nd7?**
zh: **9. Bd2 Bxd2+ 10. Qxd2 O-O 11. Bc4 Nd7?**

text: This move is considered weak by present-day theory. Better is 11... Nc6 12. O-O b6 13. Rfd1 Bb7.
zh: 本书写作时的理论认为此着软弱。较好的是11... Nc6 12. O-O b6 13. Rfd1 Bb7。

text: **12. O-O b6 13. Rad1 Bb7 14. Rfe1 Rc8 15. Bb3 Nf6**
zh: **12. O-O b6 13. Rad1 Bb7 14. Rfe1 Rc8 15. Bb3 Nf6**

text: An attempt to put pressure on the centre and induce e5, after which Black can play ...Nd5. However, White can leave his pawn on e4 for the time being and first strengthen his position in readiness for an attack on the castled king. The weak side of 15... Nf6 stems precisely from the possibility of gaining a tempo by attacking the knight with e5; without this White would have no advantage. In the very line Black used here to simplify the position (moves 6-9) the exchange of the f6-knight, the piece exposed to attack by e4-e5, is an essential part of Black's whole system; now, however, a knight appears again on f6 and with it the attacking motif e5.
zh: 试图压迫中心，诱使e5，然后...Nd5。但白方可以暂时把兵留在e4，先加强配置，准备攻击易位王。15... Nf6的弱点，恰在于白方可e5攻马、获得一拍；若无这一点，白方就没有优势。黑方在第六至第九步采用的简化路线中，兑掉f6马这一会遭到e4-e5攻击的棋子，是整个体系的重要组成；但现在，f6又出现一匹马，e5攻击构思也随之重现。

text: Even so, 15... Nf6 is not a mistake, for other moves are no better; the bad move has already been made — 11... Nd7?. It is true that the commentator Reinfeld mentions 15... Qf6 in his book on Keres, continuing with 16. e5 Qh6? 17. Qxh6 gxh6, according to the pattern of the game Reshevsky-Fine, Hastings 1937; in that game, however, Black's knight was on c6 and his queen's rook on d8, so that his simplifying manoeuvre was in order. In this position, though, White would continue 18. d5 exd5 19. Bxd5 Bxd5 20. Rxd5 Nc5 21. Rd6, and the pawn on h6 begins to totter, since 21... Kg7 or 21... Ne6 is answered by 22. Nh4 followed by Nf5.
zh: 即便如此，15... Nf6也不是错误，因为别的着法并不好些；坏着早已走出，就是11... Nd7?。评注者赖因费尔德在凯列斯专著中确实提到15... Qf6，并按雷舍夫斯基—法因，黑斯廷斯1937年的模式给出16. e5 Qh6? 17. Qxh6 gxh6。然而在那局棋中，黑马在c6，后车在d8，简化调动是妥当的；而本局白方可18. d5 exd5 19. Bxd5 Bxd5 20. Rxd5 Nc5 21. Rd6，h6兵便摇摇欲坠，因为21... Kg7或21... Ne6都可22. Nh4再Nf5。
**16. Qf4 Qc7 17. Qh4 Rfd8（见下图）**
caption_zh: 凯列斯—法因；17... Rfd8后。

text: White's pawn centre, which has now been standing on the board for a number of moves, provides a typical illustration of the sensitivity of such formations. The crisis has been mounting from move to move, and the question now is whether the time is ripe for e5 or whether the position still needs reinforcing. White cannot wait much longer, since Black has a strong card to play on the queenside, namely ...b5 and ...a5, etc. Keres decides on reinforcement and in doing so makes a mistake. Correct was 18. e5 immediately; reinforcement would perhaps also have worked, but in the shape of 18. Rd3.
zh: 白方的兵中心已经维持数步，典型地体现了这类兵阵的敏感性。危机一步步加深，现在的问题是：e5的时机是否成熟，还是仍须加强配置？白方不能再等太久，因为黑方在后翼有...b5、...a5等强大手段。凯列斯选择加强，却由此犯错。正确的是立即18. e5；加强或许也可行，但应是18. Rd3。

text: After 18. e5 there are two main ways open to Black (lines 3 and 4 below):
zh: 18. e5后，黑方主要有以下第3、第4两种选择：

text:
1) 18... Bxf3? is bad due to 19. exf6, when the threat of 20. Qg5 wins a piece.
2) 18... Ne8 is not good, e.g. 19. Ng5 h6 20. Nxe6 fxe6 21. Bxe6+ Kh7 22. d5 with a large advantage for White.
3) 18... Nd5 19. Ng5 h6 20. Ne4 Nc3 (otherwise 21. Nd6) 21. Nxc3 (21. Nf6+ is probably insufficient in view of 21... Kh8) 21... Qxc3 22. Re3 Qb4 (if 22... Qc6, then 23. Rg3) 23. Rg3 Kh8 24. Qg4 (24. Bc2 is also good) 24... Qf8 25. h4 Rc7 26. f4 Rcd7 (alternatives are 26... g6 27. h5 and 26... Bd5 27. f5) 27. f5 exf5 28. Qxf5 Rxd4 29. Rxd4 Rxd4 30. e6 with advantage to White.
zh:
1）18... Bxf3?不好，因为19. exf6，借20. Qg5的威胁得子。
2）18... Ne8也不好，例如19. Ng5 h6 20. Nxe6 fxe6 21. Bxe6+ Kh7 22. d5，白方大优。
3）18... Nd5 19. Ng5 h6 20. Ne4 Nc3（否则21. Nd6）21. Nxc3（21. Nf6+因21... Kh8恐怕不够）21... Qxc3 22. Re3 Qb4（若22... Qc6，则23. Rg3）23. Rg3 Kh8 24. Qg4（24. Bc2也好）24... Qf8 25. h4 Rc7 26. f4 Rcd7（其他选择是26... g6 27. h5，以及26... Bd5 27. f5）27. f5 exf5 28. Qxf5 Rxd4 29. Rxd4 Rxd4 30. e6，白优。

text: 4) 18... Nd7 19. Ng5 Nf8 20. Re3 h6 21. Nh3 and White has a promising attack.
zh: 4）18... Nd7 19. Ng5 Nf8 20. Re3 h6 21. Nh3，白方攻势可期。

text: 18. Rd3 may be even stronger than the move which we have just examined, for with his rook on d3 White threatens e5 immediately. Thus 18... b5 is answered by 19. e5 and if 19... Nd7, then 20. Ng5 Nf8 21. Nxh7 Nxh7 22. Rh3¹, while if 19... Nd5, then 20. Ng5 h6 21. Ne4 followed by Nd6. After 18. Rd3 Black would have to play 18... h6, in which case 19. e5 Nd5 20. Nd2 gives White the advantage.
zh: 18. Rd3甚至可能比刚才分析的18. e5更强，因为车在d3时，白方立即威胁e5。因此18... b5可应19. e5；若19... Nd7，则20. Ng5 Nf8 21. Nxh7 Nxh7 22. Rh3¹；若19... Nd5，则20. Ng5 h6 21. Ne4，再Nd6。18. Rd3后，黑方须18... h6，此时19. e5 Nd5 20. Nd2，白方占优。

text: ¹ Black can defend by 22... Be4! 23. Qxe4 Ng5, winning the exchange. Thus 21. Rg3 is a better attacking attempt, with an unclear position.
zh: ¹ 纳恩注：黑方可22... Be4! 23. Qxe4 Ng5防守，赢得交换。因此21. Rg3是更好的进攻尝试，局面不明。

text: All these continuations serve to illustrate my thesis on the critical nature of the full pawn centre; objectively, White's success was quite possible, but one imprecise move (18. Re3?) and everything has evaporated, as we shall see.
zh: 所有这些变化都说明我关于完整兵中心处于关键状态的论点：客观上白方完全可能成功，但一步不精确的18. Re3?，便让一切化为乌有。我们马上就会看到。

text: Now e5 is no longer a threat (because of the double attack after 19. e5 Nd5 20. Ng5 h6) and so Black is able to make progress on the queenside.
zh: 现在e5不再是威胁，因为19. e5 Nd5 20. Ng5 h6形成双重攻击，所以黑方能够在后翼取得进展。

caption_zh: 凯列斯—法因；20... b4后。

text: While this is positionally attractive, it allows the initiative to slip out of Black's hands, with the result that White comes back into the game with prospects which are worth a draw at least. Black should have played 20... bxa4 21. Bxa4 h6 when White's attack would have petered out: 22. e5? (22. g4 does not work because of 22... Qf4 while if 22. h3, Black plays 22... Qc4 23. Bb3 Qb4) 22... Nd5 23. Re4 Ne7 24. Rg4 Bxf3 25. gxf3 Nf5 with advantage to Black.
zh: 这着在局面棋上很诱人，却让主动权从黑方手中溜走，使白方重返争斗，至少有望求和。黑方应20... bxa4 21. Bxa4 h6，白方攻势便会消退：22. e5?（22. g4因22... Qf4而不行；若22. h3，黑方22... Qc4 23. Bb3 Qb4）22... Nd5 23. Re4 Ne7 24. Rg4 Bxf3 25. gxf3 Nf5，黑优。

text: The immediate 21. e5 was not good, but it becomes favourable when preceded by d5, for then the black knight's access to the d5-square is blocked, while the e-file and the a2-g8 diagonal are opened up. An instructive way of using a flexible centre!
zh: 立即21. e5不好，但先d5之后就有利了，因为黑马通往d5的道路被堵住，e线和a2-g8斜线却得到开放。这是运用灵活中心的一种富有启发性的方式！

text: 21... e5 will not do because of 22. Ng5 h6 (otherwise 23. Nxh7) 23. d6!.

caption_zh: 凯列斯—法因；22. e5后。

text: A mistake, after which White's initiative takes on new force. A draw could have been salvaged by 22... Ne4! 23. e6 fxe6 24. Rxe4 dxe4 25. Bxe6+! Kh8! 26. Ng5 h6 (26... g6 is weaker on account of 27. Bf7 h5 28. Bxg6 when White has an extremely promising attack) 27. Nf7+ Kh7 28. Ng5+ Kh8 29. Nf7+ with perpetual check. If, instead of 25... Kh8, Black plays 25... Kf8?, the situation turns in White's favour, e.g. 26. Qxh7! Qc3 (if 26... Qf4, then 27. Nh4 is decisive, while 26... Ke7 is no use because of 27. Bxc8) 27. Qg8+ Ke7 28. Qf7+ Kd6 29. Bxc8 Bxc8 (if 29... exf3, then 30. Qe7+ is decisive; 29... Qxc8 fails against 30. Rd1+ Kc5 31. Qe7+, while if 29... Rxc8, then 30. Rd1+ Kc6 31. Qe6+ Kc5 32. Qd6+ and 33. Nd2+) 30. Rxe4!, when White has a decisive attack.
zh: 错误，白方主动因此重获力量。黑方本可22... Ne4! 23. e6 fxe6 24. Rxe4 dxe4 25. Bxe6+! Kh8! 26. Ng5 h6（26... g6较弱，因为27. Bf7 h5 28. Bxg6，白方攻势极有希望）27. Nf7+ Kh7 28. Ng5+ Kh8 29. Nf7+，以长将挽救和棋。如果黑方不用25... Kh8，而走25... Kf8?，局面便转为对白有利，例如26. Qxh7! Qc3（若26... Qf4，则27. Nh4决定胜负；26... Ke7也因27. Bxc8而无用）27. Qg8+ Ke7 28. Qf7+ Kd6 29. Bxc8 Bxc8（若29... exf3，则30. Qe7+决定胜负；29... Qxc8挡不住30. Rd1+ Kc5 31. Qe7+；若29... Rxc8，则30. Rd1+ Kc6 31. Qe6+ Kc5 32. Qd6+接33. Nd2+）30. Rxe4!，白方攻势决定胜负。

text: Keres in his commentary continues 22... Ne4! 23. e6 fxe6 24. Rxe4 dxe4, but instead of going on with 25. Bxe6+!, he gives 25. Ng5?, which is weaker, since strangely enough the knight is better placed on f3 than g5 when Black's king goes to f8. The critical line then is 25... Qc3! 26. Bxe6+ Kf8! 27. Qf4+ Ke7 28. Qf7+ Kd6 29. Qf4+, whereupon Black need not settle for a draw by perpetual check with 29... Ke7, for he has instead 29... Kc5! 30. Rc1 Kb6 31. Bxc8 e3! 32. Qxe3+ Qxe3 33. fxe3 Rxc8 34. Rxc8 Bxc8 and his b-pawn costs the knight its head. An interesting reversal, with Black's king being saved by White's weakness on the back rank!
zh: 凯列斯评注续以22... Ne4! 23. e6 fxe6 24. Rxe4 dxe4，但随后没有25. Bxe6+!，而给出较弱的25. Ng5?。奇怪的是，黑王去f8时，马在f3比在g5更好。关键变化是25... Qc3! 26. Bxe6+ Kf8! 27. Qf4+ Ke7 28. Qf7+ Kd6 29. Qf4+，此时黑方无须29... Ke7接受长将和棋，而可29... Kc5! 30. Rc1 Kb6 31. Bxc8 e3! 32. Qxe3+ Qxe3 33. fxe3 Rxc8 34. Rxc8 Bxc8，b兵迫使白马送命。有趣的逆转：白方底线弱点，竟救了黑王！

caption_zh: 凯列斯—法因；23. Ng5后。

text: Keres did not notice the stronger move 23. Nd4! either during the game or in his commentary. Moving the knight to g5 keeps up the tempo of the attack but leads to no more than a skirmish on the focal-points h7 and f7, whereas moving it to d4, although less immediately forceful, opens up the more productive prospect of play against the focal-point g7, which is quite clearly the weakest point in Black's castled position.
zh: 凯列斯无论在实战还是评注中，都没有发现更强的23. Nd4!。马去g5保持进攻节奏，却只能在h7、f7焦点上小打小闹；去d4虽然直接威力较小，却能更有成效地针对g7展开行动，而g7显然是黑王城最薄弱的一点。

text: After 23. Nd4! Black is virtually obliged to continue 23... Nf8 24. Bc2 Ng6 25. Bxg6 fxg6 when 26. Ne6 wins the exchange, leaving him with insufficient compensation in return. Black's other continuations are weaker, e.g. 23... Nc5 (23... Nxe5? 24. Rxe5 Qxe5 does not work because of 25. Qxd8+) 24. Nf5 Ne4 (if 24... Nxb3, White wins by 25. Qg5) 25. Rxe4 dxe4 26. Qg5 Kf8 (or 26... g6 27. e6 Bd5¹ 28. Bxd5 followed by Ne7+ and Nxd5, etc.) 27. Qxg7+ Ke8 28. e6 fxe6 29. Qg8+ and 30. Qxe6#.
zh: 23. Nd4!后，黑方几乎被迫23... Nf8 24. Bc2 Ng6 25. Bxg6 fxg6，26. Ne6赢得交换，黑方补偿不足。其他续着更弱，例如23... Nc5（23... Nxe5? 24. Rxe5 Qxe5因25. Qxd8+而不行）24. Nf5 Ne4（若24... Nxb3，白方25. Qg5获胜）25. Rxe4 dxe4 26. Qg5 Kf8（或26... g6 27. e6 Bd5¹ 28. Bxd5，再Ne7+、Nxd5等）27. Qxg7+ Ke8 28. e6 fxe6 29. Qg8+，接30. Qxe6#。

text: ¹ Black can unexpectedly turn the tables by 27... Qc3! 28. exf7+ Kh8, but White can improve just before: 27. Ne7+ Kf8 28. Qf6 wins.
zh: ¹ 纳恩注：黑方可27... Qc3! 28. exf7+ Kh8意外扭转局势，但白方可以提前改进：27. Ne7+ Kf8 28. Qf6获胜。

text: The move which loses the game. Correct was 23... h6 after which there is some doubt whether White can win. Keres carries on from 23... h6 with, among other continuations, 24. e6 hxg5 25. exf7+ Kxf7 26. Re7+ Kg8 27. Qh5 (if 27. Qxg5 or 27. Qd4, Black plays 27... Qc3, while 27. Rxg7+ Kxg7 28. Qxg5+ is insufficient on account of 28... Kh8 when White has not got the time to play Re7) 27... Qc3? after which White obtains the advantage by 28. Qf7+ and 29. R7e3. However, instead of 27... Qc3?, Black can play 27... Qf4!, and after 28. Rxd7 (alternatives are 28. g3 Qf5 and 28. Qg6 Qf6) 28... Rxd7 29. Re8+ Qf8! 30. Rxf8+ Kxf8 White not only cannot win but even has the worst of it. The analysis can admittedly be improved at the beginning, for 24. e6 can be replaced by 24. Nxf7 followed by 25. e6+, but it is no longer clear that White has the advantage. Finally, one might consider trying 24. f4 hxg5 25. Qxg5, but this loses its power after 25... Qb6 26. f5 Nf8, since Black can meet 27. f6 with 27... Ne6, threatening, in addition to the queen, 28... Rc3.
zh: 败着。正确的是23... h6，此后白方能否取胜颇有疑问。凯列斯针对23... h6给出的变化之一是24. e6 hxg5 25. exf7+ Kxf7 26. Re7+ Kg8 27. Qh5（若27. Qxg5或27. Qd4，黑方27... Qc3；27. Rxg7+ Kxg7 28. Qxg5+则因28... Kh8而不够，白方来不及Re7）27... Qc3?，随后白方28. Qf7+再29. R7e3获得优势。但黑方可以27... Qf4!代替27... Qc3?；28. Rxd7（其他选择是28. g3 Qf5和28. Qg6 Qf6）28... Rxd7 29. Re8+ Qf8! 30. Rxf8+ Kxf8，白方不仅不能赢，甚至还较差。诚然，可以从开头改进分析，用24. Nxf7接25. e6+代替24. e6，但白方是否有优势已经不清楚。最后还可考虑24. f4 hxg5 25. Qxg5，不过25... Qb6 26. f5 Nf8后，它就失去力量，因为27. f6可应27... Ne6，不仅攻后，还威胁28... Rc3。

text: All these variations arising from the position on the twenty-third move provide instructive illustrations of how to spot the correct focal-point. The analysis of 23. Nd4! showed a typical attack on g7 ending in success for White, whereas in the continuation after 23. Ng5?! h6! a consistent attack could not be built up against any focal-point; White's operations instead took on the character of an attempt to destroy the black king's pawn cover, and as a result Black obtained open lines for his pieces as well as the time in which to organize his defences.
zh: 第二十三步局面引出的所有这些变化，都对如何找准焦点很有启发。23. Nd4!的分析展示了针对g7的典型进攻，白方最终成功；而23. Ng5?! h6!之后，白方无法对任何焦点建立一贯的攻势，行动反而变成试图破坏黑王的兵屏。结果黑方获得了子力的开放线路，也赢得了组织防守的时间。

text: **24. Nxh7 Nxh7 25. Rh3 Qc1 (D)**
zh: **24. Nxh7 Nxh7 25. Rh3 Qc1（见下图）**
caption_zh: 凯列斯—法因；25... Qc1后。

text: A desperate move, but Black no longer has an adequate defence. White could also have played 26. Qxd8+ now and won by virtue of being the exchange ahead, but he prefers to seek a mating attack, which brings even quicker success.
zh: 绝望的一着，但黑方已没有充分防守。白方现在也可26. Qxd8+，凭多交换取胜，不过他宁愿寻求将杀进攻，这样成功更快。

text: Or 29... Bd5 30. Qf6+ Kf8 31. Bxd5 Rxd5 32. e6.
For 31... dxe3 is defeated by 32. exf7+ Kd7 33. Qe6+, and if 33... Kc7, then 34. Rxc1+, or if 33... Kd8, then 34. Qd6#.
The bayonet attack
zh: 刺刀进攻

text: The term 'bayonet attack' is used to designate the advance of one of the attacker's pawns on the side of the board facing the opposing castled position, as a result of which the pawn drives off one of the opponent's pieces or creates a sharp threat of some kind. A typical example of the bayonet attack is the move g4, whereby White prepares the advance g5 and an attack on Black's knight at f6. The following examples show us some typical cases of the bayonet attack.
zh: “刺刀进攻”是指进攻方在面对敌王城的一翼推进一个兵，借此驱赶敌子，或制造某种尖锐威胁。典型例子是g4：白方准备g5，攻击f6黑马。以下实例展示一些典型的刺刀进攻。

text: The following position arose in Keres-Petrov, Estonia-Latvia Match, 1939 after the moves 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nd2 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nd7 5. Nf3 Be7 6. Bd3 Ngf6 7. Qe2 Nxe4 8. Bxe4 Nf6 9. Bd3 c5 10. dxc5 Qa5+ 11. Bd2 Qxc5 12. O-O-O O-O 13. Ne5 b6 (D).
zh: 下图出自凯列斯—彼得罗夫，爱沙尼亚对拉脱维亚对抗赛，1939年，由以下着法形成：1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nd2 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nd7 5. Nf3 Be7 6. Bd3 Ngf6 7. Qe2 Nxe4 8. Bxe4 Nf6 9. Bd3 c5 10. dxc5 Qa5+ 11. Bd2 Qxc5 12. O-O-O O-O 13. Ne5 b6（见下图）。
caption_zh: 凯列斯—彼得罗夫；13... b6后。

text: White now played:
zh: 白方此时走：

text: Black attempts to halt the further advance of White's pawn by indirect means, namely, by attacking the rook on h1. The other possible replies were no better; White's position is already so powerful that a bayonet attack is fully justified. If 14... h6, White would continue 15. h4, threatening g5 with even greater effect; against 14... g6 he would not play 15. g5 immediately (since Black would reply 15... Nh5), but 15. h4 followed by h5. Finally, if 14... Bd6 then 15. f4 is very strong.
zh: 黑方试图用间接手段阻止白兵继续推进，即攻击h1车。其他应手也不好；白方局面已经足够强大，完全有理由展开刺刀进攻。若14... h6，白方15. h4，使g5威胁更有力；对14... g6，白方不会立即15. g5，因为15... Nh5，而会15. h4再h5。最后，若14... Bd6，15. f4很强。

text: White does not worry about his rook, since if 15... Bxh1, he can dictate matters with 16. gxf6 Bxf6 (or 16... gxf6 17. Qg4+ Kh8 18. Rg1 Rg8 19. Nxf7#) 17. Nd7 Qc6 18. Nxf6+ gxf6 19. Qg4+ Kh8 20. Qh4 f5 21. Qf6+ Kg8 22. Rg1+ Bg2 23. Bh6 and mates.
zh: 白方不担心车，因为若15... Bxh1，他可16. gxf6 Bxf6（或16... gxf6 17. Qg4+ Kh8 18. Rg1 Rg8 19. Nxf7#）17. Nd7 Qc6 18. Nxf6+ gxf6 19. Qg4+ Kh8 20. Qh4 f5 21. Qf6+ Kg8 22. Rg1+ Bg2 23. Bh6，强制将杀。

text: Black could have answered 16. Nd7 with 16... Qc7 17. Nxf8 Nf4! forcing simplification.
zh: 若16. Nd7，黑方可以16... Qc7 17. Nxf8 Nf4!，强制简化局面。

caption_zh: 凯列斯—彼得罗夫，16... Qc7之后，白先。

text: In the event of 16... Nb4 Yudovich gave the following combination: 17. Bxb4 Qxb4 18. Rg4 Qc5 19. Bxh7+ Kxh7 20. Rh4+ Kg8 21. Qh5 Bxg5+ 22. Qxg5 f6 23. Qxg7+! Kxg7 24. Rg1+ and mates.
zh: 对16... Nb4，尤多维奇给出以下组合：17. Bxb4 Qxb4 18. Rg4 Qc5 19. Bxh7+ Kxh7 20. Rh4+ Kg8 21. Qh5 Bxg5+ 22. Qxg5 f6 23. Qxg7+! Kxg7 24. Rg1+，接着将杀。

text: Keres does not carry his attack to its logical conclusion, i.e. by the sacrifice 17. Bxh7+ Kxh7 18. Qh5+ Kg8 19. f4 threatening Rg4-h4. This attacking position is strong enough to guarantee victory, although it still demands precise play. Instead of 19. f4, Horowitz gives the weaker continuation 19. Rg3 Qxe5 20. Rh3 and shows that 20... f6 then parries White's attack.
zh: 凯列斯没有将进攻贯彻到底，即17. Bxh7+ Kxh7 18. Qh5+ Kg8 19. f4，威胁Rg4-h4。这个进攻局面强得足以保证胜利，尽管仍须精确行棋。霍洛维茨没有给19. f4，而给出较弱的19. Rg3 Qxe5 20. Rh3，并指出此时20... f6能够挡住白方的进攻。

text: After the text move Black should have played 17... f5 18. gxf6 Bxf6, whereupon White would have been left with only a slight advantage.
zh: 正文着法之后，黑方应走17... f5 18. gxf6 Bxf6，白方便只剩微弱优势。

caption_zh: 凯列斯—彼得罗夫，18... Bd6之后，白先。

text: So as to answer the threatened 19. Rxh7 with 19... Bxe5!.
zh: 准备对19. Rxh7的威胁应19... Bxe5!。

text: Thanks to Black's error the attack has again got under way, and the game now ‘plays itself’.
zh: 由于黑方失误，进攻重新展开；现在的棋局几乎“自己就会走下去”。

text: **19... Rfc8 20. Kb1 b5 21. Rg1 Be7 22. Nh6+ Kf8 23. Nxf7 Bc5 24. Rxh7 Bd4 25. Qxe6 Bg7**
zh: **19... Rfc8 20. Kb1 b5 21. Rg1 Be7 22. Nh6+ Kf8 23. Nxf7 Bc5 24. Rxh7 Bd4 25. Qxe6 Bg7**

text: White now played 26. Nd6 and won in a few moves. By 26. Nh8 he could have forced Black to resign at once.
zh: 白方现在走26. Nd6，数步后取胜。26. Nh8本可立即迫使黑方认输。
caption_zh: 阿廖欣—韦宁克，布拉格，1931年，白先。

text: This position is from the game Alekhine-Weenink, Prague 1931. In this case too White produces the bayonet in the form of:
zh: 此局面来自阿廖欣—韦宁克，布拉格，1931年。这里白方同样亮出刺刀：

text: Alekhine, in My Best Games of Chess 1924–1937, says of this move: ‘This little pawn threatens by its further advance to set on fire the black king's residence — and cannot possibly be stopped from that dark design.’
zh: 阿廖欣在《我的最佳对局1924—1937》中这样评价此着：“这个小兵威胁继续前进，纵火焚烧黑王的居所；它的这一险恶企图，已不可能被阻止。”

text: Black had intended to meet 2. g5 with 2... Qd5, but the intermediate move 2. Bg6 puts paid to that idea.
zh: 黑方原想以2... Qd5应对2. g5，但中间着2. Bg6彻底打破了这个构思。

text: The bayonet has its point in both the bishop on f6 and the pawn on h6, and nothing can be done about it.
zh: 刺刀同时指向f6象与h6兵，黑方已无可奈何。

text: If 3... Qd5 4. gxf6 Rxf6, White cannot exchange queens, it is true, but he has 5. Rd3 Nhf8 6. Bf7, holding on to the booty he has won.
zh: 若3... Qd5 4. gxf6 Rxf6，白方确实不能兑后，但有5. Rd3 Nhf8 6. Bf7，保住赢得的子力。

text: **4. gxh6 Ndf6 5. hxg7+ Kxg7 6. Qh6+ Kh8 7. Nxd4 Qxd4 8. Bb2 1-0**.
zh: **4. gxh6 Ndf6 5. hxg7+ Kxg7 6. Qh6+ Kh8 7. Nxd4 Qxd4 8. Bb2 1-0**。

text: Black's only possible attempt at resistance, 8... Qd7, is defeated by 9. Rd3 Qg7 10. Bxf6 and mate in three moves.
zh: 黑方唯一可能的抵抗8... Qd7，遇9. Rd3 Qg7 10. Bxf6，三步内被将杀。

text: The pawn avalanche
zh: 兵雪崩

text: The formation composed of two or three neighbouring pawns on the same rank is often called a ‘phalanx’ in chess literature, but when such a phalanx attacks it can also be suitably described as an ‘avalanche’ or ‘roller’. An attack based on a pawn avalanche generally entails even more positional commitments than the bayonet attack, as it involves advancing two pawns instead of only one. On the other hand, the avalanche's power is also greater than that of the bayonet, for an avalanche drives all the enemy pieces before it and offers more attacking possibilities.
zh: 两三个相邻兵处于同一横线的阵形，棋书常称为“兵方阵”；这种方阵展开攻击时，也很适合形容为“雪崩”或“滚压”。兵雪崩进攻通常比刺刀进攻受到更多局面上的约束，因为要推进的是两个兵，而非一个。但雪崩的威力也更大，它能把面前的敌子全部赶开，提供更多进攻可能。

text: When attacking by means of a pawn avalanche, it is usually important that one's opponent should be unable to retaliate in the centre or on the other wing. This is, admittedly, a general condition for any kind of attack on the castled king, but in the case of an attack using pawns it applies even more strictly, since one is more restricted positionally and the actual process of advancing pawns is slower than play with pieces, with the result that one's opponent has greater opportunities for counterplay. The next example will show us a case where the conditions for an attack using the avalanche are favourable.
zh: 采用兵雪崩时，对手不能在中央或另一翼反击，通常是很重要的条件。诚然，这也是任何攻击已易位王的一般条件；但对兵的进攻，要求更为严格，因为己方在局面上的约束更多，实际推进兵又比用棋子行动慢，对手因而有更多反击机会。下例便是适合采用兵雪崩的情形。
caption_zh: 施莱希特—塔拉什，蒙特卡洛，1903年，白先。

text: This position is from the game Schlechter-Tarrasch, Monte Carlo 1903. It is White's move.
zh: 此局面来自施莱希特—塔拉什，蒙特卡洛，1903年。白先。

text: The use of the avalanche attack is well justified in this position. Black has no counterplay worth speaking of either on the queenside or in the centre, so that the risk White accepts in being committed to deciding the game on the kingside is not great. Moreover, White already has a pawn at f5, which is in fact in his way at the moment. When the g-pawn moves up to its aid within just two moves, there is considerable prospect of the position's being loosened up a little and that the f-pawn will acquire a dynamic potential.
zh: 这里采用兵雪崩进攻十分合理。黑方无论后翼还是中央都没有值得一提的反击，因此白方决心在王翼决定胜负，所承担的风险并不大。而且白方已有f5兵，目前它其实有些碍事；只须两步，g兵就能赶来支援，很有希望使局面稍微松动，令f兵获得动态潜力。

text: 4... Nf8 would probably have been better. Moves which weaken the position, such as ...f6, should not be resorted to unless absolutely necessary. After 4... Nf8 5. Qf3 Black would, of course, already be compelled to play 5... f6.
zh: 4... Nf8大概更好。像...f6这样削弱局面的着法，除非绝对必要，不应采用。当然，4... Nf8 5. Qf3之后，黑方便已被迫5... f6。

text: Certainly weaker than 5... Nf8; on his next move Black puts the bishop back on e7 and so loses two tempi. However, even after 5... Nf8 White's attack would be overwhelming.
zh: 肯定不如5... Nf8；下一步黑方又把象放回e7，白白损失两步。不过，即使5... Nf8，白方攻势也会势不可挡。

caption_zh: 施莱希特—塔拉什，6... Be7之后，白先。

text: Tarrasch was not a master who would lightly agree to the loss of a tempo, but in this case he was clearly convinced that his original plan had no prospects. This is evident from White's threat (Black's bishop is still on f8) 7. Qg4 (not 7. Qh5 followed by 8. g6? because of 8... h6, and Black would be saved by the blocked position [note 1]) 7... Kh8 8. Bxc5 dxc5 9. Ne4, when Black's defences give way under the pressure against the squares f6 and d6.
zh: 塔拉什并不是轻易愿意损失一步的大师，但这里他显然确信原计划没有前途。从白方的威胁便可看出：假如黑象仍在f8，白方7. Qg4（而非7. Qh5再8. g6?，因为8... h6后封闭局面能挽救黑方【注1】）7... Kh8 8. Bxc5 dxc5 9. Ne4，黑方对f6和d6的防御将被压垮。

text: [Nunn's note 1] In fact the plan of Qh5 and g6 should also bring success, as after the reply ...h6 White can break through in King's Indian style by Bxh6 followed by g7, with a crushing attack.
zh: 【纳恩注1】实际上，Qh5再g6的计划也应成功，因为对...h6，白方可采用古印度式的Bxh6再g7突破，取得摧毁性攻势。

text: **7. Qh5 Nf8 8. Rg3 Ra8**
zh: **7. Qh5 Nf8 8. Rg3 Ra8**

text: There are no useful moves that Black can make in his cramped position. After, for example, 8... Ncd7 9. Rcg1 Rc8 10. Ne4 he finds himself in a sad state, without a satisfactory defence against the threat of 11. gxf6 Bxf6 12. Qh6.
zh: 黑方局促，已无有用着法。例如8... Ncd7 9. Rcg1 Rc8 10. Ne4之后，他便陷入窘境，无法满意地应付11. gxf6 Bxf6 12. Qh6的威胁。

text: **9. Bxc5 dxc5 10. d6! Qxd6**
zh: **9. Bxc5 dxc5 10. d6! Qxd6**

text: If 10... Bxd6, then 11. gxf6 is decisive.
zh: 若10... Bxd6，则11. gxf6决定胜负。

text: **11. Ne4 Qd8 12. Rd1 1-0**. Black cannot prevent the collapse of the weak point f6. If 12... Nd7, then 13. gxf6 Bxf6 14. Rxd7 Qxd7 15. Nxf6+.
zh: **11. Ne4 Qd8 12. Rd1 1-0**。黑方无法防止f6弱点崩溃。若12... Nd7，则13. gxf6 Bxf6 14. Rxd7 Qxd7 15. Nxf6+。

text: In this example three phases in White's attack should be noted. The first is the creation of the advancing pawn avalanche, the second consists of the deployment of White's pieces, and the third is the actual execution or breakthrough.
zh: 这一例中，应注意白方进攻的三个阶段：先建立前进的兵雪崩，然后部署棋子，最后实施打击，也就是突破。

text: The avalanche alone cannot, as a rule, be decisive, and its greatest enemy is the danger of blockade. Combating this danger depends for the most part on piece play, and this takes two main forms: allowing the position to be blocked and then breaking it up by sacrificing a piece; or first sacrificing the piece and then pushing forward with the pawn avalanche without any fear of its being blocked. In the following games we shall see these methods being applied; destroying the enemy pawn cover is essentially the main combinative element.
zh: 通常，兵雪崩本身不能决定胜负，最大的敌人是遭到封锁的危险。克服这种危险，主要靠棋子的行动，有两种基本方式：允许局面被封锁，再弃子破坏；或者先弃子，再让兵雪崩放心前进，不必担心被堵住。以下对局将展示这些方法；其主要组合要素，本质上就是摧毁敌方的护王兵。

text:
Rubinstein – Teichmann
Vienna Match (4), 1908
Queen's Gambit Declined, Orthodox Defence
zh:
鲁宾斯坦—泰希曼
维也纳对抗赛第4局，1908年
后翼弃兵拒弃兵变例，正统防御

text: **1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Nbd7 5. e3 Be7 6. Nf3 O-O 7. Qc2 b6**
zh: **1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Nbd7 5. e3 Be7 6. Nf3 O-O 7. Qc2 b6**

text: 7... c5 is better.

zh: **8. cxd5 exd5 9. Bd3 Bb7 10. O-O-O c5 11. h4 c4?**（见图）
caption_zh: 鲁宾斯坦—泰希曼，11... c4之后，白先。

text: Logically, Black must attack on the queenside, but his plan is too slow. Before he can set up the avalanche formation with pawns on c4 and b4, White will have a flourishing attack since his pieces are more active than Black's. Correct was 11... cxd4 in preparation for ...a6, ...b5 and ...Rc8; that would have constituted a more powerful threat.
zh: 按理黑方必须在后翼进攻，但他的计划太慢。等他把兵摆到c4、b4形成雪崩之前，子力更活跃的白方早已攻势大盛。正确的是11... cxd4，准备...a6、...b5和...Rc8，那样的威胁会强得多。

text: Kmoch, in his fine book on Rubinstein, thinks that even here ...a6 and ...b5 would have been better, but the black pawn can hardly reach b4, since after 12... a6 13. g4 there is an immediate threat of Bxf6 followed by g5, picking up the booty on h7. If, for example, Black plays 13... g6 then 14. Bxd7 followed at once by Bh6 gives White a strong initiative.
zh: 克莫赫在其出色的鲁宾斯坦专著中，认为即使这里也应以...a6和...b5为好。但黑兵很难到达b4，因为12... a6 13. g4之后，白方立即威胁Bxf6再g5，夺取h7兵。例如黑方13... g6，则14. Bxd7再立即Bh6，白方主动权很强。

text: The text move prepares the way for ...Nf8, so White immediately takes the knight on f6 to prevent this.
zh: 正文着法准备...Nf8，因此白方立即吃掉f6马，阻止这一计划。

text: Thus a ‘small avalanche’ is formed on the fourth rank. Soon it will become ‘great’ on the fifth, and finally ‘terrible’ when it reaches the sixth en masse.
zh: 第四横线上形成了“小雪崩”。很快它在第五横线将变成“大雪崩”，等到整体压上第六横线，就会成为“可怕的雪崩”。

text:
The fifth rank has been reached without Black having moved an inch on the queenside.
If Black now plays 16... Nxg5, there follows 17. Nxg5 Qxg5 18. Bxh7+ Kf8 19. h6! gxh6 20. Rdg1, etc.
zh:
白兵已到第五横线，黑方在后翼却寸步未进。
若黑方现在16... Nxg5，则17. Nxg5 Qxg5 18. Bxh7+ Kf8 19. h6! gxh6 20. Rdg1，等等。

caption_zh: 鲁宾斯坦—泰希曼，17... a6之后，白先。

text: Black reckons that nothing is threatened and devotes a tempo to his slow counterattack on the queenside. Admittedly, White would get nowhere by moving his pawns at this point: if 18. h6, the position is blocked by 18... g6; while if 18. g6, then 18... fxg6 followed by ...h6. However, White has another device, namely the sacrifice of his bishop, which enables the pawns to go ahead happily and without any fear of being blocked.
zh: 黑方以为白方没有威胁，便花一步继续缓慢的后翼反击。确实，白方此时直接动兵毫无进展：18. h6遇18... g6封闭；18. g6则18... fxg6再...h6。但白方另有办法，即弃象，让兵能顺利前进，不怕被堵住。

text: Or 19... fxg6 20. Nxe4 dxe4 21. Ng5+ and if 21... Kg8 then 22. Qxc4+ or if 21... Kh6, then 22. Nf7+ Qxf7 23. hxg6+ mating.
zh: 或19... fxg6 20. Nxe4 dxe4 21. Ng5+；若21... Kg8，则22. Qxc4+；若21... Kh6，则22. Nf7+ Qxf7 23. hxg6+，接着将杀。

text: In fact superfluous. The immediate 20. h6 was simpler, and if 20... fxg6 then 21. Rxg6 while if 20... f6, then 21. hxg7.
zh: 实际上是多余的。立即20. h6更简单，若20... fxg6则21. Rxg6，若20... f6则21. hxg7。

text: If 20... Qxe4, then 21. gxf7+ is decisive.
zh: 若20... Qxe4，则21. gxf7+决定胜负。

caption_zh: 鲁宾斯坦—泰希曼，21. h6之后，黑先。

text: The avalanche has come down on Black's pawns, which can no longer offer any help by blocking the position. Carried away by the spectacle on the board, Kmoch adds two exclamation marks, which I am unable to do, since I can see another continuation which is simpler, stronger, and even more ‘Rubinstein-like’ than h6, in that it links the combination with a positional breakthrough in the centre: 21. Ng5! Bd5 (the f-pawn must not be moved because of 22. Qxc4+) 22. gxf7+ Bxf7 23. f3! Bd5 (otherwise fxe4 and e5) 24. h6 Rac8 (or 24... g6 25. Rh4) 25. fxe4 Bxe4 26. h7+ Kh8 27. Qxe4! Qxg5 28. Qxe8+ and White wins [note 1].
zh: 雪崩已压到黑兵头上，黑兵再也不能靠堵住局面来帮助防守。克莫赫为棋盘上的景象所感染，给这步加了两个叹号；我却无法同意，因为我看到了比h6更简单、更强、也更有“鲁宾斯坦风格”的变化，把组合与中央的局面棋突破相结合：21. Ng5! Bd5（f兵不能动，否则22. Qxc4+）22. gxf7+ Bxf7 23. f3! Bd5（否则fxe4再e5）24. h6 Rac8（或24... g6 25. Rh4）25. fxe4 Bxe4 26. h7+ Kh8 27. Qxe4! Qxg5 28. Qxe8+，白胜【注1】。

text: [Nunn's note 1] However, this line is also not conclusive as instead of 23... Bd5 Black can create confusion by 23... c3, when White's plan of fxe4 followed by e5 starts to look too slow.
zh: 【纳恩注1】不过，这个变化也不具决定性；黑方可不用23... Bd5，改以23... c3制造混乱，此时白方fxe4再e5的计划就显得太慢。

text: This makes White's task easier, though the game would not have been saved by the more stubborn move 21... fxg6. 21... exf3 would have been even weaker, e.g. 22. gxf7+ Qxf7 23. hxg7 with threats against h8 and h7.
zh: 这使白方任务更容易，不过更顽强的21... fxg6也救不了棋局。21... exf3更弱，例如22. gxf7+ Qxf7 23. hxg7，威胁h8和h7。

text: After 21... fxg6 Kmoch shows that 22. Rxg6? is weak (because of 22... exf3, and Black gains too much material in return for his queen). He gives the following line as good for White: 22. Nh4 g5 23. Ng6 Qf6 24. h7+ Kf7 25. h8=Q Rxh8 26. Nxh8+. However, the situation is somewhat doubtful after 26... Ke7, for while White is extracting his knight from the corner, Black works up a counterattack, e.g. 27. Qe2 c3! 28. Qh5 (or 28. bxc3 Ba3+ followed by ...Qf5) 28... cxb2+, and if 29. Kb1, then 29... Ba3, while if 29. Kxb2, then 29... Qxf2+, etc.
zh: 对21... fxg6，克莫赫指出22. Rxg6?较弱（因为22... exf3，黑方弃后换得的子力太多）。他认为以下变化有利于白方：22. Nh4 g5 23. Ng6 Qf6 24. h7+ Kf7 25. h8=Q Rxh8 26. Nxh8+。但26... Ke7之后，局面有些可疑，因为白方设法把马从角落撤出时，黑方能组织反击，例如27. Qe2 c3! 28. Qh5（或28. bxc3 Ba3+再...Qf5）28... cxb2+；若29. Kb1，则29... Ba3；若29. Kxb2，则29... Qxf2+，等等。
**22. hxg7 exf3**（见图）
caption_zh: 鲁宾斯坦—泰希曼，22... exf3之后，白先。

text: The queen can be saved by 22... Qe6 but then 23. Rh8+ followed by 24. Rh7+ and 25. Rgh1 leads to a mating attack.
zh: 22... Qe6可以保后，但23. Rh8+，再24. Rh7+及25. Rgh1，形成将杀攻势。

text: Or 25... Qe6 26. Qh5, etc.
For if 26... Rxe7, then 27. Qxf6 is decisive.
zh: 因为若26... Rxe7，则27. Qxf6决定胜负。

text:
König – H. Weiss
Vienna, 1919
Queen's Pawn Game
zh:
柯尼希—H.魏斯
维也纳，1919年
后兵开局

text: Here it is Black who is playing the Queen's Gambit, while White is building up his position according to the pattern which Black uses in the Semi-Slav Defence, to which the move Bf4 is a useful addition. This is an example of a so-called inverted opening, in which White plays Black's system with a tempo in hand.
zh: 这里下后翼弃兵的是黑方，白方则按照黑方半斯拉夫防御的模式布阵，并多了Bf4这步有用的棋。这是所谓“反色开局”的例子，白方采用黑方体系，额外多一个先手。

text: Black has obviously lost his bearings and is not aware that he is ‘really White’; passive moves of this type do not fit in with the active position of his central pawns. Correct was 6... Bd6.
zh: 黑方显然迷失了方向，没有意识到自己“其实是白方”；这种被动着法与中央兵的活跃位置不相称。正确的是6... Bd6。

text: Black does not appreciate the real nature of the position and is not taking measures to obtain counterplay at the right time by means of an outpost on one of the central squares. He even surrenders control of the important e4 and e5 squares to White, and as a result suddenly comes up against the storm of an attack on his castled king. The correct course was 8... cxd4 9. exd4 Nxe5 10. dxe5 Nd7 11. Qh5 f5! when Black can meet 12. f3 by 12... Qc7 and 12. g4 by 12... Nc5 13. Bc2 Ne4.
zh: 黑方不理解局面的实质，没有及时利用某个中央格上的据点争取反击。他甚至把重要的e4、e5格都让给白方，结果突然遭到攻击王城的暴风骤雨。正确的是8... cxd4 9. exd4 Nxe5 10. dxe5 Nd7 11. Qh5 f5!；此后对12. f3可应12... Qc7，对12. g4可应12... Nc5 13. Bc2 Ne4。

caption_zh: 柯尼希—H.魏斯，9. g4之后，黑先。

text: Throughout the opening stage of the game the conditions required to justify a ‘bayonet attack’ have been gradually accumulating. One group of these conditions has already been noted in the shape of Black's inferior moves and his lack of concern to control at least one of the important squares e5 and e4. The other group can be revealed by an analysis of the structure of White's position. This is clearly distinguished by good piece play together with a modest but sound pawn formation in the centre. Indeed, its essence lies in the very soundness of the formation c3, d4, and e3, with the strong protection which it gives to the square d4. If this solidity in the centre did not exist, Black would be able at the last moment to organize a counterattack in the centre as an answer to White's attack on his castled king.
zh: 整个开局阶段，支持“刺刀进攻”的条件逐渐积累起来。其中一组已经指出：黑方走了劣着，并且没有关心至少控制e5、e4这两个重要格中的一个。另一组则可通过分析白方结构看出：其鲜明特点是棋子配置良好，中央兵形虽不张扬，却很稳固。关键正是c3、d4、e3兵形的坚实，尤其对d4格提供强力保护。若中央没有这种稳固性，黑方便能在最后关头组织中央反击，回应白方对王城的攻击。

text: His security against such a central counterattack — generally the main weapon in an active defence against an attack on the castled king — gives White great freedom in his attack on the castled position and is basically the main justification for the move 9. g4!.
zh: 中央反击通常是积极防守王城的主要武器；白方不怕这种反击，就有很大的进攻自由，这基本上正是9. g4!的主要根据。

text: If 9... Nd7 White will continue with g5 as in the game.
zh: 若9... Nd7，白方仍像实战一样续走g5。

text: If 11... Bxg5, then 12. Qh5 h6 13. Rg1 Bxf4 14. exf4 Kf8 15. Qg4 g6 16. Bxg6. If 11... Qc7, then 12. Bxh7+ Kxh7 13. Qh5+ Kg8 14. g6 fxg6 15. Qxg6 Rd8 (or 15... Rf8 16. Qxe6+ Rf7 17. Qxf7+ and 18. e6+) 16. Rg1 Bf8 17. Nf3 followed by Ng5.
zh: 若11... Bxg5，则12. Qh5 h6 13. Rg1 Bxf4 14. exf4 Kf8 15. Qg4 g6 16. Bxg6。若11... Qc7，则12. Bxh7+ Kxh7 13. Qh5+ Kg8 14. g6 fxg6 15. Qxg6 Rd8（或15... Rf8 16. Qxe6+ Rf7 17. Qxf7+再18. e6+）16. Rg1 Bf8 17. Nf3，再Ng5。

text: This simplifies White's task, though better moves would not help Black very much.
zh: 这使白方任务更简单，不过更好的着法也帮不了黑方多少。

text: No sooner has White's pawn avalanche established itself on the fifth rank than he carries out the characteristic piece sacrifice, which breaks up the castled position and prevents a defensive blockade from being set up.
zh: 白方兵雪崩刚在第五横线站稳，便立即实施典型的弃子，破坏王城，防止对方建立防御性封锁。

text: His position also soon collapses after 20... Kg8 21. h6 Bf8 22. Rdg1 Re7 23. Qh7+! Kxh7 (or 23... Kf7 24. hxg7) 24. hxg7+ Kg8 25. Rh8+ Kf7 26. g8=Q+, etc. [note 1].
zh: 20... Kg8 21. h6 Bf8 22. Rdg1 Re7 23. Qh7+! Kxh7（或23... Kf7 24. hxg7）24. hxg7+ Kg8 25. Rh8+ Kf7 26. g8=Q+等之后，黑方局面也很快崩溃【注1】。

text: [Nunn's note 1] In fact, White ends up material down after 26... Ke8 27. Qxf8+ Kd7, etc., so he should prefer 23. hxg7 Bxg7 24. Rh7 Qc7 25. Rgh1, followed by mate.
zh: 【纳恩注1】实际上，26... Ke8 27. Qxf8+ Kd7等之后，白方最终在子力上吃亏，所以应改走23. hxg7 Bxg7 24. Rh7 Qc7 25. Rgh1，随后将杀。

text: **21. h6 Bf6 22. hxg7+ Bxg7 23. Rh8+ Bxh8 24. Bh6+ Ke7 25. Qh7+** and mate next move.
zh: **21. h6 Bf6 22. hxg7+ Bxg7 23. Rh8+ Bxh8 24. Bh6+ Ke7 25. Qh7+**，下一步将杀。

text:
Tolush – Kotov
USSR Championship, Moscow 1945
Sicilian Defence, Scheveningen Variation
zh:
托卢什—科托夫
苏联锦标赛，莫斯科，1945年
西西里防御，舍维宁根变例

text: **1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 d6 6. g3**
zh: **1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 d6 6. g3**

text: It is more usual to play either 6. g4 or 6. Be2 at this point, which perhaps give White somewhat greater scope for attack than 6. g3.
zh: 这里更常见的是6. g4或6. Be2，它们也许比6. g3给白方更大的进攻余地。

text: Another plan would have been 7... Nxd4 and then ...Bd7, in order to play the bishop to c6. White now withdraws his knight from d4 and so makes it difficult for Black to further the development of the c8-bishop.
zh: 另一计划是7... Nxd4再...Bd7，准备把象走到c6。现在白方将马从d4撤回，使黑方难以继续展开c8象。

text: The preparation of a bayonet attack is justified in this position, for Black is still quite a long way from starting a counterattack by ...d5.
zh: 这里准备刺刀进攻是合理的，因为黑方距离以...d5发动中央反击还远。

text: Not to the point; better is 13... Rfd8.
zh: 没有切中要点；13... Rfd8更好。

text: Black has made a start to his preparations for the thrust ...d5, but White's attack is faster. White does not play 16. e5 here, as Black can then reply 16... Nfd5.
zh: 黑方已开始准备...d5突破，但白方的攻击更快。这里白方不走16. e5，因为黑方可以16... Nfd5应对。

caption_zh: 托卢什—科托夫，16... Ng8之后，白先。

text: A pawn attack on the kingside is a valuable weapon for White in the Scheveningen Variation, while Black's best response is a counter-stroke in the centre by ...d5. Black is somewhat behind in preparing for this thrust, and consequently White is able to set in motion his pawn attack. 17. Be3 was, by the way, also solid and good.
zh: 在舍维宁根变例中，王翼兵的攻击是白方的重要武器，黑方最佳应对则是...d5中央反击。黑方准备这一突破稍嫌落后，所以白方得以发动兵的进攻。顺带一提，17. Be3也是稳健好棋。

text: A weak move, which considerably helps White in regrouping his forces, because 18. Nce2! now immediately threatens c3. Correct was 17... Rfd8 preparing ...d5.
zh: 弱着，大大帮助白方重新部署子力，因为现在18. Nce2!立即威胁c3。正确的是17... Rfd8，准备...d5。

text: 19... Nxc2? would not have worked because of 20. Rc1 Rac8 21. Bc3! Ne3 22. Qd4.
zh: 19... Nxc2?不行，因为20. Rc1 Rac8 21. Bc3! Ne3 22. Qd4。

text: Black has in fact managed to play ...d5, but White has made good use of the time and now, besides his bayonet (the pawn on g5), he also has a ‘long sabre’ in the shape of his dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal!
zh: 黑方虽然终于走成...d5，白方却已充分利用时间；现在除了刺刀——g5兵——之外，还有一柄“长军刀”，就是长斜线上的黑格象！

caption_zh: 托卢什—科托夫，22. Nxg7之后，黑先。

text: Grandmaster Tolush, himself an officer, uses his weapons well. After the ‘bayonet’ and the ‘sabre’, here comes a suicide ‘bomb’. The sacrifice is correct and characteristic of an attack based on a pawn avalanche.
zh: 托卢什特级大师本人也是军官，善于使用武器。继“刺刀”和“军刀”之后，现在又投下一枚自毁式“炸弹”。弃子正确，而且很能体现兵雪崩进攻的特点。

text: The correctness of the sacrifice has its basis in the powerful threat of Nd4, as can be seen in the following variation: 22... Kxg7 23. Nd4! Bc4 (or 23... Qd7 24. Bxe4 and if 24... Bc6 in order to prevent 25. Qh5, then 25. Nxc6 Qxd1 26. Rfxd1 Nxc6 27. Bxc6 Ra7 28. Rd7, when White picks up another pawn and makes his task easy) 24. Bxe4 Rfd8 25. Qh5 Kf8 26. Qxh7 with a decisive attack.
zh: 弃子成立的根据，在于Nd4这一强大威胁，以下变化可见：22... Kxg7 23. Nd4! Bc4（或23... Qd7 24. Bxe4；若24... Bc6阻止25. Qh5，则25. Nxc6 Qxd1 26. Rfxd1 Nxc6 27. Bxc6 Ra7 28. Rd7，白方再吃一兵，取胜任务轻松）24. Bxe4 Rfd8 25. Qh5 Kf8 26. Qxh7，白方取得决定性攻势。

text: Also interesting is 22... Rad8 23. Nd4 Rxd4, when 24. Qxd4 is not very effective because of 24... Kxg7, and White does no more than win back the sacrificed material. However, if 23... Rxd4, White has the fine reply 24. Qg4!, which prevents 24... Kxg7 and creates the threat of 25. Nxe6 followed by 26. g6!. No answer to this has been found for Black.
zh: 22... Rad8 23. Nd4 Rxd4也很有趣。此时24. Qxd4因24... Kxg7而效果不佳，白方只能收回弃掉的子力。不过，对23... Rxd4，白方有妙着24. Qg4!，阻止24... Kxg7，并威胁25. Nxe6再26. g6!，尚未找到黑方的解答。

text: Aware, therefore, of the force of Nd4 Black first of all takes the knight on e2 and then accepts the sacrifice.
zh: 因此，黑方意识到Nd4的威力，先吃掉e2马，再接受弃子。

text: **23. Qxe2 Kxg7 24. Bxe4 Nd5 25. Qh5 Rfd8**
zh: **23. Qxe2 Kxg7 24. Bxe4 Nd5 25. Qh5 Rfd8**

text: If 25... Rf7 then 26. g6 hxg6 27. Qxg6+ Kf8 28. Rg1 and White wins.
zh: 若25... Rf7，则26. g6 hxg6 27. Qxg6+ Kf8 28. Rg1，白胜。

caption_zh: 托卢什—科托夫，27... Kf8之后，白先。

text: If 29... Qxh7 then 30. f7+! is decisive.
zh: 若29... Qxh7，则30. f7+!决定胜负。

text:
For 41... Kf7 is answered by 42. Qe7+ and mate in three more moves.
This game won the First Brilliancy Prize at the tournament.
zh:
因为41... Kf7遇42. Qe7+，再三步便被将杀。
本局荣获赛事精彩对局一等奖。

text: Concluding remarks
zh: 结语

text: Before we conclude this discussion of the role of the pawns in the attack on the castled king, we must warn the reader of the immense diversity of practical cases which resist all attempts to embrace them within a set of rules. Our acquaintance with certain rules should not lead us to handle the game in a routine fashion; the particular characteristics of every position must always be thoroughly examined from one move to the next.
zh: 在结束对兵在攻击已易位王中作用的讨论之前，必须提醒读者：实战情形千差万别，无法纳入一套包罗万象的规则。熟悉某些规则，不应使我们机械行棋；每走一步，都必须仔细考察该局面的具体特点。

text: In connection with pawn attacks, there are two cases worth mentioning which often arise in practice. In one case the position requires a rigid, positional use of the pawns in attack, and in the other the position is not at all suitable for the co-operation of the pawns and consequently the attack is better carried out by the pieces alone. For these two cases some suitable examples will now be given.
zh: 关于兵的攻击，实战中常有两种值得一提的情形：一种要求在进攻中采用固定兵形，发挥兵的局面棋作用；另一种则完全不适合兵参与，最好只靠棋子进攻。下面各给出适当例子。
caption_zh: 斯坦尼茨—马尔科，纽伦堡，1896年，白先。

text: This position is from the game Steinitz-Marco, Nuremberg 1896. White is the more aggressively placed but Black's position is fairly solid, especially in the centre, where White lacks a pawn base. The diagonal a2-g8 may become dangerous for Black, but it is not so yet, for if Bc4+, Black can play ...Be6. Nor are the conditions favourable for an attack with the ‘bayonet’ or ‘avalanche’ here; therefore, another way has to be found to strengthen White's position, one which is essentially of a purely positional nature. Steinitz finds it: he advances his f-pawn to f5, where it restricts Black; the fact that this leads to a blocked position is a good thing, since Black's f-pawn can then be fixed at f6 and subsequently ‘rolled up’ by g4 and g5. This is a clear positional plan, which leads to the destruction of Black's pawn chain and thence to a real attack on his castled king. There is no bayonet or avalanche here, though pawn moves are still the decisive means of attack.
zh: 此局面来自斯坦尼茨—马尔科，纽伦堡，1896年。白方位置更具攻击性，但黑方相当稳固，尤其是白方缺乏兵据点的中央。a2-g8斜线可能给黑方带来危险，目前却还没有，因为对白方Bc4+，黑方可...Be6。这里也不适合“刺刀”或“雪崩”，所以必须另找一种本质上纯属局面棋的办法加强白方。斯坦尼茨找到了：把f兵推进到f5，限制黑方。由此封闭局面反而是好事，因为黑f兵被固定在f6，随后可用g4、g5“卷掉”。这是清楚的局面棋计划，先破坏黑兵链，再真正攻击王城。这里没有刺刀或雪崩，尽管冲兵仍是决定性的进攻手段。

text: Black wants to get his bishop to c6, since it cannot settle on the diagonal a2-g8 because of f5. If 1... Bg4, then 2. Rd2 followed by h3 is strong, while 1... g6 would be a voluntary weakening of the castled position.
zh: 黑方想把象放到c6，因为有f5，象不能安置在a2-g8斜线上。若1... Bg4，则2. Rd2再h3很强；1... g6则等于主动削弱王城。

text: Black has no satisfactory answer to g5. If 4... h6 5. h4 Nh7, we get 6. g5 fxg5 7. hxg5 and then either 7... Nxg5 8. Qxg5 and 9. Rh1+ or 7... hxg5 8. Qh3, threatening 9. Qxh7+.
zh: 黑方无法满意地应付g5。若4... h6 5. h4 Nh7，则6. g5 fxg5 7. hxg5，此后或7... Nxg5 8. Qxg5再9. Rh1+，或7... hxg5 8. Qh3，威胁9. Qxh7+。

text: **5. g5 fxg5 6. Qxg5 h6**
zh: **5. g5 fxg5 6. Qxg5 h6**

text: Otherwise f6 follows.
zh: 否则白方接着f6。

text: **7. Qh5 bxc5 8. Nf7+ Kh7 9. Ng5+ Kh8 10. f6 gxf6 11. Qxh6+ Nh7 12. Nxh7 Rxh7 13. Qxf6+ Rg7 14. Rxe5 1-0**
zh: **7. Qh5 bxc5 8. Nf7+ Kh7 9. Ng5+ Kh8 10. f6 gxf6 11. Qxh6+ Nh7 12. Nxh7 Rxh7 13. Qxf6+ Rg7 14. Rxe5 1-0**

text: As our second concluding remark we cited the case where the player has a choice between attacking with his pawns and attacking with his pieces. Every practical player will have experienced the difficulty of such a choice, and an immense amount of time has been consumed in master chess on such decisions. The trouble is that it is difficult to set up any general rule, since everything depends on the particular characteristics of the situation concerned. Before discussing this question any further, let us take an example, and then, by varying the pawn structure, try to penetrate to the heart of the problem.
zh: 结语中的第二点，是棋手必须在动兵进攻与动子进攻之间作选择的情形。每个实战棋手都体会过这种抉择的困难，大师们也为此耗费了大量时间。难处在于无法建立普遍规则，因为一切都取决于具体局面的特点。进一步讨论之前，先举一个例子，再改变兵形，尝试深入问题的核心。

text: It will be easy for the reader to see that this position has arisen as the direct result of a classic bishop sacrifice. It is clear that White must aim to get a rook on to the h-file, and the only question is how to do it. One way would be f4 and then Rf3-h3, and the other Re1-e3-h3. The first is faulty and allows Black to draw, while the second is correct and leads to a win for White. The position is such that only the pieces can cope with the task; the pawns should stay at home to avoid getting in the way. The following variations prove this assertion.
zh: 读者很容易看出，这个局面是古典弃象的直接结果。显然，白方必须设法把车调到h线，问题只在如何做到。一种方法是f4再Rf3-h3，另一种是Re1-e3-h3。前者错误，让黑方得到和棋；后者正确，白方取胜。这个局面的任务只能由棋子完成，兵应该留在原处，以免碍事。以下变化证明这一判断。

text: Of course, Black must on no account play 1... Re7?, since 2. Rf3 would result in the loss of his rook.
zh: 当然，黑方绝不能1... Re7?，否则2. Rf3会使他丢车。

text: White has nothing better. After 3. g4 g6 4. Qh3 Nh7 5. Nf3 Nc6 6. Nh4 Ne7 White is still unable to play f5 as planned, while Black obtains counterplay by ...c5, etc. Also good for Black is 3. f5 exf5 4. Rxf5 Qxf5 5. Qxe8 Nc6.
zh: 白方没有更好的着法。3. g4 g6 4. Qh3 Nh7 5. Nf3 Nc6 6. Nh4 Ne7之后，白方仍不能按计划f5，黑方却可...c5等反击。3. f5 exf5 4. Rxf5 Qxf5 5. Qxe8 Nc6也对黑方有利。

text: Or 4. Qh6 Qg7.
zh: 或4. Qh6 Qg7。

text: This forces a draw. It is of no importance to our thesis whether Black can now play for a win, e.g. by 4... Qg7 followed by ...Nc6 and ...Ne7 or ...Nd8, etc.
zh: 这强制和棋。黑方是否还能争胜，例如4... Qg7再...Nc6以及...Ne7或...Nd8等，并不影响我们的论点。

text: White cannot avoid the exchange of knights; if 5. Nh3, Black gets time to bring out his queen's knight and set up a complete defence.
zh: 白方不能避免兑马；若5. Nh3，黑方便有时间出动后翼马，建立完整防御。

text: **5... Nxg5 6. Qh8+ Kf7 7. Rh7+** [note 1] **Nxh7 8. Qxh7+ Kf8**
White now has to keep up perpetual check by 9. Qh8+ Kf7! 10. Qh7+, but if the unfortunate pawn on f4 were not there, he would be able to mate by Bh6+, etc.
zh: 白方现在必须9. Qh8+ Kf7! 10. Qh7+维持长将；但若没有f4上那个倒霉的兵，他就能Bh6+等将杀。

text: [Nunn's note 1] Here Vuković overlooks that White can mate in two by 7. Qf6+. However, his thesis is basically correct, because the stronger move 4... Qg7 casts doubt on White's attack.
zh: 【纳恩注1】这里武科维奇忽略了白方可用7. Qf6+两步杀。不过，他的论点基本正确，因为更强的4... Qg7使白方的进攻受到质疑。

text: Not 1. Rd1 because of 1... Ba6! 2. Re1 Bd3 followed by ...Bh7, etc.
zh: 不能1. Rd1，因为1... Ba6! 2. Re1 Bd3，再...Bh7等。

text: If here 4... Nh7, then 5. Rh3 Nxg5 6. Qh8+ would win. In this line 5... Re7 is met by 6. Qh6 Rg7 7. Nxh7 Rxh7 8. Qxg6+ Rg7 9. Qh5 Rh7 10. Bh6 Nc6 11. Qg6+ Kh8 12. Bg5 and 13. Bf6+.
zh: 这里若4... Nh7，则5. Rh3 Nxg5 6. Qh8+胜。在这个分支中，5... Re7可应6. Qh6 Rg7 7. Nxh7 Rxh7 8. Qxg6+ Rg7 9. Qh5 Rh7 10. Bh6 Nc6 11. Qg6+ Kh8 12. Bg5，再13. Bf6+。

text: Against anything else White's bishop decides the game by reaching f6, e.g. 5... Nc6 6. Nf3 Nh7 7. Bh6 Qd7 8. Bg5, etc.
zh: 对其他任何着法，白象都可到达f6，决定胜负，例如5... Nc6 6. Nf3 Nh7 7. Bh6 Qd7 8. Bg5，等等。

text: Opening the way for the other rook, for which the f-file, for instance, has attractions.
zh: 为另一只车打开道路，例如f线就很有吸引力。

text: 8... Rac8 does not work at once because of 9. Rf3 Re7 10. Bb4.
zh: 立即8... Rac8不行，因为9. Rf3 Re7 10. Bb4。

text: A simple device to hinder ...Rac8; 9... a4 is answered by 10. b5, and the white bishop gains control of b4. Black now tries to put up a stand with ...Re7 and ...Nh7.
zh: 阻碍...Rac8的简单办法；对9... a4应10. b5，白象便控制b4。黑方现在试图以...Re7和...Nh7抵抗。

text: Black is tied up on the kingside, and White's best plan consists of trebling on the h-file. White carries out the necessary regrouping in such a way that not only is Black's bishop prevented from penetrating but also his rook's invasion along the c-file is deferred; at the same time, he over-protects the e5-square as a precaution against any desperate sacrifices.
zh: 黑方被牵制在王翼，白方最佳计划是在h线上叠加后双车。白方进行必要的重新部署，既阻止黑象渗透，又延缓黑车沿c线侵入；同时超额保护e5格，防备对手孤注一掷的弃子。

text: Only now, when his rooks are ready for the lethal blow on the h-file, can White touch his pawns.
zh: 只有到现在，双车已准备在h线上发出致命打击，白方才可以动兵。

text: **18... Rec8 19. Rh6 Bd3 20. Qh4 Rc1+ 21. Kf2 Rf1+ 22. Kg3** and Black cannot prevent mate by Rh8+.
zh: **18... Rec8 19. Rh6 Bd3 20. Qh4 Rc1+ 21. Kf2 Rf1+ 22. Kg3**，黑方无法阻止Rh8+将杀。

text: In comparing these two variations, the reader cannot but recognize the essential feature of the position that condemns 1. f4? to failure but brings victory to the attack carried out by the pieces. The move f4 obstructs both the diagonal for the bishop on c1 and the f-file for the rooks, and so limits the possibilities of action along the very two lines on which Black is weak. His weakness on the f-file can be seen at a glance, and it is not difficult to deduce (on examining the diagrammed position) that he will also be weak on the dark squares, since he will be unable to postpone ...g6 for long. After f4 White is left with only his domination of the h-file, whereas if he does not play it, he also has the f-file and a line of action for his bishop, and it is the combination of all these factors that gives him victory.
zh: 比较这两个变化，读者不能不认识到局面的本质：为什么1. f4?失败，而纯粹用棋子进攻却能获胜。f4既堵住c1象的斜线，也堵住车的f线，恰好限制了黑方薄弱的两条线路。f线的弱点一目了然；观察图示局面，也不难推断黑格会弱，因为黑方无法长期推迟...g6。走f4之后，白方便只剩对h线的控制；若不走它，则还有f线和象的活动线路。正是这些因素结合起来，带来胜利。

text: We shall now vary the position of the pawns in front of White's king in the above diagram, so as to train our eyes to be keener in spotting the various finesses contained in this kind of position.
zh: 现在改变前面图中白王面前的兵的位置，训练观察力，更敏锐地发现这类局面中的各种细微之处。

text: First let us suppose that White's f-pawn is already on f4 (instead of f2) and that it is White to move. Now, of course, 1. Rf3 will win at once, but if this possibility is excluded, e.g. by White's having his h-pawn on h3, what then? Even so, White wins — by 1. f5! exf5 (otherwise f6 is decisive) 2. Rxf5, and Black has no answer to the two threats of 3. Rf4 and 3. Qh5+ Kg8 followed by either 4. Nf7 or 4. Rxf8+ Kxf8 5. Qh8+ and the queen mates on g7. If, for example, 2... Qd7, then 3. Qxf8+, while if 2... g6, then 3. Rf4 Qxg5 4. Qxe8.
zh: 首先假设白f兵已经在f4而不在f2，且轮白先。当然，1. Rf3立即取胜；但若排除这种可能，例如白h兵在h3，又如何？白方仍能取胜：1. f5! exf5（否则f6决定胜负）2. Rxf5，黑方无法同时应付3. Rf4及3. Qh5+ Kg8的威胁；后者接4. Nf7，或4. Rxf8+ Kxf8 5. Qh8+，再由后在g7将杀。例如2... Qd7，则3. Qxf8+；若2... g6，则3. Rf4 Qxg5 4. Qxe8。

text: The pawn on f4 wins in this case precisely because it disappears and in doing so immediately opens up the f-file with disastrous consequences for Black.
zh: 这一例中，f4兵之所以能取胜，恰恰因为它消失了，立即打开f线，给黑方带来灾难性后果。

text: Let us now try a variation with the h-pawn at h4 (rather than h2) (D).
zh: 现在试把h兵放在h4而非h2（见图）。

text: This position is fairly promising; White has his f-file and the bishop's diagonal is free as in variation ‘2’, but the h-file has to be opened up by advancing the h-pawn. All White has to do is induce ...g6, after which the task of line opening is made easier and a blocked position averted.
zh: 这个局面颇有希望。和变化“2”一样，白方拥有f线，象的斜线也畅通；但必须推进h兵打开h线。白方只须诱出...g6，此后开线更容易，也能避免局面封闭。

text: White's best is 1. Re1 Qd7 2. Qh5+ Kg8 3. Re3 (forcing ...g6, since it threatens Rf3 and Rxf8+; thus if 3... Nc6 4. Rf3 Nd8, then 5. Rxf8+ Kxf8 6. Qh8+ Ke7 7. Qxg7+ Nf7 8. Nxf7 Rg8 9. Qh7 and White wins) 3... g6 4. Qg4 Nh7 5. Nh3, when he has good prospects.
zh: 白方最佳的是1. Re1 Qd7 2. Qh5+ Kg8 3. Re3（威胁Rf3和Rxf8+，迫使...g6；若3... Nc6 4. Rf3 Nd8，则5. Rxf8+ Kxf8 6. Qh8+ Ke7 7. Qxg7+ Nf7 8. Nxf7 Rg8 9. Qh7，白胜）3... g6 4. Qg4 Nh7 5. Nh3，前景良好。

text: If White's h-pawn is on h3, 1. h4 comes into consideration, with the idea of reaching a similar system to the one above, but with a tempo less.
zh: 如果白h兵在h3，可以考虑1. h4，意图达到类似上述的体系，只是少一个先手。

text: With White's g-pawn on g3 (rather than g2) the problem is more difficult, since the pawn is only in the way there. Perhaps White ought to give perpetual check at once. If 1. Re1, Black plays 1... Nc6, after which 2. Re3 does not work because of 2... Qxg5, while after 2. g4 Qd7 3. Qh5+ Kg8 4. Re3 g6 5. Qh4 Qg7 Black's defences are already in quite good shape.
zh: 若白g兵在g3而非g2，问题就更难，因为这个兵在那里只会碍事。白方也许应该立即长将。若1. Re1，黑方1... Nc6，此后2. Re3因2... Qxg5而不行；若2. g4 Qd7 3. Qh5+ Kg8 4. Re3 g6 5. Qh4 Qg7，黑方的防御已相当完整。

text: Things are different with the g-pawn at g4 (which is, admittedly, impossible after the classic bishop sacrifice, but that does not matter here) (D).
zh: g兵在g4时则不同（诚然，古典弃象后不可能出现这个局面，但这里并不重要）（见图）。

text: In this case the third rank is clear for the rook, and in addition the pawn at g4 also lends force to the thrust f5. As well as the method starting with 1. Re1 (on the pattern of variation ‘2’), still more successful here is 1. f4 (threatening Rf3) 1... Qd7 2. Qh5+ Kg8 3. f5 and White must win. Here, finally, we have a case where an attack using the pawns is correct. One tiny change in the position and already the choice between attacking with pieces or with pawns has swung in favour of the pawns. Such is the sensitivity of the attack on the castled king, and it is now clear how difficult it is to create any more definite rule on this point! Still, I shall attempt to conclude the chapter with a series of tips — which will naturally apply only generally.
zh: 这时第三横线为车畅通无阻，而且g4兵还增强了f5突破的力量。除了按变化“2”的模式从1. Re1开始，这里更有效的是1. f4（威胁Rf3）1... Qd7 2. Qh5+ Kg8 3. f5，白方必胜。终于，我们有了一个用兵进攻正确的例子。局面只变动一点，动子还是动兵的选择就转向了兵。攻击已易位王对细节如此敏感，现在应当清楚，在这一问题上制定更明确的规则多么困难！不过，我仍试着以一组提示结束本章；自然，它们只能一般适用。

text: Ten Practical Tips
zh: 十条实用提示

text: 1) It is an essential condition for any attack on the castled king that the opponent should not be able to counterattack in the centre or on the other side of the board, or rather that his counterattack should not be dangerous and not develop fully before the attack on the castled king. An attack using pawns usually progresses more slowly than one with pieces, since it often contains moves without any immediate threat. So, before embarking on a pawn attack, one should beware particularly of the possibility of a counterattack by one's opponent.
zh: 1）任何攻击已易位王的一个必要条件，是对手无法在中央或另一翼反击；更准确地说，是其反击不应危险，也不能先于王城攻击充分展开。兵的攻击通常比棋子的攻击进展慢，因为常包含没有即时威胁的着法。所以，在发动兵的进攻之前，尤其要警惕对手反击的可能性。

text: 2) A central pawn blockade prevents or limits counterattacks and so makes a pawn attack on the castled king easier.
zh: 2）中央的兵封锁会阻止或限制反击，从而使兵对王城的进攻更容易。

text: 3) One should always examine whether a promising attack can be made by the pieces alone, and if it can, the pawns should be left ‘at home’.
zh: 3）总要考察，仅用棋子能否展开有希望的进攻；如果可以，兵就应该“留在家里”。

text: 4) As a rule, it is difficult for pawn assaults to succeed against unweakened castled positions, since the possibilities of blockade are very great. A preliminary action by the pieces is necessary to produce a weakening of the castled position or to remove the possibility of a later blockade when the pawns advance.
zh: 4）一般而言，兵的冲击很难攻破未经削弱的王城，因为防守方有很大的封锁可能。因此，必须先用棋子行动，削弱王城，或消除随后兵推进时遭到封锁的可能。

text: 5) Every blockade in the castling area radically changes the character of the position, for it affects the activity of individual pieces and the whole nature of the play which follows.
zh: 5）王城区域中的每一次封锁，都会从根本上改变局面的性质，因为它会影响各子力的活跃性，以及随后整个战斗的性质。

text: 6) One's own pawns usually constitute a great obstacle to one's rooks; if a position is characterized by the opponent's weakness on the files, the rooks are important pieces and pawns have no business on these files, except when their advance actually helps to clear a file. Rooks can be particularly usefully deployed on the third rank, if it is clear of pawns (an example of this was provided by the variations arising from the diagram on p.224).
zh: 6）己方的兵通常是车的重大障碍。如果局面的特点是对手在纵线上薄弱，车就是重要子力，兵便不该占着这些线路，除非它们的推进确实有助于清空某条线。没有兵阻挡时，车部署在第三横线特别有用（第224页图示局面的变化就给出了例子）。

text: 7) A pawn storm generally increases the risk of an inferior endgame. If other elements in the position are also weighted against an endgame, the added risk entailed in an attack on the castled king is acceptable. However, if the player has the necessary conditions for a good endgame, he must make certain that his assault with the pawns will be successful, for otherwise it represents a real risk.
zh: 7）兵的猛攻通常会增加进入劣势残局的风险。如果局面中的其他因素也不利于残局，那么为攻击王城而增加的风险可以接受。但如果具备良好残局的条件，就必须确认兵的冲击能够成功，否则便是在冒实实在在的风险。

text: 8) A player who already has an advanced pawn facing his opponent's castled position but which somehow gets in his way (e.g. a pawn on f5) must contemplate advancing the adjacent pawn, so that the lone pawn can be made an active component of an avalanche. Every advanced pawn presents a pretext for an avalanche and draws its neighbour towards it. This is least so in the case of an advanced h-pawn and most so if the pawn is on f5.
zh: 8）如果已经有一个深入敌方王城前方的兵，却多少妨碍己方行动，例如f5兵，就必须考虑推进邻兵，使这个孤独的兵成为雪崩中的活跃部分。每个深入的兵都能成为发动雪崩的契机，吸引邻兵前来。这种作用以深入的h兵最小，以f5兵最大。

text: 9) Attacks on the castled king in general, and those using pawns in particular, should always be judged on the basis of an assessment of the position as a whole. The placing of the pieces, the situation in the centre and on the other side of the board, positional strengths and weaknesses, how far the position is blocked, the prospects for the endgame — all these come into the reckoning which an experienced player must make before deciding to use his pawns in an attack on the castled king.
zh: 9）一般的王城攻击，尤其是用兵的攻击，始终应以对整个局面的评估为判断基础。棋子的位置、中央与另一翼的局势、局面棋方面的长处与弱点、封闭程度、残局前景，这些都是有经验的棋手在决定动兵攻击王城之前必须考虑的因素。

text: 10) Cautious before opening his attack, the player must be incisive, consistent, and merciless once he has set out on his attacking course. For an insufficiently justified attack is not helped by belated doubts, but only by resourcefulness in the struggle to provide one's opponent with the most difficult task possible.
zh: 10）发动进攻之前应谨慎，一旦踏上进攻之路，就必须锐利、贯彻始终、毫不留情。根据不够充分的进攻，不能靠事后的迟疑来补救，只能凭战斗中的机智，尽可能给对手提出最困难的问题。

text: 9 The attack on the fianchettoed and queenside castling positions
zh: 第九章　攻击侧翼出象王城与长易位王城

text: Up till now we have, on the whole, based our examination of the various aspects of attacking play on the ordinary kingside castling position. The fianchettoed and queenside castling positions present certain special characteristics, which affect the particular forms of attack used against these types of position.
zh: 到目前为止，我们对进攻各个方面的考察，基本上都是以普通的短易位王城为基础。侧翼出象王城和长易位王城各有一些特殊特点，影响着针对这些局面所采用的具体攻击形式。

text: The attack on the fianchettoed king position
zh: 攻击侧翼出象王城

text: The term ‘fianchetto’ (from the Italian, meaning ‘little flank’) denotes a bishop being developed on the flank (on g2, b2, g7 or b7), and if a player castles behind such a fianchetto formation, we talk of a fianchettoed king position.
zh: “Fianchetto”一词来自意大利语，意为“小翼侧”，指象在翼侧出子，进入g2、b2、g7或b7。如果王易位到这种阵形后方，我们便称之为侧翼出象王城。

text: Castled positions of this kind have their own particular good and bad sides; these will be examined on the basis of Black's kingside fianchetto position, which occurs in the Dragon Variation of the Sicilian, and the King's Indian and Grünfeld defences.
zh: 这种王城有其特有的优缺点。下面以黑方王翼侧出象的阵形为例加以考察；它常见于西西里防御龙式变例、古印度防御和格林菲尔德防御。

text: The good aspect of the position is, above all, its considerable capacity to resist attack along the diagonal b1-h7, thanks to the pawn formation, f7, g6, and h7; nor are the squares f6 and h6 too weak, for they are covered by the bishop on g7. The bishop is also well concealed against attacks and possibilities of exchange, while in many cases the defence is assisted by its ability to cover not only the squares f6 and h6 but also the possible mating square h8. Finally, the fianchettoed position is also suited for those operations in which the g-pawn disappears, as in the following well-known manoeuvre: Black plays ...f5, and then, on White's reply exf5 he coolly continues ...gxf5, with the aim of strengthening his position in the centre. Without the bishop on g7 such play would be risky because of the opening of the g-file, but it often succeeds with the fianchettoed bishop, since the bishop defends Black's king on the g-file about as well as a pawn does.
zh: 这种局面的优点，首先在于f7、g6、h7兵形使其很能抵抗沿b1-h7斜线的攻击；f6和h6也并不太弱，因为g7象保护着它们。象的位置隐蔽，不易遭到攻击或兑换；许多时候，它除防守f6、h6外，还能保护潜在的将杀格h8，有助于防御。最后，这种阵形也适合g兵离开原来线路的行动，例如以下熟知的调动：黑方走...f5，对白方exf5从容应以...gxf5，意在加强中央。没有g7象时，g线的打开会使这种走法很冒险；但有侧翼象时往往可行，因为象在g线上保护黑王的作用，与兵相差不多。

text: The weak aspect of the fianchettoed position lies in the fact that the position of the g-pawn at g6 simplifies the attacker's task in opening up the h-file by the advance of his h-pawn; there is also a danger that the fianchettoed bishop may be exchanged either for its opposite number or some other enemy unit. Without the bishop the castled position becomes weak and vulnerable and the squares previously covered by the bishop form a typically weak network.
zh: 侧翼出象王城的弱点在于：g兵位于g6，使进攻方更容易推进h兵打开h线；侧翼象也可能被对方同色象或其他子力换掉。没有这只象，王城就变得薄弱而易受攻击，原先由象保护的格子会形成典型的弱格网络。

text: Naturally, an attack on the fianchettoed king position is generally directed against these weak spots, and consequently, the assault by the h-pawn and actions aimed at the exchange of the fianchettoed bishop are the principal weapons in the attack against such a position.
zh: 对侧翼出象王城的攻击，自然通常指向这些弱点。因此，h兵的冲击以及旨在换掉侧翼象的行动，便成为攻击这种局面的主要武器。

text: First, we shall give simple examples of two typical operations: namely, the elimination of the fianchettoed bishop and the breaking up of the pawn structure in front of it.
zh: 先看两种典型行动的简单例子：消灭侧翼象，以及破坏它前面的兵形。
caption_zh: 里希特—阿布拉马维丘斯，汉堡，1930年，白先。

text: The first position is from the game Richter-Abramavicius, Hamburg 1930. It is White's move, and he sacrifices both his rooks for the fianchettoed bishop in order to be able to conclude the game by an attack on the weakened dark-square network.
zh: 第一个局面来自里希特—阿布拉马维丘斯，汉堡，1930年。白先，他用双车换取侧翼象，以便攻击削弱后的黑格网络，结束棋局。

text: **1. Rh8+ Bxh8 2. Rxh8+ Kxh8 3. Qh1+ Nh7 4. Nf6 Kg7**
zh: **1. Rh8+ Bxh8 2. Rxh8+ Kxh8 3. Qh1+ Nh7 4. Nf6 Kg7**

text: Or 4... Qxf6 5. gxf6 Bxd3 6. Qh6 Rxc2+ 7. Kd1 Rg8 8. Ng5 and mates.
zh: 或4... Qxf6 5. gxf6 Bxd3 6. Qh6 Rxc2+ 7. Kd1 Rg8 8. Ng5，接着将杀。

text: The following position occurred in the game Szilagyi-Szabo, Budapest 1946. Black, to move, broke up the pawn chain h2-g3 by a sacrifice and proceeded to decide the game on a network of squares of the opposite colour to that of the fianchettoed bishop.
zh: 下图局面出现在西拉吉—萨博，布达佩斯，1946年。黑先，以弃子破坏h2-g3兵链，继而在与侧翼象异色的格子网络上决定胜负。
caption_zh: 西拉吉—萨博，布达佩斯，1946年，黑先。

text: **1... Rxh2! 2. Kxh2 Ng4+ 3. Kg1 Bxg3 4. Re2**
zh: **1... Rxh2! 2. Kxh2 Ng4+ 3. Kg1 Bxg3 4. Re2**

text: White loses, whatever the continuation, because of his weakness on the corresponding focal-points h2 and f2. Mate can be postponed only by a severe ‘letting of blood’. After 4. Nf3 exf3 5. Bxf3 Qh4 6. Re2 Bf2+ 7. Kf1 Nh2+ 8. Kg2 Qg3+ 9. Kh1 Qxf3+ Black still mates with 10... Qg3+ and 11... Qh3#.
zh: h2与f2这对对应焦点太弱，白方无论如何应对都要输，只有大出血才能推迟被将杀。4. Nf3 exf3 5. Bxf3 Qh4 6. Re2 Bf2+ 7. Kf1 Nh2+ 8. Kg2 Qg3+ 9. Kh1 Qxf3+之后，黑方仍将10... Qg3+再11... Qh3#。

text: For White loses either his rook or his queen.
zh: 因为白方非丢车即丢后。

text: Where there is a fianchettoed king position there is naturally no opportunity to sacrifice the bishop on h7; moreover, many other forms of sacrifice, typical enough in the case of normal castling, are out of the question against the specific structure of the fianchetto. A form of sacrifice which can be designated as characteristic in the case of a fianchettoed king position is that of the knight on f5. An example of such a sacrifice is provided by the next diagram.
zh: 面对侧翼出象王城，自然没有h7弃象的机会；而且，许多在普通王城中很典型的弃子，也不适用于这种特殊结构。针对侧翼出象王城，一种有代表性的弃子是在f5弃马。下图就是一例。
caption_zh: 亚历山大—帕赫曼，希尔弗瑟姆，1947年，白先。

text: This position arose in the game Alexander-Pachman, Hilversum 1947. Against Black's fianchettoed king position White has a knight aggressively placed at g5, a ‘little avalanche’ of pawns on g4 and h4, a rook on g1 and his queen covering some useful squares. Nevertheless, to ‘unlock’ Black's solid position a sacrifice is necessary.
zh: 此局面来自亚历山大—帕赫曼，希尔弗瑟姆，1947年。面对黑方侧翼出象王城，白方有进逼g5的马、g4和h4组成的“小型兵雪崩”、g1车，以及控制若干重要格子的后。尽管如此，要“解锁”黑方坚固的局面，仍须弃子。

text: Given the favourable supporting conditions, this typical ‘anti-fianchetto’ sacrifice is absolutely correct. From f5 the knight controls the squares g7 and h6 and has the intention, above all else, of eliminating the fianchettoed bishop. If Black does not accept the sacrifice but plays, for example, 1... Rae8, White continues 2. Nxg7 and then 3. f4 with good prospects, while if 1... Bf6, then 2. Nh6. The acceptance of the sacrifice leads at once to a critical situation for Black as the reply gxf5 leads to a very dangerous attack, while the f5-square is well covered, and consequently there is no danger of Black making a counter-sacrifice on it.
zh: 支援条件有利，这种典型的“反侧翼象”弃子完全正确。马在f5控制g7和h6，首要目的是消灭侧翼象。若黑方不接受弃子，例如1... Rae8，白方2. Nxg7再3. f4，前景很好；若1... Bf6，则2. Nh6。接受弃子会立即使黑方陷入危局，因为gxf5后的进攻十分危险，而f5格又得到充分保护，黑方无法通过在此反弃子解围。

text: In positions of a similar nature one is often faced with the question whether it is better to take on f5 with the g-pawn or the e-pawn. The answer depends on the various characteristics of the position; one takes with the g-pawn, if the opening of the g-file or the diagonal d1-h5 brings with it a decisive advantage, while in playing exf5 one takes into account other possible advantages, namely, freeing the square e4 (on which a knight, for example, can take up a strong position) or opening the b1-h7 diagonal for the bishop, or perhaps to keep in reserve the continuation g5. In this particular case the g-pawn is obviously indicated, since there is an immediate threat of Qh5.
zh: 类似局面中，经常要判断在f5用g兵还是e兵吃回更好。答案取决于局面的各种特点：如果打开g线或d1-h5斜线能带来决定性优势，就用g兵；而exf5则考虑其他潜在好处，即腾出e4格，例如让马占据强位，或为象打开b1-h7斜线，或保留g5的可能性。本例显然应使用g兵，因为立即威胁Qh5。

text: If 2... h6, then 3. Qh5, threatening 4. Nxf7+ as well as 4. f6. If 2... Ng8, Black does not get as far as consolidating by ...Nf6 because of 3. Nxh7 Kxh7 4. Rxg7+ Kxg7 5. Rg1+.
zh: 若2... h6，则3. Qh5，同时威胁4. Nxf7+和4. f6。若2... Ng8，黑方来不及用...Nf6巩固，因为3. Nxh7 Kxh7 4. Rxg7+ Kxg7 5. Rg1+。
**3. Nxh7 Be8**（见图）
caption_zh: 亚历山大—帕赫曼，3... Be8之后，白先。
