text: The only defence as the queen must not be allowed to reach h5.
zh: 唯一的防御，必须阻止白后进入h5。

text: The fianchettoed bishop's head has to roll!
zh: 侧翼象必须被斩除！

text: When the fianchettoed bishop vanishes from the board, its opposite number usually becomes extremely powerful.
zh: 侧翼象一旦离开棋盘，对方的同色象通常就会变得极其强大。

text: If 7... Kg8, then 8. Rg1+ Ng6 9. Rxg6+ Bxg6 10. Qxg6+ Kh8 11. Qxf6+ Kh7 12. Qg6+ Kh8 and either 13. f6 or 13. Bg5.
zh: 若7... Kg8，则8. Rg1+ Ng6 9. Rxg6+ Bxg6 10. Qxg6+ Kh8 11. Qxf6+ Kh7 12. Qg6+ Kh8，再13. f6或13. Bg5。

text: **8. fxg6+ Kg8 9. Qf5** and White won in a few moves.
zh: **8. fxg6+ Kg8 9. Qf5**，白方数步后获胜。

text: The importance of removing the fianchettoed bishop at the correct moment in this kind of attack is shown by the next position, one which I reached in an analysis of the Dragon Variation of the Sicilian in my book, Contemporary Opening Theory.
zh: 下一局面说明，这类进攻中把握时机消灭侧翼象多么重要。它来自我在《当代开局理论》中对西西里防御龙式变例的分析。

text: In my book I examined 1. Qh4, following it up by 1... bxc3 2. Qh8+ Bxh8 3. Rxh8+ Kg7 4. R1h7#.
zh: 我在书中研究了1. Qh4，接1... bxc3 2. Qh8+ Bxh8 3. Rxh8+ Kg7 4. R1h7#。

text: However, fianchettoed king positions of this kind (with the defensive bishop, the knight on f6, and a pawn on e7) offer a great deal of resistance. Consequently, in spite of the thunder on the h-file, Black can answer 1. Qh4 with 1... Nh5! 2. Bxg7 bxa3! 3. Qg5 (if 3. gxh5, then 3... Kxg7, while if 3. Bd4, then 3... axb2+ 4. Kb1 Qa5) 3... axb2+ 4. Kb1 Kxg7 [note 1], and now if 5. Rxh5, then 5... Ba2+ 6. Kxa2 b1=Q+, while if 5. gxh5, then 5... Qxc3 is in Black's favour.
zh: 不过，具有防守象、f6马和e7兵的这种侧翼出象王城，抵抗力相当强。因此，尽管h线攻声震天，黑方仍可对1. Qh4应1... Nh5! 2. Bxg7 bxa3! 3. Qg5（若3. gxh5，则3... Kxg7；若3. Bd4，则3... axb2+ 4. Kb1 Qa5）3... axb2+ 4. Kb1 Kxg7【注1】；现在若5. Rxh5，则5... Ba2+ 6. Kxa2 b1=Q+；若5. gxh5，则5... Qxc3黑优。

text: [Nunn's note 1] In this line 4... Qxc3! is immediately decisive, since 5. Bxc3 Ba2+ leads to mate.
zh: 【纳恩注1】这一变化中，4... Qxc3!立即决定胜负，因为5. Bxc3 Ba2+导致将杀。

text: Because of this I have had to amend my original analysis of the diagrammed position and apply more drastic measures to eliminate the fianchettoed bishop.
zh: 因此，我必须修正对图示局面的原有分析，采用更激烈的手段消灭侧翼象。

text: Clearly, 1... Nh5 will not do now because of 2. Qxg7+, while if Black tries to parry the threat of 2. Qh8+ by 1... Kf8 2. Qh8+ Ng8, White mates by 3. Qxg8+ and 4. Rh8+.
zh: 显然，现在1... Nh5因2. Qxg7+而不行；若黑方试图1... Kf8 2. Qh8+ Ng8来防止2. Qh8+的威胁，白方则3. Qxg8+再4. Rh8+将杀。

text: After 3. Rh8+ Kg7 4. R1h7+ Kg6 White only has perpetual check, while if 3. Rxf6, Black can reply 3... Bc4 4. Rh8+ Kg7! 5. Rfh6+ e5.
zh: 3. Rh8+ Kg7 4. R1h7+ Kg6之后，白方只有长将；若3. Rxf6，黑方可3... Bc4 4. Rh8+ Kg7! 5. Rfh6+ e5。

text:
Black is also mated after other continuations, e.g.:
1) 3... Bc4 4. Rh8+ Kg7 5. R1h7+ Kg6 6. e5+ Bxd3 7. Rh6+ Kg7 8. exf6+ exf6 9. Bxf6#.
2) 3... d5 4. Rh8+ Kg7 5. R1h7+ Kg6 6. exd5+ Ne4 7. Rg7#.
3) 3... Nh7 4. Rxh7 f6 5. Rh8+ Kf7 6. R1h7+ Kg6 7. e5+ f5 8. gxf5+ Bxf5 9. Rh6+ Kf7 10. e6+ Bxe6 11. R6h7#.
zh:
黑方走其他变化也要被将杀，例如：
1）3... Bc4 4. Rh8+ Kg7 5. R1h7+ Kg6 6. e5+ Bxd3 7. Rh6+ Kg7 8. exf6+ exf6 9. Bxf6#。
2）3... d5 4. Rh8+ Kg7 5. R1h7+ Kg6 6. exd5+ Ne4 7. Rg7#。
3）3... Nh7 4. Rxh7 f6 5. Rh8+ Kf7 6. R1h7+ Kg6 7. e5+ f5 8. gxf5+ Bxf5 9. Rh6+ Kf7 10. e6+ Bxe6 11. R6h7#。

text: The attack on the queenside castled position
zh: 攻击长易位王城

text: Before discussing the attack on the queenside castled position, one should first of all examine the differences between this type of castling and kingside castling. Some writers in the past have supposed that the difference is considerable and that castling long ‘is much weaker than castling short’; this is a great exaggeration. The castled position after long or queenside castling differs from the short castled position only in this respect, that the positions of the king and rook are both a square nearer the centre of the board. This can be useful for the rook, but it usually presents difficulties to the king, which is safer on g1 than c1. Reckoning in terms of tempi, the following picture sums up the differences: the position on the queenside which would correspond symmetrically to the one given by short castling (king on g1 and rook on f1) is king on b1 and rook on c1, and to reach such a position after castling long would require two tempi. But let us now apply a different method of calculation: the player has castled on the kingside and then spends one tempo on the move Re1. The corresponding position to this on the queenside would be king on b1 and rook on d1, and for this only one move is needed after castling long. The conclusion to be drawn from this is simple — whenever the rook is well placed on the d-file, castling long is fundamentally as good as castling short; if the rook is in fact needed on the c-file it is weaker by two tempi, while if the rook is needed on a third square it is weaker by only one tempo.
zh: 讨论如何攻击长易位王城之前，先应考察长、短易位的差别。过去有些作者认为差别很大，声称长易位“远弱于短易位”，这大大夸张了。长易位后的王城与短易位王城，区别仅在于王和车都更靠近中央一格。对车来说这可能有利，对王却通常带来困难，因为王在g1比在c1更安全。从步数来计算，可以这样概括两者的差别：与短易位后王在g1、车在f1对称的后翼局面，是王在b1、车在c1；长易位后要达到这个局面，需要再走两步。不过换一种算法：一方短易位后，再花一步Re1；与之对应的后翼局面应是王在b1、车在d1，而长易位后只须一步就能达到。结论很简单：只要车在d线位置理想，长易位基本上就与短易位一样好；若确实需要车在c线，则差两步；若需要车到其他格子，则只差一步。

text: In practice castling queenside usually occurs when the rook is well placed on the d-file, and indeed the need for it to be placed there is often the prime reason for adopting long castling. When reckoned in these terms, the practical difference between long and short castling disappears or becomes insignificant. There is yet another difference between the two forms of castling, but it is secondary and concerns the activity of the queen. However, here too the advantages and disadvantages tend to cancel each other out. Thus one can say that castling on the queenside is almost equal in status to castling on the kingside in general terms of tempo and security. If there are still players who doubt the security of castling on the queenside, it might be suggested that their reasons for this are probably of a subjective, rather than an objective, nature. That is to say, many players remember some bad experiences which they have had with castling long and are not aware of a very common mistake, one which is repeated over and over again: they accept the tempo gained on the d-file by castling long as a gift, without wanting to pay the price for it; they neglect the consolidating move Kb1, and then, when their opponent suddenly sweeps down, it is already too late and there is no time left. The results, of course, are blamed on queenside castling.
zh: 实战中，通常正是在车位于d线合适时才采用长易位；把车放到那里，往往就是选择长易位的首要原因。这样计算，长、短易位的实际差别便消失，或变得微不足道。两者还有一个关于后活跃性的次要差别，不过其利弊也往往相互抵消。因此，从一般的时间与安全性来看，长易位几乎与短易位地位相等。如果仍有棋手怀疑长易位的安全性，那原因很可能是主观的。他们记得自己长易位时的一些惨痛经历，却没有认识到一个一再重犯的常见错误：把长易位在d线上节省的一步当作无偿礼物，不肯付出应有代价；忽视巩固王城的Kb1，等对手突然扑来，才发现已经太迟，没有时间了。结果当然都归咎于长易位。

text: In master chess castling on the kingside predominates, but this is not the result of some fundamental weakness of castling long; the reasons are of another, structural, kind. Castling on the queenside requires the development of three pieces, while in the case of castling short only two need be moved to clear the back rank. Another important point is that in order to castle on the queenside the queen has to be moved first, and the best moment for doing this in many openings occurs rather later, as moving the queen at an early stage of the game can turn out to be a loss of a tempo. This is an important reason for the comparative rarity of castling on the queenside, and the trend is given further impetus by the structure of modern openings, the majority of which are directed towards a struggle over the central squares. In this the c-pawn plays an important part both in covering the d-pawn and in effecting a lateral attack; this delays the queen's development on the one hand, and also slightly weakens the queenside on the other, consequently reducing the circumstances which favour castling long.
zh: 大师对局中短易位占多数，但并不是因为长易位有什么根本缺陷，而是出于结构方面的原因。长易位须先使三枚棋子出动，短易位则只须移动两枚棋子腾出底线。另一个要点是，长易位前必须先动后，而许多开局中动后的最佳时机来得较晚，因为过早出后可能损失一步。这是长易位较少见的重要原因；现代开局的结构又进一步强化了这一趋势，因为大多数开局都围绕中央格的争夺展开。c兵在其中既保护d兵，又从侧面进攻，作用很大；这既推迟了后的出动，也略微削弱后翼，因此减少了适合长易位的情形。

text: There are quite a few situations in the openings when castling on the queenside can be usefully applied, and in some cases one can say that it in fact represents the best solution to the basic problem of building up the position. We shall now list the main factors which would usually endorse the choice of long castling in a game:
zh: 开局中有不少局面适合长易位；有时可以说，它正是解决布局基本问题的最佳办法。通常支持选择长易位的主要因素如下：

text: 1) The pawn position on the kingside has already been weakened, while that on the queenside is sound; this may incline the player towards castling long. (If castling on the kingside is quite impossible or is obstructed, then naturally there is no choice at all.)
zh: 1）王翼兵形已经削弱，而后翼兵形完好，这可能使棋手倾向长易位。（如果短易位完全不可能，或受到阻碍，那自然就根本无从选择。）

text: 2) The opponent's forces (pieces or pawns, or both) are favourably placed for an attack on the short castled position, but unfavourably for one on the long castled position.
zh: 2）对方的力量，无论是棋子、兵还是两者，位置适合攻击短易位王城，却不适合攻击长易位王城。

text: 3) The kingside is not sufficiently developed, while on the queenside the back rank is already clear. If this is the case when the situation demands castling as soon as possible, then castling takes place on the queenside.
zh: 3）王翼出子尚不充分，而后翼底线已经腾空。如果局势要求尽快易位，此时就选择长易位。

text: 4) One's opponent has castled on the kingside, and the weaknesses in his castled position can only be properly exploited by means of an assault by one or more pawns. If in such a case castling on the queenside is readily available and there are no other factors militating against it, one castles long rather than short. An assault by the h-pawn with the aim of opening up the h-file for the rook is often the answer to a fianchettoed king position, and in this case too castling on the queenside is indicated.
zh: 4）对手已经短易位，其王城弱点只有通过一个或多个兵的冲击才能充分利用。如果此时己方可以方便地长易位，又没有其他不利因素，就应选择长易位。面对侧翼出象王城，常常需要推进h兵、为车打开h线，此时也适宜长易位。

text: 5) A rapid deployment of the rook on the d-file gains an important tempo or some other advantage, and in such a case castling long can afford an excellent solution.
zh: 5）迅速将车部署到d线，可以赢得重要的一步或取得其他优势；此时长易位是极好的解决办法。

text: The factors listed here are only intended as general hints for the player, and the particular characteristics of the actual position should be surveyed each time one makes a choice between castling moves. Black, particularly, should be careful if he intends to castle on the queenside, since experience has shown that the necessary conditions for long castling more often arise for White than for Black. When Black's long castling coincides with short castling by White one gets a case of opposite-side castled positions; this leads to an intensification of the game, which naturally favours the better developed side, and this in the majority of cases is White.
zh: 这些因素只是一般提示；每次选择易位方向，都应考察实际局面的具体特点。黑方打算长易位时尤其要谨慎，因为经验表明，长易位所需的条件在白方局面中出现得更多。黑方长易位、白方短易位，就形成异向易位，使战斗更加激烈；这自然有利于出子较好的一方，而多数情况下是白方。

text: However, caution over deciding to castle on the queenside should not be overdone, since many cases arise where castling long is indicated but where the player does not do so because a prejudice about its risk deters him. Here is an example of unprejudiced castling on the queenside from the game Keres-Reshevsky, World Championship Tournament, The Hague/Moscow 1948:
zh: 不过，决定长易位时也不应过分谨慎，因为许多局面本来适合长易位，棋手却被认为它风险很大的偏见吓退。以下是抛开偏见采用长易位的例子，来自凯列斯—雷舍夫斯基，世界冠军赛，海牙／莫斯科，1948年：
caption_zh: 凯列斯—雷舍夫斯基，海牙／莫斯科，1948年，黑先。

text: Black is to move; his position is apparently inferior, since he is threatened not only by Nxd5 but also Nxb5. Besides this, he has not yet castled, so that he is faced with a double task: to discover a reply to White's threats and also make the time to castle. Here is how Reshevsky solved the problem:
zh: 黑先；局面看起来较差，因为白方既威胁Nxd5，又威胁Nxb5。此外，黑方尚未易位，因此面临双重任务：既要应付白方威胁，又要腾出时间易位。雷舍夫斯基这样解决问题：

text: Black has already shown by 1... g5 that he does not intend to castle on the kingside, and now he gives up his pawn on d5 in order to use castling long to obtain an important tempo and gain control over the central squares d4 and d5 (2... Ne7 would be weak because of 3. Nxb5).
zh: 1... g5已经表明黑方不打算短易位；现在他舍弃d5兵，以便借长易位赢得重要的一步，并控制中央的d4和d5格（2... Ne7因3. Nxb5而较弱）。

text: Black's castling on the queenside in the Open Variation of the Ruy Lopez (which was how this game began) qualifies as a curiosity, and many masters shook their heads when they saw what Reshevsky had done. In this case it was correct to overcome the prejudice about the unsuitability of castling long in the Ruy Lopez, for here this very move provides a happy solution to the problem: it gives Black the time he needs and consolidates his king position better than short castling would. It should also be noticed that the weaknesses at a6 and b5 are not particularly marked, since White does not possess the move a4 which would properly probe them. Another point is that castling long has lent power to Black's g-pawn; its advance to g4 is important in the struggle for the square d4.
zh: 本局从西班牙开局开放变例开始，黑方在这种开局中长易位可谓奇闻，许多大师看到雷舍夫斯基这样走，都摇头不已。但这里抛开“西班牙开局不适合长易位”的偏见是正确的，因为这步恰好圆满解决了问题：既给黑方所需的时间，又比短易位更好地巩固王的位置。还应注意，a6和b5的弱点并不突出，因为白方无法用a4充分攻击它们。此外，长易位还增强了黑方g兵的力量；其推进到g4，对争夺d4格十分重要。

text: The knight here is ‘attacking empty squares,’ but 4. Nc3 would have been no better. The most important point is that White cannot play 4. c4 to support the knight on d5, since it would be answered by 4... g4 5. Nh4 (or 5. Ne1 Nd4 6. Qd3 Bf5) 5... Nd4 6. Qd3, after which either 6... c6 or 6... Bxd5 is in Black's favour.
zh: 这匹马在这里“攻击空格”，但4. Nc3也不会更好。最关键的是，白方不能4. c4支持d5马，因为4... g4 5. Nh4（或5. Ne1 Nd4 6. Qd3 Bf5）5... Nd4 6. Qd3之后，6... c6或6... Bxd5都对黑方有利。

text: If 6. Qe4, then 6... Qa7!, threatening 7... Bf5.

The rest of the game is not of interest to us here; Black's active piece play serves as sufficient compensation for the pawn, there is no question of his castled position being in danger, and it is really White who is in difficulties. In the end White did in fact lose the game after making some rather weak moves.
zh: 本局余下过程与这里的讨论无关；黑方子力活跃，足以补偿少兵，王城完全没有危险，真正困难的是白方。最后白方又下了几步较弱的棋，果然输掉了对局。

text: Our further consideration of the attack on the long castled position will be confined to those features which are specific to queenside castling. This means, in the main, that we need only consider positions where the king is still on c1, since if it has already retired to b1 a position has arisen which corresponds symmetrically to that after castling kingside.
zh: 接下来对长易位王城攻击的考察，只限于长易位独有的特点。主要就是说，只须研究王仍在c1的局面；王若已经退到b1，局面就与短易位王城形成对称对应。
caption_zh: 拉宾诺维奇—罗曼诺夫斯基，莫斯科，1925年，黑先。

text: This position is taken from the game Rabinovich-Romanovsky, Moscow 1925. Black, to move, has no way of preventing exf6 and in desperation plays for a counterattack on the enemy king based on the pattern of Boden's Mate (see p.76).
zh: 这个局面来自拉宾诺维奇—罗曼诺夫斯基，莫斯科，1925年。黑先，无法阻止exf6，只得孤注一掷，依据博登杀王模式（见第76页）反击敌王。

text: White, who has in fact the better of the game, here takes the wrong path and spends a tempo on ‘burying the corpse on f6’ instead of using it to consolidate his threatened king position, e.g. 2. Rxd3! Rxd3 3. Kb1! and if 3... Qc5, then 4. Na4 and finally 5. exf6, etc.
zh: 白方本来占优，却在这里走错了路，花一步“埋葬f6上的尸体”，没有用它巩固受到威胁的王城。例如应2. Rxd3! Rxd3 3. Kb1!，若3... Qc5，则4. Na4，最后才5. exf6，等等。

text: After this second mistake Black has a winning position. White should have played 3. Rxd3 Rxd3 4. Kb1! and if 4... Bxb2, then 5. Na4, or if 4... Rxc3, then 5. bxc3!, when Black can probably draw but cannot achieve more.
zh: 第二次犯错之后，黑方已成胜势。白方应3. Rxd3 Rxd3 4. Kb1!；若4... Bxb2，则5. Na4；若4... Rxc3，则5. bxc3!。黑方大概可以和棋，但无法取得更多。

caption_zh: 拉宾诺维奇—罗曼诺夫斯基，3... Bg6之后，白先。

text: The precious bishop retires and thus stops White playing Ne1 followed by Nc2 with gain of tempo.
zh: 这只宝贵的象撤退，阻止白方Ne1再Nc2带先手调动。

text: While this does not give his opponent much trouble, White's other moves are also of little use. The situation is now typical of attacks on the queenside castling position and a similar arrangement of pieces often arises in practice. So let us look at the whole repertoire of combinations at Black's disposal which lead to mate.
zh: 这步没给对手多少困难，不过白方其他着法也无济于事。现在的局势，是攻击长易位王城的典型情形，实战中常出现类似子力配置。我们来看看黑方可用的整套将杀组合。

text: First, it is clear that White could not play 4. bxa3, because of 4... Qxa3#, with the typical pattern of Boden's Mate. Next, it can be seen that if 4. Qf4, Black has 4... Rac8, threatening 5... Qxc3+ and mate, thanks to the formidable effect of Black's bishops. It is true that White could meet 4... Rac8 with 5. Qe5, but then 5... Qb4 would be decisive. There still remain some other defences, which are worth setting out:
zh: 首先，白方显然不能4. bxa3，因为4... Qxa3#正是典型的博登杀王。其次，若4. Qf4，黑方有4... Rac8，借双象的强大作用，威胁5... Qxc3+并将杀。白方虽可对4... Rac8应5. Qe5，但5... Qb4便决定胜负。还有其他一些值得列出的防御：

text: 1) 4. Rde1 Rxd2! (if 4... Rac8, White would reply 5. Kd1! [note 1]) 5. Kxd2 (5. Nxd2 is also inadequate, e.g. 5... Qxc3+ 6. Kd1 Qc2+ [note 2] 7. Ke2 Qd3+ 8. Kd1 Rc8 9. Re4 Bb4 10. Rxb4 Rc1+ 11. Kxc1 Qc2#) 5... Rd8+ 6. Ke2 Bd3+ 7. Kd1 Be4+! 8. Ke2 (or 8. Nd2 Rxd2+ 9. Kxd2 Qd4+ and mates) 8... Qc4+ 9. Ke3 Rd3+ and Black mates.
zh: 1）4. Rde1 Rxd2!（若4... Rac8，白方应5. Kd1!【注1】）5. Kxd2（5. Nxd2也不够，例如5... Qxc3+ 6. Kd1 Qc2+【注2】7. Ke2 Qd3+ 8. Kd1 Rc8 9. Re4 Bb4 10. Rxb4 Rc1+ 11. Kxc1 Qc2#）5... Rd8+ 6. Ke2 Bd3+ 7. Kd1 Be4+! 8. Ke2（或8. Nd2 Rxd2+ 9. Kxd2 Qd4+，接着将杀）8... Qc4+ 9. Ke3 Rd3+，黑方将杀。

text: [Nunn's note 1] 4... Rac8 also wins as after 5. Kd1 Bxb2 White is defenceless.
zh: 【纳恩注1】4... Rac8同样能赢，因为5. Kd1 Bxb2之后，白方无从防守。

text: [Nunn's note 2] Black can mate in two by 6... Bc2+.
zh: 【纳恩注2】黑方6... Bc2+可两步杀。

text:
2) 4. Rhe1 Rac8 5. Re3 Qb5! (yet another threat arising from the position of the rook at c8!) 6. bxa3 Qb1#.
3) 4. Ne1 Rd4 5. Qg5 Qb4 and mates.
4) 4. Be1! (relatively the best method of defence) 4... Rxd1+ (if 4... Qf5 5. Rxd8+ Rxd8, White has the reply 6. Qe4!) 5. Kxd1 Rd8+ 6. Bd2 (if 6. Kc1, 6... Rd3 is decisive) 6... Bxb2 7. fxg7 Rc8 and White must either give back the piece or consent to 8. Na4 Qc2+ 9. Ke2 Qd3+ 10. Ke1 Bc1! 11. Qb4 a5 12. Qf4 Rc4, when Black wins.
zh:
2）4. Rhe1 Rac8 5. Re3 Qb5!（车在c8又产生一种威胁！）6. bxa3 Qb1#。
3）4. Ne1 Rd4 5. Qg5 Qb4，接着将杀。
4）4. Be1!（相对最好的防御）4... Rxd1+（若4... Qf5 5. Rxd8+ Rxd8，白方有6. Qe4!）5. Kxd1 Rd8+ 6. Bd2（若6. Kc1，6... Rd3决定胜负）6... Bxb2 7. fxg7 Rc8，白方必须归还一子，否则8. Na4 Qc2+ 9. Ke2 Qd3+ 10. Ke1 Bc1! 11. Qb4 a5 12. Qf4 Rc4，黑胜。

text: 5. Qxb5 [note 1] is defeated by 5... Rab8! 6. Qxc5 Bxb2#. Still another of the numerous mating patterns in this kind of position!
zh: 5. Qxb5【注1】遇5... Rab8! 6. Qxc5 Bxb2#败。这类局面中的将杀模式如此丰富，这又是其中一种！

text: [Nunn's note 1] Vuković does not mention the far more resilient defence 5. Qb3, when Black has to play very precisely to retain an advantage: 5... b4 6. Be3 Qc7 7. Rxd8+ Rxd8 8. Nd4 Rb8! 9. bxa3 bxc3 10. Nb5 Qc6 11. a4 a6 12. Qc3 Qxg2 13. Rd1 axb5 and White's king remains extremely exposed.
zh: 【纳恩注1】武科维奇没有提到顽强得多的防御5. Qb3。此后黑方必须十分精确才能保持优势：5... b4 6. Be3 Qc7 7. Rxd8+ Rxd8 8. Nd4 Rb8! 9. bxa3 bxc3 10. Nb5 Qc6 11. a4 a6 12. Qc3 Qxg2 13. Rd1 axb5，白王仍然极其暴露。

text: For if 6. Qb3, then 6... Rac8 and 7... Qb1#.
zh: 因为若6. Qb3，则6... Rac8，再7... Qb1#。
caption_zh: 尤伟—科勒，阿姆斯特丹，1926年，黑先。

text: This position comes from Euwe-Colle, Amsterdam 1926. It is Black's move and he hits at White's castled position by means of a bishop sacrifice.
zh: 此局面来自尤伟—科勒，阿姆斯特丹，1926年。黑先，用弃象打击白方王城。

text: If 3. bxa3, then 3... Ne5, while if 3. Qxd7+ Kf8, White is threatened by ...Qxc3+ and so has no time for Qxb7.
zh: 若3. bxa3，则3... Ne5；若3. Qxd7+ Kf8，白方受到...Qxc3+威胁，来不及Qxb7。

text: If 4. Kxb2, then 4... Qb4+ 5. Kc2 Ne5 6. Nxe5 Be4.
zh: 若4. Kxb2，则4... Qb4+ 5. Kc2 Ne5 6. Nxe5 Be4。

text: **4... Ne5 5. Nxe5 Bd5 6. Qxd5 exd5 7. Nxd7 Ra8 0-1**
zh: **4... Ne5 5. Nxe5 Bd5 6. Qxd5 exd5 7. Nxd7 Ra8 0-1**

text: The following game serves as a demonstration both of how castling queenside forms part of a plan of development and of how an attack can be carried out against such a position.
zh: 下面这盘棋既说明长易位怎样成为出子计划的一部分，也说明如何向这种王城发动攻击。

text:
Lasker – Marshall
St. Petersburg Final, 1914
Petroff Defence
zh:
拉斯克—马歇尔
圣彼得堡决赛，1914年
俄罗斯防御

text: **1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Nxe5 d6 4. Nf3 Nxe4 5. Qe2**
zh: **1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Nxe5 d6 4. Nf3 Nxe4 5. Qe2**

text: Morphy's old move; it is sound enough, though it gives White no more than a microscopic advantage.
zh: 墨菲的老着法；走法稳健，但只能给白方带来极微小的优势。

text: Correct, of course, is 7... Qxe2+ 8. Bxe2 Be7 or 7... Nbd7. Avoiding the exchange of queens favours White, whose position is the better developed. One might say that Lasker knew which opponents it paid to play drawing variations against!
zh: 正确的当然是7... Qxe2+ 8. Bxe2 Be7或7... Nbd7。避免兑后有利于出子更好的白方。可以说，拉斯克知道，对哪些对手采用和棋变化会有好处！

text: **8. Nc3 Nbd7 9. O-O-O**
zh: **8. Nc3 Nbd7 9. O-O-O**

text: Castling on the queenside is completely justified in this position, where the bishop is hemmed in at f1. Moreover, on the d-file the rook supports the d-pawn in moving to d4 and then threatening to advance to d5.
zh: 这个局面中，象被堵在f1，长易位完全合理。而且车在d线上可以支持d兵推进到d4，继而威胁d5。

text: A risky and adventurous move, typical of Lasker's play in the middlegame. The knight clearly has no good way of getting away from the h4-square, a circumstance which could have helped Black to equalize. Better would have been 14. Nd2.
zh: 这是冒险而大胆的一着，很能体现拉斯克的中局风格。马显然没有离开h4的好路，这本可帮助黑方取得均势。较好的是14. Nd2。

text: A decisive mistake. Black should have played 14... Nb6! and if 15. d5 then 15... Bd7. Against other attempts by White, the reply ...Qg5 plays an important part. However, moves like 14... Nb6! were not to Marshall's taste. What he really enjoyed was setting a trap for his opponent!
zh: 决定性错误。黑方应走14... Nb6!，若15. d5，则15... Bd7。对白方其他尝试，...Qg5是重要应着。不过，14... Nb6!这类着法并不合马歇尔口味；他真正喜爱的是给对手设陷阱！

caption_zh: 拉斯克—马歇尔，15... O-O-O之后，白先。

text: Castling is forced, since 15... Qb4 comes to grief after 16. Nxd5 Qxb5 17. Nxc7+. It was probably because of this trap that Marshall played 14... d5?, but Lasker naturally refuses to be diverted by the d-pawn and calmly plays for an attack on the castled position with 16. Qa5 [note 1].
zh: 易位被迫，因为15... Qb4遇16. Nxd5 Qxb5 17. Nxc7+败。马歇尔大概正是为了这个陷阱才走14... d5?，但拉斯克自然不肯被d兵引开，而从容16. Qa5，准备攻击王城【注1】。

text: [Nunn's note 1] Vuković doesn't actually say what the trap is — the point is that after 15... O-O-O, 16. Nxd5 fails to 16... Bxd5 17. Qxd5 Qg5+ 18. Qxg5 hxg5 and the knight is lost.
zh: 【纳恩注1】武科维奇实际上没有说明陷阱是什么。要点在于15... O-O-O之后，16. Nxd5遇16... Bxd5 17. Qxd5 Qg5+ 18. Qxg5 hxg5，白方丢马。

text: Perhaps Lasker even played 14. Nh4!? exactly because he knew Marshall would be tempted to set a trap and thereby get himself ensnared in the attack on the castled king which now follows.
zh: 拉斯克甚至可能正因为知道马歇尔会忍不住设陷阱，才走14. Nh4!?，诱使对手反而落入接下来攻击王城的圈套。

text: Clearly, 16... Kb8 fails against 17. Nb5.
zh: 显然，16... Kb8遇17. Nb5败。

text: A correct bishop sacrifice.
zh: 正确的弃象。

caption_zh: 拉斯克—马歇尔，19... Nb6之后，白先。

text: Now that the black king has moved from c8 to b8, the distinctive character of the queenside castling position no longer exists and the situation is merely a replica of a type of attack used against the short castled position.
zh: 黑王从c8走到b8之后，长易位王城的独有特点已经消失，局面只是某种攻击短易位王城的翻版。

text: An important advantage for the attacker in this position is his ability to bring a rook into action quickly (Rd3-b3), since without this Black could defend himself by ...Nc8 and then ...Bd7.
zh: 这里进攻方的一个重要有利条件，是能迅速以Rd3-b3将车投入战斗；否则，黑方便可...Nc8再...Bd7防守。

text: This move simplifies White's task somewhat. However, Black could not have saved himself even by 20... Nc4 which contains the transparent trap 21. Rb3? Qg5+ 22. Kb1 Nd2+. At the time Lasker had reckoned on defeating 20... Nc4 in the following manner (and this has found its way into the commentaries): 21. Re1? (in order to be able to meet 21... Qg5+ with 22. Re3) 21... Rd6 22. Nxd6 Qxd6 23. Rb3+ Nb6 24. a4 Bc8 25. Re8 Qd7 26. Qb5 Qxb5 27. Rxb5 Kb7? 28. a5 Bd7 29. Rxf8 Rxf8 30. Rb4 and White goes on to capture the knight, after which he is a pawn up in the ending. Let us disregard any doubts about this ending, for Black has a stronger continuation than 27... Kb7, namely 27... Bg7 28. Rxh8 Bxh8; then White must play 29. a5 (otherwise the knight remains alive on b6) whereupon the main line runs 29... Bxd4 30. axb6 c6 31. Rb3 Bxf2 32. b7 (if White allows ...Kb7, then the position is still more favourable for Black) 32... Be6 33. Kd2 c5! 34. Ke2 c4 35. Ra3 Bd4, and it is clearly White rather than Black who has to struggle for a draw. It is interesting to see how the original characteristic of the position (the inability of the knight on h4 to move) again emerges as the decisive factor as soon as the attack on the castled position peters out. Not even the best players are immune from such misfortunes!
zh: 这步使白方的任务略为简单。不过黑方即使走20... Nc4，也无法自救，其中有一个明显的陷阱：21. Rb3? Qg5+ 22. Kb1 Nd2+。当时拉斯克打算用以下方式击败20... Nc4，这个变化也被收入评注：21. Re1?（准备对21... Qg5+应22. Re3）21... Rd6 22. Nxd6 Qxd6 23. Rb3+ Nb6 24. a4 Bc8 25. Re8 Qd7 26. Qb5 Qxb5 27. Rxb5 Kb7? 28. a5 Bd7 29. Rxf8 Rxf8 30. Rb4，随后白方吃马，进入多一兵的残局。姑且不谈这个残局是否可靠，黑方就有比27... Kb7更强的27... Bg7 28. Rxh8 Bxh8；白方于是必须29. a5（否则b6马不会丢），接着主要变化为29... Bxd4 30. axb6 c6 31. Rb3 Bxf2 32. b7（若允许...Kb7，局面对黑方还更有利）32... Be6 33. Kd2 c5! 34. Ke2 c4 35. Ra3 Bd4，显然是白方而非黑方必须为和棋苦战。有趣的是，一旦对王城的进攻消退，局面原有的特点——h4马无法行动——又成为决定性因素。即使最优秀的棋手，也无法免于这样的失算！

text: This game, which was the decisive one in Lasker's victory at St. Petersburg, cannot be left to go on sleeping in the archives of chess history with an inaccurate commentary. Good games should not be allowed to go to their rest without good annotations as their lullabies! Therefore, we must show how in fact White does win after 20... Nc4 (D).
zh: 这盘棋对拉斯克在圣彼得堡夺冠具有决定性意义，不能让它带着不准确的评注，继续沉睡在棋史档案中。好棋要安眠，也该有好评注作摇篮曲！因此，必须说明20... Nc4之后白方究竟怎样取胜（见图）。
caption_zh: 拉斯克—马歇尔，分析变化20... Nc4之后，白先。

text: So that there will be no doubt about it, we shall supply two winning moves, both of them instructive as far as carrying out an attack in this kind of position is concerned.
zh: 为消除疑问，我们给出两种取胜着法；对于如何在这类局面中展开进攻，两者都很有启发。

text: 1) 21. a4! c6 (if 21... Rd6 22. Nxd6 Qxd6 23. Rb3+ Nb6, White wins easily by 24. a5) 22. Rb3! (not 22. Qxc6? because of 22... Qb7, forcing the exchange of queens and thus bringing the attack to a halt; nor does 22. Na7 work, e.g. 22... Qxa7 23. Rb3+ Nb6! 24. Rxb6+ Ka8, when White has to exchange queens, leaving Black once again with the better game; obviously the intermediate 23... Nb6! is the key element here) 22... Qg5+ 23. Kb1 Nd2+ 24. Ka2. Now Black is unable to take the rook on b3 with check, so White wins easily, e.g. 24... Qe7 25. Qb6+ Qb7 26. Qxd8+, etc. [note 1].
zh: 1）21. a4! c6（若21... Rd6 22. Nxd6 Qxd6 23. Rb3+ Nb6，白方24. a5轻松取胜）22. Rb3!（不能22. Qxc6?，因为22... Qb7强迫兑后，使进攻停顿；22. Na7也不行，例如22... Qxa7 23. Rb3+ Nb6! 24. Rxb6+ Ka8，白方必须兑后，黑方再次占优；中间着23... Nb6!显然是关键）22... Qg5+ 23. Kb1 Nd2+ 24. Ka2。现在黑方无法带将吃b3车，因此白方轻松取胜，例如24... Qe7 25. Qb6+ Qb7 26. Qxd8+等【注1】。

text: [Nunn's note 1] Black's best defence is 24... Rd7, when White must find 25. f4! Qf6 (25... gxf3 26. Nxf3 deflects the knight from the attack on b3) 26. Rc3! to keep an advantage.
zh: 【纳恩注1】黑方最佳防御是24... Rd7，白方必须找到25. f4! Qf6（25... gxf3 26. Nxf3使马无法攻击b3）26. Rc3!，才能保持优势。

text: 2) 21. Na7! [note 2] Rd6 22. Rb3+ Nb6 (forced, since 22... Rb6 is defeated by 23. Nc6#) 23. a4 Bg7 (or 23... Qd7 24. Nb5! Rc6 25. Qa7+ Kc8 26. a5) 24. Nb5! and White wins.

[Nunn's note 2] Recent analysis by Kasparov reveals a third possibility: 21. Rb3 Qg5+ 22. Kb1 Nd2+ 23. Ka1 Nxb3+ 24. cxb3 Bd6 25. Qa7+ Kc8 26. Nxd6+ Rxd6 (26... cxd6 27. f4! gxf3 28. Nxf3 and the rook reaches c1) 27. Qa8+ Kd7 28. Qxh8 with two extra pawns.
zh: 【纳恩注2】卡斯帕罗夫当时的新近分析指出了第三种可能：21. Rb3 Qg5+ 22. Kb1 Nd2+ 23. Ka1 Nxb3+ 24. cxb3 Bd6 25. Qa7+ Kc8 26. Nxd6+ Rxd6（26... cxd6 27. f4! gxf3 28. Nxf3，车将进入c1）27. Qa8+ Kd7 28. Qxh8，白方多两兵。

text: 29... Kc8 30. Qa8+ Bb8 leads to the picturesque 31. Qa6#. In this ‘posthumous finale’ of the game Black's king and rook are back once again in the original long castling position!
zh: 29... Kc8 30. Qa8+ Bb8，便出现如画的31. Qa6#。在这个“赛后终曲”中，黑王和车又回到了长易位刚完成时的位置！

text: 10 Defending against the attack on the castled king
zh: 第十章　防御对王城的攻击

text: In presenting, up to here, the various aspects of the attack on the castled king we have looked at the operation from the attacker's point of view. However, it is also true that the defence against such an attack has its own principles and particular characteristics, and it is therefore fitting that we should also try to discuss this defence systematically.
zh: 前面介绍攻击王城的各个方面时，我们一直从进攻方的角度考察。然而，防御这种攻击也有自己的原则和特点，因此也应当尝试作系统的讨论。

text: Chess literature tends for the most part to talk of active and passive defence as being the two main types of defence. Steinitz also introduced the term 'self-defence', and H. Kmoch (in his work The Art of Defence) speaks of 'automatic defence'. Although it is now fairly well established, this division is not really the happiest one for teaching purposes; moreover, when it is a question of defence against an attack on the castled king, it is an imprecise one.
zh: 棋书大多把积极防御和消极防御作为两大类型。斯坦尼茨还提出过“自我防御”这个术语，H. 克莫赫则在《防御的艺术》中谈到“自动防御”。这种分类虽然已经相当通行，但从教学角度看并非最恰当；用来讨论王城防御时，它也不够精确。

text: I think it better to talk of direct and indirect defence of the castled position, in which case the direct defence is predominantly 'passive' and the indirect always 'active'. The difference between these kinds of defence is usually clearly marked, since the former involves the defence of the actual castling area or the removal of one's opponent's aggressive pieces, while in the latter case it is a question of actions further away from the castled position, which the defender uses to keep the attacker so busy that he fails to pursue his attack to its conclusion.
zh: 我认为把王城防御分为直接防御和间接防御更好：直接防御主要是“消极的”，间接防御则始终是“积极的”。二者的区别通常很明确：前者是在王城区域本身进行防守，或消除对手的攻击子力；后者则在离王城较远的地方采取行动，使进攻方忙于应付，无法把攻势贯彻到底。

text: In actual play direct defensive moves usually occur in conjunction with those of an indirect kind, and the main rule is that direct defence should be economical and that indirect should be executed at the right moment. Economy in direct defence consists of not making superfluous moves and not employing an unnecessarily large number of pieces in defence. The right moment for indirect defence is fairly difficult to gauge, since it is normally determined by two interacting factors; on the one hand, when direct defence has reached the limits that necessary economy allows, and on the other, when the attacker has really made a move which commits him fairly strongly, i.e. he has staked his money on the success of the attack.
zh: 实战中，直接防御的着法通常与间接防御配合使用。主要原则是：直接防御应当节约，间接防御应当适时。所谓节约，就是不走多余的棋，不投入不必要的过多子力。间接防御的恰当时机比较难判断，因为通常取决于两个相互作用的因素：一方面，直接防御已达到必要的节约原则所允许的限度；另一方面，进攻方确实走出了使自己作出较大投入、受到较强约束的一着，也就是把赌注押在进攻成功上。

text: First, we shall set out clearly the various elements which go to make up each type of defence.
zh: 下面先把构成两类防御的各种要素明确列出。

text: A. Direct Defence
zh: A. 直接防御

text: 1) Protecting the squares of the castled position, including so-called over-protection.
zh: 1）保护王城区域的各格，包括所谓超额保护。

text: 2) Transforming the castled position by moving the pawns in front of the king, a particular case being the setting-up of a blocked position.
zh: 2）通过调动王前兵来改变王城结构，其中一种特殊情况是建立封闭局面。

text: 3) Altering the castled position by moving the king. Here it should be kept in mind that each move by the king changes the situation, changes the conditions necessary for an attack and, above all, changes the possible focal-points. King moves fall into the following graded categories:
zh: 3）通过动王改变王城局面。应当牢记，每动一次王，局势都会改变，进攻所需条件也会改变，尤其是可能的焦点会发生变化。动王可以按程度分成以下几类：

text: a) The consolidating move (e.g. Kb1 in the case of queenside castling and Kh1 in the case of kingside castling);
zh: a）巩固性的动王，例如长易位后的Kb1、短易位后的Kh1；

text: b) A more radical alteration of the situation as a result of moving the king (e.g. to f2, thus producing a so-called 'semi-castled' position);
zh: b）动王使局面发生更根本的变化，例如走到f2格，形成所谓“半易位”局面；

text: c) A king's flight, i.e. when it goes out in front of the castled position. Steinitz called this the king's self-defence, an older and more correct term than that of 'automatic defence' applied by Kmoch.
zh: c）王的出逃，即王走到王城前方。斯坦尼茨称之为王的自我防御；这个术语比克莫赫采用的“自动防御”出现得更早，也更准确。

text: 4) Defence by means of repulsing one's opponent's pieces, through their capture, exchange, or ejection from powerful positions.
zh: 4）通过吃掉、交换或赶离强格等办法，击退对方棋子来防御。

text: B. Indirect Defence
zh: B. 间接防御

text: Before considering the ways of using the indirect method we must first of all examine three aspects of such a defence. The first is purely spatial, i.e. whether the defender carries out his own counterattack in the centre or on the wings; the second is concerned with the degree of the threat; and the third with the question of whether the indirect action turns at some point into the direct method of defence. In the following review we shall combine these three aspects:
zh: 讨论间接防御的运用之前，必须先考察三个方面：第一是纯粹的空间问题，即防守方是在中心还是在侧翼反击；第二是威胁的程度；第三是间接行动是否会在某一时刻转变为直接防御。下面把这三方面结合起来考察：

text: l) The defender carries out a counterattack on the opposite side, where the attacker has castled. In such a case his action is usually itself an attack on the castled king, the position being one where the players have castled on opposite sides.
zh: 1）防守方在另一翼，即进攻方王城所在的一翼发起反攻。这种情况下，他的行动通常本身也是攻击王城，双方处于异侧易位的局面。

text: 2) An action on the opposite side first of all prepares the ground (files, ranks, etc.), and then turns into an outflanking manoeuvre against the attacker's castled position, i.e. while the attacker is attacking along the files, the defender gains control of the attacker's first or second rank.
zh: 2）先在另一翼准备阵地条件，例如开放线、横线等，然后迂回攻击对方王城。也就是说，进攻方沿直线进攻时，防守方控制对方第一或第二横线。

text: In this case, as in '1', the critical question is naturally either who will be the first to force mate or which of the two attacks will be brought to a halt through the diversion of pieces to provide a direct defence.
zh: 这一情况与第1项一样，关键自然在于谁先强制将杀，或者哪一方因必须抽调子力直接防守而中断进攻。

text: 3) An action on any part of the board with the aim of gaining material. Such an action obviously only has a point when a forced mate is not part of the attacker's plan. The critical continuation then is that which costs the defender the least. For instance, if he can 'pacify the attacker's wrath' at the price of a knight, then a counterattack which brings him a rook is worthwhile.
zh: 3）在棋盘任何区域采取以得子为目的的行动。只有进攻方不能按计划强制将杀时，这种行动才有意义。关键在于选择让防守方付出最小代价的后续。例如，若弃一匹马就能“平息进攻方的怒火”，那么能赢得一辆车的反击就是值得的。

text: In practice the most important case is where the attacker sacrifices; the defender's repertoire is then greatly increased, since he is given various ways in which to return material in order to counter the attacker's plan. This method of returning material is extremely important; the extent to which it is possible affects the type of sacrifice which can be made, and the sacrifice is also a signal to the defender to counter with a sacrifice which would previously have been out of the question.
zh: 实战中最重要的是进攻方弃子的情况。防守方的选择由此大为增加，因为他可以用各种方式归还子力，抵消对方的计划。这种归还子力的方法极其重要：有多少归还的可能，会影响进攻方可以采用哪种弃子；而对方弃子也向防守方发出信号，使他可以用先前根本不能考虑的弃子来反击。

text: 4) The counterattack results in material equality, but the question of position still remains open. Mate cannot be forced, both attacks are brought to a halt, and eventual simplification leads towards an ending. The resulting position, which is often extremely difficult to assess beforehand, is then decisive.
zh: 4）反攻后子力相等，但局面优劣仍未确定。双方都无法强制将杀，两个攻势都被遏止，随后简化趋向残局。此时，所得局面的性质便具有决定意义，而这一局面事前往往极难判断。

text: 5) The defender's counterattack does not lead to a mating attack, nor to material or positional advantages, but instead consists of an eventual transition to the direct method.
zh: 5）防守方的反击既不形成杀王攻势，也不取得子力或局面优势，而是最终转为直接防御。

text: As a rule, this takes the form of either attacking the enemy pieces 'from the rear' or of gaining control of a file or diagonal so as to cover a certain square in one's king position (e.g. when the white queen has captured the square c7 and from there covers the focal-point h2).
zh: 通常表现为“从背后”攻击敌子，或控制某条直线、斜线，从而保护己方王城中的某格；例如白后占据c7格，并从那里保护h2焦点。

text: 6) A special case of the kind of counterattack mentioned in '3' is provided by the advance of a queenside pawn majority. Its aim is to promote a pawn to a queen, and such an advantage justifies the most generous surrender of material in order to curb the attacker's forces.
zh: 6）第3项反击的一种特殊形式，是推进后翼多兵。目标是升后；这种收益足以证明，为遏制进攻子力而大量交还子力是合理的。

text: 7) Retaliation in the centre can have the features of sections '3' to '5' either separately or combined. The following possibilities are particularly worth noting here:
zh: 7）在中心反击，可以分别或同时具有第3至5项的特点。以下几种可能尤其值得注意：

text: a) A central thrust demolishes or weakens the attacker's formation there and prepares the ground for further operations by the defender, or it enables him to transpose to direct defence 'via a turning manoeuvre' ;
zh: a）中心突击摧毁或削弱进攻方在那里的阵形，为防守方进一步行动铺路，或使他能“通过迂回调动”转入直接防御；

text: b) The destruction of the pawn centre eliminates its auxiliary function with regard to an attack on the castled king. For example, the disappearance of a pawn on e5 can also mean the end of an attack on the castled king, if the pawn is vital to a certain continuation;
zh: b）摧毁兵中心，便消除了它对攻击王城的辅助作用。例如，若某条变化必须依靠e5兵，那么该兵消失可能就意味着攻势结束；

text: c) Because of the danger of a central thrust, many attackers at a suitable moment deliberately create a blocked position in the centre. As a rule such a central formation cannot be rapidly activated except by the sacrifice of a piece. If the attacker has already used a sacrifice in attack, the defender is presented with an opportunity of making a return sacrifice in the centre. For example, the defender's knight on c6 is sacrificed for White's pawns on e5 and d4, thereby creating the necessary conditions for various kinds of defence without loss of material;
zh: c）由于中心突击的危险，许多进攻者会在适当时刻主动封闭中心。通常，若不弃子，这种中心阵形无法迅速活跃起来。如果进攻方已经弃子，防守方就有机会在中心回弃。例如，防守方把c6马换取白方e5、d4两兵，由此在不亏损子力的前提下，为各种防御创造必要条件；

text: d) The destruction of the attacker's centre usually gives the defender the prospect of better conditions for positional play, as mentioned in section '4'. For it is not only that the opponent's centre pawns disappear, but the actual central squares also come under the defender's control; consequently, if the attack is held, the considerable positional advantage enjoyed by the defender persists, even when the material is equally balanced, until well into the endgame.
zh: d）摧毁进攻方的中心，通常会像第4项所说的那样，使防守方获得更有利的局面棋条件。不仅对方的中心兵消失，中心格本身也落入防守方控制。因此，只要挡住攻势，即使子力相等，防守方的显著局面优势仍会一直保持到残局深处。

text: This outline of defensive methods brings out above all else the richness of their variety and the flexible way in which they can be combined. Because of this, defence as a whole is harder than attack, and its finesses are as a rule more concealed than those of the attacker, a point already noticed long ago by Lasker. The importance of the centre must be particularly emphasized as the critical area where the decisive step is often made. The great variety of possibilities afforded by a defence based on an action against the centre gives such an operation first place in the defender's repertoire, and so every attacker must be able to calculate accurately what is likely to happen in the centre during an attack on the castled king.
zh: 上述防御方法的概述，首先体现了手段之丰富及其组合之灵活。因此总体而言，防御比进攻困难，防守的精妙之处通常也比进攻方更隐蔽；拉斯克早已注意到这一点。尤其必须强调中心的重要性，因为决定性的步骤往往发生在那里。针对中心采取行动，能给防守带来极其丰富的可能性，因此这种行动在防守方的手段中应居首位。每位进攻者都必须准确算清：攻击王城期间，中心可能发生什么。

text: Defence by over-protection
zh: 以超额保护防御

text: Passing now to some examples of direct defence, let us examine the following position, which can arise in the Closed Defence to the Ruy Lopez.
zh: 下面考察直接防御的实例。先看下面这个可能出现在西班牙开局封闭防御中的局面。

text: It is Black's move; he has to think how to supplement the direct defence of his king position, especially in view of White's threat of 1. Nh2 followed by 2. f4 and 3. f5. Black plays:
zh: 轮黑走。他必须考虑如何加强王城的直接防御，尤其要应付白方1. Nh2，接着2. f4、3. f5的威胁。黑方走：

text: Now 3. f4 can be met by 3... Nf7. Moreover, he can also answer most other moves by 3... Nf7, setting up a distinctive position with a 'double knight fianchetto'.
zh: 现在3. f4可以用3... Nf7应对。大多数其他着法也可用3... Nf7，形成一种独特的“双马侧翼出子”阵形。

text: This position offers very strong resistance against all kinds of attack, and the reason for this lies in the over-protection of the squares f5, g5, and h5, at which points White might have been able to execute a breakthrough. These squares are now covered both by Black's pawns and his knights, an example of 'prophylactic over-protection' , to use Nimzowitsch's phrase.
zh: 这个局面对各种进攻都有很强的抵抗力，原因在于对白方可能突破的f5、g5、h5三格实行了超额保护。黑兵与黑马同时控制这些格子；借用尼姆佐维奇的术语，这就是“预防性超额保护”。

text: The over-protection which Black achieves by transferring his knight to f7 is in this case neither a passive nor an uneconomical means of defence. It is not difficult to establish that Black's knight on b7 has no better position anywhere than on f7 (if ...c4, for example, White plays b4 and does not allow ...Nc5); it is better to use the knight for defence, freeing Black's other pieces for later queenside activity. In some cases over-protection can mean economical direct defence; on the other hand, depending on the position, it may be superfluous.
zh: 在这里，黑方把马调到f7实现超额保护，既非消极，也不浪费子力。不难看出，b7马没有比f7更好的去处；例如...c4，白方就走b4，不让黑方...Nc5。因此，用马防守，让其他黑子能够随后在后翼活动，更为合理。有时超额保护就是节约的直接防御；另一方面，也可能因局面而显得多余。

text: Defence by blockade
zh: 以封锁防御

text: A blocked pawn formation means a general reduction in the number of actions possible in any position, and as a result blockade is often the weapon employed by the weaker side. A means of defence which stands out as particularly important is the blockade of the pawns in front of the king.
zh: 无论什么局面，封闭的兵形都会普遍减少可行的行动，所以劣势一方常把封锁作为武器。其中尤其重要的一种防御手段，是把王前的兵封闭起来。

text: The continuation from the above position shows us first of all a typical case of defence by blockade, and then the way to overcome this method of defence.
zh: 从上图继续，可以先看到一个典型的封锁防御实例，再看到克服这种防御的方法。

text: Although White has the superior position with all his pieces directed against Black's kingside, he still can not achieve anything by 'normal' methods. If 1. g6, Black plays 1... h6, while if I h6, then 1... g6; in both cases blocking the pawns brings the attack to a halt. Attempts to break through by sacrificing a knight can simply be ignored by Black. Thus after I g6 h6 2. Nf3 Bd7 3. Ng5 Black does not take the knight but waits; while if I h6 g6 2. Nh5, Black again does not need to take, for by playing 2... Kh8 3. Nf6 Qf7 he can hold the draw.
zh: 白方局面占优，全部子力都瞄准黑方王翼，但用“常规”办法仍无所获。1. g6，黑方走1... h6；1. h6则1... g6。两种情况下，封闭兵形都会使攻势停顿。试图弃马突破，黑方完全可以不予理会：1. g6 h6 2. Nf3 Bd7 3. Ng5，黑方不吃马而等待；1. h6 g6 2. Nh5，黑方也不必吃，只要2... Kh8 3. Nf6 Qf7就能守和。

text: White's only chance in this position is:
zh: 这个局面白方唯一的机会是：

text: 1. Nhg6 Bd7
zh: 1. Nhg6 Bd7

text: Clearly, the knight cannot be taken. 1... Kf7 is met by 2. h6 and a breakthrough, since if 2... hxg6, then 3. h7 Be7 4. Qh4 followed by 5. Nxg6.
zh: 显然不能吃马。1... Kf7可用2. h6突破，因为2... hxg6之后3. h7 Be7 4. Qh4，接着5. Nxg6。

text: 2. Rgh1!
zh: 2. Rgh1!

text: White must play with great precision and thoroughly prepare for the breakthrough by h6 and hxg7. If he tries 2. h6 immediately, then Black replies 2... hxg6; then 3. hxg7 Bxg7 is not dangerous [Nunn note 1], while after 3. h7+ Kh8 4. Rh6 gxh6 5. gxh6 White's attack will probably not succeed.
zh: 白方必须走得非常精确，充分准备h6、hxg7的突破。立即2. h6，黑方就2... hxg6；3. hxg7 Bxg7并不危险〔纳恩注1〕；3. h7+ Kh8 4. Rh6 gxh6 5. gxh6之后，白方进攻恐怕也不能成功。

text: 2... c6 3. Qh2 Rb7 4. h6 hxg6 5. hxg7 Bxg7 6. Rh8+ and White wins.
zh: 2... c6 3. Qh2 Rb7 4. h6 hxg6 5. hxg7 Bxg7 6. Rh8+，白胜。

text: Defence by elimination
zh: 以消除攻击子力防御

text: Many examples could be given of defence based on the diversion or elimination of important attacking pieces, since such operations are often undertaken; however, they are limited on the whole to one or two moves and do not normally provide a complete system of defence but only force the attacker to remodel or reorganize his attack. Thus, for example, in the quite normal case where the attacker's knight has to retreat from g5 when faced with ...h6, the problem of defence has not as a rule been fundamentally solved, but rather the attacker has been obliged to redirect his attack, either by transferring his target from h7 to h6 or g7 or else by strengthening the pressure on h7 along the diagonal b1-h7. Special examples and analysis are not necessary in the case of such straightforward diversion of opposing pieces. We are interested here in those special cases when the diversion or elimination of the attacker's pieces represents the essence of the defence and is in fact fundamental in driving back the attacking force. The simplest example of this is the exchange of queens, which is usually to the advantage of the defender and in many cases altogether eliminates the danger of attack. The queen is generally an essential piece in a mating attack and it is therefore useful to the defender if it is removed. However, other pieces too can be essential to an attack and can be the target of a defensive plan based on elimination. One of the most typical instances involves the attacker's bishop which is covering a network of weak squares. Such a visitor should, as soon as circumstances permit, be dismissed from the castling area or be eliminated by exchange. The following diagram shows a case of a bishop commanding a network of squares, and we give two possible continuations: the one actually taken, where Black misses the opportunity to defend himself by tackling the bishop; and an alternative one, which indicates the correct method of defence.
zh: 引离或消除重要攻击子力的防御实例很多，因为实战中经常采取这类行动。不过，这通常只涉及一两着，不能构成完整的防御体系，只是迫使进攻方重塑或重新组织攻势。例如，进攻方g5马遇到...h6不得不后退，这种常见情况通常没有从根本上解决防守问题，只是迫使进攻方改变进攻方向：把目标从h7转到h6或g7，或沿b1—h7斜线加强对h7的压力。这类简单的驱离无需专门举例分析。这里关心的是一些特殊情形：引离或消除进攻子力本身就是防御的实质，是击退进攻力量的根本。最简单的例子就是兑后。这通常有利于防守方，而且常能彻底消除进攻危险。后一般是杀王攻势中的必需子力，因此消除它对防守方很有帮助。然而，其他棋子也可能是进攻所必需的，从而成为消除式防御计划的目标。其中最典型的是控制弱格网络的进攻方象。条件一旦允许，就应把这个来客赶出王城，或者兑掉。下图是一只象控制弱格网络的例子。我们给出两种后续：实战中黑方错过了针对这只象进行防御的机会；另一条变化则说明正确的防御方法。
caption_zh: 布莱克本—施瓦茨，柏林，1881年；白先。

text: 1 Although after 4. Qh4 followed by Qh7+ White wins the g6-pawn, when the resulting position appears very unpleasant for Black. However, it is true that White risks nothing by building his position up further before playing h6.
zh: 〔纳恩注1〕不过，4. Qh4之后接Qh7+，白方可以赢得g6兵，所得局面对黑方似乎很难受。但白方先进一步加强阵形，再走h6，确实没有任何风险。

text: This position comes from the game Blackburne-Schwarz, Berlin 1881, and it is White's move. He is a pawn down and, in addition, he has the inferior pawn structure. On the other hand, he enjoys far greater activity for his pieces and has prospects of controlling the network of weak dark squares around the enemy king. It is exactly with this in mind that he plays:
zh: 此局面出自布莱克本—施瓦茨，柏林，1881年，轮白走〔纳恩注1〕。白方少一兵，兵形也较差，但子力活跃得多，而且有希望控制黑王周围的黑格弱格网络。正是为了这一目标，白方走：

text: 1. Bf6 Nf4+?
zh: 1. Bf6 Nf4+?

text: Black throws away the chance of defending himself by eliminating the bishop on f6 (with 1... Be7!) and falls into a trap.
zh: 黑方放弃了用1... Be7!消除f6象进行防御的机会，落入陷阱。

text: 2. Qxf4! Bxf4 3. Rxh5 gxh5 4. Rxh5 and there is no remedy against mate on h8.
zh: 2. Qxf4! Bxf4 3. Rxh5 gxh5 4. Rxh5，h8格的将杀已无法防御。

text: In the original edition, this diagram was incorrectly given without the black pawn on b5. Vuković's comments have been modified to take account of this correction.
zh: 〔纳恩注1〕原版的这幅图漏画了b5黑兵。武科维奇的评注已相应修改，以反映这一订正。

text: The essential attacking piece here is the bishop on f6 and it should have been eliminated. Therefore the only correct course is 1... Be7! (D).
zh: 这里必不可少的攻击子力是f6象，应当把它消除。因此唯一正确的走法是1... Be7!（见图）。
caption_zh: 布莱克本—施瓦茨分析，1... Be7后。

text: After 2. Be5 (or 2. Bxe6 fxe6 3. Qg5 Bxf6 4. Qxf6 Qd8! and Black is the better placed) 2... Bd6 White has nothing better than 3. Bf6 and a repetition of moves; on any other move the elimination of White's dark-squared bishop affords Black a complete defence and the prospect of victory on the basis of his other advantages. Thus after 3. f4 Bxe5 4. dxe5 Ng7 White has nothing, while he is too weak for 3. Rxh5? because of 3... gxh5 4. Rxh5 Bxe5 5. dxe5 Rd4, whereupon the threat of ...Nf4+ destroys all his hopes.
zh: 2. Be5（或2. Bxe6 fxe6 3. Qg5 Bxf6 4. Qxf6 Qd8!，黑优）2... Bd6之后，白方没有比3. Bf6重复局面更好的办法。白方走其他着法，黑方就能消除黑格象，获得完整防御，并凭其他优势争胜。因此3. f4 Bxe5 4. dxe5 Ng7，白方无所得；3. Rxh5?的力量也不足，因为3... gxh5 4. Rxh5 Bxe5 5. dxe5 Rd4，随后...Nf4+的威胁打破他的一切希望。

text: Before we leave the theme of defence by elimination, the reader must be warned of the mistakes which are often made in applying this method. Many players defend themselves by endeavouring to exchange all the attacker's aggressive pieces. Such a formula can easily lead to defeat. As a rule, one should aim to exchange those pieces which are essential to the execution of the attacker's mating threats, while on the other hand one should preserve those of one's own pieces which are carrying out an important defensive function. We have already seen how important it is to preserve the fianchettoed bishop, and much the same can be said for a knight at f6 covering the important square h7.
zh: 结束这一主题前，必须提醒读者注意运用这种方法时常犯的错误。许多棋手试图兑掉对方所有攻击子力来防御。照此行事，很容易输棋。通常应争取兑掉对方实现将杀威胁必需的子力，同时保留己方承担重要防守任务的棋子。我们已经看过保留侧翼象有多么重要；对保护h7要格的f6马，也可以作类似判断。

text: The king's self-defence
zh: 王的自我防御

text: There is a graded scale which can be applied to the king's self-defence starting from the so-called consolidating move and ending with the full flight of the king to the other side of the board. Examples have already been given of the former type, so we shall begin with cases where the king is already definitely on the move, even though it may only be along the edge of the castling area. The next diagram is a typical example of self-defence by classically simple means: faced with White’s pressure on h7, Black defends his pawn by advancing it and is not concerned about the square h7 itself; Black’s king reduces the value of the square by moving, for it no longer comes into consideration as a focal-point.
zh: 王的自我防御有一系列程度不同的形式，从所谓巩固性的动王，一直到王彻底逃往棋盘另一翼。前一种已举过例，因此这里从王已经明确开始转移的情况谈起，尽管它可能只沿王城边缘移动。下图是以经典而简单的方法自卫的典型：面对白方对h7的压力，黑方把兵挺起来保护，并不在意h7格本身；黑王一走，这个格就不再作为焦点考虑，其价值随之降低。
caption_zh: 波戈留波夫—列蒂，卡尔斯巴德，1923年；黑先。

text: This position is from Bogoljubow-Réti, Carlsbad 1923. Black played:
zh: 此局面出自波戈留波夫—列蒂，卡尔斯巴德，1923年。黑方走：

text: 1... h6! 2. Bxf6 Bxf6 3. Qh7+ Kf8
zh: 1... h6! 2. Bxf6 Bxf6 3. Qh7+ Kf8

text: The Black king defends itself by flight; if now 4. Qh8+ Ke7, White's position would only be made worse by his loss of a tempo. In the actual game White's initiative dissolved after 4. Rcd1 Red8 5. Kh1 Ke7 6. Nce2 Rh8 7. Qc2 a5, and, thanks to the good self-defence effected by his king, Black soon obtained rather the better game.
zh: 黑王通过逃跑自卫。若4. Qh8+ Ke7，白方只是浪费一步，使自己局面更坏。实战4. Rcd1 Red8 5. Kh1 Ke7 6. Nce2 Rh8 7. Qc2 a5之后，白方的主动权消失了。由于黑王很好地实现了自我防御，黑方很快反而略占上风。

text: Another example of self-defence can be provided by my analysis of one of the critical positions in the game Reshevsky-Botvinnik, World Championship Tournament, The Hague/Moscow 1948.
zh: 我的另一段分析，也能说明王的自卫。局面来自雷舍夫斯基—鲍特维尼克，1948年海牙／莫斯科世界冠军赛的一个关键时刻。
caption_zh: 雷舍夫斯基—鲍特维尼克，世界冠军赛，1948年；黑先。

text: Botvinnik (Black) played here 1... Ng8?, which is an absolutely passive method of defence. It means that Black's king is left in the corner, and White is offered the chance to prepare the opening of the e-file by a pawn sacrifice based on Bf6+. After the moves 2. Re1 Qf7 3. c3 Na5 4. Nf4 Rc6 White made the mistake of playing 5. Bf6+ too early, without the preparatory 5. Rge3!, and thus did not make correct use of Black's error; we will therefore not concern ourselves with the game's actual course.
zh: 鲍特维尼克执黑走了1... Ng8?，是完全消极的防御。黑王仍困在角落，白方得以准备基于Bf6+的弃兵，打开e线。2. Re1 Qf7 3. c3 Na5 4. Nf4 Rc6之后，白方没有先走5. Rge3!准备，却过早5. Bf6+，未能正确利用黑方的错误。因此我们不再讨论实战后续。

text: Correct would have been 1... Kg8!, followed perhaps by ...Kf7, in which case the black king is only apparently 'courting danger'; in fact, it avoids all the difficulties associated with being in the corner and itself provides assistance in covering the important light squares e6 and g6; moreover, with the dark-square network alone White can clearly achieve nothing. Black is also left with an initiative on the queenside, where he is positionally set to win. If the reader tests the different variations after 1... Kg8, he will convince himself of the strength of the black king's self-defence in this position.
zh: 正确的是1... Kg8!，以后或许...Kf7。黑王只是表面上“自寻险境”，实际上摆脱了角落中的全部困难，还亲自协助保护e6、g6两个重要白格；仅靠黑格网络，白方显然无所作为。黑方仍保有后翼主动权，在那里凭局面棋条件足以争胜。读者若自行检验1... Kg8后的各种变化，就会确信此局面中黑王自卫的力量。

text:
Capablanca - Ragozin
Moscow, 1935
Nimzo-Indian Defence
zh:
卡帕布兰卡—拉戈津
莫斯科，1935年
尼姆佐-印度防御

text: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. a3 Bxc3+ 5. bxc3 d6
zh: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. a3 Bxc3+ 5. bxc3 d6

text: 5... c5 and 5... O-O are more common nowadays.
zh: 在本书写作时，5... c5和5... O-O更常见。

text: 6. Qc2
zh: 6. Qc2

text: Capablanca is happy to avoid 'auxiliary pawn moves' , and here he prepares e4 with the aid of the queen and not by f3.
zh: 卡帕布兰卡乐于避免“辅助性的冲兵”，此处借助后而非f3来准备e4。

text: White should have answered 8... c5 with an immediate d5, whereas now Black ought to have played 10... Na5 followed by ...b6 and ...Ba6, according to the well-known plan for attacking c4. He moved the knight to e7 in order to prepare ...f5, but in this position Black is too weak for that.
zh: 白方本应在8... c5后立即d5。现在黑方则应10... Na5，接着...b6、...Ba6，采用熟知的攻击c4的计划。他把马走到e7是为了准备...f5，但在这个局面黑方太弱，无法实行。

text: However one looks at it, Black is getting into a cramped and difficult position. He cannot make ...f5 work, as is shown by the following variation: 11... Ne8 12. g4 g6 13. Bh6 Ng7 14. O-O-O f5? 15. gxf5 gxf5 16. Rdg1 Rf7 17. exf5 Bxf5 18. Bxg7 when White wins.
zh: 无论怎样看，黑方都陷入了拥挤困难的局面。...f5行不通，例如11... Ne8 12. g4 g6 13. Bh6 Ng7 14. O-O-O f5? 15. gxf5 gxf5 16. Rdg1 Rf7 17. exf5 Bxf5 18. Bxg7，白胜。

caption_zh: 卡帕布兰卡—拉戈津，13. g4后。

text: The beginning of a faulty plan. Black intends to move his king away from the endangered kingside. He does in fact succeed in conveying it without difficulty as far as a8, but in doing so he condemns himself to a passive game with no prospect of activity. Counterplay is possible only on the queenside, based on ...b5. That is where Black's chances lie, and consequently his king does not belong on the queen's wing but should stay where it is; the pawns in front of the king should not be touched, in order that he may retain as much chance as possible of defending himself by blocking the position. Correct therefore was 13... Bd7 planning ...Na4 followed by ...a6 and ...b5. If White plays 14. a4 then 14... Qe8 15. a5 Nbc8 followed by ...Rb8 and ...b5, etc.
zh: 错误计划的开始。黑方想把王从危险的王翼转移出去。他确实毫不困难地把王送到a8，却因此使自己只能消极行棋，毫无活跃的前景。反击只能以...b5为基础在后翼进行，黑方的机会都在那里，所以王不该去后翼，而应留在原处；王前的兵也不应动，以尽可能保留封闭局面进行防御的机会。正确的是13... Bd7，计划...Na4，再...a6、...b5。若白方14. a4，则14... Qe8 15. a5 Nbc8，再...Rb8、...b5等。

text: Capablanca handles the game supremely calmly. His strategy results in his knight being established on the advanced post g7.
zh: 卡帕布兰卡处理得极其沉着。他的战略最终使马稳稳占据g7前哨。

text: 18... Kd8 19. Nh5 Kc7 20. gxf6 gxf6 21. Ng7 Bd7 22. h5 Rac8 23. h6 Kb8 (D)
zh: 18... Kd8 19. Nh5 Kc7 20. gxf6 gxf6 21. Ng7 Bd7 22. h5 Rac8 23. h6 Kb8（见图）

text: Now Black has a 'short castled position on the queenside'. White has everything else.
zh: 现在黑方有了一个“后翼上的短易位王城”，其他一切则都属于白方。
caption_zh: 卡帕布兰卡—拉戈津，23... Kb8后。

text: 24. Rg1 Rf7 25. Rb1 Qf8 26. Be2 Ka8 27. Bh5 Re7 28. Qa2 Qd8 29. Bd2 Na4 30. Qb3 Nb6 31. a4!
zh: 24. Rg1 Rf7 25. Rb1 Qf8 26. Be2 Ka8 27. Bh5 Re7 28. Qa2 Qd8 29. Bd2 Na4 30. Qb3 Nb6 31. a4!

text: It is an irony of fate that Black's wandering king can be reached by an attack on the queenside too! If he now plays 31... Bxa4, there follows 32. Qa2 Bd7 (or 32... Qd7 33. Rxb6 axb6 34. Bd1) 33. Ne6 Bxe6 34. dxe6, and Black has no reply to Bf7 and Bxg8.
zh: 命运真会捉弄人：黑方四处流浪的王，到了后翼也同样受到攻击！若31... Bxa4，则32. Qa2 Bd7（或32... Qd7 33. Rxb6 axb6 34. Bd1）33. Ne6 Bxe6 34. dxe6，黑方无法应对Bf7、Bxg8。

text: Black, who has been 'breathing through his gills' for a long time already, is now left with only his queen to move.
zh: 黑方早已被压得喘不过气来，现在竟只剩后能够移动。

text: At last he has had enough! Any further passive play would have permitted White to organize a winning breakthrough on the g-file.
zh: 终于受不了了！若继续消极等待，白方就可以在g线组织决定性的突破。

text: 39. cxb5 Nb6 40. Qa2 c4 41. Qa3 Qc7 42. Kc1 Rf8 43. Rbg2 Qb8 44. Qb4 Rd8 45. Rg3 Rf8 46. Ne6 Bxe6
zh: 39. cxb5 Nb6 40. Qa2 c4 41. Qa3 Qc7 42. Kc1 Rf8 43. Rbg2 Qb8 44. Qb4 Rd8 45. Rg3 Rf8 46. Ne6 Bxe6

text: Or 46... Rc8 47. Bxb6 axb6 48. a7! and Black loses his knight or is mated.
zh: 或46... Rc8 47. Bxb6 axb6 48. a7!，黑方不是失马就是被将杀。

text: 47. dxe6 Rc7
zh: 47. dxe6 Rc7

text: Otherwise Bf7 is decisive.
zh: 否则Bf7即决定胜负。

text: 49... Nbc8 could be answered by 50. Qb4 Nb6 51. Rg7 Nbc8 52. Rd7, etc.
zh: 49... Nbc8可用50. Qb4 Nb6 51. Rg7 Nbc8 52. Rd7等应对。

text: Pawn majority on the wing
zh: 侧翼多兵

text: Passing now to the theme of indirect defence, we first of all examine a counterattack by means of a pawn majority on the queenside. An analysis of a classic masterpiece will be helpful here.
zh: 现在转入间接防御。先考察利用后翼多兵进行反击。分析一盘经典名局会有帮助。

text:
Pillsbury - Tarrasch
Hastings, 1895
Queen's Gambit Declined, Orthodox Defence
zh:
皮尔斯伯里—塔拉什
黑斯廷斯，1895年
后翼弃兵拒弃兵变例，正统防御

text: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. Nf3 Nbd7 6. Rc1 O-O 7. e3 b6
zh: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. Nf3 Nbd7 6. Rc1 O-O 7. e3 b6

text: These days it is considered more accurate to play ...b6 before committing the b8-knight to d7.
zh: 本书写作时的看法是：先走...b6，再决定把b8马走到d7，较为精确。

text: 8. cxd5 exd5 9. Bd3 Bb7 10. O-O c5 11. Re1?!
zh: 8. cxd5 exd5 9. Bd3 Bb7 10. O-O c5 11. Re1?!

text: A move which does not belong to the system and only wastes time. At this point Pillsbury usually played 11. Ne5 and his opponents allowed him to strengthen the position of his knight by f4. Marco later showed that after 11. Ne5 one should play 11... Nxe5 12. dxe5 Ne8 13. Bf4 g6 14. Bh6 Ng7 15. f4 d4! answering 16. f5 with 16... Bg5.
zh: 这着不符合该体系，只是浪费时间。皮尔斯伯里在这里通常11. Ne5，对手往往允许他以f4巩固马的位置。马尔科后来指出，11. Ne5之后应11... Nxe5 12. dxe5 Ne8 13. Bf4 g6 14. Bh6 Ng7 15. f4 d4!，16. f5则16... Bg5。

text: Today 11. Qe2 is considered strongest.
zh: 本书写作时认为11. Qe2最强。

text: Thus Black creates a pawn majority on the wing but surrenders his influence in the centre. It is now known that the situation in the centre is the more important; moreover, against an attack on the castled king it is easier to build up a counterattack using the centre rather than by means of a slow advance of the wing pawns.
zh: 黑方在侧翼建立了多兵，却放弃了中心影响力。现在已经明白，中心的状况更重要；而且面对王城攻击，在中心组织反攻，比缓慢推进侧翼兵容易。

text: Instead of 11... c4? Black could have played, for example, 11... a6, which is in keeping with the system and does not immediately forsake the centre in the process. The modern answer would be 11... Ne4, with the aim of clarifying the situation.
zh: 黑方可不走11... c4?，例如11... a6就符合体系，也不立即放弃中心。现代的应法会是11... Ne4，以澄清局面。

caption_zh: 皮尔斯伯里—塔拉什，13. Ne5后。

text: Because of Black's mistake this move is now extremely strong, since White is able to consolidate the knight on e5 and use it as the basis for a later attack on the king. 13... Nxe5 will not do now, since 14. dxe5 is extremely awkward for Black.
zh: 由于黑方的错误，现在这着极其有力：白方能够巩固e5马，以之为日后杀王的基础。现在不能13... Nxe5，因为14. dxe5使黑方极其难受。

text: This formation with a knight on e5 and pawns on d4 and f4 is called the 'Pillsbury attack', and it was in this game that the attack originated. Pillsbury was still experimenting with his idea here, hence his unsystematic move 11. Re1?!.
zh: e5有马，d4、f4有兵，这一阵形称为“皮尔斯伯里进攻”，正起源于这盘棋。皮尔斯伯里当时还在试验自己的构想，所以才有不成体系的11. Re1?!。

text: Black prepares to defend his king position by ...Nf8.
zh: 黑方准备用...Nf8防守王城。

text: 15. Qf3 Nf8 16. Ne2 Ne4 17. Bxe7 Rxe7
zh: 15. Qf3 Nf8 16. Ne2 Ne4 17. Bxe7 Rxe7

text: More precise, in fact, is 17... Qxe7 as will be seen from the note to Black's nineteenth move.
zh: 实际上17... Qxe7更精确，参见黑方第19着的注解。

text: 18. Bxe4
zh: 18. Bxe4

text: Pillsbury's contemporaries were a little surprised by this exchange, which he used to make regularly in this system. In fact, the move is absolutely logical from the positional point of view. White cannot worry Black any more as regards his control of e4, and it is better that the square should be occupied by a blocked pawn than an active knight. In view of Black's complete hold on e4, White's bishop on b1 cannot be better employed than in dispatching Black's knight. This is an example of the logic, consistency, and lack of prejudice which runs through Pillsbury's style.
zh: 与皮尔斯伯里同时代的棋手，对这次交换稍感意外；他在这一体系中经常这样走。实际上，从局面棋角度看，这着完全合乎逻辑。白方已无法再动摇黑方对e4的控制，让这里放一个被封闭的兵，总比放一匹活跃的马好。既然黑方已完全掌握e4，白方b1象最好的用途就是消除这匹黑马。这体现了贯穿皮尔斯伯里棋风的逻辑性、一贯性与不存成见。

text: This move has been censured by earlier commentators because 'White's knight retreats with gain of tempo' , but closer investigation shows that the move is not a bad one, or rather that Black has nothing better. 19... f5 would be dangerous (because of White's eventual assault with g4), but otherwise it is difficult to find a natural way of parrying White's threat of 20. f5 followed by Nf4 or f6. It is important to note that 19... Qd6 20. f5 f6 fails because of 21. Ng6! Rd7 22. Ngf4, when White has realized his aim of posting a knight on f4 without having to exchange queens. On the other hand, 19... Qc7 contains some dangers on account of 20. b3. If Black had recaptured with his queen on the seventeenth move, 19... Qd6 would now work, for 20. f5 f6 would force the exchange of queens. A small and instructive detail!
zh: 早期评注者批评这着，因为“白马获得先手后退”，但细看便知此着并不差，或者说黑方没有更好的办法。19... f5很危险，因为白方以后可用g4突击；但不用它，又难找到自然的办法应付20. f5接Nf4或f6的威胁。注意19... Qd6 20. f5 f6因21. Ng6! Rd7 22. Ngf4而失败，白方无需兑后，就实现了把马放到f4的目标。另一方面，19... Qc7因20. b3而有危险。假如黑方第17着用后回吃，此处19... Qd6就可行，因为20. f5 f6将强制兑后。一个细小而有启发性的区别！

text: 20. Ng4 Kh8 21. f5! Qd7 22. Rf1 Rd8
zh: 20. Ng4 Kh8 21. f5! Qd7 22. Rf1 Rd8

text: Black is planning ...Qd6, but he should have noted that White will be unable to play the fundamentally important move Nf4 for some time (because of ...Qxf5). He could therefore have devoted the tempo to preparing ...b4, e.g. by 22... Rc8.
zh: 黑方计划...Qd6，但本应注意：白方一时无法走出具有根本意义的Nf4，因为有...Qxf5。所以黑方可以利用这一步准备...b4，例如22... Rc8。
23. Rf4（见图）
caption_zh: 皮尔斯伯里—塔拉什，23. Rf4后。

text: Here we shall stop a moment to describe the course of the game so far and to point out the characteristic features of the position.
zh: 这里稍停片刻，回顾至今的进程，指出局面的特点。

text: Black released his pressure on the centre early on and thereby allowed White considerable freedom in arranging his pieces for an attack on the king. Against this attack Black built up a typical, direct defensive position which offers considerable, but not absolute, resistance. His principal weapon in the event of a further concentration of White's pieces is, however, an indirect defence in the shape of the advance of the pawn majority on the queenside. Against a whole series of attacking plans Black has successful replies in the form of retaliation on the flank; a particular point is that White cannot force the move Nf4. It was because of this that Pillsbury decided on 23. Rf4, i.e. he now abandons his preparations for Nf4 and regroups with the apparent intention of attacking e4.
zh: 黑方过早减轻中心压力，使白方可以相当自由地布置子力杀王。黑方建立了典型的直接防御阵形，抵抗力很强，却并非绝对可靠。白方若进一步集结子力，黑方的主要武器仍是间接防御，即推进后翼多兵。对于一系列进攻计划，黑方都能以侧翼反击成功应对。尤其是白方不能强行实现Nf4。因此皮尔斯伯里选择23. Rf4，放弃准备Nf4，重新部署，表面上准备攻击e4。

text: A weak move, for Black could now have played 25... b4 26. Na4 Bd5 27. Nc5 Nd7 28. Nxd7 Rxd7, after which there is nothing left of White's attack, while on the queenside Black has moved closer to his goal. 25. Nf2 was better, to prepare g4. Admittedly, if 25... Kg8!, then 26. g4 does not work (because of 26... g5 27. fxg6 Nxg6 28. Qxf6 Nxf4! 29. Qxd6 Nxe2+ and 30... Nxc1, with a whole fistful of pieces for the queen); however, White can play 26. Qh3, to be followed by Rh4, g4, and Nf4, etc.
zh: 弱着。黑方现在可以25... b4 26. Na4 Bd5 27. Nc5 Nd7 28. Nxd7 Rxd7，白方攻势消散，黑方后翼则更接近目标。25. Nf2准备g4较好。诚然25... Kg8!之后26. g4不行，因为26... g5 27. fxg6 Nxg6 28. Qxf6 Nxf4! 29. Qxd6 Nxe2+，接着30... Nxc1，黑方用后换得一大把子力。不过白方可以26. Qh3，再Rh4、g4、Nf4等。

caption_zh: 皮尔斯伯里—塔拉什，25... Bd5后。

text: Not only does this throw away the chance of playing ...b4, it also allows White the following opportunity to simplify the position: 26. a4 b4 27. Nxd5 Qxd5 28. Nxf6 gxf6 29. Qxf6+ Rg7 30. Rg4 Qf7 31. Qxg7+ Qxg7 32. Rxg7 Kxg7 33. Rxc4, when the ending favours White.
zh: 这不仅放弃...b4的机会，还允许白方这样简化：26. a4 b4 27. Nxd5 Qxd5 28. Nxf6 gxf6 29. Qxf6+ Rg7 30. Rg4 Qf7 31. Qxg7+ Qxg7 32. Rxg7 Kxg7 33. Rxc4，残局有利于白方。

text: White also retains the better prospects this way, though best would in fact have been 26. a4 as given above.
zh: 这样白方同样保持较好的前景，不过最佳的仍是上述26. a4。

text: Black could well have played 26... b4 and if 27. Ne2 then 27... a5. 27. Ncxe4? would fail against 27... Qc6 followed, after a knight retreat, by 28... Rxe3. However, the text move is also correct.
zh: 黑方完全可以26... b4，若27. Ne2则27... a5。27. Ncxe4?会遭27... Qc6，马退后就28... Rxe3。不过实战着也正确。

text: A tactical mistake, since the rook is not well placed here.
zh: 战术错误，因为车在这里位置不好。

text: This loses important tempi. Correct was 28... c3! 29. b3! (if 29. bxc3 then 29... Bc4 followed by ...Bxe2 and ...bxc3, after which Black's position is preferable) 29... a5 when Black proceeds along similar lines to those in the actual game (i.e. by ...Ra8 and ...a4, etc.) but much more quickly.
zh: 浪费重要步数。正确的是28... c3! 29. b3!（29. bxc3则29... Bc4，再...Bxe2、...bxc3，黑优）29... a5，黑方按与实战相似的路线继续，如...Ra8、...a4等，但快得多。
29. Ng4 Nd7 30. R4f2（见图）

text: The move is not a bad one, although it would not inspire commentators nowadays to pour on it the praise with which it was once honoured. The point is that by 30. Nc1 c3 31. b3 White obtains a position analogous to that actually reached, and the only difference is that 30. R4f2 sets a trap for 30... Qxa2. However, even that trap is not so terrible, for after 31. Nf4 Bf7 32. Ng6+ Kg8! (Réti only analyses the inferior 32... Bxg6?) 33. Nxe7+ Rxe7 34. Qg3 Kf8 35. h3 (otherwise ...h5 wins the knight) 35... Qa5 Black still retains good prospects of counterplay, and it is not certain whether White can use his small material advantage to any real effect.
zh: 这着不坏，不过按本书写作时的标准，已不值得像从前那样大加赞扬。30. Nc1 c3 31. b3可得与实战相似的局面，唯一区别是30. R4f2给30... Qxa2设了陷阱。但陷阱也没那么可怕：31. Nf4 Bf7 32. Ng6+ Kg8!（列蒂只分析较差的32... Bxg6?）33. Nxe7+ Rxe7 34. Qg3 Kf8 35. h3（否则...h5得马）35... Qa5，黑方仍有很好的反击前景，白方能否有效利用微小的子力优势尚不确定。
caption_zh: 皮尔斯伯里—塔拉什，30. R4f2后。

text: Preparing for Nh2 and then g4-g5.
zh: 准备Nh2，再g4—g5。

text: A mistake which luckily is not properly exploited. It was not yet time for a bayonet attack by g4. White should have played 35. bxa4 or else brought his queen back to the defence via g4 and d1.
zh: 这是一个错误，幸而没有被正确利用。以g4发动刺刀进攻的时候还没到，白方应35. bxa4，或经g4、d1把后调回防守。

text: Since he lacks a satisfactory defence against ...Ra3 and ...Rxb3, White has no choice but to try to force home his attack on the enemy king.
zh: 白方对...Ra3、...Rxb3缺乏满意防御，只得尝试强行贯彻杀王攻势。

text: A decisive mistake, entirely altering the situation. Black should at this point have thought a little about defence himself, leaving the tit-bit on b3, which could not run away, until later. Correct was 38... fxg5! 39. Qxg5 Nf6 when both 40. Ne5 Qd6 and 40. Rg2 Kf8 leave Black the better placed. The essence of Black's defence in this case is the correctly-timed blockade of White's f-pawn by ...Nf6, without which there would be no answer to a breakthrough by White on that critical square (f6).
zh: 决定性的错误，完全改变了局势。黑方此时自己也该稍想防守，把b3这块不会逃跑的肥肉留待以后。正确的是38... fxg5! 39. Qxg5 Nf6，40. Ne5 Qd6和40. Rg2 Kf8都使黑方占优。防御的实质是适时以...Nf6封锁白方f兵，否则无法应付白方在f6这个关键格的突破。

text: The move which decides the game, since it threatens both gxf6 and Nxf6+.
zh: 这着决定胜负，同时威胁gxf6和Nxf6+。

text: After 39... fxg5 40. Qxg5, 40... Nf6 is no longer feasible, and accordingly the breakthrough by f6 wins in all variations.
zh: 39... fxg5 40. Qxg5后，40... Nf6已不可行，因而f6突破在所有变化中都能取胜。

text: 40. gxf6 gxf6?!
zh: 40. gxf6 gxf6?!

text: This loses quickly. A better resistance and even some chances of a draw were offered by the continuation 40... Nxf6 41. Ne5 Qe8 42. Nxb3 Rxb3 43. Ng6+ Kg8 44. Nxe7+ Qxe7 45. Qg3.
zh: 这导致速败。40... Nxf6 41. Ne5 Qe8 42. Nxb3 Rxb3 43. Ng6+ Kg8 44. Nxe7+ Qxe7 45. Qg3抵抗更顽强，甚至有些和棋机会。

text: 41. Nxb3 Rxb3 (D)
zh: 41. Nxb3 Rxb3（见图）
caption_zh: 皮尔斯伯里—塔拉什，41... Rxb3后。

text: 42. Nh6! Rg7 43. Rxg7 Kxg7 44. Qg3+! Kxh6 45. Kh1 Qd5
zh: 42. Nh6! Rg7 43. Rxg7 Kxg7 44. Qg3+! Kxh6 45. Kh1 Qd5

text: 45... c2 would also be met by 46. Rg1.
46. Rg1 Qxf5 47. Qh4+ Qh5 48. Qf4+ Qg5 49. Rxg5 fxg5 50. Qd6+ Kh5 51. Qxd7 c2
zh: 46. Rg1 Qxf5 47. Qh4+ Qh5 48. Qf4+ Qg5 49. Rxg5 fxg5 50. Qd6+ Kh5 51. Qxd7 c2

text: Black allows himself to be mated, but after 51 ...Rb1+ 52. Kg2 Rb2+ 53. Kg3 Kg6 Black must lose eventually.
zh: 黑方允许自己被将杀，不过51... Rb1+ 52. Kg2 Rb2+ 53. Kg3 Kg6也终究会输。

text: This famous game has its place in chess literature as a classic example of an attack on the castled king which is stronger than the counterattack on the queenside. But in the light of my annotations, which differ fundamentally from all annotations hitherto, from Tarrasch to Réti, this game takes on a new appearance. Black's numerous opportunities to strengthen his game at various stages point rather to the equal balance between the attack and the indirect defence, and it was only the decisive mistake on the thirty-eighth move which swung the balance in White's favour. This view of the game also qualifies it as a good example of the importance of indirect defence against an attack on the castled king, and of the part played by operations with wing pawns in particular.
zh: 这盘名局在棋书中一向被视为王城攻势胜过后翼反击的经典。但我的注解与从塔拉什到列蒂此前所有注解都有根本区别，使此局呈现新面貌。黑方在不同阶段多次可以加强行棋，这反而说明进攻与间接防御大体均衡；只是第38着的决定性错误才使天平倾向白方。这样看，这盘棋也很好地说明了面对王城攻击时间接防御的重要性，尤其是侧翼兵行动的作用。

text: Indirect defence by means of advancing a pawn majority on the queenside was at one time held in high esteem and was more often practised than nowadays; the real reason for this is that we have acquired a better understanding of the centre and the technique of centralization, thanks to the hypermodern school. It is clear that the player who has a majority on the wing, when the material is equally balanced, will usually not have the greater influence or pressure in the centre, nor will he have the necessary conditions for a central action. A majority on the wing is created at the expense of the centre and means giving up lateral pressure on the centre, and that is the sort of strategy which the masters of today are reluctant to adopt. The struggle for the centre is a characteristic feature of all present-day openings, and the centralization of the pieces is an important theme of modern positional play; as a result, a majority on the wing appears nowadays more as a by-product of a particular strategy than its primary aim (for example, in the Exchange Variation of the Grünfeld Defence).
zh: 推进后翼多兵的间接防御曾受到高度重视，采用得比本书写作时更多。这种方法后来用得较少，真正原因是：超现代学派使我们对中心及子力中心化的技术有了更好理解。在子力相等时，侧翼多兵的一方通常在中心并无更大影响或压力，也缺乏中心行动所需条件。侧翼多兵以中心为代价，意味着放弃对中心的侧面压力，这是现代大师不愿采用的战略。争夺中心是现代所有开局的特征，子力中心化也是现代局面棋的重要主题。因此，侧翼多兵如今更多是某种战略的副产品，而非主要目标，例如格林菲尔德防御兑换变例。

text: Thus, concern for the centre is driving majority actions out of use, and it should be added that an indirect defence against an attack on the castled king is more effective and holds better prospects of success in the form of a central action than one using wing pawns. This is shown by the following general considerations.
zh: 重视中心，正使多兵行动逐渐失去地位。还应补充：防御王城攻击时，采用中心行动的间接防御比运用侧翼兵更有效，成功前景也更好。以下一般性理由说明这一点。

text: l) Advancing pawns on the opposite wing is a slow process, since, as a rule, the whole pawn chain must move forward for a passed pawn to be created.
zh: 1）在另一翼推进兵很慢，因为通常必须推动整条兵链，才能制造通路兵。

text: 2) The attacker knows which pawn is going to be dangerous and so can arrange to contain it economically, either by preparing to block the pawn with a piece or by planning ahead to sacrifice a piece for the passed pawn, which in fact means surrendering the piece in return for a considerable number of tempi.
zh: 2）进攻方知道哪个兵会变得危险，因而可节约地限制它：或者准备以子力封锁，或者预先计划为这个通路兵弃子；后者实际上是用一子换取相当多的步数。

text: 3) Advancing pawns on the opposite wing is an action which is furthest in distance from the threatened castled position and which is the hardest to combine with, or transform into, direct defence.
zh: 3）在另一翼推进兵，距离受威胁的王城最远，也最难与直接防御结合，或转变为直接防御。

text: These are the general deficiencies of indirect defence using the wing pawns, and they limit its use mainly to the following cases:
zh: 这些是利用侧翼兵间接防御的一般缺点，使它主要适用于以下情况：

text: a) The attack on the castled king develops slowly, demanding a regrouping or perhaps a series of pawn moves; it does not lead to a forced mate, for a defence can be bought at the price of material;
zh: a）王城攻势发展缓慢，需要重新部署，或连续冲兵；攻势不能强制将杀，因为防守方能付出子力代价换得防御；

text: b) Direct defence is on the whole sufficient but it may be usefully combined with something else; in other words, the defender has some tempi left over which he can devote to alternative actions, including those using the wing pawns.
zh: b）直接防御总体已足够，但还可有益地配合其他行动。换言之，防守方有富余步数，可以投入别的行动，包括侧翼兵行动。

text: These, then, are the general factors which speak for, or against, indirect defence by means of the wing pawns, but in this case too the reader must overcome any inclination to think merely in terms of formulae, since the essence of a formula often consists of 'exceptions which prove the rule'.
zh: 以上是赞成或反对用侧翼兵间接防御的一般因素。但读者在这里也必须克服仅凭公式思考的倾向，因为公式的实质，往往就在那些“证明规则的例外”之中。

text: Defence by counterattack
zh: 以反击防御

text: Venturing further into the broad field of indirect defence, we next concern ourselves with a series of cases in which methods other than a pawn thrust in the centre are used. We shall examine five examples from the point of view of the following factors:
zh: 进一步进入间接防御的广阔领域，接下来讨论一组采用中心冲兵以外其他方法的情况。我们考察五个实例，着重注意以下因素：

text: 1) The area of the counterattack and the conditions underlying it.
zh: 1）反击所在区域及基础条件。

text: 2) The part played by the material situation in relation to positional considerations.
zh: 2）子力状况相对于局面棋因素所起的作用。

text: 3) The interweaving of indirect defence with direct and the switching from one to the other.
zh: 3）间接防御与直接防御的交织，以及二者之间的转换。

text: 4) The dependence of timing and the form of defence on the state of the attacker's commitments.
zh: 4）防御的时机、形式怎样取决于进攻方已有的投入及其带来的约束。

text: The following position is from the game K.Treybal-H.Wolf, Teplitz-Schönau 1922. Black, to move, has the task of organizing a defence against an attack on his king position. A single glance is enough to show that he has no move to make in the way of direct defence. The only move in keeping with that would be 1... Kh7, but that would simply make White's attack easier. For example, White will in any case play Rf4-h4 and then (with the king on h7) the square g5 will be available for his queen, besides which there is a threat of Bc1 followed by Rxh6 with check. Therefore, indirect defence must be used to obstruct White's plan to gain control of h6. With that aim, only an action on the queenside can be considered, for Black cannot achieve anything in the centre.
zh: 下图出自K. 特雷巴尔—H. 沃尔夫，特普利采-舍瑙，1922年。轮黑走，必须组织防御，应对王城攻势。一眼就能看出，他没有什么直接防御可走。唯一相符的是1... Kh7，但这只会便利白方进攻。例如白方无论如何都会Rf4—h4；黑王在h7时，g5便可供白后使用，此外还有Bc1再Rxh6的威胁。这次吃子还带将军。因此，必须用间接防御妨碍白方控制h6的计划。为此只能考虑后翼行动，因为黑方在中心无所作为。
caption_zh: K. 特雷巴尔—H. 沃尔夫，特普利采-舍瑙，1922年；黑先。

text: 1... a5 2. Rf4 a4 3. Raf1 axb3 4. axb3 Ra2!
zh: 1... a5 2. Rf4 a4 3. Raf1 axb3 4. axb3 Ra2!

text: Very well played! Black first of all makes it difficult for White to redeploy his queen and bishop, a course which is necessary for an attack on h6; moreover, there is an eventual threat of ...Rxb2 followed by ...Nd3.
zh: 走得很好！首先使白方难以重新布置后与象，而这正是攻击h6所必需的；此外还潜伏着...Rxb2再...Nd3的威胁。

text: 5. Rh4 Rb8
zh: 5. Rh4 Rb8

text: Suddenly Black threatens 6... Nxc4; he has worked up a definite counterattack, and White is still quite a long way from having any serious threats on the kingside.
zh: 黑方突然威胁6... Nxc4，已经组织起具体反击，而白方距王翼上真正有力的威胁还很远。

text: 6. Qc3
zh: 6. Qc3

text: Black has succeeded in persuading White’s queen to leave the attacking diagonal. 6. Rxh6 would not have worked because of 6... Rxb2 7. Qg5 Qg4 and White has nothing. An interesting possibility was 6. Nf5, which probably leads to a draw; objectively, this would not have been at all bad, for Black could have gained some advantage after White’s actual move. The analysis runs 6. Nf5 gxf5 (6... Rxb2 fails against 7. Nxh6+ Bxh6 8. Qxh6) 7. Rxh6 Rxb2 8. Qg5+ Ng6 9. Rxg6+ fxg6 10. Qxg6+ Kh8 11. Rf4 (this attempt does not give more than perpetual check, which White would also obtain by 11. Qh5+) 11... Rb1+ 12. Kf2 Rb2+ 13. Ke1 Rb1+ (if 13... Qxe4+ 14. Rxe4 fxe4, White wins by 15. f7!) 14. Kd2 Rb2+ 15. Kc1 Rb1+! 16. Kxb1 Rxb3+ 17. Ka2 Rb2+ [Nunn note 1] 18. Ka3 (or 18. Kxb2 Qe5+ and 19... Qxf4) 18... Ra2+, and White’s king cannot escape from perpetual check.
zh: 黑方成功迫使白后离开攻击斜线。6. Rxh6因6... Rxb2 7. Qg5 Qg4而无效，白方毫无所得。6. Nf5很有意思，可能导致和棋；客观上这已不差，因为实战着后黑方可能略占优势。分析如下：6. Nf5 gxf5（6... Rxb2因7. Nxh6+ Bxh6 8. Qxh6而失败）7. Rxh6 Rxb2 8. Qg5+ Ng6 9. Rxg6+ fxg6 10. Qxg6+ Kh8 11. Rf4（这也只有长将；11. Qh5+同样可得长将）11... Rb1+ 12. Kf2 Rb2+ 13. Ke1 Rb1+（13... Qxe4+ 14. Rxe4 fxe4则15. f7!白胜）14. Kd2 Rb2+ 15. Kc1 Rb1+! 16. Kxb1 Rxb3+ 17. Ka2 Rb2+〔纳恩注1〕18. Ka3（或18. Kxb2 Qe5+，再19... Qxf4）18... Ra2+，白王逃不出长将。

text: 1 Black can play for a win by 17... Rh3! since after 18. gxh3 Qxc4+ he can win the rook on f4 with a series of checks.
zh: 〔纳恩注1〕黑方可以17... Rh3!争胜，因为18. gxh3 Qxc4+之后，可以连续将军赢得f4车。

text: The wrong turning, since White now plays Bc1 with gain of tempo, placing the bishop on the diagonal where it really belongs. The correct continuation of the defence consisted in giving, not taking, material, e.g. 6... Rxb2! 7. Qxb2 Nxc4 8. Qc3 (or 8. Qc1 Ne5 9. Rxh6 Rxb3 after which both 10. Qg5 Qg4 and 10. Rf5 Ng4 are in Black's favour) 8... Ne5 9. Rb1 c4 10. b4 Qxf6 11. Rh3 Bg7 and Black has the better prospects. Wolf, of course, was not the master to decide on 'giving' when he could 'take'. His saying was: 'Why should I sacrifice when nobody sacrifices for me!?' But the consistent implementation of a plan with a sound positional basis often demands sacrificial conceptions, as in the analysis above, which is both typical and instructive. We can see here how an element of direct defence is also involved — the elimination of White's bishop, which plays an essential part in his mating plans. White's attack then flags, whereupon Black takes some pawns, centralizes his position, and brands White's rook on h4 as misplaced; the defence welds the various elements of the position into a single whole.
zh: 方向错了。白方现在获得先手走Bc1，把象放到真正应在的斜线上。正确的防御不是吃子，而是送还子力，例如6... Rxb2! 7. Qxb2 Nxc4 8. Qc3（或8. Qc1 Ne5 9. Rxh6 Rxb3，此后10. Qg5 Qg4和10. Rf5 Ng4均有利于黑方）8... Ne5 9. Rb1 c4 10. b4 Qxf6 11. Rh3 Bg7，黑方前景较好。沃尔夫当然不是那种能“拿”时却决定“给”的大师。他的名言是：“别人都不为我弃子，我为什么要弃子？！”但要一贯执行具有可靠局面棋基础的计划，往往就需要弃子构想，正如上面典型而有启发性的分析。这里也包含直接防御因素：消除在白方将杀计划中必不可少的象。白方攻势随后衰退，黑方就吃兵、子力中心化，并使白方h4车显得错位。防御把局面的各种要素结合成一个整体。
7. Bc1（见图）
caption_zh: K. 特雷巴尔—H. 沃尔夫，7. Bc1后。

text: In sharp positions like this everything should be considered, including moves like 7... g5. The latter represents a simultaneous combination of direct and indirect defence: Black drives back the rook, blocks the diagonal of the enemy bishop, and frees the square g6 for the knight — all direct elements — while the indirect appears in certain continuations where Black's g-pawn takes part in a counterattack. Let us look at some ways in which White can go astray after 7... g5. First of all, the 'natural' move 8. Rh5? is unsatisfactory because of 8... Ne5 9. Bxg5 (after 9. Nf5 Ng4! the attack on the e-pawn gains a tempo) 9... Rxb3 10. Qc1 Rxg3 11. hxg3 Qg4.
zh: 在这种尖锐局面，一切都应考虑，包括7... g5。此着把直接与间接防御同时结合起来：赶车、堵住敌象斜线、腾出g6给马，都是直接防御因素；间接因素则出现在某些变化中，黑方g兵参与反击。先看看7... g5后白方可能怎样走错。“自然”的8. Rh5?不行，因为8... Ne5 9. Bxg5（9. Nf5 Ng4!，攻击e兵获得先手）9... Rxb3 10. Qc1 Rxg3 11. hxg3 Qg4。
