text: Nor is 8. Nf5? gxh4 9. Qf3 Ne5 10. Qh5 good, e.g. 10... Rxb3 11. Nxh6+ (or 11. Bxh6 Rbb2!) 11... Bxh6 12. Qxh6 Qg4 when the clearing of the g-file enables Black to cover the focal-point at g7. The g-pawn takes an active role in the continuation 8. Rh3 g4 9. bxc4 gxh3 when the threat of ...Rxg2+ costs White a decisive tempo.
zh: 8. Nf5? gxh4 9. Qf3 Ne5 10. Qh5也不好，例如10... Rxb3 11. Nxh6+（或11. Bxh6 Rbb2!）11... Bxh6 12. Qxh6 Qg4，g线打开，使黑方得以保护g7焦点。在8. Rh3 g4 9. bxc4 gxh3中，g兵则积极行动；...Rxg2+的威胁使白方损失决定性的一步。

text: The correct response to 7... g5 is 8. Rh3! g4 (if 8... Ne5 then 9. Nf5 after which the b-pawn is protected) and now 9. Rh5! (instead of 9. bxc4 as above) 9... Ne5 10. Bxh6 Bxh6 (if 10... Rxb3 then 11. Qc1 wins) 11. Rxh6 Rxb3 12. Qc1 Ng6 13. Rh8+ Nxh8 14. Qh6 and White wins. Here White's play against the focal-point g7 is unhindered, since g4 is blocked by Black's own pawn.
zh: 对7... g5的正确应法是8. Rh3! g4（8... Ne5则9. Nf5，b兵得到保护），然后9. Rh5!（不是上述9. bxc4）9... Ne5 10. Bxh6 Bxh6（10... Rxb3则11. Qc1白胜）11. Rxh6 Rxb3 12. Qc1 Ng6 13. Rh8+ Nxh8 14. Qh6，白胜。这里g4被黑方自己的兵堵住，白方攻击g7焦点不再受阻。

text: 8. Bxh6 Bxh6?
zh: 8. Bxh6 Bxh6?

text: At the very least, this is a tactical mistake; for, by 8... Rxb3 Black could have presented White with an exceptionally difficult problem and involved him in considerable risk if he persisted in playing for a win. The text move, however, gives White no difficulties and allows him to win easily.
zh: 至少从战术上说，这是错误。8... Rxb3能给白方出一道极难的题；若白方坚持争胜，便须承担很大风险。实战着却没给白方任何困难，让他轻易获胜。

text: Grünfeld and Becker, the authors of the tournament book — one of the best in the literature of the game — rightly censure Black's move, but their analysis of the continuation 8... Rxb3! is not correct. In the variation which they conclude with a drawn ending Black can eventually win, while in that which they consider won for Black the position can be resolved in White's favour. These lines together with my analysis will interest the reader as general studies of the middlegame. Here is a diagram after the alternative 8... Rxb3! (D).
zh: 赛会棋谱集的作者格林菲尔德和贝克尔——他们的书是棋书中的佳作之一——正确地批评了黑方此着，但对8... Rxb3!的分析不正确。他们认为进入和棋残局的一条变化，黑方最终可以赢；他们认为黑方获胜的另一条变化，却可以对白方有利地解决。这些变化与我的分析一起，可作为一般性的中局研究供读者参考。下图是另选8... Rxb3!后的局面（见图）。
caption_zh: K. 特雷巴尔—H. 沃尔夫分析，8... Rxb3后。

text: Grünfeld and Becker reach a draw as follows: 9. Bxf8 g5! (otherwise Bg7 and mate) 10. Rh5 Rxc3 11. Bg7 Ng6 12. Nf5. In their opinion Black now has no defence against perpetual check by Nh6+. In fact, Black still has something to say and can play 12... Rxg2+! 13. Kh1 (if 13. Kxg2 then 13... Qxe4+ and Black has no trouble picking up the rook on h5) 13... Rxh2+ 14. Kxh2 (or 14. Rxh2 Qxe4+ followed by ...Nh4) 14... Qe5+ 15. Kg1 Rg3+ 16. Kh2 (16. Nxg3 Qxg3+ 17. Kh1 Qg4 followed by ...Qxe4+, ...c4, etc.) 16... Rf3+ 17. Kg1 (or 17. Kg2 Rxf5 18. exf5 Qe2+ 19. Rf2 Nf4+) 17... Rxf1+ 18. Kxf1 Qf4+ and White loses either his rook or his knight.
zh: 格林菲尔德和贝克尔以下列变化论证和棋：9. Bxf8 g5!（否则Bg7将杀）10. Rh5 Rxc3 11. Bg7 Ng6 12. Nf5。他们认为黑方不能防御Nh6+长将。实际上黑方还有话说：12... Rxg2+! 13. Kh1（13. Kxg2则13... Qxe4+，黑方很容易吃掉h5车）13... Rxh2+ 14. Kxh2（或14. Rxh2 Qxe4+，再...Nh4）14... Qe5+ 15. Kg1 Rg3+ 16. Kh2（16. Nxg3 Qxg3+ 17. Kh1 Qg4，再...Qxe4+、...c4等）16... Rf3+ 17. Kg1（或17. Kg2 Rxf5 18. exf5 Qe2+ 19. Rf2 Nf4+）17... Rxf1+ 18. Kxf1 Qf4+，白方不是失车就是失马。

text: The second line given by the same commentators aims to show that 8... Rxb3! cannot be answered by 9. Qc1 because of 9... Ng4 10. Bxf8 Rbb2 11. Bg7 Rxg2+ 12. Kh1 Rxh2+ 13. Rxh2 Rxh2+ 14. Kg1 Qa2 and Black wins. But if White, instead of 11. Bg7?, plays 11. Qxb2! Rxb2 12. Bg7 then Black loses. Correct after 9. Qc1 is at once 9... Rbb2 whereupon 10. Bxf8 does not work because of 10... Rxg2+ 11. Kh1 Ng4!.
zh: 同一组评注者给出的第二条变化，试图证明8... Rxb3!之后不能9. Qc1，理由是9... Ng4 10. Bxf8 Rbb2 11. Bg7 Rxg2+ 12. Kh1 Rxh2+ 13. Rxh2 Rxh2+ 14. Kg1 Qa2，黑胜。但白方若不11. Bg7?而11. Qxb2! Rxb2 12. Bg7，黑方就输了。9. Qc1后正确的是立即9... Rbb2，10. Bxf8不行，因为10... Rxg2+ 11. Kh1 Ng4!。

text: Now here is my analysis. First of all, let me explain why 9. Bxf8? g5! 10. Qc1, not mentioned by the commentators, does not work. Black replies 10... gxh4 and then 11. Qh6 is useless on account of 11... Qg4 while 11. Qg5+ fails against 11... Kxf8 12. Nf5 Rbb2! when White’s attack is halted — he cannot get any further than Qh6+ and Ng7+ because of the threat of mate that faces him on g2 and h2. A third possibility is 11. Nf5 Rbb2! 12. Ne7+ Qxe7 13. Qg5+ (if 13. Qxb2 then 13... Qe6) 13... Kxf8 14. fxe7+ Ke8 when it can be seen that White has achieved nothing. In return for his rooks Black will win the queen and the pawns on g2 and e7, thus obtaining an advantage in the ending.
zh: 下面给出我的分析。先解释评注者未提的9. Bxf8? g5! 10. Qc1为什么不行。黑方10... gxh4，11. Qh6因11... Qg4无用；11. Qg5+则11... Kxf8 12. Nf5 Rbb2!，白方攻势被遏止，由于自身g2、h2面临将杀，除了Qh6+、Ng7+以外无法推进。第三种可能是11. Nf5 Rbb2! 12. Ne7+ Qxe7 13. Qg5+（13. Qxb2则13... Qe6）13... Kxf8 14. fxe7+ Ke8，可以看出白方没有取得成果。黑方将用双车换得后及g2、e7两兵，取得残局优势。

text: The above diagram is a hard nut to crack, and the way to attempt it is as follows: 9. Qc1! Rbb2! 10. Qxb2! Rxb2 11. Bxf8 g5 12. Rh5 Ng6 13. Bg7. Now White has the same position as in the first line above but with a tempo less and a rook more. He wins in the following variations:
zh: 上图是个棘手的难题，应这样尝试：9. Qc1! Rbb2! 10. Qxb2! Rxb2 11. Bxf8 g5 12. Rh5 Ng6 13. Bg7。白方与上述第一条变化相比，少一步但多一车。以下变化白方获胜：

text: 1) 13... c4 14. Nf5 Rxg2+ (otherwise Ne7+ wins) 15. Kxg2 [Nunn note 1] Qxe4+ 16. Kg3 Qe5+ 17. Kh3 g4+ (if 17... Qc3+ the king escapes from the checks on g1) 18. Kg2 Qb2+ 19. Kg1 Qb6+ 20. Rf2! Qb1+ 21. Kg2 Qe4+ 22. Kg3 Qd3+ 23. Kxg4 Qd1+ (or 23... Ne5+ 24. Kg5 Nf3+ 25. Kh6) 24. Rf3! Ne5+ 25. Kg5 Nxf3+ 26. Kf4 Qd2+ 27. Ne3 Qd4+ 28. Kxf3 and White wins.
zh: 1）13... c4 14. Nf5 Rxg2+（否则Ne7+获胜）15. Kxg2〔纳恩注1〕Qxe4+ 16. Kg3 Qe5+ 17. Kh3 g4+（17... Qc3+，王可到g1躲开将军）18. Kg2 Qb2+ 19. Kg1 Qb6+ 20. Rf2! Qb1+ 21. Kg2 Qe4+ 22. Kg3 Qd3+ 23. Kxg4 Qd1+（或23... Ne5+ 24. Kg5 Nf3+ 25. Kh6）24. Rf3! Ne5+ 25. Kg5 Nxf3+ 26. Kf4 Qd2+ 27. Ne3 Qd4+ 28. Kxf3，白胜。

text: 2) 13... Qg4 14. Rh6 Rb8 (parrying the threat of Rxg6) 15. Re1 Re8 16. Nf5 Rxe4 (otherwise Rxg6) 17. Ne7+ Rxe7 18. fxe7 Nxe7 19. Bf6 and White wins.
zh: 2）13... Qg4 14. Rh6 Rb8（防Rxg6）15. Re1 Re8 16. Nf5 Rxe4（否则Rxg6）17. Ne7+ Rxe7 18. fxe7 Nxe7 19. Bf6，白胜。

text: 3) 13... Rb8 14. Nf5 Re8 (if 14... Qxe4, then a round of checks by the knight — Nh6+, Nxf7+, Nh6+, Nf5+ — and finally f7+ leads to the win of the queen) 15. Nh6+ Kh7 16. Nxf7+ Kg8 17. Nxg5 Qe5 18. h4 Ra8 (or 18... Rf8 19. f7+ Kxg7 20. Rh7#) 19. Rh6 Ra1 20. f7+ Kxg7 21. Rxg6+ Kxg6 22. f8=Q and again White wins.
zh: 3）13... Rb8 14. Nf5 Re8（14... Qxe4则马连续将军Nh6+、Nxf7+、Nh6+、Nf5+，最后f7+赢后）15. Nh6+ Kh7 16. Nxf7+ Kg8 17. Nxg5 Qe5 18. h4 Ra8（或18... Rf8 19. f7+ Kxg7 20. Rh7#）19. Rh6 Ra1 20. f7+ Kxg7 21. Rxg6+ Kxg6 22. f8=Q，白方仍胜。

text: 1 15. Kh1! wins straight away.
zh: 〔纳恩注1〕15. Kh1!立即获胜。

text: Of Black's other moves the most difficult to deal with is 13... Qc4, threatening 14... Qc2. White is then able to draw by 14. Ra1 Ra2 15. Rb1 Rb2 [Nunn note 1] 16. Ra1 etc., but can he also win? This may be left to the reader to examine; we shall return to the game, where Black played 8... Bxh6? (D).
zh: 黑方其他着法中，最难应付的是13... Qc4，威胁14... Qc2。白方可14. Ra1 Ra2 15. Rb1 Rb2〔纳恩注1〕16. Ra1等求和，但能否争胜？留给读者检验。现在回到实战，黑方走了8... Bxh6?（见图）。
caption_zh: K. 特雷巴尔—H. 沃尔夫，8... Bxh6后。

text: 9. Rxh6 Qxb3
zh: 9. Rxh6 Qxb3

text: Black also loses after 9... Rxb3 10. Qc1 Ng4 11. Qg5! Rbb2 12. Rxg6+.
zh: 9... Rxb3 10. Qc1 Ng4 11. Qg5! Rbb2 12. Rxg6+也导致黑方输棋。

text: Now the main defect in Black's eighth move can be seen: White is at once threatening 11. Rh8+.
zh: 现在可看出黑方第8着的主要缺陷：白方立即威胁11. Rh8+。

text: 10... Ng4 11. Nf5! Re8 12. Rh4 Rxe4 13. Ne7+ Rxe7 14. fxe7 Re2 15. Rxg4 Qe3+ 16. Qxe3 Rxe3 17. Rxg6+! Kh7 18. Rgf6 1-0
zh: 10... Ng4 11. Nf5! Re8 12. Rh4 Rxe4 13. Ne7+ Rxe7 14. fxe7 Re2 15. Rxg4 Qe3+ 16. Qxe3 Rxe3 17. Rxg6+! Kh7 18. Rgf6 1-0
caption_zh: 耶茨—马尔科，15. Ng3后。

text: 1 In this line 15... Qd4+ 16. Kh1 Ra1 wins for Black — indeed, White seems to be struggling after 13... Qc4.
zh: 〔纳恩注1〕这条变化中，15... Qd4+ 16. Kh1 Ra1黑胜。实际上，13... Qc4以后白方似乎就已陷入苦战。

text: This position, from the game Yates-Marco, The Hague 1921, arose after the moves 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 Nd7 4. Bc4 c6 5. Nc3 Be7 6. O-O h6 7. Be3 Ngf6 8. Bb3 Qc7 9. Nd2 g5 10. a4 Nf8 11. a5 Ng6 12. Re1 Nf4 13. f3 Rg8 14. Nf1 Be6 15. Ng3 (D). Black has played his favourite Hanham Variation of the Philidor, obtaining the advantage and an attack on the white king; this is the natural result of White’s extravagant treatment of the opening (unmotivated moves a5 and f3 at an earlier stage of the game). Marco (Black), to move, spoils his position by provoking d5 which he does in order to continue with a sacrifice in the old ‘paprika style’.
zh: 此局面出自耶茨—马尔科，海牙，1921年，形成于：1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 Nd7 4. Bc4 c6 5. Nc3 Be7 6. O-O h6 7. Be3 Ngf6 8. Bb3 Qc7 9. Nd2 g5 10. a4 Nf8 11. a5 Ng6 12. Re1 Nf4 13. f3 Rg8 14. Nf1 Be6 15. Ng3（见前图）。黑方采用了自己喜爱的菲利道尔防御汉哈姆变例，取得优势并攻击白王；这是白方开局挥霍步数的自然结果，如早期无根据的a5、f3。轮执黑的马尔科走，他为按老派“火辣风格”弃子而诱使对手d5，破坏了自己的局面。

text: Black had excellent prospects of carrying out an attack using his pawns (15... g4 or 15... h5) without any material risk, but he has seen the chance of a bishop sacrifice on h3 with play against the focal-point g2 and cannot resist it.
zh: 黑方本可用兵进攻（15... g4或15... h5），前景很好，也不必冒子力风险。但他看到了在h3弃象、攻击g2焦点的机会，便无法抗拒。

text: White rightly falls in with Black's intentions and forces him to continue with ...Bh3.
zh: 白方顺势而为是对的，迫使黑方继续...Bh3。

caption_zh: 耶茨—马尔科，16... Bh3后。

text: White decides to accept the sacrifice and to employ direct defence against the attack on his king. With good play he could certainly have come through by this method, but the right way to refute the offer is not by accepting it but by applying indirect defence in the shape of a counterattack on the queenside. After d5 there is also some point to the earlier advance a5, since an attack can now be made on Black's pawn chain at b7 and c6, as a result of which White obtains the better pawn structure and an advantage in space on the queenside and also frees the square d5 for a piece. The analysis runs 17. a6! Nxg2 (if 17... Bxg2 then 18. axb7 Qxb7 19. Ba4 when White wins the exchange and gains space, while if Black advances his b-pawn, then 18. dxc6 Qc8 represents a strengthening of White's position, after which the conditions for accepting the sacrifice are extremely good) 18. axb7 Qxb7 19. dxc6 (if 19. Ba4 as mentioned by Tartakower in The Hypermodern Game, Black would reply 19... Nxe3 20. Rxe3 Bd7) 19... Qc8 20. Nd5! (a typical example of play on the principle that the most important feature of the position, in this case White's pressure on the queenside, takes priority; it should be observed that in pursuing this policy White must also be prepared to lose the exchange) 20... Nxe1 (it might seem more consistent for Black not to make this capture but to press on with his assault; in fact, the chief attacking moves do not work, e.g. 20... h5 21. Nxf6+ and 22. Nxh5, 20... g4 21. Nxe7 Kxe7 22. Nf5+ and White stands better and finally 20... Nxd5 21. Bxd5 after which 21... Qc7, to prevent the advance of the c-pawn, is strongly answered by 22. b4) 21. Qxe1 Be6 (Black must abandon his attack on the king and defend himself in the centre and on the queenside; the decisive factor is that 21... g4 is useless because of 22. f4) 22. Qa5 Bxd5 23. Bxd5 Nxd5 24. Qxd5 Qe6 (otherwise c7!) 25. b4! and White has an overwhelming game.
zh: 白方决定接受弃子，以直接防御应付杀王。若走得好，这条路当然也能过关。但正确反驳弃子的办法，是不吃，而以攻击后翼进行间接防御。d5之后，先前的a5也有了意义，因为现在能攻击b7、c6兵链，获得较好的兵形及后翼空间优势，同时腾出d5供子力中心化。分析如下：17. a6! Nxg2（若17... Bxg2，则18. axb7 Qxb7 19. Ba4，白方得半子并获得空间；若黑方推进b兵，则18. dxc6 Qc8加强白方局面，此后接受弃子的条件极佳）18. axb7 Qxb7 19. dxc6（若像塔塔科维尔在《超现代国际象棋》中所提的19. Ba4，黑方就19... Nxe3 20. Rxe3 Bd7）19... Qc8 20. Nd5!（典型地优先考虑局面最重要的特点，此处就是白方后翼压力；注意，执行这个方针也必须准备损失半子）20... Nxe1（黑方不吃而继续突击似乎更一贯；但主要攻击着都无效，如20... h5 21. Nxf6+再22. Nxh5；20... g4 21. Nxe7 Kxe7 22. Nf5+，白优；最后20... Nxd5 21. Bxd5，若21... Qc7阻止c兵推进，则22. b4有力应对）21. Qxe1 Be6（黑方必须放弃杀王，转在中心和后翼防守；关键是21... g4因22. f4无效）22. Qa5 Bxd5 23. Bxd5 Nxd5 24. Qxd5 Qe6（否则c7!）25. b4!，白方取得压倒性优势。

text: The chief feature of this line is the complete absence of direct defence. White gives up the pawn on g2 and the exchange, which effectively blunts Black's attack, while his excellently-founded action on the queenside gains in power with every move.
zh: 这条变化的主要特点是完全不作直接防御。白方交出g2兵和半子，便有效削弱黑方攻势，而他基础极好的后翼行动则步步增强。

caption_zh: 耶茨—马尔科，17... Qxh3后。

text: After this excessively passive move Black has the better chances. In such positions it is often important to oppose the attacker's queen with one's own — in this case on f1. It was with this aim that Maroczy proposed 18. Re2! g4 19. Qf1.
zh: 这着过于消极，此后黑方机会更好。在这种局面，常须用自己的后迎战进攻方的后，此处是在f1格。为此，马洛契提出18. Re2! g4 19. Qf1。

text: Naturally, White gladly offers the exchange in order to weaken the attack by giving back some material while at the same time still retaining some material advantage. Thus after 19... gxf3 20. Qxf3 Nxe2+ 21. Nxe2 Black's only move to prevent White from consolidating completely is 21... Ng4, but then White immediately gets the chance to counterattack, i.e. 22. dxc6! Qxh2+ 23. Kf1 Nxe3+ 24. Qxe3. The further sharpening of the attack by 24... Bh4 would be dangerous because of 25. cxb7.
zh: 自然，白方乐意交还半子，以部分归还子力削弱攻势，同时仍保留一定子力优势。因此19... gxf3 20. Qxf3 Nxe2+ 21. Nxe2后，黑方为阻止白方完全巩固，唯一着是21... Ng4。但这样白方立即有反击机会：22. dxc6! Qxh2+ 23. Kf1 Nxe3+ 24. Qxe3。24... Bh4继续加强攻势会因25. cxb7而危险。

text: We shall examine two more variations arising out of 19... gxf3 20. Qxf3 (D):
zh: 再考察19... gxf3 20. Qxf3产生的两条变化（见图）：
caption_zh: 耶茨—马尔科分析，19... gxf3 20. Qxf3后。

text: 1) 20... N6h5 21. Bxf4! exf4 22. dxc6. Black cannot win a piece now, since 22... fxg3? permits the white queen to capture on f7, while 22... Nxg3 can be met by 23. Rg2. Black must be modest and play 22... bxc6, allowing White to consolidate by 23. Rg2. The risk involved in 22... O-O-O is illustrated by the continuation 23. Nd5! Nxg3 (23... fxg3 24. Qf5+ Qxf5 25. Nxe7+ Kb8 26. exf5 favours White) 24. Nxe7+ Kb8 25. Rg2 Ne2+ 26. Qxe2 f3 27. c7+ Kxc7 28. Nd5+ Kb8 29. Nf4!, with a characteristic switch from indirect to direct defence; after 29... Rxg2+ 30. Qxg2 White captures the pawn on f3 and remains the better placed [Nunn note 1].
zh: 1）20... N6h5 21. Bxf4! exf4 22. dxc6。黑方现在不能得子，因为22... fxg3?允许白后吃f7，而22... Nxg3可用23. Rg2应对。黑方必须知足地22... bxc6，允许23. Rg2巩固。22... O-O-O的风险见：23. Nd5! Nxg3（23... fxg3 24. Qf5+ Qxf5 25. Nxe7+ Kb8 26. exf5白优）24. Nxe7+ Kb8 25. Rg2 Ne2+ 26. Qxe2 f3 27. c7+ Kxc7 28. Nd5+ Kb8 29. Nf4!，典型地从间接转入直接防御；29... Rxg2+ 30. Qxg2之后白方吃掉f3兵，仍占优〔纳恩注1〕。

text: 2) 20... Rg4 (covering the square f4, lessening the danger on f7, and preparing ...h5-h4) 21. a6! (logically switching to the positional motif on the queenside and thus exploiting the slower tempo of Black’s attack betrayed by the move ...Rg4) 21... b6 (after 21... O-O-O? 22. axb7+ Kb8 23. dxc6 Black would be in great difficulties) 22. dxc6 h5 23. Kh1! (having made good his superiority on the queen’s wing, White goes over to direct defence; he returns the extra piece in order to simplify into a favourable ending) 23... h4 (Black would recover less material by 23... Nxe2 24. Ncxe2, since then 24... h4 is met by 25. Qf1, when White clarifies the position at the further expense of his e-pawn [Nunn note, page 274]) 24. Bxf4 exf4 (the alternative 24... Rxf4 25. Qg2 is equally in White’s favour) 25. Qf1 Rxg3 26. Qxh3 Rxh3 27. Kg2 f3+ 28. Kxh3 fxe2 29. Re1 with a clear advantage to White.
zh: 2）20... Rg4（保护f4，减轻f7的危险，并准备...h5—h4）21. a6!（合乎逻辑地转向后翼的局面棋主题，利用...Rg4暴露的攻势减速）21... b6（21... O-O-O? 22. axb7+ Kb8 23. dxc6，黑方非常困难）22. dxc6 h5 23. Kh1!（确立后翼优势后，白方转为直接防御，归还多子，简化为有利残局）23... h4（23... Nxe2 24. Ncxe2得到的子力更少；24... h4则25. Qf1，白方再付出e兵使局面明朗〔纳恩注2，见274页〕）24. Bxf4 exf4（24... Rxf4 25. Qg2同样有利于白方）25. Qf1 Rxg3 26. Qxh3 Rxh3 27. Kg2 f3+ 28. Kxh3 fxe2 29. Re1，白方明显占优。

text: 1 Actually this just wins for White.
zh: 〔纳恩注1〕实际上，这里白方就是胜势。

text: Now we return to the game after 18. Qd2 (D).
zh: 现在回到实战18. Qd2后的局面（见图）。
caption_zh: 耶茨—马尔科，18. Qd2后。

text: Commentators have praised this move, which, however, could have allowed White to escape. Correct was 18... h5! which excludes the possibility of simplification and wins back the piece without giving up the attack .
zh: 评注者赞扬此着，但它却可能让白方脱身。正确的是18... h5!，排除简化可能，不放弃攻势便可赢回一子〔纳恩注2〕。

text: White misses the chance to liquidate the position which Maroczy pointed out: 19. Nxh5! Qxf3 20. Bxf4 (forced) 20... gxf4+ 21. Ng3 fxg3 22. h3! and Black's attack loses its power. He must be satisfied with winning the exchange by 22... Qf2+ 23. Qxf2 gxf2+ 24. Kxf2 Bh4+ 25. Ke2 Bxe1 26. Rxe1 with a probable draw.
zh: 白方错过了马洛契指出的简化机会：19. Nxh5! Qxf3 20. Bxf4（强制）20... gxf4+ 21. Ng3 fxg3 22. h3!，黑方进攻失去力量。他只能满足于22... Qf2+ 23. Qxf2 gxf2+ 24. Kxf2 Bh4+ 25. Ke2 Bxe1 26. Rxe1得半子，可能和棋。

text: Interesting is 20. Nxh5 Nxh5 21. Qg2 (or 21. f4 g3!) 21... gxf3! 22. Qxg8+ Kd7 when White's queen has not a single square on the g-file from which to defend g2.
zh: 20. Nxh5 Nxh5 21. Qg2（或21. f4 g3!）21... gxf3! 22. Qxg8+ Kd7很有意思，白后在g线上找不到任何能保卫g2的格子。

text: 20... gxf3 21. Rg1 Bh4 22. Bxf4 exf4 23. Nxh5 Bxf2 24. Rxg8+ Ke7 25. Nxf4 Qh4 26. Rg7
zh: 20... gxf3 21. Rg1 Bh4 22. Bxf4 exf4 23. Nxh5 Bxf2 24. Rxg8+ Ke7 25. Nxf4 Qh4 26. Rg7

text: 1 This is still not totally clear after 25... Rxg3 26. Nxg3 Qg4, but White can improve earlier by 25. Ng1! Rxg3 26. Qxg3 with an instant win.
zh: 〔纳恩注1，续273页变化2〕25... Rxg3 26. Nxg3 Qg4后仍不完全明朗。但白方可更早改进：25. Ng1! Rxg3 26. Qxg3，立即获胜。

text: 2 I do not see how this wins back the piece. White can play (amongst other promising ideas) 19. Bc4 h4 20. Bf1 Qd7 21. dxc6 bxc6 22. Nf5, and Black has nothing to show for his sacrifice.
zh: 〔纳恩注2〕我看不出怎样能赢回这枚棋子。白方可以走19. Bc4 h4 20. Bf1 Qd7 21. dxc6 bxc6 22. Nf5，这只是几个有前途的方案之一；黑方的弃子没有得到补偿。

text: Or 26. Rxa8 Bg3 27. h3 Bxf4.
zh: 或26. Rxa8 Bg3 27. h3 Bxf4。

text: 26... Kf8 27. Rxf7+ Kxf7 28. dxc6+ Kg7 29. Ne6+ Kh8 30. Nd5 bxc6 0-1
zh: 26... Kf8 27. Rxf7+ Kxf7 28. dxc6+ Kg7 29. Ne6+ Kh8 30. Nd5 bxc6 0-1

text: This game won the Second Brilliancy Prize.
zh: 此局获得第二佳对局奖。

text: In this position Black is to move and must discover a defence against White's two threats of Nh5 and Nf5. It is fairly easy to reach the conclusion that there is not a large choice; only two moves are worth considering — 1... f5 and 1... Kh8. The first appears more natural than the second, but in fact only the second provides an adequate defence. If 1... f5?, White replies 2. Bxf5! , after which 2... Rxf5 does not work because of 3. Nxf5 gxf5 4. Qg5+ Kf7 5. Qf6+ Ke8 (or 5... Kg8 6. Rf3) 6. e6, and Black loses; nor is 2... gxf5 satisfactory, e.g. 3. Nh5 Rd7 4. e6, when the rook is lost, since if 4... Re7, then 5. Rf3 is decisive: the one course remaining, therefore, is to decline the sacrifice by 2... Ne7, but then White plays 3. Bd3, threatening f5 as well as Nh5.
zh: 此局轮黑走，必须应付Nh5、Nf5两个威胁。不难看出选择不多，只有1... f5和1... Kh8值得考虑。前者看似更自然，实际上只有后者能充分防御。1... f5?则2. Bxf5!，2... Rxf5因3. Nxf5 gxf5 4. Qg5+ Kf7 5. Qf6+ Ke8（或5... Kg8 6. Rf3）6. e6而败；2... gxf5也不行，例如3. Nh5 Rd7 4. e6，车将丢失，因为4... Re7则5. Rf3决定胜负。只剩下2... Ne7拒绝弃子，但白方3. Bd3，同时威胁f5、Nh5。

text: 1... f5? is weak because it 'opens up the position', with the result that White's queen becomes even more effective and is always creating new threats. On the other hand, 1... Kh8, which is also primarily a form of direct defence, should enable Black, provided he can survive the immediate pressure, to make good his material advantage and territorial superiority on the queenside. Let us now examine this second move.
zh: 1... f5?的弱点在于“打开局面”，使白后更有效，不断制造新威胁。另一方面，1... Kh8也主要是直接防御；只要顶住眼前压力，黑方就应能发挥多子和后翼空间优势。现在考察此着。

text: After 2. Nh5 Rg8 3. Nf6 (otherwise 3... Bf8!) 3... Rg7 4. Rf3 Black can just defend himself in time by 4... Qc3 5. Rd1 Be7 and if 6. Rh3, then 6... Bxf6.
zh: 2. Nh5 Rg8 3. Nf6（否则3... Bf8!）3... Rg7 4. Rf3之后，黑方可以4... Qc3 5. Rd1 Be7，6. Rh3则6... Bxf6，恰好及时守住。

text: 2... Rg8 3. Rf3 gxf5
zh: 2... Rg8 3. Rf3 gxf5

text: Forced, since even 3... Bf8 does not prevent White from sacrificing his queen on h7 and mating with the rook on the h-flle.
zh: 强制。即使3... Bf8，也无法阻止白后在h7弃后，再由车在h线将杀。

text: 4. Rh3 Rg7 5. Bxf5 (D)
zh: 4. Rh3 Rg7 5. Bxf5（见图）

text: Now White threatens 6. Bxh7 and 7. Bg6+ followed by mate with the queen at h8, but Black is a knight up at this stage, so the possibility of defence by giving back material arises. As a result of this increase in his resources, Black's defence turns suddenly from direct to indirect, only in the end to return again, after the 'detour' , to direct defence.
zh: 白方现在威胁6. Bxh7、7. Bg6+，再由后在h8将杀；但黑方此时多一马，所以可归还子力防守。防御资源增加，使黑方突然由直接转为间接防御，最终又在“绕行”后回到直接防御。

text: If 6. Rg3, then 6... Rdg8; anything else is answered by the same manoeuvre as now follows.
zh: 若6. Rg3则6... Rdg8。其他着法均可用下面的同一调动应对。

text: 6... Bxe3 7. Bxh7 Bxf4! 8. Qh5
zh: 6... Bxe3 7. Bxh7 Bxf4! 8. Qh5

text: Or 8. Qxf4 Qxf4 9. Bf5+ Kg8 10. gxf4 Nd4 11. Bd3 c5, when Black stands better.
zh: 或8. Qxf4 Qxf4 9. Bf5+ Kg8 10. gxf4 Nd4 11. Bd3 c5，黑优。

text: 8... Bh6 9. Bf5 Nxe5 10. Qxh6+ Qxh6 11. Rxh6+ Kg8 and Black has a winning advantage [Nunn note 1].
zh: 8... Bh6 9. Bf5 Nxe5 10. Qxh6+ Qxh6 11. Rxh6+ Kg8，黑方获得胜势〔纳恩注1〕。

text: In this example too we observe how a successful defence is flexible and unites a diversity of elements. Direct and indirect defence alternate, the attacker’s sacrifice provokes a counter-sacrifice from the defender, and in the end the basic soundness of Black’s position proves itself.
zh: 这一例也说明成功的防御如何灵活地统一各种因素：直接与间接防御交替，进攻方弃子引出防守方反弃，最终黑方局面的基本可靠性得到证实。

text: 1 Although Vuković is correct with his general principles, the above example is hardly a convincing demonstration; whatever Black plays, he cannot hope to defend the position with most of his pieces stuck far away on the queenside. After 1... Kh8 White can play 2. f5! Nxe5 3. Nh5 Rg8 4. fxg6 fxg6 5. Qg5! Nd7 6. Rf7 with a decisive attack, for example 6... Qc3 7. Rd1 Rdf8 8. Rxd7 Qxd3 9. Qe5+ and mates. Moreover, even one of Vuković’s own lines favours White: after 2. Nh5 Rg8 3. Nf6 Rg7 4. Rf3 Qc3 5. Rd1 Be7 White need not allow the capture on f6 but can simply play 6. Qh4! threatening 7. Rh3. Black has nothing better than 6... h5 7. Qg5 Bxf6 8. exf6 Rh7 9. f5 Qe5, but after 10. h4! he is clearly in serious trouble as his rook on h7 is totally out of play.
zh: 〔纳恩注1〕武科维奇所说的一般原则固然正确，但上例很难说有说服力。黑方大部分子力滞留后翼，离王很远，无论怎样走都无法指望守住。1... Kh8后白方可2. f5! Nxe5 3. Nh5 Rg8 4. fxg6 fxg6 5. Qg5! Nd7 6. Rf7，取得决定性攻势，如6... Qc3 7. Rd1 Rdf8 8. Rxd7 Qxd3 9. Qe5+，接着将杀。而且武科维奇自己的一条变化也有利于白方：2. Nh5 Rg8 3. Nf6 Rg7 4. Rf3 Qc3 5. Rd1 Be7后，白方无需允许吃f6，只须6. Qh4!威胁7. Rh3。黑方最好也只能6... h5 7. Qg5 Bxf6 8. exf6 Rh7 9. f5 Qe5，但10. h4!后黑方显然非常困难，因为h7车完全脱离战斗。

text: This position is from the game Rossolimo-Pachman, Hilversum 1947. It is Black's move; he has a promising game and ought really to continue along positional lines, e.g. 1... a5 2. a4 e4 3. Qe2 b6, etc. Instead, he decides to 'invest his advantage in an attack on the king', though the conditions for this are not particularly suitable.
zh: 此局面出自罗索利莫—帕赫曼，希尔弗瑟姆，1947年。轮黑走，黑方局面有前途，本应继续走局面棋路线，例如1... a5 2. a4 e4 3. Qe2 b6等。他却决定“把优势投入杀王”，尽管条件并不特别合适。
caption_zh: 罗索利莫—帕赫曼，希尔弗瑟姆，1947年；黑先。

text: Black opened his attack at the cost of his advantage in the centre. Now White, by ridding himself of his doubled pawns, eliminates the last element of Black's positional superiority, with the result that the latter has only his kingside attack left.
zh: 黑方以中心优势为代价发起进攻。现在白方通过消除自己的叠兵，抹去了黑方局面优势的最后一个因素，结果黑方只剩王翼攻势。

text: As a general rule, the fianchettoed bishop protecting the castled position should not be touched, but here it is a question of gaining a tempo in order to play cxd6 before Nd2. If at once 4. cxd6, Black replies 4... f3, attacking the bishop on g2.
zh: 通常不应调动保护王城的侧翼象，但这里是为了获得一步，先cxd6，再Nd2。立即4. cxd6，黑方就4... f3攻击g2象。

text: If 4... f3, White is not obliged to go in for the double-edged 5. Bxh7+. He also has 5. cxd6 cxd6 6. Nd2 Bg4 7. Qc4, forcing the exchange of queens.
zh: 4... f3后，白方不必选择双刃的5. Bxh7+。还可以5. cxd6 cxd6 6. Nd2 Bg4 7. Qc4，强制兑后。

text: 5. cxd6 cxd6
zh: 5. cxd6 cxd6

text: Black’s position is not strong enough for the uncompromising 5... f3 6. Nd2 Bg4. White would continue 7. Rab1, not allowing his opponent to escape from his material commitments; at the same time, he has a direct defence at hand in the shape of an attack on Black’s queen by Rb5. After, for instance, 7... Rf6 8. Rxb7 Black’s obligations are too great in proportion to the force of his attack. Consequently, if 8... Rh6, White can permit himself 9. h4, a weakening which does not entail danger, since 9... g5 can be countered by 10. Rb5. If instead 8... Qh3, then 9. Nxf3 Bxf3 (otherwise Nh4 and Bg2) 10. Bxf3 Rh6 11. Re1 leads to a win for White.
zh: 黑方局面还不足以支持强硬的5... f3 6. Nd2 Bg4。白方会7. Rab1，不让对手摆脱已经付出的子力代价；同时可随时以Rb5攻后，转入直接防御。例如7... Rf6 8. Rxb7，黑方付出的代价相对于其攻势力量过大。所以8... Rh6后白方可以9. h4，虽削弱却无危险，因为9... g5可10. Rb5应对。若8... Qh3，则9. Nxf3 Bxf3（否则Nh4、Bg2）10. Bxf3 Rh6 11. Re1，白胜。

text: 6. Nd2
zh: 6. Nd2

text: Now ...f3 is no longer possible.
zh: 现在...f3已不可行。
6... Rf6 7. Bf3 Bg4（见图）
caption_zh: 罗索利莫—帕赫曼，7... Bg4后。

text: 8. Bxg4?
zh: 8. Bxg4?

text: This exchange involves the loss of a tempo. White should have switched at once to a counterattack on the queenside, where he is the better placed, for example 8. Rab1! Rh6 9. h4. Then, as we saw above, 9... g5 does not work, nor does 9... a6 because of 10. Rxb7 g5 11. Qc4+. Lastly, there is 9... d5 10. Rxb7, and again 10... g5 is insufficient since after 11. Bxd5+ Kh8 12. Bf7 Be2 13. Qf5 White wins.
zh: 这次交换浪费一步。白方应立即在自己占优的后翼反击，如8. Rab1! Rh6 9. h4。前面已见9... g5无效；9... a6也因10. Rxb7 g5 11. Qc4+不行。最后还有9... d5 10. Rxb7，10... g5仍不足，因11. Bxd5+ Kh8 12. Bf7 Be2 13. Qf5白胜。

text: This is an example of how indirect defence, by clearing the ground on the queenside, makes it easier to revert to direct defence at the critical moment.
zh: 这说明间接防御如何通过清理后翼阵地，便利在关键时刻重新转入直接防御。

text: Here too 10. Rab1 would probably have been better.
zh: 这里也可能10. Rab1更好。

text: After a period of timid play White aims to save himself by blocking the position.
zh: 一段畏缩的行棋后，白方希望封闭局面自救。

text: This move and, in particular, the next, are not the best. Black should have played 13... Re8 14. Rfe1 (otherwise ...Rxe4) 14... Re7, which would have enabled him to retain a slight advantage.
zh: 这着尤其是下一着，都非最佳。黑方应13... Re8 14. Rfe1（否则...Rxe4）14... Re7，保持微弱优势。

text: Admittedly, this forces f3, which shuts the long diagonal to White's queen, but on the other hand, it undertakes an attacking obligation for which there is insufficient justification. The point is that Black is obliged to obtain some concrete advantage before his pawn at h5 becomes an anxiety and he is forced to strengthen White's position by exchanging it on g4. After this mistake White is the better placed and should in the end make his presence felt on the queenside.
zh: 诚然，这迫使f3，堵住白后的长斜线；但也使黑方在依据不足的情况下，承担了必须进攻见效的约束。黑方必须在h5兵成为负担、不得不在g4交换从而加强白方阵形之前，取得某种具体收益。此错之后白方较好，最终应能在后翼有所作为。
15. f3 Na5（见图）
caption_zh: 罗索利莫—帕赫曼，15... Na5后。

text: Though this does not mar White's position much, it would have been stronger to have played 16. Rb5! Nc4 17. Qf2!, when Black's discomfort over the h-pawn is revealed in various ways. Thus, 17... Qxf2+ 18. Rxf2 hxg4 19. fxg4 leaves two pawns en prise, one of which will obviously fall, while if 17... Qxh3, then 18. Ng5 Qg3+ (or 18... Rxg5 19. Rxg5 hxg4 20. Qh2 Qxh2+ 21. Kxh2 Ne3 [Nunn note 1] 22. Rb1 gxf3 23. Kg1 is good for White) 19. Qxg3 fxg3 20. gxh5 a6 21. hxg6 axb5 22. Re1 and White is the better placed.
zh: 这没有严重损害白方局面，但16. Rb5! Nc4 17. Qf2!更强，可从多方面看出h兵给黑方带来的不便。17... Qxf2+ 18. Rxf2 hxg4 19. fxg4后两兵受攻，显然必丢其一；17... Qxh3则18. Ng5 Qg3+（或18... Rxg5 19. Rxg5 hxg4 20. Qh2 Qxh2+ 21. Kxh2 Ne3〔纳恩注1〕22. Rb1 gxf3 23. Kg1，白方较好）19. Qxg3 fxg3 20. gxh5 a6 21. hxg6 axb5 22. Re1，白优。

text: This line, wherein the union of direct and indirect defence is especially close, would have been a much better way of handling the position than the passive one actually chosen.
zh: 这条变化中，直接与间接防御结合得尤其紧密，比实战选择的消极处理好得多。

text: The decisive error. He should have played 17. Qf2; then 17... Qe7 (17... Qxf2+ eventually loses a pawn) 18. gxh5 Rh6 19. Rg1 Rxh5 20. Rxb7! Rxh3+ (or 20... Qxb7 21. Nf6+) 21. Kxh3 Qxb7 22. Qh4 leaves the advantage with White.
zh: 决定性错误。应17. Qf2；17... Qe7（17... Qxf2+最终丢兵）18. gxh5 Rh6 19. Rg1 Rxh5 20. Rxb7! Rxh3+（或20... Qxb7 21. Nf6+）21. Kxh3 Qxb7 22. Qh4，白方保持优势。

text: 21... Nd2! leads to a rook and pawn ending which is winning for Black. White 1 can improve earlier in this variation, but only to the extent of holding the balance. It is therefore doubtful if 16. Rb5 was any stronger than the move played.
zh: 〔纳恩注1〕21... Nd2!导致黑方获胜的车兵残局。白方可以在这条变化中更早改进，但最多只能维持均势。因此16. Rb5是否比实战着更强，值得怀疑。

text: This loses material, but even the more stubborn 18. Nc5 would not help much The deciding point here is that 18. Qf2 does not work because of 18... Qxf2+ 19. Nxf2 Nd2!. and White loses the exchange.
zh: 这会失子，但即使更顽强的18. Nc5也帮不了多少〔纳恩注1〕。关键是18. Qf2因18... Qxf2+ 19. Nxf2 Nd2!而不行，白方丢半子。

text: 18... hxg4 19. fxg4 Re6 20. Qf2 Qe7 21. Rxb7 Qxb7 22. Nc5 Qe7 23. Nxe6 Qxe6 24. Qxf4 Rf8 25. Qg3 Nd2 0-1
zh: 18... hxg4 19. fxg4 Re6 20. Qf2 Qe7 21. Rxb7 Qxb7 22. Nc5 Qe7 23. Nxe6 Qxe6 24. Qxf4 Rf8 25. Qg3 Nd2 0-1

text: In this position White played:
zh: 此局面白方走：

text: 1. Re3
zh: 1. Re3

text: He is clearly preparing to deploy the rook on g3 or h3 in order to attack the opposing king. Moves of this type belong on the whole to a rather more advanced stage of the game, when all the other pieces have been developed; they are also good in closed positions, where the opponent has no chance of counterattacking on an open file. However, even here this sortie on the part of the rook does not entail a very serious commitment for White, since the rook can turn back if it does not succeed in its mission.
zh: 显然，他准备把车调到g3或h3，进攻敌王。这类着法通常适合对局更后面的阶段，即其他子力全已出动；在封闭局面中也好，因为对手无法沿开放线反击。不过，即使此处出车，白方受到的约束也不太大：若任务不能成功，车还可以退回来。

text: 1... Bc6 2. Rg3 Kh8
zh: 1... Bc6 2. Rg3 Kh8

text: This parries the threat of 3. Bh6 without weakening the castled position. 2... Be4 3. Bh6 Bg6 is not so good because of 4. Bxg6 hxg6 5. Be3, when White has attacking chances along the h-file.
zh: 这在不削弱王城的前提下应付了3. Bh6。2... Be4 3. Bh6 Bg6不那么好，因为4. Bxg6 hxg6 5. Be3，白方沿h线有进攻机会。

text: 3. Be3 Be4
zh: 3. Be3 Be4

text: Black is still applying prophylactic direct defence, since the conditions are not yet favourable for a counterattack; the exchange of light-squared bishops ought to lessen the force of the attack and at the same time clear the squares on the c-file for an eventual counterattack.
zh: 黑方仍在作预防性的直接防御，因为反击条件尚不成熟。兑白格象应能削弱攻势，同时清空c线上各格，为日后的反击准备。

text: I Actually White can resign after the reply 18... Ne3.
zh: 〔纳恩注1，接前例〕实际上18... Ne3后白方就可以认输。

text: This threatens Bxe4 followed by Qh5, but it does not take sufficient account of temporal factors, with the result that the initiative now passes to Black. It would have been better to contest the c-file by 4. Rc1.
zh: 威胁Bxe4再Qh5，却没有充分考虑时间因素，主动权因而转到黑方手里。4. Rc1争夺c线较好。

text: The second logical step along a dangerous path: if the attack does not succeed, White will obviously suffer from the lack of communication between his rooks.
zh: 沿危险道路迈出的第二个合乎逻辑的步骤：若进攻不成，白方双车失联显然会造成痛苦。

text: 5... Bxd3 6. Qxd3 (D)
zh: 5... Bxd3 6. Qxd3（见图）
caption_zh: 6. Qxd3后，黑先。

text: Up to here Black has correctly carried through a direct defence without weakening his pawn position, at the same time keeping his trumps in reserve (the c-file and control of the central post at d5). All this has been entirely appropriate to the fairly modest commitments taken on by White. Now he mistakenly supposes that the moment for a counterattack has arrived and makes a careless move, which White could have punished. The situation required direct defence to be continued for one more move, namely, by a renewed consolidation of the king's position by 6... Kg8. The reason is that Black may eventually be forced (by Bg5) to play ...g6, after which Bh6 would threaten the rook protecting f7. This point can be covered by the king after ...Kg8; consequently, Black may then use both his rooks on the c-file, while retaining a sufficient direct defence of the castled position by ...g6, if necessary. 6... h6 would be weaker on account of7 g4, while 6... Rc7 is also incorrect, e.g. 7. Bg5 h6 8. Bf4 followed by g4.
zh: 至此黑方正确地直接防御，没有削弱兵形，同时保留王牌，即c线及对d5中心据点的控制。这完全适合白方相对有限的投入及其约束。现在黑方误以为反击时机已到，随手一着，本可被白方惩罚。局势要求再作一着直接防御，即6... Kg8再次巩固王的位置。原因是黑方以后可能被Bg5迫使...g6，届时Bh6将攻击保护f7的车。...Kg8后，王本身可以保护f7；因此黑方可把双车用于c线，必要时仍用...g6充分直接防御王城。6... h6因7. g4较弱；6... Rc7也不对，例如7. Bg5 h6 8. Bf4，接着g4。

text: This throws away the chance of victory which was afforded by 7. Nd7!. Owing to the threat of Nxf6, Black loses the exchange. He is not helped by 7... Bxh2+ 8. Rxh2! (not 8. Kxh2? Qxd7 9. Bg5, since Black defends himself by 9... Qc7+ and 10... Qc2!) 8... Qxd7 9. Bg5, when he either loses his knight or is mated. After the erroneous text move Black reasserts his advantage [Nunn note 1, page 282].
zh: 放弃了7. Nd7!带来的获胜机会。由于Nxf6的威胁，黑方要丢半子。7... Bxh2+ 8. Rxh2!也无济于事（不是8. Kxh2? Qxd7 9. Bg5，因为黑方9... Qc7+再10... Qc2!可以防守）8... Qxd7 9. Bg5，黑方不是失马就是被将杀。实战错误着以后，黑方重新确立优势〔纳恩注1，见282页〕。

text: Black was threatening 8... Nh5; if 8. Bh6, Black can of course reply 8... Bxe5.
zh: 黑方原来威胁8... Nh5；8. Bh6当然可8... Bxe5。

text: 8... Rc7 9. Qe3 Rfc8
zh: 8... Rc7 9. Qe3 Rfc8

text: Black's counterattack is growing rapidly in strength.
zh: 黑方反击迅速增强。

text: 10. Bg5 Bxe5 11. dxe5 Ng8
zh: 10. Bg5 Bxe5 11. dxe5 Ng8

text: This is not a defensive move but a preparation for later action against the bishop by means of ...h6.
zh: 这不是防守着，而是准备以后...h6针对白象。

text: White concedes that his attack has been beaten off and tries to provide some resistance on the second rank. After 12. Bf6+ Nxf6 13. exf6 Qc5 Black has the better ending.
zh: 白方承认进攻已被击退，试图在第二横线稍作抵抗。12. Bf6+ Nxf6 13. exf6 Qc5则黑方残局更好。

text: The bishop is in danger! A sad fate for an unsuccessful attacker!
zh: 象危险了！进攻失败者的悲惨命运！

text: Otherwise Black opens up White's king position by ...hxg4.
zh: 否则黑方...hxg4打开白王阵地。

text: 19. h6+ Kh7 would not help White either.
zh: 19. h6+ Kh7也无助于白方。

text: He could have put up a better fight by 20. Kh3, though even then Black's game is overwhelming.
zh: 20. Kh3能抵抗得更好，尽管黑方仍占压倒性优势。

text: If 21. Rd1, Black can play 21... Qxd1!.
zh: 21. Rd1，黑方可以21... Qxd1!。

text: 21... Rxf4+ 22. Kxf4 Qd4+ 23. Re4 Qf2! 24. Kg5 Qd2+ 25. Rf4 Qd8+ 26. Kg4 Qxh4#
zh: 21... Rxf4+ 22. Kxf4 Qd4+ 23. Re4 Qf2! 24. Kg5 Qd2+ 25. Rf4 Qd8+ 26. Kg4 Qxh4#

text: If one leaves aside Black’s unpunished mistake on the sixth move, then the whole course of the game is a good illustration of the relationship between the scale of the attacker’s commitment and the method of defence employed. In the first phase White is not heavily committed by his rook’s excursion and Black carries out a cautious direct defence without compromising his king position. He also maintains his hold on the c-file and the centre and eliminates one enemy unit — the light-squared bishop. With f3 and g4 White has already taken on greater obligations and so the time is ripe for indirect defence by means of an action along the c-file. As soon as another unit is eliminated (the knight on e5) it is all over with White’s attack, whereas the counterattack grows from move to move, with the lack of communication between the white rooks as the main cause of White’s misfortune.
zh: 若撇开黑方第6着未被惩罚的错误，对局全过程很好地说明了进攻方投入所形成的约束程度与防御方法之间的关系。第一阶段白车出游，白方受到的约束不大；黑方谨慎地直接防御，不损害王城，同时保持c线与中心的控制，消除一枚敌子——白格象。f3、g4后白方受到的约束增大，沿c线行动进行间接防御的时机成熟。再消除e5马以后，白方攻势完全结束，黑方反击则步步增强；白双车失联是白方不幸的主要原因。

text: 1 White has an even simpler win by 7. Bg5!, after which Black must surrender a piece to avoid being mated on h7.
zh: 〔纳恩注1〕白方还有更简单的7. Bg5!获胜，黑方必须送掉一子，才能避免在h7被将杀。

text: Defence by a central thrust
zh: 以中心突击防御

text: Attacks on the castled king in which the situation in the centre does not play a greater or lesser part are extremely rare, and as a rule it is precisely the soundness of the attacker's central formation which provides the basis for his attack. If this formation is not sound enough, the defender may use indirect defence against it in the first instance, aimed against the central formation's most vulnerable point.
zh: 中心状况完全不起作用的王城攻击极少。通常正是进攻方中心阵形的稳固性，构成进攻基础。若阵形不够稳固，防守方首先可以针对它最脆弱的一点进行间接防御。

text: Why is it that the centre is quite so important and sensitive in the particular case of an attack on the castled king? Because this kind of attack is one of the most complex and many-sided operations in chess, demanding the maximum collaboration of the pieces and a control over all possible consequences right up to the endgame. The centre is the most versatile area on the chessboard; it provides the best conditions for the full co-operation of the pieces — the basis on which positional play is founded and a prerequisite for a favourable endgame. Many-sidedness is the common property belonging to a sound attack on the castled king and to the centre, and this accounts for their mutual interdependence. Correct defence must also be many-sided — this we have seen in the last series of examples — and so each 'little crack in the centre' is more important to the defence than a variety of other weaknesses on the attacker's side.
zh: 为什么中心在王城攻势中尤其重要而敏感？因为这类攻击是棋局中最复杂、最多面的行动之一，要求子力最大程度合作，并掌握一直到残局的所有可能后果。中心是棋盘上用途最广的区域，为子力充分协作提供最佳条件；这既是局面棋的基础，也是有利残局的前提。多面性是可靠的王城攻击与中心的共同属性，解释了两者相互依存。前面一组实例已表明，正确防御也必须具有多面性，因此“中心的每一道小裂缝”，对防守方都比进攻方其他各种弱点更重要。

text: In some of the examples so far we have seen the centre acting as the basis of an attack, while in others the defender has employed indirect defence based on destroying the attacker's centre by sacrificing a piece. We have noticed particularly the case where the defender strives to centralize his pieces — giving a position which as a rule makes possible a combination of direct defence and the indirect form on the other flank. It still remains for us to look at the case of defence by means of a pawn thrust against the attacker's central formation.
zh: 此前有些实例中，中心充当攻击基础；另一些实例中，防守方通过弃子摧毁进攻方的中心，进行间接防御。我们尤其注意过防守方力求把子力集中到中心的情况：这种局面通常允许把直接防御与另一翼的间接防御结合起来。剩下还要考察的是，以兵突击进攻方的中心阵形来防御。

text: Before we pass on to examples, we must be clear that we are concerned here with a central thrust of a particular kind. For why should such a thrust be significant just at the critical phase of the attack? Why did the player not employ it earlier? The point is precisely that we are dealing here with cases where in fact the central thrust is not useful before the crisis, because the attacker has good replies to it. Only when he has increased his commitments and deployed his pieces for the attack does the moment for a thrust in the centre arise; and very often this occurs at a precise, given moment, not a move earlier or later.
zh: 举例前必须明确，这里讨论的是特殊的中心突击。为什么它恰在进攻的关键阶段才有意义？棋手为何不早用？要点就在于：危机出现之前，中心突击其实没有用，因为进攻方有良好应对。只有在进攻方受到更多约束、部署子力进攻之后，中心突击的时机才出现；而且往往恰在某一精确时刻，早一步或晚一步都不行。

text: The following famous game provides a good example of a defensive thrust in the centre.
zh: 下面这盘名局，是防守性中心突击的好例子。

text:
Alekhine - Botvinnik
Nottingham, 1936
Sicilian Defence, Dragon Variation
zh:
阿廖欣—鲍特维尼克
诺丁汉，1936年
西西里防御，龙式变例

text: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 g6 6. Be2 Bg7 7. Be3 Nc6 8. Nb3 Be6 9. f4 O-O 10. g4 (D)
zh: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 g6 6. Be2 Bg7 7. Be3 Nc6 8. Nb3 Be6 9. f4 O-O 10. g4（见图）
caption_zh: 阿廖欣—鲍特维尼克，10. g4后。

text: In choosing the pawn avalanche as a means of attacking the castled king at an early stage of the game, White has undertaken a considerable obligation to carry out his attack incisively to the end. For if Black has his say, his counterattack will find a mass of weak points, files, and diagonals in White's territory; if an endgame is reached, White's advanced pawns may easily become 'cannon-fodder'.
zh: 白方选择在对局早期发动兵雪崩攻击王城，就必须把攻势有力地贯彻到底，已很难回头。因为若黑方获得发言权，其反击会在白方阵地找到大量弱点、直线和斜线；若进入残局，白方前冲的兵容易成为“炮灰”。

text: The moment of undertaking an obligation is also the moment of crisis, the moment for the thrust in the centre, which in the Sicilian as a whole, and in this position particularly, is unstable. Botvinnik perceived the correct moment and struck with 10... d5!.
zh: 作出这种难以回头的投入之时，也是危机的时刻，是中心突击的时刻。整个西西里防御的中心都不稳定，此局面尤其如此。鲍特维尼克识别了正确时机，以10... d5!出击。

text: Let us first see why ...d5 is correct at the precise moment when White plays g4. Let us suppose he has played 10. O-O and examine the difference.
zh: 先看为什么恰在白方g4时...d5正确。假设白方10. O-O，比较二者区别。

text: 1) 10. O-O d5? 11. e5 Ne8 (11... d4 does not work, since White can simply take the pawn) 12. Bf3 Nc7 13. Nc5, when Black must accept the weakening of his position by Nxe6 fxe6, since 13... d4 is defeated by 14. Bxc6.
zh: 1）10. O-O d5? 11. e5 Ne8（11... d4无效，白方直接吃兵即可）12. Bf3 Nc7 13. Nc5，黑方必须容忍Nxe6 fxe6削弱兵形，因为13... d4有14. Bxc6反驳。

text: 2) 10. g4 d5! 11. e5 d4! (now this move is good) 12. Nxd4 (or 12. exf6 Bxf6, when Black wins the piece back with the better game) 12... Nxd4 13. Bxd4 Nxg4! 14. Bxg4 Bxg4, and Black preserves the material balance while gaining the advantage with regard to space, position, and time. There is undoubtedly a great difference between the first and second instances of ...d5.
zh: 2）10. g4 d5! 11. e5 d4!（现在此着很好）12. Nxd4（或12. exf6 Bxf6，黑方吃回一子且局面更好）12... Nxd4 13. Bxd4 Nxg4! 14. Bxg4 Bxg4，黑方保持子力均衡，同时在空间、局面与时间上占优。前后两种...d5的差别无疑很大。

text: Now the question arises why ...d5! is necessary in answer to 10. g4 and what happens if Black does not employ the defensive central thrust. This can be answered by citing the continuation of the game Foltys-Eliskases, Podebrad 1936, where in the same position Black met 10. g4 with 10... Na5 aiming at the square c4. The continuation was 11. g5 Ne8 12. Bd4 (in the game Kan-Botvinnik, Moscow, 1936, 12. Qd2 was played, but Foltys’ move is better) 12... Rc8 13. h4 Nc4 14. Bxc4 Rxc4 15. Qd3 Rc8 16. O-O-O Qd7 17. Rd2 Bg4 (to combat h5, but it surrenders d5 to the enemy knight) 18. Nd5 b6 19. f5! (the avalanche begins to move; Black cannot take the pawn, since the eventual Nxe7+ is decisive) 19... e6 20. Bxg7 Kxg7 21. f6+ Kh8 22. Ne7 Rd8 23. Nd4 Qa4 24. Kb1 Nc7 25. h5 gxh5 26. Rdh2 Rd7 27. e5 (threatening 28. Qxh7+ Kxh7 29. Rxh5+ mating) 27... Rxe7 28. Rxh5 Bxh5 29. Rxh5 1-0.
zh: 现在的问题是，为什么10. g4后必须...d5!？黑方若不用这次防守性中心突击会怎样？福尔蒂斯—埃利斯卡塞斯，波杰布拉迪，1936年的后续可以回答。同一局面，黑方10... Na5瞄准c4。此后11. g5 Ne8 12. Bd4（卡恩—鲍特维尼克，莫斯科，1936年走12. Qd2，但福尔蒂斯此着更好）12... Rc8 13. h4 Nc4 14. Bxc4 Rxc4 15. Qd3 Rc8 16. O-O-O Qd7 17. Rd2 Bg4（应付h5，却把d5交给敌马）18. Nd5 b6 19. f5!（雪崩开始滚动；黑方不能吃兵，因为以后Nxe7+决定胜负）19... e6 20. Bxg7 Kxg7 21. f6+ Kh8 22. Ne7 Rd8 23. Nd4 Qa4 24. Kb1 Nc7 25. h5 gxh5 26. Rdh2 Rd7 27. e5（威胁28. Qxh7+ Kxh7 29. Rxh5+将杀）27... Rxe7 28. Rxh5 Bxh5 29. Rxh5 1-0。

text: Now to return to the Nottingham game, in which Botvinnik did not allow himself to be smothered in this way.
zh: 现在回到诺丁汉之局，鲍特维尼克没有允许自己这样窒息。

text: Clearly, this is the only alternative to 11. e5 which has already been analysed. If 11. exd5 Nxd5 12. Nxd5, Black would gladly exchange queens by 12... Qxd5, thus winning the b-pawn, to say nothing of the ending.
zh: 显然，除了已分析的11. e5，只剩这一选择。11. exd5 Nxd5 12. Nxd5，黑方乐于12... Qxd5兑后，这样会赢得b兵，更不必说残局也对黑方有利。

text: Though the bishop has to withdraw, it is still aggressively placed as far as White's weak pawns at f5 and g4 are concerned.
zh: 象虽然后退，但针对白方f5、g4弱兵而言，它的位置仍有攻击性。

text: 12. exd5 Nb4
zh: 12. exd5 Nb4

text: There is to be no more talk of an attack on the king; the players are now concerned with a struggle for the centre pawn and the d5-square. If White holds out, he can expect success, but if Black overcomes the advancing pawn, the first player's prospects are poor.
zh: 杀王已经谈不上了，双方现在争夺中心兵与d5格。白方若能撑住，就有望成功；黑方若征服这个前进兵，则白方前景堪忧。

text: Whenever Alekhine made an unexpected move the world of commentators dutifully gave it one or two exclamation marks. This happened in the case of this move too, which abandons the struggle for the square d5 and, in fact, also risks losing the game.
zh: 每当阿廖欣走出意外之着，评注界总尽职地加一两个叹号。这着也如此；但它放弃d5争夺，实际上还冒着输棋风险。

text: A better line here is 13. Bf3! gxf5 14. a3 fxg4 15. Bg2. Suggested long ago by Dr Euwe, this was tried in the 2nd match game between Fischer and Reshevsky, New York 1961 when White secured an advantage after 15... Na6 16. Qd3 e6 17. O-O-O Nxd5 18. h3 g3 19. Rhg1 Qd6 20. Bxd5 exd5 21. Nxd5 Kh8 22. Bf4 Qg6. Now Fischer played 23. Qd2 but 23. Qf3! seems to me to be even stronger.
zh: 较好的是13. Bf3! gxf5 14. a3 fxg4 15. Bg2。尤伟博士很早就提出过，后来菲舍尔—雷舍夫斯基，纽约，1961年对抗赛第2局采用。15... Na6 16. Qd3 e6 17. O-O-O Nxd5 18. h3 g3 19. Rhg1 Qd6 20. Bxd5 exd5 21. Nxd5 Kh8 22. Bf4 Qg6，白方取得优势。菲舍尔接着23. Qd2，但我看23. Qf3!更强。

text: Alekhine's original assertion that 13... exd6! was impossible because of 14. a3 Nc6 15. g5 Ne8? 16. f6 etc., has remained unchallenged in chess literature. It is clear, however, that in this kind of situation it is worth looking to see whether the sacrifice of a piece will work or not. Indeed, sound logic argues that it must work, for the whole variation quoted by Alekhine so strengthens Black's position that it is worth his giving up a knight for two pawns. Above all, White's position is exposed as a result of his pawn advances: the thrust d6 leaves him without a 'backbone' in the centre; the reply ...exd6 opens up the e-file and the diagonal d8-h4, while g5 relinquishes control of the c8-h3 diagonal to Black's c8-bishop. The sacrifice can take a number of forms, but I shall give the one which seems best to me. It runs 13... exd6! 14. a3 Nc6 15. g5 Re8! with the following possibilities:
zh: 阿廖欣最初断言，13... exd6!不行，因为14. a3 Nc6 15. g5 Ne8? 16. f6等。这一说法在棋书中一直未受质疑。然而，这种局面显然值得检查弃子是否可行。事实上，合乎逻辑的推理表明它一定可行：阿廖欣给出的整个变化如此加强黑方局面，值得以一马换两兵。首要的是白方冲兵使局面暴露：d6令中心失去“脊梁”；...exd6打开e线和d8—h4斜线；g5则把c8—h3斜线交给c8象。弃子可有多种形式，这里给出我认为最好的一种：13... exd6! 14. a3 Nc6 15. g5 Re8!，有以下可能：
caption_zh: 阿廖欣—鲍特维尼克，13. d6后。

text: 1) 16. gxf6 Rxe3 17. fxg7 (or 17. Nd5 Re5 18. fxg7 Qh4+ 19. Kf1 Bxf5! and Black has a strong attack) 17... Qh4+ 18. Kd2 (or 18. Kf1 Bxf5) 18... Qh6 19. Ke1 and Black has excellent chances. He has no need to consent to a draw by 19... Qh4+ 20. Kd2 Qh6, but can play for a win with 19... Bxf5.
zh: 1）16. gxf6 Rxe3 17. fxg7（或17. Nd5 Re5 18. fxg7 Qh4+ 19. Kf1 Bxf5!，黑方攻势强大）17... Qh4+ 18. Kd2（或18. Kf1 Bxf5）18... Qh6 19. Ke1，黑方机会极佳。他不必19... Qh4+ 20. Kd2 Qh6同意和棋，而可19... Bxf5争胜。

text: 2) 16. Bd4 Nxd4 17. Nxd4 Ng4 18. f6 Bxf6 19. gxf6 Qxf6 20. Rf1 Qh4+ 21. Kd2 Ne3 22. Nf3 Qh6 and Black wins.
zh: 2）16. Bd4 Nxd4 17. Nxd4 Ng4 18. f6 Bxf6 19. gxf6 Qxf6 20. Rf1 Qh4+ 21. Kd2 Ne3 22. Nf3 Qh6，黑胜。

text: 3) 16. Bf2 Ne4 17. Nxe4 (or 17. f6 Nxc3 18. bxc3 Bg4 19. Nc1 Qa5 20. Bd4 Nxd4 21. Qxd4 Qxg5 22. fxg7 Bxe2 23. Nxe2 Qg2 and Black wins) 17... Rxe4 18. f6 Bg4 19. Nc1 Qa5+ 20. Qd2 Qe5 21. Kf1 Qxb2 22. Bxg4 Rxg4 23. Ra2 Qb5+ 24. Ne2 (alternatives are 24. Nd3 Qd5 and 24. Qd3 Qxg5) 24... Re4 25. fxg7 Rxe2 26. Qxe2 Qb1+ with advantage to Black.
zh: 3）16. Bf2 Ne4 17. Nxe4（或17. f6 Nxc3 18. bxc3 Bg4 19. Nc1 Qa5 20. Bd4 Nxd4 21. Qxd4 Qxg5 22. fxg7 Bxe2 23. Nxe2 Qg2，黑胜）17... Rxe4 18. f6 Bg4 19. Nc1 Qa5+ 20. Qd2 Qe5 21. Kf1 Qxb2 22. Bxg4 Rxg4 23. Ra2 Qb5+ 24. Ne2（还可24. Nd3 Qd5和24. Qd3 Qxg5）24... Re4 25. fxg7 Rxe2 26. Qxe2 Qb1+，黑优。

text: Botvinnik must certainly have prepared the move 10... d5! in his private analysis and so should have known all the important continuations. He had probably not reckoned with 13. d6?, and when Alekhine confronted him with it, did not venture on 13... exd6 but was bluffed into playing the drawing move 13... Qxd6?. All great masters, from Homer onwards, have engaged in a little bluff at times.
zh: 鲍特维尼克肯定在私下分析中准备过10... d5!，应当知道所有重要后续。他大概没算到13. d6?，当阿廖欣出此着时，不敢13... exd6，而被虚张声势唬得走了求和的13... Qxd6?。从荷马以来，各领域的大师偶尔都搞一点虚张声势。

text: 14. Bc5 Qf4!
zh: 14. Bc5 Qf4!

text: 14... Qxd1+ would have been weaker, e.g. 15. Rxd1 Nc6 (not 15... Nxc2+ 16. Kd2!) and then White really can play 16. g5 Nd7 17. f6.
zh: 14... Qxd1+较弱，如15. Rxd1 Nc6（不是15... Nxc2+ 16. Kd2!），此时白方确实可以16. g5 Nd7 17. f6。

text: 15. Rf1 Qxh2
zh: 15. Rf1 Qxh2

text: The breakthrough in the centre has allowed Black's queen to infiltrate into White's position, which was weakened by the move g4. Perpetual check is now already in sight.
zh: 中心突破让黑后侵入因g4而削弱的白方阵地，现在已经看得到长将。

text: 16. Bxb4 Nxg4! 17. Bxg4
zh: 16. Bxb4 Nxg4! 17. Bxg4

text: An attempt to defend by 17. Ne4 Qh4+ 18. Nf2? would result in unfortunate consequences, i.e. 18... Ne3 19. Qd2 Qxb4!, etc.
zh: 17. Ne4 Qh4+ 18. Nf2?试图防御，会有不幸后果：18... Ne3 19. Qd2 Qxb4!等。

text: Not 18. Kd2 Bh6+! nor 18. Ke2 Qxg4+ and 19... Qxb4.
zh: 不能18. Kd2 Bh6+!，也不能18. Ke2 Qxg4+，再19... Qxb4。

caption_zh: 科托夫—凯列斯，布达佩斯候选人赛，1950年；黑先。

text: This position is from the game Kotov-Keres, Budapest Ct 1950. White's attack is extremely dangerous, his main threat being Bb1 followed by Qc2. It is Black's move, and the moment is clearly suitable for a thrust in the centre, where Black has not yet engaged his opponent. Keres decided on 1... d5?, but the correct choice was 1... d6!, as we shall see later. Let us first follow the course the game actually took.
zh: 此局面出自科托夫—凯列斯，布达佩斯候选人赛，1950年。白方攻势极其危险，主要威胁是Bb1再Qc2。轮黑走，显然正适合在尚未与对手交锋的中心突击。凯列斯选择1... d5?，但正确的是1... d6!，后面就会看到。先看实战进程。

text: 1... d5? 2. Bb1! (he surrenders both the pawn and the square c4 to Black and threatens Qc2) 2... g5 (if 2... Bxc4, then 3. Qc2 g6 4. Qd2 Kh7 5. Bf6 Nb3 6. Ng5+ Kg8 7. Qf4 Nxa1 8. Qh4 h5 9. Qxh5! followed by mate with the bishop on h7) 3. Qc2 Ng6 4. Nf4! gxh4 5. Nxg6 Re8 6. Nh8! Re7 7. Qh7+ Kf8 8. f4 Nxc4 9. f5 exf5 10. O-O Bc8 11. Bxf5 Bxf5 12. Rxf5 Ke8 13. Rxf7 Kd7 14. Qf5+ Kc6 15. Qf6+ Kd7 16. e6+ Kc6 (or 16... Kd6 17. Rxe7 Qxe7 18. Nf7+, winning the queen) 17. Rxe7 Qxh8 18. Rxc7+ Kb5 (or 18... Kxc7 19. Qe7+ Kb8 20. Rf1) 19. Qe7 a5 20. Qd7+ Ka6 21. Rb1 1-0
zh: 1... d5? 2. Bb1!（把c4兵与c4格都交给黑方，威胁Qc2）2... g5（2... Bxc4则3. Qc2 g6 4. Qd2 Kh7 5. Bf6 Nb3 6. Ng5+ Kg8 7. Qf4 Nxa1 8. Qh4 h5 9. Qxh5!，再以象在h7将杀）3. Qc2 Ng6 4. Nf4! gxh4 5. Nxg6 Re8 6. Nh8! Re7 7. Qh7+ Kf8 8. f4 Nxc4 9. f5 exf5 10. O-O Bc8 11. Bxf5 Bxf5 12. Rxf5 Ke8 13. Rxf7 Kd7 14. Qf5+ Kc6 15. Qf6+ Kd7 16. e6+ Kc6（或16... Kd6 17. Rxe7 Qxe7 18. Nf7+赢后）17. Rxe7 Qxh8 18. Rxc7+ Kb5（或18... Kxc7 19. Qe7+ Kb8 20. Rf1）19. Qe7 a5 20. Qd7+ Ka6 21. Rb1 1-0。

text: After 1... d5?, what is the outstanding feature of the play? Thanks to this move Black won the pawn on c4, but he neither obtained a proper counterattack nor did he harass White's 'captain in the centre' , his pawn on e5. White's attack flowed on unchecked. So the move 1... d5? had only the form of a central thrust and, in essence, did not greatly alter the situation. The true central thrust here, which does in fact parry the attack, is 1... d6! — this has White’s e-pawn as its target. Let us look at the variations that arise from this.
zh: 1... d5?以后，对局最突出的特点是什么？黑方借此赢得c4兵，却既未得到真正的反击，也没骚扰白方的“中心统帅”e5兵，白方攻势畅通无阻。因此1... d5?只有中心突击的形式，实质上没有大改局势。这里真正能抵御攻势的中心突击，是以e兵为目标的1... d6!。下面考察变化。

caption_zh: 科托夫—凯列斯分析，1... d6后。

text: 2. Bb1
zh: 2. Bb1

text: White could, admittedly, maintain his wedge in the centre by 2. f4, but Black would profit from this in two ways: f4 is closed to White's knight, while the continuation 2... Qe8 3. Qd1 Bxc4 4. Bb1 Nf5 5. Qc2 Qc6 shows that Black also has a tempo more here, since the white queen has needed two moves to reach c2; the combination of these factors turns things in Black's favour.
zh: 诚然，白方可2. f4保持中心楔子，但黑方有双重好处：f4堵住白马去路；2... Qe8 3. Qd1 Bxc4 4. Bb1 Nf5 5. Qc2 Qc6还说明黑方多一步，因为白后用了两步才到c2。这些因素结合，使局势有利于黑方。

text: 2... dxe5 3. dxe5
zh: 2... dxe5 3. dxe5

text: Now 3. Qc2 can of course be answered by 3... f5.
zh: 现在3. Qc2当然可用3... f5应对。

text: 3... Qe8 4. Qc2 Ng6 5. Nf4
zh: 3... Qe8 4. Qc2 Ng6 5. Nf4

text: Or 5. O-O Bxc4 6. Re1 Nb3 7. Ra2 Nd4! 8. cxd4 Bxa2 9. Bxa2 Nxh4, when White is left with neither an attack nor any compensation for the exchange.
zh: 或5. O-O Bxc4 6. Re1 Nb3 7. Ra2 Nd4! 8. cxd4 Bxa2 9. Bxa2 Nxh4，白方既无攻势，也没有半子的补偿。

text: The counterattack in the centre by ...d6 has attained its object: now White cannot sustain both his attack and his pawn on e5. He cannot achieve anything by 6. Nh5 Ncxe5 7. Bf6 because of7...Nd3+ 8. Kd1 Bb5 9. a4 Bxa4 10. Rxa4 Qxa4 and Black wins. If 6. Nxg6 fxg6 7. Bg3, Black plays 7... Rd8, after which the threats of ...Rd2 and ...Ne3 guarantee him a material advantage. Should White take the g-pawn, then the exchange of queens leads to a won ending for Black.
zh: ...d6的中心反击已经达到目标：白方无法同时维持攻势和e5兵。6. Nh5 Ncxe5 7. Bf6无所获，因为7... Nd3+ 8. Kd1 Bb5 9. a4 Bxa4 10. Rxa4 Qxa4，黑胜。6. Nxg6 fxg6 7. Bg3，黑方7... Rd8，...Rd2与...Ne3的威胁保证得子。若白方吃g兵，兑后会进入黑方获胜的残局。

text: The various continuations which result from the thrust 1... d6! provide good examples of the following themes:
zh: 1... d6!突击产生的各种后续，很好地说明以下主题：

text: 1) the destruction of the centre when this centre is essential to the attack; in this case Black also gained space for a counterattack via the centre;
zh: 1）摧毁进攻不可或缺的中心；此例中黑方还赢得了经中心反击的空间；

text: 2) liquidating the position to bring about a favourable ending on the basis of the defender's strength in the centre.
zh: 2）凭防守方中心实力，简化为有利残局。

text: Particular attention should be paid to those cases where the central thrust does not lead immediately to a decision but merely serves to maintain the tension in the centre. The next example illustrates the significance of this method of defence.
zh: 尤其应注意：有些中心突击不立即决定胜负，只是维持中心紧张。下一例说明这种防御方法的意义。

text: The diagram below is taken from the game Marshall-Burn, Paris 1900. The opening ran as follows: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 b6 (nowadays this is usually preceded by ...h6) 7. Bd3 Bb7 8. cxd5 exd5 9. Bxf6 (the so-called Albin-Marshall Attack in the Queen's Gambit) 9... Bxf6 10. h4 (D)
zh: 下图取自马歇尔—伯恩，巴黎，1900年。开局如下：1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 b6（本书写作时通常先...h6）7. Bd3 Bb7 8. cxd5 exd5 9. Bxf6（所谓后翼弃兵中的阿尔宾—马歇尔进攻）9... Bxf6 10. h4（见图）。
caption_zh: 马歇尔—伯恩，10. h4后。

text: Here Burn timidly played 10... g6?; this was followed by 11. h5 Re8 12. hxg6 hxg6 13. Qc2 Bg7? (he should have played 13... Kg7 and if 14. O-O-O then 14... Rh8) 14. Bxg6 fxg6 15. Qxg6 Nd7 16. Ng5 Qf6 17. Rh8+ Kxh8 18. Qh7#.
zh: 伯恩怯懦地10... g6?，随后11. h5 Re8 12. hxg6 hxg6 13. Qc2 Bg7?（应13... Kg7；14. O-O-O则14... Rh8）14. Bxg6 fxg6 15. Qxg6 Nd7 16. Ng5 Qf6 17. Rh8+ Kxh8 18. Qh7#。

text: In playing 10... g6? Burn probably wished to exclude the possibility of the classic bishop sacrifice; 10... h6? would not have been correct on account of 11. g4. But is the sacrifice really threatened? And has Black no better move to prevent it than one which weakens his king position? It is an interesting fact here that there is no threat of a sacrifice at all in the original position, yet, if Black plays 10... Re8 or 10... Nd7, it is already, in practice anyway, rather dangerous, although it would still really be incorrect. Let us now play Black's most natural move, 10... c5!, and see why the sacrifice is incorrect: 11. Bxh7+ Kxh7 12. Ng5+ 12... Kh6! (not 12... Kg6 because of 13. Qd3+ nor 12... Kg8 on account of 13. Qh5) 13. Ne2 (White’s most incisive move) 13... g6 14. Nf4 Bxg5! (otherwise 15. h5 is strong; 14... Kg7 fails against 15. Nge6+) 15. hxg5+ Kg7 (if 15... Kxg5 then 16. Rh5+ affords good attacking prospects) 16. Rh6 (had Black played ...Nd7 rather than ...c5 on his tenth move, White would now have a chance with 16. Qg4) 16... Rh8! [Nunn note 1] (16... Qxg5 allows White to get some material back by 17. Rxg6+) 17. Rxg6+ (or 17. Qg4 Rxh6 18. gxh6+ Kh7) 17... fxg6 18. Ne6+ Kg8 19. Nxd8 Rh1+ 20. Kd2 Rxd1+ 21. Rxd1 Bc8 22. dxc5 Kf8! 23. c6 Ke8 24. c7 Na6 with advantage to Black.
zh: 伯恩10... g6?大概是想排除古典弃象；10... h6?因11. g4也不对。但弃象真有威胁吗？黑方难道没有不削弱王城的防范办法？有趣的是，初始局面中根本没有弃象威胁；但若黑方10... Re8或10... Nd7，实际对局中弃象就已相当危险，尽管客观上仍不正确。现在走黑方最自然的10... c5!，看看弃象为何不成立：11. Bxh7+ Kxh7 12. Ng5+，12... Kh6!（不是12... Kg6，因为13. Qd3+；也不是12... Kg8，因为13. Qh5）13. Ne2（白方最锐利的着法）13... g6 14. Nf4 Bxg5!（否则15. h5很强；14... Kg7有15. Nge6+反驳）15. hxg5+ Kg7（15... Kxg5则16. Rh5+，白方有良好进攻前景）16. Rh6（黑方第10着若走...Nd7而非...c5，白方现在可16. Qg4获得机会）16... Rh8!〔纳恩注1〕（16... Qxg5允许17. Rxg6+追回部分子力）17. Rxg6+（或17. Qg4 Rxh6 18. gxh6+ Kh7）17... fxg6 18. Ne6+ Kg8 19. Nxd8 Rh1+ 20. Kd2 Rxd1+ 21. Rxd1 Bc8 22. dxc5 Kf8! 23. c6 Ke8 24. c7 Na6，黑优。

text: Accordingly, there was no threat of a sacrifice and Burn's 10... g6? simply weakened the position without any necessity; this is always a much more dangerous thing than a forced weakening, as Tartakower so finely expressed in his Hypermodern. (For compulsion creates antitheses and hence the possibility of counterplay or compensation, while in the case of a voluntary weakening there is only a naked weak spot without compensation ! )
zh: 因此，本来没有弃象威胁，伯恩10... g6?只是无必要地削弱局面。正如塔塔科维尔在《超现代国际象棋》中说得妙，这永远比被迫削弱危险得多。（被迫行动会产生对立因素，因而可能得到反击或补偿；主动削弱却只有赤裸裸的弱点，没有补偿！）

text: We shall now examine an example of play from the above diagram, where Black correctly maintains the tension in the centre as a means of defence, while avoiding as much as possible any weakening of his king position.
zh: 现在从上图考察一种示范走法：黑方正确维持中心紧张来防御，同时尽量避免削弱王城。

text: White sees that 11. Qc2 g6 12. h5 can be answered by 12... Qe8 protecting g6 and threatening ...cxd4. If he then continues with 13. O-O-O Black resolves the central tension and starts an attack on the castled king (by 13... c4 14. Be2 b5, etc.) which is stronger than White's. 11. Qb1 meets a similar response — and White can no longer castle queenside.
zh: 白方看出11. Qc2 g6 12. h5可12... Qe8应对，保护g6并威胁...cxd4。若13. O-O-O，黑方就解除中心紧张，以13... c4 14. Be2 b5等发起比白方更强的王城攻势。11. Qb1会遇到类似应对，且白方已不能长易位。

text: Putting pressure on White’s d-pawn; now 12. g5 fails against 12... Bxd4.
zh: 向d兵施压；现在12. g5因12... Bxd4失败。

text: The pressure in the centre has made White resort to artificial castling.
zh: 中心压力迫使白方采取人工易位。

text: This weakening is necessary and well-founded here, and therefore not an error. Black perceives the prospects that his light-squared bishop has on the long diagonal, and to open this up he needs to maintain the pressure against d4; to achieve this his dark-squared bishop must also remain on its long diagonal, and accordingly the square g7 must be vacated to provide against g5. Black is naturally not afraid of the ‘hanging pawns’ arising from dxc5; indeed he actually wants to induce them. In the presence of the two bishops such pawns are not usually considered a weakness in any case; here there is the additional matter of forcing open the light-squared diagonal.
zh: 这里的削弱是必要而有根据的，所以并非错误。黑方看到了白格象在长斜线上的前景，而要打开它，就必须保持d4压力；为此黑格象也须留在自己的长斜线上，因此必须腾出g7以应付g5。黑方自然不怕dxc5形成的“悬兵”，实际上还想诱使它们出现。有双象时，这类兵通常本就不算弱点；这里还可借此强制打开白格斜线。

text: 16... Bc8 may be even stronger. By covering e6, Black eliminates the Rxg6+ 1 trick and can safely take on g5 next move.
zh: 〔纳恩注1〕16... Bc8可能更强。保护e6就消除了Rxg6+的战术，黑方下一着可安全吃g5。

text: The move 12... Nc6 is worth mentioning too; this also increases the pressure on the square d4, but it allows 13. g5 after which 13... cxd4 is insufficient on account of 14. gxf6 dxc3 15. Bxh7+!. The classic bishop sacrifice, incorrect on the eleventh move and replaced by g4, has appeared in a correct form in an altered situation [Nunn note 1].
zh: 12... Nc6也值得一提，同样增加d4压力，但允许13. g5，此后13... cxd4因14. gxf6 dxc3 15. Bxh7+!而不足。在第11着不正确、由g4代替的古典弃象，在局面改变后以正确形式出现了〔纳恩注1〕。
caption_zh: 马歇尔—伯恩示范变化，12... g6后。

text: White holds his ground in the centre and at the same time prepares for an eventual doubling on the h-file.
zh: 白方坚守中心，同时准备日后在h线叠车。

text: Not for the sake of the c-file, but to bring the rook to e7, where it will be equally well placed for attack and defence.
zh: 不是为c线，而是准备把车调到e7，兼顾攻守。

text: 16. Kg2 Nb4
zh: 16. Kg2 Nb4

text: Black gives up the pressure on the centre temporarily in order to drive White's bishop back to b1, thus making it more difficult for the rook on a1 to go into action; this is important, since without both the rooks it is hard to carry out an attack on Black's 'artificially-fianchettoed' king position.
zh: 黑方暂时放弃中心压力，把白象赶回b1，从而增加a1车投入战斗的困难。这很重要，因为没有双车，就难以攻击黑方这种“人工侧翼出子”的王城。

text: If 17. Bb5 Black would be able to play 17... Re4! aiming to eliminate the enemy rook, which is very annoying for him at h4. White could not accept the sacrifice, e.g. 18. Nxe4 dxe4 19. Nd2 cxd4!, etc.
zh: 17. Bb5，黑方可17... Re4!，意图消除令他很烦恼的h4车。白方不能接受弃子，如18. Nxe4 dxe4 19. Nd2 cxd4!等。

text: 1 Vukovié offers no analysis to support his view that the sacrifice is correct in this position. It still looks unsound to me.
zh: 〔纳恩注1〕武科维奇没有给出分析，支持他认为此局面中弃象正确的看法。在我看来仍不成立。

text: 18. Nb5 Rce7 19. Nxa7? would be incorrect in view of 19... Ba6 20. a3 Rxa7 21. axb4 Bf1+.
zh: 18. Nb5 Rce7 19. Nxa7?不正确，因为19... Ba6 20. a3 Rxa7 21. axb4 Bf1+。

text: White takes this pawn at a moment when 19... fxg6 would still be dangerous because of the possibility of 20. Rxh7. If White waits any longer, hxg6 will lose its effect and the answer ...fxg6 will be good, opening up the f-file to Black's advantage. If 19. dxc5 Black has the powerful reply 19... Ne5!.
zh: 白方在这个时刻吃兵，因为19... fxg6仍会因20. Rxh7而危险。若再等，hxg6就失效，...fxg6将成为好着，开放f线有利于黑方。19. dxc5则有强力的19... Ne5!。

text: 19... hxg6 20. Ne2 Rce7 21. Nf4 cxd4
zh: 19... hxg6 20. Ne2 Rce7 21. Nf4 cxd4

text: The tension in the centre served Black well while he was defending. Now he turns to attack with the intention of conquering both the d-pawn and the square on which it stands.
zh: 中心紧张在防守时为黑方效力良多。现在他转入进攻，打算同时征服d兵与它占据的格。

text: 22. exd4 (D)
zh: 22. exd4（见图）

text: If 22. Nxd4, Black can either play 22... Ne5 or 22... Nxd4 23. exd4 Re1.
zh: 22. Nxd4，黑方可22... Ne5，或22... Nxd4 23. exd4 Re1。
caption_zh: 马歇尔—伯恩示范变化，22. exd4后。

text: If White does not accept the sacrifice, he loses his d-pawn.
zh: 白方若不接受弃子，就丢d兵。

text: Or 24. Ne5 Nxd4 when Black is attacking the knight on e5 as well.
zh: 或24. Ne5 Nxd4，黑方还攻击e5马。

text: 24... Nxd4 25. Kg1 Qxg5+ 26. Rg4 Qf5 27. Qa4 Bc6 28. Qxa7 Nf3+ and Black wins.
zh: 24... Nxd4 25. Kg1 Qxg5+ 26. Rg4 Qf5 27. Qa4 Bc6 28. Qxa7 Nf3+，黑胜。

text: 11 The phases of the attack on the castled king
zh: 第十一章　攻击已易位王的各个阶段

text: The exposition up to this point may have appeared to some readers to have been a series of fragments, in which the various aspects of the attack on the castled king have been closely looked at but which still need to be combined into a whole. However, it was essential first to collect together as much knowledge as possible about the various elements of the attack on the castled king, then to get to know the main principles of defence against this attack, and only after that to begin to bring everything together in this chapter, which is devoted to the temporal aspect or phases of the attack on the castled king. The temporal aspect here is naturally a framework for the points we wish to make, which rest on the following basic theses, already fairly well elaborated in earlier chapters.
zh: 有些读者可能觉得，前面的论述是一系列片段，虽详细考察了攻击已易位王的各个方面，却仍须整合为一个整体。不过，我们确实必须先尽可能掌握这种进攻各种要素的知识，再了解主要防御原则，然后才能在本章中把一切结合起来。本章讨论的是攻击已易位王的时间进程，也就是各个阶段。时间进程自然只是组织论点的框架，我们要说明的观点，建立在前几章已相当充分阐述的以下基本命题上。

text: 1) An attack on the castled king cannot be successfully carried out on the basis of the attacker's wishes or ‘brilliance’ alone, but the essential conditions for it must also be present.
zh: 1）攻击已易位王，不能只凭进攻者的愿望或“才华”就取得成功，还必须具备必要条件。

text: 2) These preconditions may be fulfilled to a greater or lesser degree, and the attacker's game must adapt itself accordingly.
zh: 2）这些先决条件的满足程度有高有低，进攻方必须相应调整自己的行棋。

text: 3) The degree and type of these preconditions accurately determines the extent of the commitments which the attacker can undertake without harm; thus there is a logical and reciprocal relationship between preconditions and commitments, and by this the actual phase which the attack has reached can be recognized.
zh: 3）先决条件的程度和类型，准确地决定了进攻方能够作出多大的投入、承受多大的约束，而不损害自身局面。因此，先决条件与投入之间存在合乎逻辑的相互关系，由此可以辨认进攻实际处于哪个阶段。

text: The proposition of these theses, which will be illustrated in later examples, leads us first of all to a brief discussion of preconditions and commitments.
zh: 这些命题将在后面的例子中得到说明。提出它们之后，首先需要简要讨论先决条件与投入。

text: Types of preconditions
zh: 先决条件的类型

text: Preconditions are naturally contained in the position itself, whether in the attacker's territory or his opponent's.
zh: 先决条件自然蕴含在局面本身，既可能在进攻方阵地，也可能在对手阵地。

text: The attacker, for instance, may have his pieces strongly deployed in the vicinity of the enemy king position or aimed in that direction, and it may also be that the general mobility of his pieces or his advantage in space assists him in attacking.
zh: 例如，进攻方子力可能有力地部署在敌王附近，或指向那里；也可能是子力整体机动性较好，或空间优势有助于进攻。

text: At the same time, there must be some deficiencies in the defender's camp; the chief of these is the vulnerability of the king position, either through weaknesses in the pawn structure or because pieces are misplaced in relation to the castled position, being overburdened by obligations to cover squares on other parts of the board.
zh: 同时，防守方阵地必须存在某些缺陷，主要是王的位置容易受攻击：或者兵形有弱点，或者棋子对王城而言位置不当，因为它们忙于保护棋盘其他地方的格子，负担过重。

text: These and similar preconditions should generally be fulfilled at the first or initial phase of the attack, but it may also be that they can be created by force at this stage, e.g. by the provocation of weaknesses.
zh: 这些及类似先决条件，一般应在进攻的第一阶段，也就是起始阶段具备；不过，也可以在这个阶段用强制手段创造，例如诱使对手产生弱点。

text: The second phase of an attack can follow a wide variety of courses. It may be a question of a quick attack leading to mate, usually by means of a sacrifice, and in this case it is naturally unimportant to talk of further preconditions. However, if the attack is slower or does not have an uncompromising character, the second phase is usually concerned with the creation of further conditions as guarantees of success. The following are among the most important operations at this stage: the provocation of further weaknesses; the exclusion of one's opponent's counterattack or its suppression; control of the centre; restraint against a central counter-thrust by one's opponent, and so on.
zh: 进攻的第二阶段可能以多种方式发展。有时通过弃子迅速将杀，此时自然不必再谈进一步的先决条件。但如果进攻较慢，或并非孤注一掷，第二阶段通常就要继续创造条件，以保证成功。这个阶段最重要的行动包括：诱出更多弱点，排除或压制对手反击，控制中央，遏制对手中央反突破，等等。

text: The third phase of an attack is of course characterized by the execution, either in the form of mate, of obtaining a decisive material advantage, or of being able to call off the actual attack on the king and obtain a positional advantage or favourable ending.
zh: 进攻的第三阶段，自然以兑现成果为特点：或者将杀，或者获得决定性的子力优势，或者结束直接攻王，转化为局面棋优势或有利残局。

text: Types of commitment
zh: 投入的类型

text: To the above-mentioned types of preconditions necessary for an attack there also correspond various types of commitment which the attacker can, and indeed must, enter on, if he is going to attack.
zh: 与上述进攻必要条件的各种类型相对应，进攻方为了发动攻击，也可以，而且确实必须，作出各种投入，并承受相应约束。

text: The commitments which correspond to the first phase are, of course, minor ones, usually a question of tempi. A player, for instance, spends a tempo improving his prospects for an eventual attack, transferring a piece from one side of the board to the other or the like; admittedly, the degree of commitment involved is not great, but it can become significant if the attack on the king is never carried out. It is natural that contemporary masters, in an era of precise opening play, aim first of all at sound moves, which give nothing away to their opponents and constantly strengthen their general positional build-up; the result of play according to this recipe on both sides is that a drawn position is reached. It should also be said that Alekhine [note 1] knew how to instil a little aggressiveness into his moves even in the opening and create some conditions for attack with a minimum of commitments. This is precisely where his skill lay, and it is this which is lacking in many masters.
zh: 第一阶段相应的投入当然较小，通常只是时间。例如，花一步改善未来的进攻前景，把棋子从一翼调到另一翼，等等。投入程度固然不大，但如果攻王始终未能实现，它也可能变得重要。在开局行棋精确的时代，当代大师自然首先追求稳健着法，不给对手机会，持续加强整体布局；双方都按此行棋，结果就会达到和棋局面。还应指出，阿廖欣【注1】即使在开局，也懂得使着法带上一点攻击性，以最小投入创造一些进攻条件。他的本领恰在于此，而许多大师恰恰欠缺这一点。

text: [Nunn's note 1] and Kasparov!
zh: 【纳恩注1】还有卡斯帕罗夫！

text: A somewhat greater degree of commitment is entailed in the second phase. It may be a question here of a sacrifice accompanied by considerable compensation, of the dislocation of a number of pieces, or, in particular, of the advance of the wing pawns, which as a rule represents a fairly far-reaching positional commitment. Still, in this phase too the sensible player aims to conduct his game with a minimum of commitments, unless he is undertaking an uncompromising mating attack that is certain to succeed. It is especially important that the attacker should avoid a pattern of thinking whereby an unclear attack is reckoned as part of his compensation. For instance, he may sacrifice a knight for two pawns and an ‘attack’; when that ‘attack’ peters out, his reckoning naturally falls to the ground.
zh: 第二阶段需要较大的投入：可能是具有充分补偿的弃子，可能是若干棋子偏离原位，尤其可能是翼兵推进，后者通常意味着影响深远的局面约束。不过，即使在这一阶段，理智的棋手仍会尽量减少投入，除非正在进行必定成功、不容退让的将杀进攻。尤其要避免把尚不明确的攻势算作补偿。例如弃一马换两兵和“进攻”，等这个“进攻”消退，原先的算盘自然就落空了。

text: Assessment of preconditions and commitments
zh: 评估先决条件与投入

text: One of the attacker's most important tasks is assessing the extent to which the preconditions for an attack are present and the degree of commitment which may be incurred. The following positions provide examples of this task.
zh: 进攻方最重要的任务之一，是评估进攻条件具备到什么程度，以及可以承担多大投入。以下局面提供了例子。
caption_zh: 鲍特维尼克—切霍韦尔，莫斯科，1935年，白先。

text: This position is from the game Botvinnik-Chekhover, Moscow 1935. It is White's move, and he has to decide on how to pursue what is already a promising initiative. He has the upper hand in the centre, a strong knight on e5, and well-placed bishops; all these factors together mean that he has some of the preconditions for an attack on the king, without yet having entered on any commitments. He can therefore be said to be on the threshold of the first phase and must consequently look for further moves which will prepare an attack, while committing himself as little as possible. Thus, it would clearly be out of the question to make a pawn advance with h3 and g4, since Black would then find it easy to parry the main threat, after which White would be left only with pawn weaknesses, to say nothing of the dangers which would arise on the diagonal a8-h1.
zh: 此局面来自鲍特维尼克—切霍韦尔，莫斯科，1935年。白先，必须决定如何继续发展已有的可观主动权。白方中央占优，e5马强大，双象位置良好；这些因素结合起来，说明已经具备一些攻王条件，却尚未作出任何会束缚自身的投入。因此可以说，他刚到第一阶段的门槛，应寻找继续准备进攻、同时尽量少受约束的着法。显然不能h3、g4推进兵，因为黑方很容易挡住主要威胁，此后白方只剩兵弱点，更不必说a8-h1斜线上将出现的危险。

text: A slightly lesser degree of commitment would be entailed by White's manoeuvring his a1-rook to h3 via e1 and e3, but it can be shown that such a displacement of the rook would in fact be premature; Black could easily parry the threats involved and then himself prepare for the counter-thrust ...b5 (e.g. by ...Nf8 and ...Rac8) thereby opening up the c-file, over which the white rook on h3 no longer has any influence. Because of this Botvinnik decided on a third plan, which involved the least degree of commitment; this consisted of transferring the c3-knight via d1 and f2 to h3 and thence on to g5. Admittedly, there is a definite commitment here too — in the shape of the number of tempi used; however, Black cannot really take advantage of this, and there is the additional point that the threat posed by the position of the knight on g5 is quite genuine and cannot be easily parried. Now here is the course that the game took:
zh: 把a1车经e1、e3调到h3，投入程度稍小，但也可以证明，这种车的转移实际上过早。黑方很容易挡住威胁，再例如以...Nf8和...Rac8准备...b5反突破，打开c线；h3白车对此便毫无影响。因此，鲍特维尼克选择了投入最小的第三个计划：c3马经d1、f2转到h3，再进入g5。诚然，这也要付出若干步，但黑方无法真正利用这点时间；而且马在g5的威胁是实实在在、难以轻易化解的。实战过程如下：

text: First White thoroughly eliminates the possibility of Black's playing ...b5.
zh: 白方首先彻底排除黑方...b5的可能。

text: 2... Ne8 would probably have been better.
zh: 2... Ne8大概更好。

text: Now there is a weakness in the black king position as well. White still presses on.
zh: 现在黑方王城也出现了弱点。白方继续施压。

text: **5. Ng5! hxg5 6. fxg5**
zh: **5. Ng5! hxg5 6. fxg5**

text: This is of course already the second phase, since White is committed materially; at the same time, his attack breaks through. If now 6... N6h7 7. Nxf7 Nxg5 (or 7... Bxg5 8. Bxh7+ Nxh7 9. Qxe6 [note 1]) 8. Qh5 Ngh7, then 9. d5 exd5 10. Nh6+ Kh8 11. Qf7 Nf6 12. Qg8+ and 13. Nf7#.
zh: 这当然已是第二阶段，因为白方投入了子力；同时，他的进攻取得突破。若现在6... N6h7 7. Nxf7 Nxg5（或7... Bxg5 8. Bxh7+ Nxh7 9. Qxe6【注1】）8. Qh5 Ngh7，则9. d5 exd5 10. Nh6+ Kh8 11. Qf7 Nf6 12. Qg8+，再13. Nf7#。

text: [Nunn's note 1] This allows 9... Bc8, when no win is apparent, so White should prefer 9. Nxd8 Qxd8 10. Qxe6+ Kh8 11. Rae1 with a large advantage.
zh: 【纳恩注1】这允许9... Bc8，白方看不出赢法，因此应改走9. Nxd8 Qxd8 10. Qxe6+ Kh8 11. Rae1，优势很大。

text: [Nunn's note 2] Recent analysis has shown that this further sacrifice is quite wrong, in that Black could later play 8... Kf8! with fair defensive chances. Therefore White should have chosen 7. Nxd7, as given by Vuković.
zh: 【纳恩注2】近来的分析表明，这次进一步弃子完全错误，因为黑方稍后可8... Kf8!，获得相当的防守机会。因此，白方应选择武科维奇给出的7. Nxd7。

text: In fact, it would have been simpler and quicker to play 7. Nxd7 Rxd7 8. gxf6 Bxf6 9. Rxf6 gxf6 10. Qg4+ Kf8 11. Ba3+ Rd6 12. Qf4 Ke7 13. c5.
zh: 实际上，更简单、更快的是7. Nxd7 Rxd7 8. gxf6 Bxf6 9. Rxf6 gxf6 10. Qg4+ Kf8 11. Ba3+ Rd6 12. Qf4 Ke7 13. c5。

text: **7... Kxf7 8. g6+ Kg8 9. Qxe6+ Kh8 10. Qh3+ Kg8 11. Bf5 Nf8 12. Be6+ Nxe6 13. Qxe6+ Kh8 14. Qh3+ Kg8 15. Rxf6! Bxf6 16. Qh7+ Kf8 17. Re1 Be5 18. Qh8+ Ke7 19. Qxg7+ Kd6 20. Qxe5+ Kd7 21. Qf5+ Kc6 22. d5+ Kc5 23. Ba3+ Kxc4 24. Qe4+ Kc3 25. Bb4+ Kb2 26. Qb1#**
zh: **7... Kxf7 8. g6+ Kg8 9. Qxe6+ Kh8 10. Qh3+ Kg8 11. Bf5 Nf8 12. Be6+ Nxe6 13. Qxe6+ Kh8 14. Qh3+ Kg8 15. Rxf6! Bxf6 16. Qh7+ Kf8 17. Re1 Be5 18. Qh8+ Ke7 19. Qxg7+ Kd6 20. Qxe5+ Kd7 21. Qf5+ Kc6 22. d5+ Kc5 23. Ba3+ Kxc4 24. Qe4+ Kc3 25. Bb4+ Kb2 26. Qb1#**
caption_zh: 阿廖欣—吉尔格，塞默灵，1926年，白先。

text: This position arose in the game Alekhine-Gilg, Semmering 1926. It is White's move, and he decided on an attack, although the preconditions were only partially fulfilled. Black's king position is weakened and some of White's pieces are well placed, but there is as yet no communication between his rooks. Meanwhile, it is of decisive importance that Black is able to launch a counterattack based on his control of d4 and the exposed position of the white king; the general instability in the centre is also to Black's advantage. We shall see how Alekhine's attack came to grief in this position.
zh: 此局面出现在阿廖欣—吉尔格，塞默灵，1926年。白先，尽管条件只部分具备，仍决定进攻。黑方王城已经削弱，白方部分棋子位置很好，但双车尚未联通。另一方面，黑方能够利用对d4的控制以及白王的暴露发动反击，这一点具有决定性意义；中央整体不稳定，也有利于黑方。下面会看到，阿廖欣的进攻怎样在这个局面中失败。

text: Seeing that the preconditions for an attack have not been fulfilled, this additional commitment by White turns against him. The correct move, objectively speaking, was 1. Be3, which would have led to approximate equality but not to an attack on the king.
zh: 进攻条件尚未具备，白方这次额外投入便反噬自身。客观而言，正确的是1. Be3，能得到大致均势，却不能发动攻王。

text: **1... Nf6 2. Nxf6+ Qxf6 3. f5 Nd4 4. g5 Nxf3+ 5. Qxf3 hxg5 6. h4 Re8! 7. Kd1** (D)
zh: **1... Nf6 2. Nxf6+ Qxf6 3. f5 Nd4 4. g5 Nxf3+ 5. Qxf3 hxg5 6. h4 Re8! 7. Kd1**（见图）
caption_zh: 阿廖欣—吉尔格，7. Kd1之后，黑先。

text: Black threatened 7... Qxf5.
zh: 黑方原来威胁7... Qxf5。

text: It is clear that White's attack has been repulsed and that he must now defend himself against an action by Black.
zh: 显然，白方进攻已被击退，现在必须防御黑方的行动。

text: **9. Bd2 Ra6! 10. Qh5 Ba4+ 11. Kc1 Rb6 12. Ra2 Bd4 13. b4 Be3 14. Bxe3 Qc3+ 15. Bc2 Qxe3+ 16. Kb1 Bxc2+ 17. Rxc2 axb4 18. Qxh4 bxa3+ 19. Ka2 Qh6!**
zh: **9. Bd2 Ra6! 10. Qh5 Ba4+ 11. Kc1 Rb6 12. Ra2 Bd4 13. b4 Be3 14. Bxe3 Qc3+ 15. Bc2 Qxe3+ 16. Kb1 Bxc2+ 17. Rxc2 axb4 18. Qxh4 bxa3+ 19. Ka2 Qh6!**

text: Since the exchange of queens is now forced (if 20. Qe1, then 20... Qf6 would be decisive) the danger on the h-file disappears and Black's superiority in the endgame is decisive. White lost the game in due course. The game is also, of course, a good example of indirect defence.
zh: 现在兑后已不可避免（若20. Qe1，则20... Qf6决定胜负），h线的危险消失，黑方的残局优势具有决定性。白方随后输棋。当然，本局也是间接防御的好例子。
caption_zh: 格利戈里奇—科斯蒂奇，萨格勒布，1947年，白先。

text: This position is from the game Gligorić-Kostić, Zagreb 1947. White was afraid that, if he allowed ...cxd4 cxd4, he would not be able to maintain his backward pawn at d4, so he played 1. d5 exd5 2. Bxd5, intending to support the centralized bishop on d5, if necessary, by c4.
zh: 此局面来自格利戈里奇—科斯蒂奇，萨格勒布，1947年。白方担心，若允许...cxd4 cxd4，就守不住d4落后兵，于是1. d5 exd5 2. Bxd5，准备必要时以c4支持中央d5象。

text: However, this is not a good plan, since it leaves White with an inflexible position as well as the danger of an inferior endgame. On the other hand, the backward d-pawn is not a great drawback, as long as White strives to obtain compensation in an attack on the king. The preconditions are in fact there, for Black's position has been weakened by ...h6, and White can rapidly post his queen and bishop on the b1-h7 diagonal and so force a further weakness in the shape of ...g6. It should also be noted that Black has no minor pieces on the kingside, while his knight and bishop on the queen's wing are obviously not suitably placed for defence. In the centre Black can only exchange pawns on d4, while a pawn advance on the queenside is too slow. The preconditions for an attack on the castled king are therefore fulfilled to a considerable measure; White can play for an attack — indeed he must, for otherwise he may well find himself in difficulty over the backward pawn.
zh: 但这不是好计划，因为它使白方局面僵化，并有进入劣势残局的危险。反过来，只要白方努力通过攻王取得补偿，d落后兵就不是什么重大缺陷。条件其实已经具备：...h6削弱了黑方，白方可以迅速将后和象部署到b1-h7斜线，迫使黑方再走...g6，产生新弱点。还应注意，黑方王翼没有轻子，后翼的马与象显然也不适合防守。中央黑方只能在d4兑兵，后翼兵的推进又太慢。因此，攻王条件已在很大程度上满足，白方可以，而且确实必须，争取进攻，否则落后兵很可能给他带来困难。

text: If Black plays 1... Rd8 2. Qe4 Nd7 in order to have ...Nf8 in reserve, then the continuation 3. Rfd1 cxd4 4. cxd4 Nf8 5. Bb3 leaves him at a loss to complete his development, whereas White can either play on the c-file or manoeuvre with Nd2-c4-d6.
zh: 若黑方1... Rd8 2. Qe4 Nd7，准备保留...Nf8，则3. Rfd1 cxd4 4. cxd4 Nf8 5. Bb3之后，他便不知如何完成出子；白方则可在c线上行动，或以Nd2-c4-d6调动。

text: **2. Qe4 cxd4 3. cxd4 Rd8**
zh: **2. Qe4 cxd4 3. cxd4 Rd8**

text: After 3... Na5 4. Bd3 g6, White first of all plays 5. Rac1, whereupon counterplay commencing with 5... Bd7 can be answered by 6. d5 exd5 7. Qxd5. If 3... Nb4 4. a3, Black loses a tempo, since his knight cannot go to d5.
zh: 3... Na5 4. Bd3 g6之后，白方先5. Rac1；对5... Bd7开始的反击，可以6. d5 exd5 7. Qxd5应付。若3... Nb4 4. a3，黑方损失一步，因为马不能去d5。

text: **4. Bd3 g6 5. Rac1 Nb4 6. Bb1 Nd5 7. h4 h5**
zh: **4. Bd3 g6 5. Rac1 Nb4 6. Bb1 Nd5 7. h4 h5**

text: Otherwise 8. h5 is strong.
zh: 否则8. h5很强。

text: **8. g4 hxg4 9. Qxg4**, and White has a promising kingside attack.
zh: **8. g4 hxg4 9. Qxg4**，白方在王翼获得有希望的攻势。

text: The creation of preconditions
zh: 创造先决条件

text: The preconditions for a successful attack on the castled king can arise in a number of different ways. Some arise out of the normal process of building up a position; some are created by the player's own moves, which are specifically aimed at such an attack; some occur unnoticed, as it were, in the course of the game; and others are the result of risky or even faulty play by the opponent. Let us leave aside those cases where the preconditions are created ‘unnoticed’ or through faulty play and turn our attention to those whose origin is conscious and calculated. In this connection we are already acquainted with a rule which has few exceptions.
zh: 成功攻击已易位王的先决条件，可以通过多种方式产生。有些来自正常的局面构筑过程，有些由棋手专门针对攻王的着法创造，有些仿佛在行棋过程中不知不觉出现，还有些来自对手的冒险甚至错误走法。暂且不谈“不知不觉”或错误行棋造成条件的情形，转而关注有意识、有计划地创造条件。在这方面，我们已经熟悉一条很少有例外的规则。

text: Of all the different preconditions for an attack on the king, one should create first those which entail the lesser degree of commitment, i.e. those which are of use not only in the event of an attack on the king, but also go to strengthen one's position in general.
zh: 在各种攻王条件中，应该先创造投入较小的那些，也就是不仅对攻王有用，而且能总体加强己方局面的条件。

text: Good posts for one's pieces, spatial advantage, strength in the centre, the security of one's own king — all these are factors of use in an attack on the castled king but which do not commit one to it. Commitment occurs gradually as weaknesses in the castled position are induced and as a flexible central formation is transformed into a fixed one (e.g. when, with pawns at e4 and d4, one plays e5).
