In other words, weaknesses in a castled position can be full of point if it comes to an attack, but otherwise they may be without significance or even useful to the side which has incurred them, e.g. ...h6 may provide a flight square for the king; or ...g6 may prepare the advance ...f5. Equally, a premature advance in the centre can entail a general positional commitment and so profit the opponent in various ways. More gradual commitments also arise from a regrouping of minor pieces outside the castling area but with the sole aim of attacking the castled king. It is already more difficult when it comes to transferring a rook to the third rank, since this rook will need some time to return and reopen communication with the other one, should the attack not succeed. The engagement of minor pieces in the vicinity of the castling area (e.g. as a result of moving a knight to g5) also involves a heavier commitment in terms of tempi. However, the heaviest commitments are those incurred in an attack carried out with the aid of pawns. Of these the heaviest is usually incurred by advancing the g-pawn, next comes the advance of the h-pawn, while advancing the f-pawn entails the least commitment. Now we have a small graduated scale for the degree of commitment incurred by the various operations which are necessary to create the preconditions for an attack on the castled king; it need not be emphasized, perhaps, that this scale has only a general and approximate validity. Let us now examine the following example from practical play.
zh: 棋子的良好据点、空间优势、中央力量、己王安全，这些因素都对攻王有用，却不会迫使己方非攻王不可。投入与约束是在诱出王城弱点、把灵活中央转变为固定阵形的过程中逐渐产生的，例如e4、d4兵形走e5。换言之，若真正发动进攻，王城弱点可能很有意义；否则它们可能毫无影响，甚至有利于拥有它们的一方，例如...h6给王留下逃格，...g6准备...f5。同样，过早推进中央兵也会造成总体上的局面约束，以各种方式便宜对手。在王城区域之外，仅为攻王而重新部署轻子，也会逐渐增加投入。把车调到第三横线，约束已经更大，因为进攻若不成功，车须花时间回撤，重新联通双车。轻子进入王城附近，例如马跳g5，也意味着更大的时间投入。不过，最大的投入来自兵参与的攻击，其中通常以g兵推进最大，h兵次之，f兵最小。这样，我们便有了一份简略的递增等级，衡量为创造攻王条件而采取各种行动所付出的投入。不必强调，这个等级只能一般而近似地适用。下面看一个实战例子。
caption_zh: 阿廖欣—韦宁克，布拉格，1931年，白先。

text: This position is from the opening stages of the game Alekhine-Weenink, Prague 1931. It is White to move.
zh: 此局面来自阿廖欣—韦宁克，布拉格，1931年的开局阶段。白先。

text: The textbooks gave Bc4; Alekhine's move takes into account the fact that Black is about to castle kingside and threatens e4 and e5 followed by Bxh7 (whether Black castles or not). As a result, Black has no better move than ...h6, which means that a weakness in his castled position has already been brought about, and without any special expenditure in time by White, since Bd3 is a natural developing move in this position. Inducing weaknesses like this is naturally correct in any circumstances.
zh: 教科书给的是Bc4；阿廖欣考虑到黑方即将短易位，威胁e4、e5再Bxh7，无论黑方是否易位。结果黑方没有比...h6更好的棋，王城已经被迫产生弱点，而白方没有额外花费时间，因为Bd3在这里是自然的出子着法。这样诱出弱点，自然在任何情况下都正确。

text: With his second move White occupied the centre, with his third he made his king secure, and now he safeguards his central position against the counter-thrust ...c5. Apart from this, b4 prepares the ground for piece regrouping on the queenside.
zh: 白方第二步占据中央，第三步保障王的安全，现在又防备...c5反突破，保护中央。此外，b4还为后翼的子力重新部署作准备。

text: This contains the threat of 6. e5 followed by 7. Qe4 but, at the same time, does not yet commit White in the centre.
zh: 威胁6. e5再7. Qe4，同时尚未固定白方中央的走向。

text: It would be a mistake to play 5. e5 Nd5 6. Rb3 Re8 7. Qe2 Nf8, since Black would then have managed to centralize his knight at d5 and invalidate the attack based on Qe4. The move e5 must clearly be reserved for a later moment when everything else is ready.
zh: 5. e5 Nd5 6. Rb3 Re8 7. Qe2 Nf8则是错误，因为黑方成功将马集中到d5，使Qe4的攻击无效。显然，e5应留到其他准备全已完成之后。

text: Primarily, this frees the square b1 for the bishop so that the queen may be placed in front of it on the diagonal b1-h7. It also makes it possible to transfer the rook to g3 or h3 as part of the attack later on, but it does not otherwise commit White to an attack on the castled king, since the rook can also be used for play, for instance, on the c-file.
zh: 首先是为象腾出b1，让后能在b1-h7斜线上置于象前。它也使车日后能调到g3或h3参与进攻，但并不迫使白方一定攻王，因为车还可用于其他行动，例如转到c线。

caption_zh: 阿廖欣—韦宁克，7... Nh7之后，白先。

text: Black is too weak to fight back in the centre by 7... e5. After 8. dxe5 Nxe5 9. Nxe5 Qxe5 10. Bb2 White obtains a strong attacking position. If 7... Nf8 (in order to meet 8. e5 with 8... Nd5) then 8. Ne5 followed by Rg3, etc.
zh: 黑方太弱，无法7... e5中央反击。8. dxe5 Nxe5 9. Nxe5 Qxe5 10. Bb2之后，白方获得强大的进攻局面。若7... Nf8，准备对8. e5应8... Nd5，则8. Ne5再Rg3等。

text: This central pawn thrust commits White more than any other move hitherto. Clearly, he is now no longer thinking of the endgame but is intent on forcing home an attack on the castled king. It is of decisive importance that Black does not have ...Nd5 available; if he plays, for example, 8... Nb6, White's threats take effect even more quickly, e.g. 9. Qe4 Nf8 10. Qg4 Kh8 11. Qh5, etc. So Black must resort to defence and not play for ...Nd5.
zh: 这次中央兵突破，比此前任何一步都让白方承担更大投入。显然，他已不再考虑残局，而决心把攻王进行到底。关键在于黑方不能走...Nd5；例如8... Nb6，白方威胁反而更快见效：9. Qe4 Nf8 10. Qg4 Kh8 11. Qh5，等等。因此黑方必须防守，不能争取...Nd5。

text: To rid himself of some of the pressure. It also sets a trap, i.e. 9. Qc4 Nhf8 10. Bxf5? Nb6 11. Bxe6+ Kh8, when White loses his bishop.
zh: 减轻一些压力，同时设下陷阱：9. Qc4 Nhf8 10. Bxf5? Nb6 11. Bxe6+ Kh8，白方丢象。

text: **9. exf6 Bxf6 10. Qe4 Nhf8 11. Qg4 Kh8 12. Qh5 Nh7**
zh: **9. exf6 Bxf6 10. Qe4 Nhf8 11. Qg4 Kh8 12. Qh5 Nh7**

text: Otherwise 13. Bxh6 wins.
zh: 否则13. Bxh6取胜。

text: **13. Re1 Rad8 14. g4!**, and now we have reached the position which was dealt with on page 212. White's heaviest positional commitment in the game, the move g4, occurs exactly at the moment when the attack on the castled king has come to a head.
zh: **13. Re1 Rad8 14. g4!**，现在到达第212页讨论过的局面。本局白方最大的局面投入g4，恰好发生在王城攻击达到高潮之时。

text: The reader should observe the time sequence of each operation in this game, particularly with reference to the degree of commitment. The mild commitment incurred by Rb3!, the greater one by e5, and the heaviest one by g4, correspond exactly to the phases of the attack and to the strength of the threats which White has at his disposal.
zh: 读者应注意本局各项行动的先后次序，尤其是投入程度。Rb3!的小投入、e5的较大投入，以及g4的最大投入，准确地对应进攻各阶段以及白方能够制造的威胁强度。

text: After this example, in which we have seen the temporal relationship between the various operations designed to create the preconditions for an attack, let us turn to a separate examination of each of these operations.
zh: 这个例子展示了创造进攻条件的各种行动之间的时间关系，下面分别考察这些行动。

text: First, the inducement of weaknesses in the castled position. This is an important operation, although it usually forms part of another operation and tends to be limited to one or two moves. It can take the form either of the unprovoked or faulty weakening of the castled position or of the correct advance of a pawn or pawns in front of the king which, because of faulty play later on, results in an appreciable weakness (e.g. when a flight square for the king, originally advantageous, becomes a weakness); then there is the case of the weakness which is enforced early on without any loss of tempo, while on the other hand, there are weak points which arise in the sacrificial whirlpool of the attack's final phase. All these cases show our theme in its wider sense. In the narrower sense, the inducement of weaknesses implies an operation on which the attacker spends one or more tempi with the sole aim of weakening his opponent's castled position in a definite way. An operation of this kind which entails an expenditure of several tempi represents a very real commitment, and so it usually belongs to a stage when most of the conditions necessary for an attack have already been fulfilled.
zh: 首先是诱出王城弱点。这是重要行动，虽然通常包含在其他行动之中，往往只有一两步。可能是对手无端或错误地削弱王城，也可能是原本正确推进护王兵，却因后续错误行棋而形成显著弱点，例如原本有利的逃格变成弱点；还有早期不损失时间就迫出的弱点，以及进攻最后阶段在弃子漩涡中产生的弱点。这些都是广义上的相关情形。狭义的“诱出弱点”，是进攻方专门花一步或几步，以特定方式削弱对方王城。若为此花费多步，投入就很实际，因此通常应在大部分进攻条件已经具备的阶段进行。

text: There have already been many examples of the inducement of weaknesses, so two will be sufficient here.
zh: 前面已有许多诱出弱点的例子，这里再举两个便足够。
caption_zh: 利林塔尔—邦达列夫斯基，苏联绝对冠军赛，列宁格勒／莫斯科，1941年，白先。

text: This position is from the game Lilienthal-Bondarevsky, USSR Absolute Championship, Leningrad/Moscow 1941. Black had come to grief through playing an incorrect version of the Marshall Attack in the Ruy Lopez; a pawn up, White does not have a hard task ahead.
zh: 此局面来自利林塔尔—邦达列夫斯基，苏联绝对冠军赛，列宁格勒／莫斯科，1941年。黑方采用了不正确的西班牙开局马歇尔进攻走法，陷入困境；白方多一兵，任务并不艰巨。

text: Provoking Black to weaken his kingside by ...f6, which is difficult to avoid.
zh: 诱使黑方...f6削弱王翼，而这步很难避免。

text: White has devoted a tempo to inducing the weakness ...f6; we shall soon see that it is well worth it.
zh: 白方花一步诱出...f6弱点，很快便会看到，这完全值得。

text: **2... Kh8 3. Re1 Qf8 4. d4 Bd6 5. Nxd6 Qxd6 6. Qh5 g6**
zh: **2... Kh8 3. Re1 Qf8 4. d4 Bd6 5. Nxd6 Qxd6 6. Qh5 g6**

text: The threat of Re8+ provokes a new weakness.
zh: Re8+的威胁又诱出一个新弱点。

caption_zh: 利林塔尔—邦达列夫斯基，8... Kg7之后，白先。

text: White threatened 9. Bxd5 Bxd5 10. Bf4 Qc6 11. Re7.
zh: 白方原来威胁9. Bxd5 Bxd5 10. Bf4 Qc6 11. Re7。

text: Black is lost anyway, with or without this; for example, he faced a threat of 11. Bf4 Qf8 12. Bxc7.
zh: 无论是否走这步，黑方都已败势；例如白方威胁11. Bf4 Qf8 12. Bxc7。

text: The main variation of the combination runs 12... fxg5 13. Qxg5+ Kf8 14. Rf4+! Nxf4 15. Qg8+ Ke7 16. Qf7+ Kd6 17. Qxf4+ Ke7 18. Qf7+ Kd6 19. Qf6+ Qe6 20. Qxe6#.
zh: 组合的主要变化是12... fxg5 13. Qxg5+ Kf8 14. Rf4+! Nxf4 15. Qg8+ Ke7 16. Qf7+ Kd6 17. Qxf4+ Ke7 18. Qf7+ Kd6 19. Qf6+ Qe6 20. Qxe6#。

text: White wins after both 13... Qxg5 14. Rg4 and 13... fxg5 14. Qxc6.
zh: 无论13... Qxg5 14. Rg4，还是13... fxg5 14. Qxc6，白方都胜。

text: Black did not wait for the unanswerable 14. Bxd5.
zh: 黑方没有等待无法应付的14. Bxd5便认输。

text: The continuation from this diagram shows the correct enforcing of a weakness on g6 followed up by consistent play against the focal-point g7; an alternative line illustrates how provocation can be exaggerated with the result that it turns against the attacker.
zh: 从此图开始的变化，展示了正确迫出g6弱点，再贯彻攻击g7焦点的方法；另一分支则说明，诱弱也可能过头，反而不利于进攻方。

text: The queen, on its way to d3, gains a tempo by attacking the knight. The alternative 1. Qb1 h6 2. Qd1 b5 3. Qd3 g6 is inferior. Here, besides the essential weakness at g6, White has also extracted a ‘secondary’ one at h6, but in fact this is not a weakness at all, since it simplifies Black's defence of the focal-point g7. For example, after 4. Bf6 Bd8 5. Qh3 Bxf6 6. exf6 Kh7 7. Rf1 Rh8! 8. Rf3 Kg8 Black has defended himself against White's main threat of Qxh6+, and consequently the situation is no longer clear.
zh: 后在转往d3途中攻击马，赢得一步。另一种1. Qb1 h6 2. Qd1 b5 3. Qd3 g6较差。这里白方除了必要的g6弱点，还多诱出了一个h6“次要弱点”；但它实际上根本不是弱点，因为它使黑方更容易防守g7焦点。例如4. Bf6 Bd8 5. Qh3 Bxf6 6. exf6 Kh7 7. Rf1 Rh8! 8. Rf3 Kg8，黑方防住了主要威胁Qxh6+，局面便不再清楚。

text: Now 3... h6 proves too late, e.g. 4. Qh3 Kh7 5. Rf1 Bd8 6. Rf3 Bxf6 7. exf6 e5 (if 7... Rh8, then 8. Qxh6+) 8. g4 exf4 9. Qh5 Rh8 10. Nxf4 Kg8 11. Bxg6 fxg6 12. Qxg6+ Kf8 13. Re2, and White wins.
zh: 现在3... h6已经太迟，例如4. Qh3 Kh7 5. Rf1 Bd8 6. Rf3 Bxf6 7. exf6 e5（若7... Rh8，则8. Qxh6+）8. g4 exf4 9. Qh5 Rh8 10. Nxf4 Kg8 11. Bxg6 fxg6 12. Qxg6+ Kf8 13. Re2，白胜。

text: **4. Qh3 Bxf6 5. exf6 h5 6. Ng3 e5 7. Qh4 Bg4 8. Nxh5! Bxh5 9. Qg5 Kh7 10. Qxh5+** followed by Qh6 and Qg7#.
zh: **4. Qh3 Bxf6 5. exf6 h5 6. Ng3 e5 7. Qh4 Bg4 8. Nxh5! Bxh5 9. Qg5 Kh7 10. Qxh5+**，再Qh6和Qg7#。

text: The next three examples are concerned with cases where the creation of the preconditions for the attack on the king demands the removal of the opponent's pieces from defensive positions or their displacement in some way.
zh: 接下来三个例子，讨论为创造攻王条件而把对方棋子引离防守位置，或以某种方式使其偏离原位的情形。
caption_zh: 奥凯利—卡斯塔尔迪，希尔弗瑟姆，1947年，白先。

text: This position is taken from the game O'Kelly-Castaldi, Hilversum 1947. Here Black's king position has already been weakened, White's pieces are all well posted, and there is no danger of counterplay in the centre or, indeed, anywhere; the only real obstacle is Black's queen, which is defending the kingside well at the moment, e.g. if 1. Qh6, then 1... Qg7. So the action White takes has the aim of inveigling Black's queen to as far away as b8!
zh: 此局面来自奥凯利—卡斯塔尔迪，希尔弗瑟姆，1947年。黑方王城已被削弱，白方各子位置良好，中央以及其他任何地方都没有反击危险；真正的唯一障碍，是此刻很好地保护王翼的黑后，例如1. Qh6遇1... Qg7。因此，白方行动的目的，是把黑后诱到遥远的b8！

text: Threatening to win Black's a-pawn by 2. Qa5.
zh: 威胁2. Qa5，赢得黑a兵。

text: If 1... Rd7, then 2. Re8, after which both 2... Rd6 and 2... Qg7 are answered by 3. Qa5.
zh: 若1... Rd7，则2. Re8；之后无论2... Rd6还是2... Qg7，都应3. Qa5。

text:
There is no defence against Ng5, e.g. 4... Qf4 5. Ng5 Nf6 6. Bxf7+ Kh8 7. Bxg6.
Actions of this type might be called indirect attacks on the castled king.
zh:
无法防御Ng5，例如4... Qf4 5. Ng5 Nf6 6. Bxf7+ Kh8 7. Bxg6。
这类行动可以称为对已易位王的间接攻击。

text: In the following diagram, some of the preconditions for an attack on Black's king position are already present. White's pieces are fairly well placed, and the blocked centre makes it difficult for Black to counterattack. A breakthrough by ...b5-b4 would require rather lengthy preparation, while the other possibility — capturing White's a-pawn — would bring him too little in return for the tempi spent on it. On the other hand, there are Black's unweakened king position and White's weakness on the light squares. The latter makes itself felt if the position is opened up. But how is White to progress, if he is not to play f5, i.e. if he does not loosen up the situation on the light squares a little? Surely not by 1. Ng5, which clearly involves a doubtful sacrifice. Nor by 1. g4 Nc6 2. Nh4, on which Black plays 2... f5; for while, logically, the blocked position should then be overcome by 3. exf6, in fact the reply 3... gxf6 opens up the prospect of counterplay for Black by ...e5.
zh: 下图中，攻击黑王的部分条件已经具备。白方子力位置较好，中央封闭使黑方难以反击。...b5-b4突破需要相当漫长的准备；另一可能，即吃白a兵，所得又不足以抵偿所花时间。但另一方面，黑方王城尚未削弱，白方白格则薄弱，一旦局面打开便会显现。可是，若不走f5，也就是不稍稍松动白格上的局面，白方又怎样取得进展？当然不能1. Ng5，因为这显然涉及可疑的弃子。也不能1. g4 Nc6 2. Nh4，因为黑方2... f5；按理白方应以3. exf6克服封闭，但实际上3... gxf6却给黑方...e5反击的机会。

text: There is no doubt about it: the position is not yet ripe for an attack on the king; it needs to be strengthened still further, or more exactly, the black pieces need to be driven further away. This can be done by playing the dark-squared bishop, with gain of tempo, on to the diagonal a3-f8, where it will settle.
zh: 毫无疑问，攻王时机尚未成熟，还须加强局面；更准确地说，必须把黑子赶得更远。可以带先手把黑格象调到a3-f8斜线，安置在那里。

text: **1. Bc1 Re8 2. Ba3 Qd7**
zh: **1. Bc1 Re8 2. Ba3 Qd7**

text: The defence is even more difficult after 2... Qc7.
zh: 2... Qc7之后，防守更难。

text: If 3... Qxa4?, then 4. Be7 Qd7 5. Bf6, when Black is without resource.
zh: 若3... Qxa4?，则4. Be7 Qd7 5. Bf6，黑方束手无策。

text: Sacrificing the knight would be not only unclear but also superfluous. The more expendable pawns will now have their say and so bring about the weakening of Black's king position.
zh: 弃马不仅不清楚，而且多余。现在该轮到价值较低、可以投入的兵发挥作用，削弱黑方王城。

text: The pawn on a4 does not count, but the one on c2 must be kept alive.
zh: a4兵无关紧要，但c2兵必须保住。

text: Otherwise White plays 11. gxh6 Qh4 12. Qxh4, followed by 13. Rxg7+ and 14. Ng5.
zh: 否则白方11. gxh6 Qh4 12. Qxh4，再13. Rxg7+及14. Ng5。

text: **11. Rf1 Bd7 12. Rg4 Nf8 13. gxh6 g6 14. Ng5 gxh5 15. Nxf7+ Kh7 16. Rg7#**
zh: **11. Rf1 Bd7 12. Rg4 Nf8 13. gxh6 g6 14. Ng5 gxh5 15. Nxf7+ Kh7 16. Rg7#**
caption_zh: 耶茨—塔卡奇，凯奇凯梅特，1927年，白先。

text: This position is from the game Yates-Takacs, Kecskemet 1927. The preconditions for an attack on Black's king position have been only partially fulfilled; White is hindered particularly by the possibility of a counterattack by Black in the centre or down the c-file. White's prospects would be better if he could succeed in driving away the f6-knight by e5 and then play Ne4. To manage this he must first repulse the black knight from c4, which means sacrificing a pawn. That was just the sort of thing Yates was in the mood for.
zh: 此局面来自耶茨—塔卡奇，凯奇凯梅特，1927年。攻击黑王的条件只部分具备；特别妨碍白方的是黑方可能在中央或沿c线反击。如果能e5赶走f6马，再Ne4，白方前景就会更好。为此必须先把黑马从c4赶开，意味着要弃一兵；这正合耶茨的心意。

text: Black falls in with White's plan and imperils his knight on a3. In taking on this commitment he enables White to acquire additional preconditions for an attack on the king. If Black had played 1... Nb6, which would have been better, White would have had to build up more slowly with 2. Bb2.
zh: 黑方顺着白方计划走，把马置于a3险地。承担这一约束，等于让白方获得额外攻王条件。如果改走较好的1... Nb6，白方便必须2. Bb2，较慢地加强局面。

text: Relatively the best solution for Black would have been to sacrifice a piece for three pawns by 2... Nxc2! 3. exf6 Bxf6 4. Nxc2 Qxc3, although even then the advantage lies with White after 5. Bd3.
zh: 黑方相对最好的办法，是2... Nxc2! 3. exf6 Bxf6 4. Nxc2 Qxc3，以一子换三兵；但即使如此，5. Bd3之后仍是白方占优。

text: 2... dxe5 3. fxe5 Qxc3 leads to interesting possibilities, for example 4. Rd3! Ne4 (or 4... Qc7 5. exf6 Qxg3 6. Rxg3, when Black's knight at a3 and his bishop at e7 are both hanging) 5. Qf4 Qb4 (alternatively, 5... Qc5 6. b4 Qd5 7. Bxa3, and White's threats are just too strong) 6. Qxe4 Nxc2 7. Rh3 g6 8. Qf4, and White wins.
zh: 2... dxe5 3. fxe5 Qxc3会出现有趣的可能，例如4. Rd3! Ne4（或4... Qc7 5. exf6 Qxg3 6. Rxg3，黑方a3马、e7象同时受攻）5. Qf4 Qb4（另一着5... Qc5 6. b4 Qd5 7. Bxa3，白方威胁太强）6. Qxe4 Nxc2 7. Rh3 g6 8. Qf4，白胜。

text: Now the preconditions for an attack on the king are suddenly fulfilled. One black knight has been driven back to e8 and the other deflected to a3; while White's pawn on e5, supported by two good knights, provides a wedge in the centre. All this has cost only one pawn.
zh: 现在攻王条件突然齐备。一匹黑马被赶回e8，另一匹被引到a3；白方e5兵则由两匹好马支持，成为中央楔子。这一切只付出一兵。

text: Although an interesting move, this is nevertheless not the strongest. Correct was 4. Ng5 followed by Bd3; for example, if 4... h6, then 5. Nxf7 Kxf7 6. Bh5+ Kg8 7. Qg6 Qd8 8. f5 exf5 9. e6 Bc6 10. Nxf5 wins for White.
zh: 这步虽有趣，却并非最强。正确的是4. Ng5再Bd3；例如4... h6，则5. Nxf7 Kxf7 6. Bh5+ Kg8 7. Qg6 Qd8 8. f5 exf5 9. e6 Bc6 10. Nxf5，白胜。

text: 4... Bxf6 5. Bxa3 Bd8 would have been rather unpleasant for Black; however, White's attack would not have been so strong in that case on account of the defensive possibility ...f5.
zh: 4... Bxf6 5. Bxa3 Bd8对黑方也颇难受；不过有...f5的防御可能，白方攻势就不会那么强。

text: The decisive mistake. Black ought not to weaken his dark squares, particularly in view of the commitment of his dark-squared bishop to cover a3, as a result of which it is only half at the disposal of the defence. The right course to take was 6... h6! 7. Bxa3 Bxa3 8. exf6 Bf8, for after 9. Nf3 Qd8 10. Ne5 Be8 Black has a complete defence.
zh: 决定性错误。黑方不该削弱黑格，尤其是黑格象还得兼顾a3，因而只能部分用于防守。正确的是6... h6! 7. Bxa3 Bxa3 8. exf6 Bf8，因为9. Nf3 Qd8 10. Ne5 Be8之后，黑方防御完整。

text: **7. exf6 Bf8 8. Nf3 Kg8 9. Ng5 h6 10. Bxa3**
zh: **7. exf6 Bf8 8. Nf3 Kg8 9. Ng5 h6 10. Bxa3**

text: White captures the knight at precisely the most inconvenient moment for Black.
zh: 白方恰在黑方最不方便的时刻吃掉马。

caption_zh: 耶茨—塔卡奇，10... hxg5之后，白先。

text: White can also win simply by 11. Qxg5 Bxa3 12. Bxg6 Kf8 13. Bxf7 Kxf7 14. Qg7+ Ke8 15. f7+ Kd8 16. Qf6+ with a quick mate.
zh: 白方也可以简单地11. Qxg5 Bxa3 12. Bxg6 Kf8 13. Bxf7 Kxf7 14. Qg7+ Ke8 15. f7+ Kd8 16. Qf6+，很快将杀。

text: If 12. Rf3 e5, White must still play Bxg6.
zh: 若12. Rf3 e5，白方仍须Bxg6。

text: Not 13. f7+, since 13... Kf8 14. Qh8+ Ke7 15. Qf6+ sees Black's king wriggling out to d6.
zh: 不能13. f7+，因为13... Kf8 14. Qh8+ Ke7 15. Qf6+后，黑王可钻到d6脱身。

text: If Black meets the threat of 14. Rh3 by 13... e5, his king would not have found refuge on d6. After the text move, Black hopes to meet 14. Qh6 by 14... Kf7, heading for e8, but Yates now finds a new point at which to trouble him!
zh: 若黑方以13... e5应付14. Rh3的威胁，王就无法在d6避难。实战着法后，黑方希望对14. Qh6应14... Kf7，转往e8；但耶茨又找到了制造麻烦的新要点！

text: If 15... Kf7, then 16. Qxb4, and Black is either mated or loses his queen.
zh: 若15... Kf7，则16. Qxb4，黑方非被将杀即丢后。

text: Of the cases where the opponent himself creates a precondition for an attack on the castled king the most important is that which involves the release of tension in the centre. The next diagram provides a good example.
zh: 在对手自行创造王城攻击条件的各种情形中，最重要的是解除中央紧张。下图就是一个好例子。
caption_zh: 尤伟—马洛契，赞德沃特，1936年，黑先。

text: This position is from the game Euwe-Maroczy, Zandvoort 1936. It is Black's move.
zh: 此局面来自尤伟—马洛契，赞德沃特，1936年。黑先。

text: This releases the tension in the centre and so creates the one precondition which White still lacked before he could embark on an attack against the enemy king. Maroczy, a great expert on defence, is playing here under the influence of the thinking of the old school, which paid insufficient attention to the problems of the centre. In the Orthodox Defence to the Queen's Gambit, resolving the central tension by ...c4 generally gives White a powerful attack on the king, for a counterattack based on a pawn majority on the wing is much slower than that which takes place in the centre.
zh: 这解除中央紧张，为白方攻王补齐了最后一项欠缺的条件。马洛契虽是防御大师，此刻却受到旧学派思想的影响，没有充分注意中央问题。在后翼弃兵正统防御中，以...c4解除中央紧张，通常会给白方强大的攻王机会，因为依靠翼侧多兵的反击，比中央反击慢得多。

text: The thematic move for Black here would be 1... Qb6, but that entails the danger of his knight being diverted from the defence of the square h7; e.g., 2. Nxd7 Nxd7 3. dxc5 Nxc5 4. Bb1, threatening Qc2. Sounder, therefore, is 1... Rc8.
zh: 黑方这里符合主题的着法是1... Qb6，但有把马引离h7防守的危险；例如2. Nxd7 Nxd7 3. dxc5 Nxc5 4. Bb1，威胁Qc2。因此1... Rc8更稳健。

text: After 2... Nd5 3. Nxd5 exd5 4. Qc2 Nf6 5. Ng4 Re8 6. Be5 Black's position would be most uncomfortable.
zh: 2... Nd5 3. Nxd5 exd5 4. Qc2 Nf6 5. Ng4 Re8 6. Be5之后，黑方将十分难受。

text: Black's position is too weak for this method of defence; it allows White to get his rooks into active play via d1 and d4. He should have preferred 3... Nf8, although even then White would have retained the advantage.
zh: 黑方局面太弱，不适合这种防守方式，因为白方能经d1、d4激活双车。应选择3... Nf8，尽管那样白方仍保持优势。

text: **4. dxe5 Nh7 5. Qh5 Nf8 6. Rcd1 Qc7 7. Bxh6!**
zh: **4. dxe5 Nh7 5. Qh5 Nf8 6. Rcd1 Qc7 7. Bxh6!**

text: Since Black abandoned the centre, the preconditions for a successful attack on his king have increased with every move. Now the situation is even ripe for a sacrifice.
zh: 自黑方放弃中央以来，成功攻王的条件每一步都在增加。现在甚至连弃子的时机都已成熟。

text: **7... gxh6 8. Rd4 f5 9. exf6 Bxf6 10. Rg4+ Bg7 11. Qxh6 Rad8** (D)
zh: **7... gxh6 8. Rd4 f5 9. exf6 Bxf6 10. Rg4+ Bg7 11. Qxh6 Rad8**（见图）
caption_zh: 尤伟—马洛契，11... Rad8之后，白先。

text: White would have faced a harder task after 11... Re7 12. Ne2 e5, since he could not then have played 13. Ng3 because of 13... Qc6, forcing the exchange of queens. White would have had to play 13. Bf5 Qc6 14. Qg5.
zh: 11... Re7 12. Ne2 e5之后，白方任务会更艰巨，因为不能13. Ng3，否则13... Qc6迫兑后。白方必须13. Bf5 Qc6 14. Qg5。

text: If 12... Rd7, then the manoeuvre Ng3-h5-f6+ is decisive.
zh: 若12... Rd7，则Ng3-h5-f6+的调动决定胜负。

text: 14... Qe7 would not have worked because of 15. Rxg7+!, but 14... e4 would have offered a little more resistance.
zh: 14... Qe7因15. Rxg7+!而不行，但14... e4会稍微顽强一些。

text: **15. Nf5 Ng6 16. Qh5 Qf7 17. h4! Bf8 18. Nh6+ Bxh6 19. Qxh6 Qh7 20. Qg5 Kf7 21. Bxd3 cxd3 22. Qf5+ 1-0**
zh: **15. Nf5 Ng6 16. Qh5 Qf7 17. h4! Bf8 18. Nh6+ Bxh6 19. Qxh6 Qh7 20. Qg5 Kf7 21. Bxd3 cxd3 22. Qf5+ 1-0**

text: Old and modern styles in building up an attack on the king
zh: 构建攻王时的旧式与现代风格

text: The following three games reflect the differences of two periods and three individual styles in preparing and conducting attacks on the king. The first is a sample of old-time brilliance, showing the unfolding of an overwhelming attack resulting from feeble opening play by the opponent. In the second Black makes a risky experiment, and one of his pawns, wandering lonely among the white pieces on the kingside, remains as a consolation and the germ of the subsequent attack. In the third game the underlying conception of the attack is quite different, its main feature being Capablanca’s rational and cautious method of ensuring that every possible means of counterplay on the part of his opponent is first suppressed.
zh: 以下三局体现了两个时代、三种个人风格在准备和实施杀王攻势上的差异。第一局展现往日的辉煌：对手开局软弱，导致压倒性攻势展开。第二局黑方冒险试验，一个兵孤独地游荡在王翼白子之间，作为慰藉留了下来，也成为随后攻势的萌芽。第三局的基本构想大不相同，主要特点是卡帕布兰卡理性而谨慎的方法：首先确保对手的一切可能反击都被压制。

text:
Pillsbury - H. Wolf
Monte Carlo, 1903
Queen’s Gambit Declined, Orthodox Defence
zh:
皮尔斯伯里—H. 沃尔夫
蒙特卡洛，1903年
后翼弃兵拒弃兵变例，正统防御

text: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Nbd7 5. Nf3 Be7 6. e3 O-O 7. Rc1 b6 8. cxd5 exd5 9. Ne5
zh: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Nbd7 5. Nf3 Be7 6. e3 O-O 7. Rc1 b6 8. cxd5 exd5 9. Ne5

text: This is not the best. The normal way of building up the formation known as the Pillsbury Attack is 9. Bd3 followed by O-O and Ne5. However, even in this improved version, Pillsbury's entrenched knight is by no means as great an asset for White as it seemed to Pillsbury's contemporaries (see also the notes to the Pillsbury-Tarrasch game, p.258).
zh: 这并非最佳。所谓皮尔斯伯里进攻阵形，正常构筑方法是9. Bd3，再O-O、Ne5。但即使在这个改进版本中，皮尔斯伯里据守的马给白方带来的益处，也远不如他的同时代人想象的那么大，另参见258页皮尔斯伯里—塔拉什一局的注解。

text: The right procedure was 10... Ne8 11. Bxe7 Qxe7 12. Qf3 Nxe5 13. fxe5 Rd8 14. Bd3 f6, which shows up White's attack to be premature.
zh: 正确的是10... Ne8 11. Bxe7 Qxe7 12. Qf3 Nxe5 13. fxe5 Rd8 14. Bd3 f6，证明白方进攻过早。
caption_zh: 皮尔斯伯里—H. 沃尔夫，10... a6后。

text: We have censured this move in similar positions in the games Pillsbury-Tarrasch and Euwe-Maroczy. It was an error of judgement of a bygone period to abandon the important central tension for the sake of the dim chance of a slowly-advancing queenside pawn majority. It may be said here that modern knowledge of the importance of tension in the centre is the main deterrent against kingside attacks nowadays.
zh: 在皮尔斯伯里—塔拉什、尤伟—马洛契的相似局面中，我们已批评过此着。为了后翼多兵缓慢推进的渺茫机会，放弃重要的中心紧张，是过去那个时代的判断错误。可以说，现代棋手对中心紧张重要性的认识，是本书写作时抑制王翼进攻的主要因素。

text: A rook manoeuvre characteristic of the Pillsbury Attack. Its first aim is to provoke a weakening of the enemy king position in the shape of either ...g6 or ...h6.
zh: 皮尔斯伯里进攻中典型的车调动，首先想诱使敌方王城以...g6或...h6形式削弱。

text: The feebleness of Black's defensive resources — a consequence of his earlier failure to play 12... Re8 instead of 12... c4? — is shown in the alternative line 14... b4 15. Na4 h6 16. Bxh6 gxh6 17. Rg3+ Kh8 18. Nxd7 Nxd7 19. Qh5 and White wins. Therefore, Black cannot appease his opponent with the somewhat lesser evil of ...h6 but will be forced to play ...g6.
zh: 黑方防御资源薄弱，是前面不走12... Re8却走12... c4?的后果。这从14... b4 15. Na4 h6 16. Bxh6 gxh6 17. Rg3+ Kh8 18. Nxd7 Nxd7 19. Qh5，白胜，即可看出。因此黑方不能用危害稍小的...h6安抚对手，而会被迫...g6。

text: If 15... h6 then 16. Bxh6 gxh6 17. Rg3+ Kf8 18. Bxd7 Nxd7 19. Qh5 and mates, while 15... Nf8 is answered by 16. Bxf6 Bxf6 17. Bxh7+ Nxh7 18. Qh5.
zh: 15... h6则16. Bxh6 gxh6 17. Rg3+ Kf8 18. Bxd7 Nxd7 19. Qh5，接着将杀；15... Nf8则16. Bxf6 Bxf6 17. Bxh7+ Nxh7 18. Qh5。

text: 16. Bb1 Nxe5
zh: 16. Bb1 Nxe5

text: From bad to worse; 16... Nf8 offered a better chance of resistance.
zh: 每况愈下。16... Nf8抵抗机会更好。

text: 17. fxe5 Nd7 18. Bxe7 Rxe7 19. Qf3 Nf8 20. Rf1 Qd7 21. Qf6 b4 (D)
zh: 17. fxe5 Nd7 18. Bxe7 Rxe7 19. Qf3 Nf8 20. Rf1 Qd7 21. Qf6 b4（见图）
caption_zh: 皮尔斯伯里—H. 沃尔夫，21... b4后。

text: White has a won game anyway, but this is not the best move. Correct was 22. Ne2 followed by either Nf4-h5 or Ng3-f5. Sacrificing the knight is the typical way to exploit positions of this kind; one of the critical variations runs 22. Ne2 Qc7 (or 22... Qd8 23. Qh4 Rc7 24. Rf6) 23. Nf4 Rd8 24. Nh5! gxh5 (or 24... Ne6 25. Qh4 gxh5 26. Qf6! and wins) 25. Bxh7+ Nxh7 26. Rg3+ Kf8 27. Qh8#.
zh: 白方无论如何已是胜势，但这不是最佳。正确的是22. Ne2，再Nf4—h5或Ng3—f5。弃马是利用这类局面的典型方式。一条关键变化为22. Ne2 Qc7（或22... Qd8 23. Qh4 Rc7 24. Rf6）23. Nf4 Rd8 24. Nh5! gxh5（或24... Ne6 25. Qh4 gxh5 26. Qf6!，白胜）25. Bxh7+ Nxh7 26. Rg3+ Kf8 27. Qh8#。

text: Unaware of the approaching trap, Black proceeds on his slow way. The immediate 24... Rb8 was more resourceful, for then 25. Rf4 (25. Nxa6 Bxa6 26. Qxa6 c3 yields good chances for Black) 25... Rb6 26. e6 Rbxe6! (not 26... Bxe6? 27. Bxg6!) 27. Nxe6 Rxe6 28. Qg5 allows Black the chance to fight back by 28... c3 29. bxc3 Qxc3. The best move for White after 24... Rb8 is 25. e4!.
zh: 黑方没意识到陷阱逼近，仍慢慢前进。立即24... Rb8更有韧性：25. Rf4（25. Nxa6 Bxa6 26. Qxa6 c3，黑方机会很好）25... Rb6 26. e6 Rbxe6!（不是26... Bxe6? 27. Bxg6!）27. Nxe6 Rxe6 28. Qg5，黑方可28... c3 29. bxc3 Qxc3反击。24... Rb8后白方最佳是25. e4!。
25. Rf4 Rb8?（见图）
caption_zh: 皮尔斯伯里—H. 沃尔夫，25... Rb8后。

text: The final blunder; 25... Be6 was the only move.
zh: 最后的败着；25... Be6是唯一着。

text: The coup de grace. If now 26... Nxg6, then 27. Rxg6+ hxg6 28. Rh4.
zh: 致命一击。26... Nxg6则27. Rxg6+ hxg6 28. Rh4。

text: 26... Rb6 27. Qxb6 Nxg6
zh: 26... Rb6 27. Qxb6 Nxg6

text: Or 27... Qxb6 28. Bxf7+ and 29. Rxb6.
28. Qf6 Re8 29. Rf1 Be6 30. Qg5 Kh8 31. Qh5 Nf8 32. Nxe6 Rxe6 33. Rxe6 1-0
zh: 28. Qf6 Re8 29. Rf1 Be6 30. Qg5 Kh8 31. Qh5 Nf8 32. Nxe6 Rxe6 33. Rxe6 1-0

text:
Rauzer - Botvinnik
Leningrad, 1933
Sicilian Defence, Dragon Variation
zh:
劳泽尔—鲍特维尼克
列宁格勒，1933年
西西里防御，龙式变例

text: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 d6 6. Be2 g6 7. Be3 Bg7 8. Nb3 Be6 9. f4 O-O 10. O-O Na5 11. Nxa5
zh: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 d6 6. Be2 g6 7. Be3 Bg7 8. Nb3 Be6 9. f4 O-O 10. O-O Na5 11. Nxa5

text: Translator’s collation note: the scan prints 10... a5 without a knight symbol. The corrected score reads 10... Na5: after 11. Nxa5 Qxa5 the c6-knight has been exchanged, matching the diagram on page 314 and allowing the later 24... Qf6. The corrected full main line is legal.
zh: 〔译者校勘注〕扫描原书第313页印作10... a5，a5前没有马图标。此处校订为10... Na5：11. Nxa5 Qxa5后，c6马已被交换，与第314页棋图相符，并使后来的24... Qf6合法。订正后的完整主线已通过合法性复盘。

text: Nowadays this whole line is reckoned to be harmless for Black.
zh: 本书写作时认为，整条变化对黑方无害。

text: 11... Qxa5 12. Bf3 Bc4 13. Re1 Rfd8 14. Qd2 Qc7
zh: 11... Qxa5 12. Bf3 Bc4 13. Re1 Rfd8 14. Qd2 Qc7

text: Black withdraws his queen in order not to have constantly to reckon with Nd5, which is admittedly not threatened at the moment but which may become a nuisance later.
zh: 黑方撤后，以免总要计算Nd5。虽然目前没有这个威胁，以后却可能造成麻烦。

text: The beginning of a faulty plan. White is preparing for b3 followed by c4, but he does not have the time to carry it out. Correct was 15. Qf2 whereupon Black has nothing better than 15... Qa5.
zh: 错误计划的开始。白方准备b3再c4，却没有时间实施。正确的是15. Qf2，黑方最好也只能15... Qa5。

text: White keeps to his faulty plan. A sounder line was 16. fxe5 dxe5 17. Qf2 though Black would still have somewhat the superior game.
zh: 白方坚持错误计划。较稳妥的是16. fxe5 dxe5 17. Qf2，尽管黑方仍略好。
caption_zh: 劳泽尔—鲍特维尼克，16. b3后。

text: A reckless conception, which has a flaw. The right way to continue was 16... Ba6 17. Nd5 Nxd5 18. Qxd5 (if 18. exd5 then 18... e4 followed by ...Bc3) 18... exf4 19. Bxf4 Bc3! 20. Red1 Bb2 21. Rb1 Be5 22. g3 Qc3! with advantage to Black.
zh: 鲁莽而有缺陷的构想。正确的是16... Ba6 17. Nd5 Nxd5 18. Qxd5（18. exd5则18... e4，再...Bc3）18... exf4 19. Bxf4 Bc3! 20. Red1 Bb2 21. Rb1 Be5 22. g3 Qc3!，黑优。

text: After 17. bxc4 dxe4 Black would win back the piece with the better game; 17. Nxd5 Bxd5 18. exd5 e4 and 17. fxe5 Nxe4 18. Bxe4 dxe4 19. Qf2 Qxe5! are also favourable for Black.
zh: 17. bxc4 dxe4，黑方吃回一子，局面更好；17. Nxd5 Bxd5 18. exd5 e4，以及17. fxe5 Nxe4 18. Bxe4 dxe4 19. Qf2 Qxe5!，也都有利于黑方。

text: After 18. Nxe4 Nxd5 Black retains the initiative without giving up any material, thanks to the threat of ...Nxe3 followed by ...Bd4.
zh: 18. Nxe4 Nxd5，黑方凭借...Nxe3、...Bd4的威胁，不损失子力而保留主动权。

text: 19. gxf3? Qxc4 20. Red1 Rac8 21. Bd4 is unsatisfactory on account of 21... Nxd5 22. Bxg7 Nxc3 23. Qxc3 Rxd1+, after which Black exchanges queens and reaches a won ending. Thus the pawn on f3 is left alive for the time being.
zh: 19. gxf3? Qxc4 20. Red1 Rac8 21. Bd4不行，因为21... Nxd5 22. Bxg7 Nxc3 23. Qxc3 Rxd1+，黑方兑后，进入获胜残局。因此暂时让f3兵存活。

text: White failed to find an answer to Black's double threat (...Nxd5 and ...Ng4) and instead of discovering the flaw in his opponent's bold plan, he gets himself into a difficult position.
zh: 白方未找到应付...Nxd5、...Ng4双重威胁的办法，没有发现对手大胆计划的缺陷，反使自己陷入困难。

text: Ragozin pointed out the continuation 20. Qd3! Ng4 21. Ne4 f5 22. Ng5 f2+ 23. Bxf2 Nxf2 24. Kxf2 (if 24. Qc4 then 24... Qc3 while if 24. Qb3, Black plays 24... Bd4 25. d6+ Kh8, and White has no more than a draw) 24... Qxc5+ 25. Kg3. If Black were then to take the d-pawn, the material balance would be restored but at the cost of allowing White to assume the initiative. For example, after 25... Rxd5 (not 25... Qxd5 because of 26. Re8+) 26. Qb3 Black is suddenly in difficulties owing to the threat of Rcd1 which is decisive even against ...Kh8; consequently, he is forced to play 26... Qb5 27. Rcd1 Qxb3 28. cxb3 Rxd1 29. Rxd1 and go into an unfavourable ending with the white rook on the seventh rank. It is interesting that H. Müller, in his book on Botvinnik, ends the analysis at White's twenty-sixth move, stating that he will have to fight for a draw !
zh: 拉戈津指出：20. Qd3! Ng4 21. Ne4 f5 22. Ng5 f2+ 23. Bxf2 Nxf2 24. Kxf2（24. Qc4则24... Qc3；24. Qb3则24... Bd4 25. d6+ Kh8，白方最多和棋）24... Qxc5+ 25. Kg3。若黑方接着吃d兵，子力虽恢复均衡，却让白方获得主动权。例如25... Rxd5（不是25... Qxd5，因为26. Re8+）26. Qb3，威胁Rcd1，即使...Kh8也决定胜负，黑方突然困难。因此他被迫26... Qb5 27. Rcd1 Qxb3 28. cxb3 Rxd1 29. Rxd1，进入白车占据第七横线的不利残局。有趣的是，H. 米勒在他的鲍特维尼克专著中，在白方第26着就结束分析，声称白方须为和棋苦战〔纳恩注1〕！

caption_zh: 劳泽尔—鲍特维尼克，21. Bd4后。

text: The pawn virus begins to take effect. 22. Bxf2 does not work on account of 22... Bxc3, while 22. Kh1 is defeated by 22... Rxd5! 23. Nxd5 f1=Q+, and White loses his queen.
zh: 兵病毒开始发作。22. Bxf2因22... Bxc3不行；22. Kh1则22... Rxd5! 23. Nxd5 f1=Q+，白方失后。

text: 22. Kf1 Qa6+
zh: 22. Kf1 Qa6+

text: Now the black queen hastens across to h4 via f6; out of the one small pawn there has grown a real kingside attack, which requires the assistance of the queen.
zh: 现在黑后经f6迅速转赴h4。一个小兵竟发展成真正的王翼攻势，需要后的协助。

text: If 23. Ne2 then 23... Bxd4 24. Qxd4 Rxd5 while 23. Qd3 is met by 23... Bxd4 24. Qxa6 Ne3+ 25. Ke2 f1=Q+ 26. Rxf1 bxa6.
zh: 23. Ne2则23... Bxd4 24. Qxd4 Rxd5；23. Qd3则23... Bxd4 24. Qxa6 Ne3+ 25. Ke2 f1=Q+ 26. Rxf1 bxa6。

text: I Many years later Botvinnik published some new analysis of this game, in which he claimed that after 20. Qd3, 20... b6! gives Black a satisfactory position.
zh: 〔纳恩注1〕多年后，鲍特维尼克发表了此局的新分析，声称20. Qd3之后20... b6!能给黑方满意局面。

text: 23... Bxd4 24. Rxd4 Qf6 25. Rcd1
zh: 23... Bxd4 24. Rxd4 Qf6 25. Rcd1

text: 25. Qd3 would have posed Black a more difficult, though still soluble, task. 25... Qh4? is not good because of 26. Qg3 Nxh2+ 27. Kxf2 when Black can only obtain perpetual check with his knight. Instead, Black would have to play 25... Re8 26. d6 Qh4 (not 26... Re3? on account of 27. Nd5) 27. Re4 Nxh2+ 28. Ke2 f5 29. Qc4+ Kf8 30. Re7 Rxe7+ 31. dxe7+ Qxe7+ 32. Kxf2 Ng4+ picking up the rook.
zh: 25. Qd3会给黑方更困难、但仍可解决的任务。25... Qh4?因26. Qg3 Nxh2+ 27. Kxf2而不好，黑方只能用马长将。应改走25... Re8 26. d6 Qh4（不能26... Re3?，因27. Nd5）27. Re4 Nxh2+ 28. Ke2 f5 29. Qc4+ Kf8 30. Re7 Rxe7+ 31. dxe7+ Qxe7+ 32. Kxf2 Ng4+，接着吃车。

text: If 30. Rf1, then 30... Rad8 31. Rxf2 Rxe6+ 32. dxe6 Qg4+ wins.
zh: 30. Rf1则30... Rad8 31. Rxf2 Rxe6+ 32. dxe6 Qg4+，黑胜。

text:
Capablanca - Kan
Moscow, 1935
Queen’s Gambit Declined, Orthodox Defence
zh:
卡帕布兰卡—卡恩
莫斯科，1935年
后翼弃兵拒弃兵变例，正统防御

text: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 d5 4. Nf3 Nbd7 5. Bg5 Be7 6. e3 O-O 7. Rc1 c6 8. Bd3 dxc4 9. Bxc4 Nd5 10. Bxe7 Qxe7 11. O-O N5b6?
zh: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 d5 4. Nf3 Nbd7 5. Bg5 Be7 6. e3 O-O 7. Rc1 c6 8. Bd3 dxc4 9. Bxc4 Nd5 10. Bxe7 Qxe7 11. O-O N5b6?

text: The main line of this variation is 11... Nxc3 12. Rxc3 e5. Moving the knight to b6 is not good, since it neglects to give proper consideration to the central squares; the result is that White's knights can now become very active there.
zh: 此变例主线是11... Nxc3 12. Rxc3 e5。把马调到b6不好，忽视了中心格的重要性，使白马能够在中心变得非常活跃。

text: A strong move, which poses Black a difficult task After 13... exd4 14. Qxd4 he would find himself hard pressed for a satisfactory continuation.
zh: 强着，向黑方提出难题。13... exd4 14. Qxd4后，黑方很难找到令人满意的续着。

text: Creating an unnecessary weakness. Worth considering was the immediate 13... Kh8, preparing ...f5. White could then employ the following simplifying manoeuvre, probably his most promising course in this position: 14. dxe5 Nxe5 15. Nxe5 Qxe5 16. Qd6 Nd7 17. Qxe5 Nxe5 18. Nd6.
zh: 制造不必要的弱点。值得考虑的是立即走13... Kh8，准备...f5。白方可用以下简化调动，可能也是此局面最有前途的路线：14. dxe5 Nxe5 15. Nxe5 Qxe5 16. Qd6 Nd7 17. Qxe5 Nxe5 18. Nd6。
caption_zh: 卡帕布兰卡—卡恩，13... h6后。

text: 14. Qd3 Kh8 15. Ng3 exd4 16. Bc2!
zh: 14. Qd3 Kh8 15. Ng3 exd4 16. Bc2!

text: An intermediate move, the purpose of which is to provoke the weakening ...g6.
zh: 这是一着中间着，目的是诱使对方走...g6，削弱王城。

text: Owing to the threat of 18. e5, Black cannot avoid this weakness; if 17... Nbd7 then 18. Nf5 is strong.
zh: 由于18. e5的威胁，黑方不能避免这一弱点；17... Nbd7则18. Nf5很强。

text: Up to here White has built up a series of preconditions for an attack on the enemy king without making any moves which commit him to it. Now, without any real need, he goes in for such a move. Black's position is not yet ready to be taken by storm, so h4 is still premature. According to the scheme which we have worked out, now would be the time to complete the preconditions for the attack without incurring any positional commitments. White's queen is not yet secure in its possession of the long dark diagonal in view of the possibility of ...Rad8 followed later by ...Na4, and accordingly, priority should have been given to restraining such counterplay, e.g. by 19. b3 Rad8 20. Qc3. Then after 20... Rac8, intending ...c5, Black's plan would be frustrated by 21. Qa5.
zh: 至此白方建立了一系列攻击敌王的条件，却没有走出使自己必须进攻的着法。现在他却在并无实际需要的情况下，作出了迫使自己继续进攻的投入。黑方局面尚未适合强攻，所以h4仍过早。按前面建立的步骤，现在应继续完善进攻条件，而不给自己的局面带来新的约束。黑方可以...Rad8，再...Na4，因此白后在黑格长斜线上尚未稳固；应优先限制这种反击，如19. b3 Rad8 20. Qc3。20... Rac8打算...c5，则21. Qa5可挫败计划。

text: Moreover, h4 is unsuitable in that it makes it more difficult to carry out the thematic move f4 (because of the hole left on g4). However, White's position is strong enough to stand even h4 though it entails the expenditure of greater effort than otherwise would have been necessary.
zh: 此外，h4留下g4漏洞，使主题性的f4更难实施，也因此不合适。不过白方阵地足够强，连h4也承受得起，只是需要比原本更多的努力。

text: After this White's pawn on h4 acquires a function. A better plan would have been either to double rooks on the d-file by 20... Rd7 or to contest control of d4 by 20... c5.
zh: 此后白方h4兵有了作用。更好的计划是20... Rd7在d线叠车，或20... c5争夺d4。

text: 21. Rfe1 Nbd7 22. Bb1 Rfe8 (D)
zh: 21. Rfe1 Nbd7 22. Bb1 Rfe8（见图）
caption_zh: 卡帕布兰卡—卡恩，22... Rfe8后。

text: Starting with 21. Rfe1, this is already White's third consolidating move. Before storming the castled position White first of all excludes every prospect of counterplay by Black; a3 is intended particularly to deprive Black's queen of the square b4. This type of preparation for an attack on the king characterizes many of Capablanca's games. Alekhine preferred a different way of restraining counterplay, namely indirectly by means of dynamic blows. Hence the impression of Alekhine's excessive eagerness and Capablanca's exaggerated caution as the characteristics of their styles. In fact everything depends on the specific position; in some cases Alekhine's method is correct, in others Capablanca's.
zh: 从21. Rfe1开始，这已经是白方第三着巩固局面的棋。强攻王城之前，他先排除黑方一切反击前景；a3主要是为了不让黑后利用b4格。卡帕布兰卡许多对局都以这种准备杀王的方法为特征。阿廖欣则偏爱另一种限制反击的方法，即通过动态打击间接实现。因此人们印象中，阿廖欣过分急切，卡帕布兰卡过分谨慎，成为两人的风格特征。实际上，一切取决于具体局面；有时阿廖欣的方法对，有时卡帕布兰卡的方法对。

text: This makes it easier for White to go over to the attack. 23... Nf8 would not have worked because of 24. Nf5 but 23... Qf8 deserved consideration.
zh: 这使白方更容易转入进攻。23... Nf8因24. Nf5不行，但23... Qf8值得考虑。

text: The queen comes within striking distance of the weakened network of dark squares around the enemy king. There is no need to worry about 27... Ng8, as then 28. Nxg4 fxg4 29. Kf2 is very strong.
zh: 后逼近黑王周围已削弱的黑格网络。27... Ng8无须担心，因为28. Nxg4 fxg4 29. Kf2很强。

text: This thrust in the centre signifies a critical phase of the attack; it is the prelude to the shattering of Black's pawn structure.
zh: 这次中心突击标志着进攻进入关键阶段，是粉碎黑方兵形的序幕。

text: 29... Nd5 30. Nxg4 hxg4 31. h5 Rh8 32. hxg6 fxg6 33. e6! Nf8 34. Bxg6! (D)
zh: 29... Nd5 30. Nxg4 hxg4 31. h5 Rh8 32. hxg6 fxg6 33. e6! Nf8 34. Bxg6!（见图）
caption_zh: 卡帕布兰卡—卡恩，34. Bxg6后。

text: After thorough preparation White's attack is ripe for a sacrificial finish. In view of the threat of Nf5+, Black has nothing better than to accept the offer.
zh: 经过周密准备，白方攻势已经成熟，可以用弃子收尾。由于Nf5+的威胁，黑方最好也只能接受。

text: This allows Black to prolong the game a little. White could have won at once by 38. Re5 Nf6 39. Qh4+ Kg7 40. Nf5+.
zh: 这让黑方稍稍延长对局。白方可38. Re5 Nf6 39. Qh4+ Kg7 40. Nf5+立即获胜。

text: Not, however, 39. Qh4+ and 40. Qxd8 on account of 40... Qd4+.
zh: 不过不能39. Qh4+再40. Qxd8，因为40... Qd4+。

text: 39... Kxg7 40. e7 Re8 41. exf8=Q+ Rexf8 42. f5 Rh4 43. Rcd1 Rf4+ 44. Kg1 Rg4 45. Rd3 Kf7 46. Kf2 Rh8 47. Rb3 b5 48. Ne4 Rh6 49. g3 Rg8 50. Kf3 a5 51. Rd3 a4 52. Rd2 1-0 (Black exceeded the time limit).
zh: 39... Kxg7 40. e7 Re8 41. exf8=Q+ Rexf8 42. f5 Rh4 43. Rcd1 Rf4+ 44. Kg1 Rg4 45. Rd3 Kf7 46. Kf2 Rh8 47. Rb3 b5 48. Ne4 Rh6 49. g3 Rg8 50. Kf3 a5 51. Rd3 a4 52. Rd2 1-0（黑方超时）。

text: Fluctuations in the phases of attack
zh: 进攻阶段中的起伏

text: To conclude the chapter some observations should be added, with examples, to dissuade the reader from accepting the principles and maxims expounded as a rigid pattern. The game of chess is too complex and rich for it to be possible to reveal its finer points fully on the basis of a few formulae.
zh: 本章结束前，还须补充一些观察与实例，免得读者把上述原则和格言当作僵硬模式。国际象棋太复杂、太丰富，无法仅凭几个公式揭示全部精妙。

text: The practical player comes up against exceptions at every turn. Consequently, Lasker is right when he recommends in his book Common Sense in Chess that players should follow the principles of chess with a dash of humour...
zh: 实战棋手处处都会遇到例外。因此拉斯克在《国际象棋常识》中建议，遵循棋理原则时不妨加一点幽默，这是对的……

text: So if we have already seen how the preconditions for an attack on the castled king are created and how the attacker's commitments grow in proportion to the force and form of his attack, it still remains to point out some cases where things develop rather differently: cases where the attack appears to slacken off and, instead of a vigorous assault, suddenly requires quiet moves; where the player only toys with his attack and is in fact aiming at other goals; or where great masters grope in the dark and fail to see something right in front of their noses.
zh: 前面已经看过，如何创造攻击王城的条件，以及进攻方所承担的约束如何随攻势的力度和形式增加。现在还要指出发展方式大不相同的情况：攻势似乎松弛，突然需要安静着而非猛烈突击；棋手只是以进攻作姿态，实际瞄准其他目标；或者大师在黑暗中摸索，竟看不见鼻子前的东西。

text: Quiet moves that kindle the attack
zh: 点燃攻势的安静着

text: So-called quiet moves are often only apparently quiet, and may in fact spark off a fire just as violent ones do. Moves of this type usually occur in positions where the attack appears to be flagging but has in fact reached a point at which a belated addition has to be made to the preconditions in the form of a quiet move, if the attacker is to get any further. Here are a few examples of this kind of quiet move, illustrating the fluctuations that occur in the phases of attack.
zh: 所谓安静着，往往只是表面安静，实际也能像激烈着一样引起大火。这类着法通常出现在攻势看似衰退的局面；实际上是要继续推进，就必须用一着安静着补足此前欠缺的进攻条件。下面几个安静着实例，说明进攻阶段中发生的起伏。

text: The following position is from the game Teichmann-Schlechter, Carlsbad 1911. It is White's move, and he begins with a sacrifice on f7.
zh: 下例出自泰希曼—施莱希特，卡尔斯巴德，1911年。轮白走，他先在f7弃子。
caption_zh: 泰希曼—施莱希特，卡尔斯巴德，1911年；白先。

text: 1. Bxf7+ Kxf7 2. Ng5+ Kg8 3. Qh5 Nxf5 4. Qxh7+ Kf8 5. Qxf5+ Kg8
zh: 1. Bxf7+ Kxf7 2. Ng5+ Kg8 3. Qh5 Nxf5 4. Qxh7+ Kf8 5. Qxf5+ Kg8

text: After 5... Ke7 6. Qe6+ Kd8 7. Nf7+ Black would lose his queen.
zh: 5... Ke7 6. Qe6+ Kd8 7. Nf7+，黑方失后。

text: After a series of checks we suddenly get this quiet move, which does not provide any additional threat but merely blocks the g-pawn. This is precisely to the point in this position, since if, for example, 6. Re3, Black plays 6... g6 7. Qxg6+ Qg7, when White is still a long way from his goal. The fact that it is both possible and good to devote a whole tempo to blocking the g-pawn is a result of Black's inability to organize an effective defence. He cannot move his queen or rook to e7 on account of Qh7+ and Qh8#, while 6... Ne7 is answered by 7. Qf7+ followed by 8. Re3.
zh: 连续将军后，突然出现这着安静着；没有增加任何威胁，只是堵住g兵，而这正是局面所需要的。例如6. Re3，黑方6... g6 7. Qxg6+ Qg7，白方离目标仍远。能而且应当花整整一步堵住g兵，是因为黑方组织不起有效防御。后或车不能走到e7，因为Qh7+、Qh8#；6... Ne7则7. Qf7+，再8. Re3。

text: The game ended 6... Qd7 7. Re3 1-0, Black having no reply to 8. Rf3 and 9. Qh7#.
zh: 实战以6... Qd7 7. Re3 1-0结束，黑方无法应对8. Rf3、9. Qh7#。
caption_zh: 斯坦尼茨—拉斯克，伦敦，1899年；黑先。

text: This position is from the game Steinitz-Lasker, London 1899. Black began with a double sacrifice.
zh: 此局面出自斯坦尼茨—拉斯克，伦敦，1899年。黑方以连续两次弃子开始。

text: 1... Nxg2! 2. Kxg2 Bxh3+ 3. Kf2
zh: 1... Nxg2! 2. Kxg2 Bxh3+ 3. Kf2

text: White cannot accept the second sacrifice; if 3. Kxh3, then 3... Qh5+ 4. Kg2 Qg4+ 5. Kh1 Qh3+ 6. Kg1 Qg3+ 7. Kh1 Re4 8. Bg5 Rde8!, etc.
zh: 白方不能接受第二次弃子：3. Kxh3则3... Qh5+ 4. Kg2 Qg4+ 5. Kh1 Qh3+ 6. Kg1 Qg3+ 7. Kh1 Re4 8. Bg5 Rde8!等。

text: A quiet move after the sacrifice. Black first deprives White's pieces of the squares e5 and g5 and at the same time prepares the advance of his g-pawn — a sound and positionally well-founded plan.
zh: 弃子之后的安静着。黑方先剥夺白子e5、g5格，同时准备推进g兵；这是可靠且具有充分局面棋依据的计划。

text: 4. Rg1 g5 5. Bxg5
zh: 4. Rg1 g5 5. Bxg5

text: White's other moves all lose as well.
zh: 白方其他着法也都输。

text: 5... fxg5 6. Rxg5 Qe6 7. Qd3 Bf4 8. Rh1
zh: 5... fxg5 6. Rxg5 Qe6 7. Qd3 Bf4 8. Rh1

text: Black wins easily after both 8. Rg7 Bf5 and 8. Ra5 Rg8.
zh: 8. Rg7 Bf5和8. Ra5 Rg8，黑方都轻易获胜。

text: 8... Bxg5 9. Nxg5 Qf6+ 10. Bf3 Bf5
zh: 8... Bxg5 9. Nxg5 Qf6+ 10. Bf3 Bf5

text: If 11. Qd2, then 11... h6 is decisive.
zh: 11. Qd2则11... h6决定胜负。

text: 11. Nxh7 Qg6 12. Qb5 c6 13. Qa5 Re7 14. Rh5 Bg4 15. Rg5 Qc2+ 16. Kg3 Bxf3 0-1
zh: 11. Nxh7 Qg6 12. Qb5 c6 13. Qa5 Re7 14. Rh5 Bg4 15. Rg5 Qc2+ 16. Kg3 Bxf3 0-1
caption_zh: 斯塔尔贝里—阿廖欣，汉堡，1930年；黑先。

text: This position is from the game Ståhlberg-Alekhine, Hamburg 1930. It is Black's move, and he starts by provoking f3.
zh: 此局面出自斯塔尔贝里—阿廖欣，汉堡，1930年。轮黑走，先诱使白方f3。

text: 1... Rdf7 2. f3 Rf4
zh: 1... Rdf7 2. f3 Rf4

text: Opening the way for the queen.
zh: 为后开路。

text: 3. Bd3 Qh5 4. Bf1
zh: 3. Bd3 Qh5 4. Bf1

text: Black threatened 4... e4.
zh: 黑方原来威胁4... e4。

text: This apparently insignificant move is necessary in order to protect the queen in readiness for a combination starting with ...Rxf3. There is in fact an immediate threat of 6... Rxf3 7. Qxg5 Rxf2 followed, when White has parried the threat of mate on f1, by 8... hxg5, winning material.
zh: 这看似微不足道的一着，是为了保护后，为...Rxf3起始的组合做准备。其实已直接威胁6... Rxf3 7. Qxg5 Rxf2，白方挡住f1将杀后，再8... hxg5得子。

text: 6. Kh1 Rxf3 0-1
zh: 6. Kh1 Rxf3 0-1

text: White did not notice the threat when he moved his king, so he resigned at this point. 6. Qd2 would have offered more resistance, though even then Alekhine pointed out an easy win for Black by 6... Bxf3 7. Nxf3 Nxf3+ 8. Rxf3 Rxf3 9. Qxg5 Rxf1+ 10. Rxf1 Rxf1+ 11. Kxf1 hxg5, and White loses the king and pawn ending.
zh: 白方动王时没注意威胁，因此在这里认输。6. Qd2能抵抗更久，但即使如此，阿廖欣也指出了黑方的简单胜法：6... Bxf3 7. Nxf3 Nxf3+ 8. Rxf3 Rxf3 9. Qxg5 Rxf1+ 10. Rxf1 Rxf1+ 11. Kxf1 hxg5，白方输掉王兵残局。

text: This position comes from an analysis of a critical variation in the game Marshall-Mieses, Cambridge Springs 1904. White has sacrificed a rook, and it is now his move. It would appear that the game must end in a rapid mating attack after 1. Nce4!?. However, this ‘powerful move’ is in fact weak, since Black plays 1... Nc3!, after which 2. Nf6+ gxf6 3. exf6 does not work on account of 3... Ne2+ followed by 4... Qc1+, 5... Qb2+ and 6... Qxf6. If White tries 2. Rd7, then Black cannot take the rook (e.g. 2... Qxd7 3. Nd6! [Nunn note 1] or 2... Bxd7 3. Nf6+) but he can play 2... Ne2+ 3. Kf1 Qc1+ 4. Kxe2 Qxg5! 5. Nxg5 Bxd7, defending himself excellently and preserving the balance of material [Nunn note 2].
zh: 此局面来自马歇尔—米泽斯，剑桥泉，1904年一条关键变化的分析。白方已经弃车，轮他走。1. Nce4!?似乎应很快杀王结束。但这“强着”实际很弱，黑方1... Nc3!，2. Nf6+ gxf6 3. exf6因3... Ne2+，再4... Qc1+、5... Qb2+、6... Qxf6而不行。若2. Rd7，黑方不能吃车，如2... Qxd7 3. Nd6!〔纳恩注1〕，或2... Bxd7 3. Nf6+；但可2... Ne2+ 3. Kf1 Qc1+ 4. Kxe2 Qxg5! 5. Nxg5 Bxd7，很好地守住，同时保持子力均衡〔纳恩注2〕。
caption_zh: 马歇尔—米泽斯分析，剑桥泉，1904年；白先。

text: Another possibility is 1. Rxd1, the intention being to safeguard the back rank. Black loses now if he plays 1... Qxc3, e.g. 2. Qh7+ Kf8 3. Qh8+ Ke7 4. Qxg7, and if 4... Rf8, then 5. Qf6+ and 6. Rd8#. 1... Qxe5 is also bad after 2. Nce4 followed by f4. However, he still has the reply 1... Rd8!, which eliminates the danger on the d-file [Nunn note 3].
zh: 另一可能是1. Rxd1，意图保护底线。1... Qxc3会输，例如2. Qh7+ Kf8 3. Qh8+ Ke7 4. Qxg7，4... Rf8则5. Qf6+、6. Rd8#。1... Qxe5也不好，因为2. Nce4再f4。不过他仍有1... Rd8!，消除d线危险〔纳恩注3〕。

text: The correct procedure is to begin by checking, and only when Black's rook is engaged to go over to securing the position's foundations.
zh: 正确方法是先将军，只有黑车忙于应付后，才转而巩固自身阵形基础。

text: 1 This move doesn’t even have a serious threat, so Black can defend easily, for example by 3... Nb5. Instead, White should force a draw by 3. Nf6+ gxf6 4. Qh7+, etc.
zh: 〔纳恩注1〕这着甚至没有严重威胁，黑方可以轻易防御，例如3... Nb5。白方应改以3. Nf6+ gxf6 4. Qh7+等强制求和。

text: 2 Here 6. Qh7+ Kf8 7. Qh8+ Ke7 8. Qxg7 appears very good for White, e.g. 8... Bb5+ 9. Ke3 Rf8 10. Qf6+ Ke8 11. Nh7 Rg8 12. Qh4.
zh: 〔纳恩注2〕这里6. Qh7+ Kf8 7. Qh8+ Ke7 8. Qxg7看起来对白方很好，例如8... Bb5+ 9. Ke3 Rf8 10. Qf6+ Ke8 11. Nh7 Rg8 12. Qh4。

text: 3 After 1... Rd8, 2. Qh7+ Kf8 3. Qh8+ Ke7 4. Qxg7 Rxd1+ 5. Nxd1 wins the f7-pawn with check; the g-pawn then falls too, when White is clearly better.
zh: 〔纳恩注3〕1... Rd8之后，2. Qh7+ Kf8 3. Qh8+ Ke7 4. Qxg7 Rxd1+ 5. Nxd1后，白方可以带将吃掉f7兵；g兵也会丢，白方明显较好。

text: 1. Qh7+ Kf8 2. Qh8+ Ke7 3. Qxg7 Rf8 4. Rxd1!
zh: 1. Qh7+ Kf8 2. Qh8+ Ke7 3. Qxg7 Rf8 4. Rxd1!

text: Just as soon as the attacking formation is completely developed, this precautionary waiting move follows with full force. Black is now powerless against the threat of Qf6+ followed by Ne4-d6+. If 4... Ke8, then 5. Nh7 Qe7 6. Nxf8 Qxf8 7. Rd8+; while if 4... Bd7, then 5. Qf6+ Ke8 6. Nce4.
zh: 攻击阵形刚好完全展开，这着预防性的等待着便发挥全部力量。黑方现在无力应付Qf6+再Ne4—d6+。4... Ke8则5. Nh7 Qe7 6. Nxf8 Qxf8 7. Rd8+；4... Bd7则5. Qf6+ Ke8 6. Nce4。

text: The solution is simple when it is demonstrated, but for psychological reasons it is difficult to find; first, because we would rather believe in 'finessing and strengthening the position by indirect moves' than in a banal pursuit of the king; and secondly, because the move Rxd1 needs to be inserted at exactly the right moment.
zh: 解法演示出来很简单，但由于心理原因很难发现：首先，我们宁愿相信“以间接着法施展精妙手段、加强局面”，而不愿平庸地追王；其次，Rxd1必须插在恰好的时刻。

text: Toying with an attack
zh: 以进攻作姿态

text: An attack on the king as an alternative which never materializes but which acts solely as a subsidiary threat in the context of play with other objectives is a phenomenon which is abundantly represented in the games of the masters. The player merely toys with the plan of an attack on the king while, in fact, he is preparing and carrying out some other operation — a procedure which has a point if the threat to attack brings the player some advantage in tempi or helps the deployment of his pieces for the other operation.
zh: 把杀王作为始终不实际发生的备选，只在其他目标的行棋中起辅助威胁作用，是大师对局中大量存在的现象。棋手只是摆出杀王计划，实际准备、执行的却是其他行动。若杀王威胁能带来步数上的收益，或帮助另一行动的子力部署，这样做就有意义。

text: The advantage may take the form of the opponent's withdrawing a piece to the defence, as a result of which its effectiveness elsewhere is lost or diminished. Or it may be that the move by which the player has built up the threat of an attack at the same time gains a tempo for the other operation. These are the simple ingredients of an objective 'toying' with the attack on the castled king.
zh: 收益可能是对手调子回防，使它在别处的作用丧失或减弱；也可能是构筑杀王威胁的一着，同时为另一行动赢得一步。这些就是客观地以王城攻击“作姿态”的简单组成因素。

text: The subjective or psychological exploitation of the threat to the castled position can also involve various other motives. The threat can, for example, produce a feeling of insecurity in the opponent, oblige him to spend too much time in thinking, or even induce him to make some precautionary move merely to relieve his anxiety by the easiest means available. This last case can often be seen in the games of weaker players, when they play ...h6 'for safety's sake' , but in a subtler and less perceptible way it also happens that masters weaken their king positions in order to parry imaginary threats. We need only recall Burn's move ...g6 (page 289) as a defence against an incorrect classic bishop sacrifice!
zh: 从主观或心理上利用王城威胁，还可涉及其他动机。例如让对手感到不安，花过多时间思考，甚至只为用最方便的办法减轻焦虑，就走出某种预防着。较弱棋手“为安全起见”走...h6，是常见例子；大师也会以更微妙、不易察觉的方式，为防范想象中的威胁而削弱王城。只须回想伯恩为了防御不正确的古典弃象而走...g6（289页）！

text: Questions like this fall outside the range of an objective treatment of the theme; the various forms of camouflage, the use of imaginary threats, speculation on an opponent's shortcomings, all these are features of practical play which have resulted from the dictates of that 'cruel, heavy-handed tournament machine' — the clock. We are interested here only in the objective (i.e. correct) threat and the objective (i.e. properly justified) reaction to it.
zh: 这些问题不在本主题的客观讨论范围内。各种伪装、虚构威胁、利用对手弱点，都是那部“残酷而粗暴的比赛机器”——棋钟——所造成的实战特征。这里我们只关心客观的、即正确的威胁，以及客观的、即具有充分依据的回应。

text: White is the better placed; he owes his superiority to the advanced position of his e-pawn, which secures him an advantage in space and cramps Black. The active placing of his pieces, the blocked centre, and the weakened enemy king position are all preconditions for an attack on the castled king. However, White has yet another advantage, namely, his rooks are united and he is a tempo ahead as regards control of the c-file; this would incline him towards a positional treatment of the game rather than an attack.
zh: 白方较好，因为前进的e兵确保空间优势，限制黑方。活跃的子力、封闭的中心、削弱的敌王城，都是杀王条件。但白方还另有优势：双车已经联络，在控制c线上领先一步；这又使他倾向于走局面棋，而不是发动攻击。

text: One asks oneself whether the best plan is to attack or play on the c-file? The answer is that one should threaten an attack and continue to promote the preconditions for it; then, if Black defends correctly, the prospects of successful play on the c-file will be enhanced.
zh: 最好的计划究竟是进攻，还是在c线行棋？答案是：应威胁进攻，继续改善进攻条件；这样，黑方若正确防守，白方在c线成功行动的前景便会增强。

text: Two moves which threaten the enemy king position are worth considering, i.e. I Bb1, threatening Qc2, and I Qe3, which threatens a sacrificial assault on h6. If I Bb1, Black plays 1... Re8 and parries 2. Qc2 with 2... Nf8. It would appear that the time is then ripe for play on the c-file, but after the continuation 3. Qc7 Qxc7 4. Rxc7 Rab8 5. Rfc1 it is clear that this particular bolt has been shot; Black plays 5... Bd8 followed by ...Bb6, and White has nothing left on the c-file. The other method is better.
zh: 两着威胁敌王城的棋值得考虑：1. Bb1威胁Qc2；1. Qe3威胁在h6弃子突击。1. Bb1，黑方1... Re8，2. Qc2则2... Nf8。似乎该转向c线了，但3. Qc7 Qxc7 4. Rxc7 Rab8 5. Rfc1后，会发现这一招已经用尽：黑方5... Bd8再...Bb6，白方c线无所获。另一个办法较好。

text: 1. Qe3! Re8
zh: 1. Qe3! Re8

text: This is forced; Black cannot defend himself without ...Nf8, as the following variations show:
zh: 强制。黑方若没有...Nf8便无法防守，变化如下：

text: 1) 1... Rc8 2. Bxh6 gxh6 3. Qxh6 f5 4. exf6 Rxf6 (or 4... Nxf6 5. Qg6+ Kh8 6. Ng5, when Black has no defence against Qh6+ followed by Bh7+, Bf5+ and Bxe6+) 5. Qh7+ Kf8 6. Qh8+ Kf7 7. Ng5#.
zh: 1）1... Rc8 2. Bxh6 gxh6 3. Qxh6 f5 4. exf6 Rxf6（或4... Nxf6 5. Qg6+ Kh8 6. Ng5，黑方无法应付Qh6+再Bh7+、Bf5+、Bxe6+）5. Qh7+ Kf8 6. Qh8+ Kf7 7. Ng5#。

text: 2) 1... Qb6 2. Bxh6 gxh6 3. Qxh6 f5 4. exf6 Nxf6 (for 4... Rxf6 see above) 5. Qg6+ Kh8 6. Ng5 Bc8 7. Rc3 e5 8. Qh6+ Kg8 9. Bh7+ Kh8 10. Bf5+ Kg8 11. Qg6+ followed by mate.
zh: 2）1... Qb6 2. Bxh6 gxh6 3. Qxh6 f5 4. exf6 Nxf6（4... Rxf6见上）5. Qg6+ Kh8 6. Ng5 Bc8 7. Rc3 e5 8. Qh6+ Kg8 9. Bh7+ Kh8 10. Bf5+ Kg8 11. Qg6+，接着将杀。

text: 3) 1... Nb6 2. Bb1! [Nunn note 1], and now, besides Bxh6, there is also a threat of Qd3, etc.
zh: 3）1... Nb6 2. Bb1!〔纳恩注1〕，现在除了Bxh6，还威胁Qd3等。

text: 2. Rc3 Nf8
zh: 2. Rc3 Nf8

text: Black has to withdraw his knight to the defence, since there is once again a threat of Bxh6. If, for example, 2... Qb6 (2... b4 3. axb4 Bxb4 4. Rb3 allows White to gain an important tempo for his attack) then 3. Bxh6 gxh6 4. Qxh6 Nf8 5. Ng5 Bxg5 6. Qxg5+ Kh8 7. Bb1.
zh: 黑方不得不把马调回防守，因为再次威胁Bxh6。例如2... Qb6（2... b4 3. axb4 Bxb4 4. Rb3让白方为进攻获得重要一步）3. Bxh6 gxh6 4. Qxh6 Nf8 5. Ng5 Bxg5 6. Qxg5+ Kh8 7. Bb1。

text: 3. Rfc1 (D)
zh: 3. Rfc1（见图）

text: One might well consider strengthening the attack even further by 3. h4. However, that is a commitment, and its consequences are not clear. With 3. Rfc1 White goes for play on the c-file, for which the conditions now are fundamentally better than in the position with which we started. On the one hand, White has gained the time to double rooks, and on the other, he has driven Black’s knight back to f8, where it is now one tempo further away from the critical square c4, on which it clearly belongs. White owes his advantage here to his ‘toying’ with an attack on the castled king. The rest of the game is a matter of positional technique, and it could run as follows: 3... Rc8 (if Black allows Rc7, then the threat of a sacrifice on h6 is renewed!) 4. Rxc8 Bxc8 5. Qe1 Bb7 6. Bd2! (if a good ending is White’s objective, the dark-squared bishops should be exchanged as soon as possible) 6... Qd7 7. Bb4 Rc8 (or 7... Bd8 8. Ba5, when 8... Be7 fails against 9. Rc7) 8. Bxe7 Rxc1 9. Qxc1 Qxe7 10. Qc3 Qd7 (if 10... Nd7, then 11. Qc7 is decisive) 11. Nd2, and White has a considerable advantage by virtue of his better bishop and more active knight. Black cannot avoid exchanging queens, after which an exchange of knights or of the white bishop for the black knight would eventually leave White with a very favourable ending.
zh: 或许可以3. h4进一步加强进攻，但这会给局面带来约束，后果尚不清楚。3. Rfc1则转向c线，这里的条件已比最初根本改善。一方面，白方赢得叠车时间；另一方面，把黑马赶回f8，使它离显然应该占据的c4关键格又远一步。白方优势来自以杀王“作姿态”。接下来是局面棋技术，可以这样继续：3... Rc8（若允许Rc7，h6弃子的威胁又出现！）4. Rxc8 Bxc8 5. Qe1 Bb7 6. Bd2!（若目标是好残局，应尽快兑掉黑格象）6... Qd7 7. Bb4 Rc8（或7... Bd8 8. Ba5，8... Be7则9. Rc7）8. Bxe7 Rxc1 9. Qxc1 Qxe7 10. Qc3 Qd7（10... Nd7则11. Qc7决定胜负）11. Nd2，白方凭较好的象与更活跃的马，拥有很大优势。黑方无法避免兑后；此后兑马，或白象兑黑马，最终都会留下非常有利的残局。

text: In this line White can still play 2. Bxh6. 1
zh: 〔纳恩注1〕这条变化中，白方仍然可以2. Bxh6。

text: 'Not seeing in front of one's nose'
zh: “看不见鼻子前的东西”

text: It is a good thing to co-ordinate one's moves in an 'integrated action', but one should always try to see what is 'in front of one's nose' ; that is, if one can mate at once, one should do so and not philosophize about pawns. This somehow happened once to Dr Vidmar, who (as White) reached the following position against Yates at London, 1922.
zh: 把各着协调为“整体行动”是好事，但始终应看到“鼻子前”的东西：若能立即将杀，就应将杀，别去对兵大发哲学议论。维德马尔博士就曾犯过这样的错误；他执白对耶茨，伦敦，1922年，到达下图局面。
caption_zh: 维德马尔—耶茨，伦敦，1922年；白先。

text: This position is one in which White can win easily, but in a misguided moment he hit on the idea of 'combining everything into an integral whole' , i.e. he wanted both to attack and, at the same time, to 'cash in' on Black's e-pawn. As a result of this faulty desire to achieve two ends a drawn position was reached, which Black, however, proceeded to spoil and eventually to lose.
zh: 白方本可轻易赢棋，却一时糊涂，想到“把一切结合成一个整体”：既进攻，又同时想吃掉黑方的e兵来“兑现”优势。想一举两得的错误愿望，导致局面变成和棋；不过黑方后来又走坏，最终输棋。

text: Let us look first at the course the game took.
zh: 先看实战进程。

text: 1. d5?! Ba8 2. Qh3 h6 3. Rfg4 Kh7 4. Nxe4? Qf8 5. Nxf6+
zh: 1. d5?! Ba8 2. Qh3 h6 3. Rfg4 Kh7 4. Nxe4? Qf8 5. Nxf6+

text: In his book A Half-Century at the Chessboard the great Yugoslav master records that he spent three-quarters of an hour thinking at this point and then decided on the sacrifice. After his incorrect capture of the e-pawn there was no other choice left.
zh: 这位南斯拉夫大师在《棋盘旁的半个世纪》中记载，他在这里想了四十五分钟，然后决定弃子。错误吃掉e兵后，已别无选择。

text: 5... Qxf6 6. Rg6 Qf8?
zh: 5... Qxf6 6. Rg6 Qf8?

text: This is a mistake; Black now lost after 7. Qg4! Qf7 8. Qg5 Kh8 (otherwise Qxh6+ wins) 9. f6 Qxd5 10. Rhxh6+ 1-0.
zh: 错误。黑方接着7. Qg4! Qf7 8. Qg5 Kh8（否则Qxh6+获胜）9. f6 Qxd5 10. Rhxh6+ 1-0，输了。

text: Black could have drawn by playing the natural move 6... Qxb2, e.g. 7. Rhxh6+ Kg8 8. Rh8+ Kf7, and if 9. Rxg7+, then 9... Qxg7 10. Rh7 Bxd5, when White has nothing better than perpetual check.
zh: 黑方本可自然地6... Qxb2求和，例如7. Rhxh6+ Kg8 8. Rh8+ Kf7，9. Rxg7+则9... Qxg7 10. Rh7 Bxd5，白方最好也只能长将。

text: In the book mentioned above Dr Vidmar emphasizes how in this game the attack on the black king and the pressure on his e-pawn 'combined together to form a greater whole'. But it is precisely this false union of ideas which was the reason for White's failure to discover the correct path to victory as, after 4... Qf8, he listened to Big Ben chime quarter after quarter while his knight remained suspended in mid-air at e4. It is true that in the diagrammed position there are two factors making up White's advantage: a powerful kingside attack and a favourable knight versus bishop ending (once all the heavy pieces are exchanged). These two elements could only be combined if the attack led to the exchange of the queens and rooks, but the attack can break through without exchanges, and consequently it is beside the point how good the ending is. In fact, taking the pawn on e4 promotes neither White' s attack nor his endgame prospects, but simply gives Black an opportunity of counterattacking along the e-file. Victory for White is an altogether easy matter, as long as he concerns himself entirely with the attack and forgets the pawn on e4:
zh: 在上述书中，维德马尔博士强调，此局对黑王的攻击与对e兵的压力“结合成了一个更大的整体”。然而恰恰是这种错误结合，使白方没找到正确胜路：4... Qf8后，白马悬在e4，他听着大本钟一刻又一刻地报时。图中白方优势确有两部分：强大的王翼攻势，以及兑掉所有重子后有利的马对象残局。但只有进攻导致后、车全部交换时，两者才可结合；攻势无需交换便能突破，残局有多好就无关紧要。吃e4兵既不促进进攻，也不改善残局，只给黑方沿e线反击的机会。白方只要全心进攻，忘掉e4兵，取胜完全容易：

text: 1. Qh3 h6 2. Rfg4 Kh7
zh: 1. Qh3 h6 2. Rfg4 Kh7

text: This is all forced.
zh: 这些都是强制的。
3. Ne2!（见图）

text: White simply transfers the knight to h5 and carefully avoids the poisonous pawn on e4!
zh: 白方只需把马调往h5，小心避开e4毒兵！
caption_zh: 维德马尔—耶茨分析，3. Ne2后。

text: White also wins after both 3... Rh8 4. Nf4 Bd7 5. Rg6 Kg8 6. Nh5 [Nunn note 1] and 3... Qf8 (or 3... Bd5 4. Nf4) 4. Nf4 followed by Rg6 and Nh5.
zh: 3... Rh8 4. Nf4 Bd7 5. Rg6 Kg8 6. Nh5〔纳恩注1〕，以及3... Qf8（或3... Bd5 4. Nf4）4. Nf4，再Rg6、Nh5，也都使白方获胜。

text: 4. Rg6 Qf8 5. Nf4 b4 6. Nh5 Rf7
zh: 4. Rg6 Qf8 5. Nf4 b4 6. Nh5 Rf7

text: Otherwise White wins even more quickly by Nxf6+.
zh: 否则Nxf6+使白方赢得更快。

text: 1 Unfortunately this runs into 6... Qxg6, but White could have won earlier by 5. Nh5 Bxf5 6. Rxg7+ Qxg7 7. Qxf5+ Qg6 8. Nxf6+ Kg7 9. Rg4.
zh: 〔纳恩注1〕可惜这会遇到6... Qxg6。不过白方可以更早5. Nh5 Bxf5 6. Rxg7+ Qxg7 7. Qxf5+ Qg6 8. Nxf6+ Kg7 9. Rg4获胜。

text: 7. Nxg7 Rxg7 8. Rhxh6+ Kg8 9. Qh5!
zh: 7. Nxg7 Rxg7 8. Rhxh6+ Kg8 9. Qh5!

text: The quickest and most precise.
zh: 最快且最精确。

text: 9... Rxg6 10. Rh8+ Kf7 11. Rh7+ Qg7 12. Qxg6+ with a quick mate.
zh: 9... Rxg6 10. Rh8+ Kf7 11. Rh7+ Qg7 12. Qxg6+，很快将杀。

text: This shows how play should have proceeded from the original position, but things would have gone much the same way if, instead of 4. Nxe4?, White had played 4. Ne2!, a point of which the reader can easily convince himself. I d5?! was only the first step along the wrong path, but 4. Nxe4? was a mistake which could have cost half a point.
zh: 这说明初始局面应怎样走；若实战中不4. Nxe4?而4. Ne2!，大致也会如此，读者容易自行验证。1. d5?!只是在错误道路上迈出的第一步，4. Nxe4?才是可能损失半分的错误。

text: So it turned out that Dr Vidmar failed to see something 'in front of his nose' in London in 1922, nor did he see it thirty years later when he was writing his book. In this there is without doubt a touch of humour, the humour which Lasker recommended as an addition to every sizeable dose of chess principles.
zh: 于是维德马尔博士1922年在伦敦没看到“鼻子前”的东西，三十年后写书时也没看到。其中无疑有点幽默，正是拉斯克建议每服一大剂棋理原则时都该加一点的那种幽默。

text: From attack to endgame
zh: 从进攻转入残局

text: A host of examples could be given to illustrate the transition from an attack on the king into the endgame. It may be a question of heading for a drawn position as a lesser evil to the failure which would result from continuing the attack; it may also be that one variation of the attacker's combination leads to an ending. However, cases such as these do not really belong here. We are only interested at this point in cases where the attacker deliberately calls off the attack because his success is better assured by a favourable endgame.
zh: 杀王转入残局的实例不胜枚举。有时是继续进攻将失败，退而求其次走入和棋；也可能是进攻组合的一条变化导致残局。但这些不属于这里的主题。这里仅关心进攻方主动中止攻势，因为有利残局更能确保成功的情况。

text: The classic exponent of the liquidation of an attack and the transition into the endgame was Pillsbury, so we shall open a series of examples with one of his games.
zh: 简化攻势并转入残局的经典代表是皮尔斯伯里，因此这一组实例先看他的一盘棋。
caption_zh: 皮尔斯伯里—马洛契，巴黎，1900年；白先。

text: This position is from Pillsbury-Maroczy, Paris 1900. Although the situation is still far removed from the endgame, White is thinking about it all the same.
zh: 此局面出自皮尔斯伯里—马洛契，巴黎，1900年。虽然离残局还远，白方却已在考虑。

text: 1. Ra5
zh: 1. Ra5

text: He prepares for the exchange of the dark-squared bishops by means of Bc5, after which there is both an eventual threat of a bishop sacrifice on h7 and the prospect of an ending with White having a good knight against a bad bishop.
zh: 白方准备用Bc5兑黑格象，此后既潜伏着h7弃象的威胁，也有好马对坏象的残局前景。

text: 1... f5 2. Kh1 Rce8
zh: 1... f5 2. Kh1 Rce8

text: Avoiding the possibility of 3. Bc5 Bxc5 4. Rxc5 Qb6? 5. Rxc8.
zh: 防止3. Bc5 Bxc5 4. Rxc5 Qb6? 5. Rxc8的可能。

text: 3. Bc5 Qc7 4. Bxe7 Rxe7 5. g4
zh: 3. Bc5 Qc7 4. Bxe7 Rxe7 5. g4

text: The positional obligation entailed by such a move is balanced by the fact that in this position White has no need to fear the endgame. If his opponent's darksquared bishop were still there, the move would be risky.
zh: 这次冲兵虽给局面带来约束，但白方此时无须害怕转入残局，足以抵消这一负担。若对方黑格象仍在，此着就冒险。

text: 5... Nc6 6. Raa1 fxg4 7. Qh4 g6 8. Qxg4 Rg7 9. h4 Ne7?!
zh: 5... Nc6 6. Raa1 fxg4 7. Qh4 g6 8. Qxg4 Rg7 9. h4 Ne7?!

text: Black defends himself against an attack which is not dangerous and neglects something much more important, namely, the central point d4, which is of deci- Sive significance in many types of ending. Precisely the opposite course was correct, that is, to increase his influence over d4 and at the same time, by 9... Qb6, to question White with regard to what his plans were for the dark-square network. In view of the threat of 10... Qe3 White would have to play 10. Rae1, after which 10... Kh8 11. Re2 d4, opening up the long light-square diagonal, already makes things easier for the defender.
zh: 黑方防备并不危险的进攻，却忽视更重要的中心d4点；它在许多残局中具有决定意义。正确做法恰恰相反：加强d4影响，同时9... Qb6询问白方打算怎样处理黑格网络。由于10... Qe3的威胁，白方必须10. Rae1，此后10... Kh8 11. Re2 d4打开白格长斜线，防守方已轻松些。
10. Nd4 Nf5?（见图）

text: And now 10... Nc6 was correct.
zh: 现在也应10... Nc6。
caption_zh: 皮尔斯伯里—马洛契，10... Nf5后。

text: 11. Bxf5
zh: 11. Bxf5

text: A step closer to the ending with knight versus bad bishop. Pillsbury was a specialist in such exchanges.
zh: 离好马对坏象的残局更近了一步。皮尔斯伯里是这种交换的专家。

text: If 12... Be8 13. Qh6 Rg6, White plays 14. Rg1 and is one step further towards an endgame.
zh: 12... Be8 13. Qh6 Rg6，白方14. Rg1，离残局又近一步。

text: 13. Rg1 Rff7 14. Qh6 Qe7 15. Nf3
zh: 13. Rg1 Rff7 14. Qh6 Qe7 15. Nf3

text: White decides, after all, on an attack instead of simple liquidation by 15. Rxg7+ and 16. Rg1. While attacking, he is always guaranteed a good ending when he wants it.
zh: 白方最终还是选择了进攻，而不是用15. Rxg7+、16. Rg1直接简化局面。在进攻过程中，只要愿意，他始终可以转入有利残局。

text: Pillsbury intends to establish his knight on the outpost at g5 and so gives up the line of play leading to an ending which he has followed up to here.
zh: 皮尔斯伯里打算把马放上g5前哨，因此放弃一直遵循的转残局路线。

text: The end of the game, which is no longer germane to our theme, runs as follows: 17... Rg4 18. Ng5 Rxf4 19. Nf7+ Qxf7 20. Qxf4 Qxh5+ 21. Kg3 Qe2 22. Kh4 Rc8 23. Rae1 Qxb2 24. Kh3 Rxc3+ 25. Rg3 Rc2 26. Rh1 Rc8 27. Qh6 1-0 [Nunn note 1]. If 27... Qxe5, then 28. Qxh7+ and 29. Kg2#.
zh: 后续已不切本主题，实战如下：17... Rg4 18. Ng5 Rxf4 19. Nf7+ Qxf7 20. Qxf4 Qxh5+ 21. Kg3 Qe2 22. Kh4 Rc8 23. Rae1 Qxb2 24. Kh3 Rxc3+ 25. Rg3 Rc2 26. Rh1 Rc8 27. Qh6 1-0〔纳恩注1〕。27... Qxe5则28. Qxh7+，再29. Kg2#。
caption_zh: 波戈留波夫—普热皮乌尔卡，皮耶什佳尼，1922年；白先。

text: In this position from Bogoljubow-Przepiorka, Pistyan 1922 the liquidation leading to an ending comes as the direct consequence of White's combination.
zh: 波戈留波夫—普热皮乌尔卡，皮耶什佳尼，1922年的这个局面中，简化转入残局直接来自白方的组合。

text: 1. Rxh5 gxh5 2. Rxd7 Rxc3
zh: 1. Rxh5 gxh5 2. Rxd7 Rxc3

text: Necessary, since 2... Qxd7 allows 3. Qg5+ followed by 4. Qf6+ and 5. Bxe5.
zh: 必要；2... Qxd7则3. Qg5+，再4. Qf6+、5. Bxe5。

text: 3. Nxc3 Qxd7 4. Qg5+ Kh8 5. Qf6+ Kg8 6. Nd5 Re8
zh: 3. Nxc3 Qxd7 4. Qg5+ Kh8 5. Qf6+ Kg8 6. Nd5 Re8

text: If 6... h6, then 7. Ne7+? Kh7 8. Nf5? would be incorrect on account of 8... Qd1+ and 9... Rg8+; however, White can play 7. Qxh6 f5 8. Qg6+ Kh8 (or 8... Qg7 9. Ne7+ Kh8 10. Qxh5+ Qh7 11. Ng6+, when White wins easily) 9. Nf6 Rxf6 10. Qxf6+, and the ending is won for White.
zh: 6... h6后7. Ne7+? Kh7 8. Nf5?不对，因为8... Qd1+再9... Rg8+。但白方可7. Qxh6 f5 8. Qg6+ Kh8（或8... Qg7 9. Ne7+ Kh8 10. Qxh5+ Qh7 11. Ng6+，轻易获胜）9. Nf6 Rxf6 10. Qxf6+，残局白胜。

text: I This last section of the game certainly contains some ups and downs, but readers will have to look elsewhere for the details!
zh: 〔纳恩注1〕最后这段对局确实有些起伏，但细节须请读者另寻资料！

text: 7. Qg5+ Kh8 8. Nf6 Qd8 9. Qh6 Qd1+ 10. Kg2 Rg8+ 11. Nxg8 Kxg8 12. Qg5+, and White continued with Qxe5 and won the ending.
zh: 7. Qg5+ Kh8 8. Nf6 Qd8 9. Qh6 Qd1+ 10. Kg2 Rg8+ 11. Nxg8 Kxg8 12. Qg5+，白方接着Qxe5，赢得残局。
caption_zh: 鲍特维尼克—拉宾诺维奇，列宁格勒，1934年；白先。

text: This position is from the game Botvinnik-Rabinovich, Leningrad 1934. At first White's attack follows a regular pattern.
zh: 此局面出自鲍特维尼克—拉宾诺维奇，列宁格勒，1934年。起初白方进攻循着常规模式。

text: 1. Ng4 Nxg4 2. Qxg4 Bh6 3. Bf6 Rd7
zh: 1. Ng4 Nxg4 2. Qxg4 Bh6 3. Bf6 Rd7

text: Black could not play 3... Rxd3 4. Rxd3 Be4 5. Rg3 Bg6 because of 6. Qh4!, when White remains the exchange ahead. However, 3... Rc8 would have been better than the text move.
zh: 黑方不能3... Rxd3 4. Rxd3 Be4 5. Rg3 Bg6，因为6. Qh4!，白方仍多半子。不过3... Rc8比实战着好。

text: 4. Bf1
zh: 4. Bf1

text: 4. Bxh7+ would also have been sufficient.
zh: 4. Bxh7+也足够。

text: 4... Qc8 [Nunn note 1] 5. Rxd7 Qxd7 6. Rd1 Qc7 7. Bg5!
zh: 4... Qc8〔纳恩注1〕5. Rxd7 Qxd7 6. Rd1 Qc7 7. Bg5!

text: White breaks off his attack and steers the game towards an ending in which there are two factors which ensure him a clear advantage: control of the d-file and play against Black's weak c-pawn.
zh: 白方中止进攻，导向残局；控制d线与攻击黑方c线弱兵这两个因素，保证白方拥有明显优势。

text: 7... Bxg5 8. Qxg5 h6
zh: 7... Bxg5 8. Qxg5 h6

text: White now continued with the thematic 9. Qd2 allowing the reply 9... Be4; the result was that after 10. Qd7 Rc8 11. f3 Bc2 12. Rd2 Bb1 Black's bishop got in among the small fry on the queenside, and it needed further incorrect play by Rabinovich before he eventually lost. Instead of 9. Qd2, White should have played 9. Qe3, which indirectly maintains his control of the d-file and also prepares for Rd3 and Qd2.
zh: 白方接着主题性地9. Qd2，允许9... Be4；10. Qd7 Rc8 11. f3 Bc2 12. Rd2 Bb1，黑象钻入后翼小兵群，拉宾诺维奇又走错才最终输棋。白方应以9. Qe3代替9. Qd2，间接保持d线控制，并准备Rd3、Qd2。

text: The next example will serve as an excellent conclusion to our discussion of the transition to the endgame. White’s attack has got to the point where it exerts strong pressure on the focal-point h7, and it seems that the end must come quickly. However, appearances are deceptive, for there is no mate and Black can escape into an ending in which he can continue to resist.
zh: 下一例为转残局的讨论作绝佳结尾。白方攻势已向h7焦点施加强大压力，似乎马上就要结束。但表象骗人：并无将杀，黑方可逃入能继续抵抗的残局。

text: 1 Vukovié incorrectly gave 4... Qe8 as the move played.
zh: 〔纳恩注1〕武科维奇把实战着误写成4... Qe8。

text: Thus, after 1. Bh7+ Kh8 2. Bg6+ Kg8 3. Bxf7+ Qxf7 4. Nxf7 Kxf7, White runs out of checks and is unable to prevent Black from posting his rook on d7, after which it is not at all clear how White can win.
zh: 1. Bh7+ Kh8 2. Bg6+ Kg8 3. Bxf7+ Qxf7 4. Nxf7 Kxf7之后，白方将军用尽，无法阻止黑车占据d7，此后怎样赢，完全不清楚。

text: Another possibility is 1. Nh7, and this leads to even greater material gains; Black is obliged to play 1... Ne4!, but after 2. Bxe4 dxe4 3. Nf6+ Qxf6 4. Qxf6 e3 the black pawn forces White's queen to retire, e.g. 5. Qf1 (or 5. Qg5+ Kf8) 5... e2 6. Qe1 Kf8, and White can hardly count on victory.
zh: 另一可能1. Nh7，能赢得更多子力；黑方必须1... Ne4!。但2. Bxe4 dxe4 3. Nf6+ Qxf6 4. Qxf6 e3，黑兵迫使白后退回，例如5. Qf1（或5. Qg5+ Kf8）5... e2 6. Qe1 Kf8，白方很难指望赢。

text: Here we have, as a start, two ways in which the position resolves itself into an ending; the further analysis of the position should soon convince the reader that at every move there is a variety of possible simplifying lines, most of which lead to different types of endings.
zh: 开头就有两种转入残局的方法。进一步分析，很快就会使读者确信：每一步都有各种简化可能，多数导致不同类型的残局。

text: The winning process for White is based on the gradual preparation of the pawn structure on the queenside in readiness for the transition into an ending. In this two factors are decisive: the first is that, besides his knight on f6, Black's queen is also immobilized since it cannot move from e7 because of the need to cover the squares f7 and f6; the second is that Black's pawns are also condemned to stay where they are. Any move on their part leads to Black's losing in the endgame after the manoeuvre Bh7+, Bg6+ and Bxf7+. Accordingly, Black may only move his rook up and down, and even then he is denied the use of the square f8 because of Nh7. Now for the analysis:
zh: 白方取胜的基础，是逐步准备后翼兵形，以便转入残局。有两个决定因素：第一，除了f6马，黑后也不能动，因为须保护f7、f6，无法离开e7；第二，黑兵也都被迫原地不动，任何冲兵都会在Bh7+、Bg6+、Bxf7+调动后导致残局败局。因此黑方只能来回动车；即使如此，也不能到f8，因为有Nh7。现在分析：

text: Forced; White threatened 2. cxd5 cxd5 3. Bh7+ Kh8 4. Be4+ Kg8 5. Bxd5 Rf8 6. Qg6+ Kh8 7. Bxf7. If 1... dxc4, then 2. Bh7+ followed by 3. Bd3+ and 4. Bxc4 wins in the same way.
zh: 强制。白方威胁2. cxd5 cxd5 3. Bh7+ Kh8 4. Be4+ Kg8 5. Bxd5 Rf8 6. Qg6+ Kh8 7. Bxf7。1... dxc4则2. Bh7+，再3. Bd3+、4. Bxc4，同样取胜。

text: A step further towards a favourable ending. If 2. cxd5, then Black’s best reply is 2... Rxd5!. Also possible here is 2. Bh7+ Kh8 3. Bg6+ Kg8 4. Bxf7+ Qxf7 5. Qh8+ Kxh8 6. Nxf7+ Kg8 7. Nxd8, but after 7... dxc4 8. bxc4 b5, Black’s prospects of a draw are more than good.
zh: 朝有利残局更进一步。2. cxd5，黑方最好2... Rxd5!。这里也可以2. Bh7+ Kh8 3. Bg6+ Kg8 4. Bxf7+ Qxf7 5. Qh8+ Kxh8 6. Nxf7+ Kg8 7. Nxd8，但7... dxc4 8. bxc4 b5，黑方和棋前景相当好。

text: Now 2... Re8 does not work because of 3. Nh7 Ne4 4. Kc1!, when Black is left without the possibility of ...Qd6 (which would have been an effective answer prior to c5) and at the same time there is a threat of 5. Bxe4, etc., now that the white king can hold the enemy e-pawn. If 4... f6, then 5. Bxe4 dxe4 6. Qg6+ Kh8 7. Nxf6 and White wins.
zh: 现在2... Re8因3. Nh7 Ne4 4. Kc1!不行：黑方失去...Qd6这一在c5以前有效的应法，同时威胁5. Bxe4等，因为白王现在可以限制敌e兵。4... f6则5. Bxe4 dxe4 6. Qg6+ Kh8 7. Nxf6，白胜。

text: 3. Ka3 Rb8
zh: 3. Ka3 Rb8

text: It is easy to see that after 3... a5 White will win an ending with queen versus rook and knight because the pawn on a5 must fall. If 3... b5, White similarly simplifies into an ending, and this time Black loses the pawns on a6 and c6, e.g. 4. Bh7+ Kh8 5. Nxf7+ Qxf7 6. Bg6+ Kg8 7. Bxf7+ Kxf7 8. Qf4 Rc8 9. Kb4 Ke7 10. Qd6+ Kf7 11. Ka5 Kg6 12. Kxa6 followed by 13. Kb7, etc.
zh: 容易看出，3... a5后白方赢得后对车马的残局，因为a5兵必丢。若3... b5，白方同样可以简化到残局，这次黑方将丢掉a6、c6两兵，例如4. Bh7+ Kh8 5. Nxf7+ Qxf7 6. Bg6+ Kg8 7. Bxf7+ Kxf7 8. Qf4 Rc8 9. Kb4 Ke7 10. Qd6+ Kf7 11. Ka5 Kg6 12. Kxa6，再13. Kb7等。

text: 4. Ka4 Ra8
zh: 4. Ka4 Ra8

text: If 4... b5+, then 5. cxb6 Rxb6 6. Bh7+ followed by capturing the queen at f7 and winning the ending of queen versus rook and knight, much as above.
zh: 4... b5+则5. cxb6 Rxb6 6. Bh7+，再吃掉f7上的黑后，赢得后对车马残局，大致同上。

text: 5. c4! Rb8 6. cxd5 cxd5 7. Ka3!
zh: 5. c4! Rb8 6. cxd5 cxd5 7. Ka3!

text: White threatens 8. Bh7+ followed by 9. Be4+ and 10. Bxd5, which would not have worked at once on account of 10... Qd7+. Black's rook must now go to d8.
zh: 白方威胁8. Bh7+，再9. Be4+、10. Bxd5。立即这样做不行，因为10... Qd7+。黑车现在必须去d8。

text: 7... Rd8 8. Bh7+ Kh8 9. Bg6+ Kg8 10. Bxf7+ Qxf7 11. Qh8+ Kxh8 12. Nxf7+ Kg8 13. Nxd8 and White has at last attained a won ending.
zh: 7... Rd8 8. Bh7+ Kh8 9. Bg6+ Kg8 10. Bxf7+ Qxf7 11. Qh8+ Kxh8 12. Nxf7+ Kg8 13. Nxd8，白方终于取得获胜残局。

text: The reader may care to investigate this rather studied example further, all the secrets of which lie in the moves made by the pawns on the queenside; the final outcome of the ending rests with them, for without them White is unable to win.
zh: 读者不妨进一步研究这个精心构造的例子。一切秘密都在后翼兵的着法中；残局的最终结果取决于它们，没有这些兵，白方便赢不了。

text: 12 The attack on the king as an integral part of the game
zh: 第十二章　杀王进攻作为对局整体的一部分

text: We have examined the various aspects of the attack on the castled king and have covered each topic on the basis of present-day knowledge of the art of chess. This material has been presented with all the difficulties and deficiencies of a pioneer, but with the joy of a discoverer who has seen in new knowledge a confirmation of his faith in the values of chess and his own general theory of the game.
zh: 我们已经考察了攻击易位王的各个方面，并依据本书写作时的棋艺认识讨论了各个专题。这些材料的呈现，难免带有开拓者所面对的困难和不足；但其中也有发现者的喜悦，因为新的认识进一步印证了他对国际象棋价值的信念，以及他本人关于这一游戏的总体理论。

text: The attentive reader who has battled his way with the writer from chapter to chapter will have observed the steady widening of the problem of the attack on the king; we began with the basic techniques of combination and have progressed to the kind of understanding which characterizes mastery of the game. The logical path we have taken has justified its call for a high degree of effort in return for new knowledge; its purpose is to show us the significance of the attack on the castled king in the full context of a game of chess.
zh: 细心的读者一路随作者逐章探究，应当已经注意到，杀王进攻这个课题的范围在不断扩大：我们从组合的基本技术出发，逐步进入只有掌握高深棋艺才能达到的认识层次。沿着这条合乎逻辑的道路付出大量努力，我们获得了新的知识，因而这些努力是值得的。这条道路的目的，是让我们把攻击易位王放到整盘棋的背景中，理解它的意义。

text: From our examination of the defence against a kingside attack and of the phases of such an attack, it has become clear that a correct attack is conditioned by the situation on all parts of the board and also by all that has happened in the earlier course of the game. An attack on the king is not some strange, exceptional, and daring operation like a grand slam in bridge. It is an action which is both logical and necessary; an action on which a player decides at a certain stage of the game; sometimes, indeed, he must decide on it, if his opponent is not to obtain an advantage or if the position is not to fizzle out into a draw.
zh: 通过考察抵御王翼进攻的方法及进攻的各个阶段，我们已经明白：正确的进攻取决于棋盘各处的形势，也取决于此前整盘棋的发展。杀王进攻并不是桥牌大满贯那样奇异、特殊而大胆的行动，而是合乎逻辑、确有必要的行动，是棋手在对局某一阶段作出的决定。有时，为了不让对手取得优势，或不让局面逐渐消解为和棋，他甚至必须作出这样的决定。

text: Lasker observed long ago that every action is essentially a diversion, a transition from equality to some spatial or temporal commitment. An attack on the king demands a very large diversion both in terms of the number of pieces involved and of the degree of commitment arising out of any pawn moves it entails. A considerable diversion of this kind also logically needs a considerable number of preconditions, as well as a knowledge of how these conditions are interrelated.
zh: 拉斯克早就指出，任何行动本质上都意味着力量的转移，也意味着从均衡状态转向在空间或时间上作出某种难以收回的投入。杀王进攻所需的力量转移很大：参与的棋子很多，随之而来的冲兵又会使局面发生程度不等的不可逆变化。如此大规模的力量转移，合乎逻辑地要求相当多的先决条件，同时还要求理解这些条件之间的关系。

text: It follows, therefore, that the attack on the castled king is an extremely difficult operation, which is based on a perfect mastery of all the forms of chess technique. Even in the early stages of the opening the first seeds of the preconditions for an attack on the king are already being sown, and the tense struggle for the central squares is tightly bound up with the successful outcome of the attack or defence. The characteristic features of a position, the weaknesses on both sides, and the elements that affect the endgame — all these accumulate and become intertwined in such a way that at a certain moment they impel the player to decide on the final objective of his play.
zh: 因此，攻击易位王是一项极其困难的行动，需要全面、熟练地掌握各种棋艺技术。早在开局初期，杀王进攻先决条件的种子就已播下；对中心格的紧张争夺，与此后进攻或防守的成败密切相连。局面的特点、双方的弱点，以及影响残局的各种因素，不断积累、交织，到了某一时刻，就会促使棋手决定自己行棋的最终目标。

text: This is the moment of crisis in the drama of the games of great masters, when it has to be decided whether it is best to continue promoting the preconditions for an attack on the king or to seek a favourable ending. The decision is not easy, for both courses demand not only technique but the ability to weld all the elements involved into a whole; moreover, we are still in the dark about many of the laws governing this process.
zh: 这就是大师对局这出戏剧中的关键时刻：应当继续创造杀王条件，还是谋求有利残局？这一决定并不容易，因为两条道路都不仅要求技术，还要求把所有相关因素融合成一个整体；而支配这一过程的许多规律，我们仍然没有弄清。
