text: Chess skill at the present time comprises a mastery of combinative techniques and the possession of mature positional judgment, while the science of the game has cleared up the problem of the centre in the majority of openings. However, we are still a long, long way from a thorough knowledge of the laws governing the methods of integrating all the elements into a strategic whole. And where there is insufficient knowledge one proceeds 'by feel', or in other words, one takes risks. The endgame and the attack on the king are two areas about which our knowledge is incomplete, but they are also two directions in which chess can be further explored and through which the ancient game can be raised to a still higher level.
zh: 就本书写作时而言，高超棋艺包括熟练的组合技术和成熟的局面棋判断；国际象棋理论也已阐明了大多数开局中的中心问题。然而，要彻底认识如何把各种因素整合为战略整体，我们还相去甚远。知识不足时，就只能“凭感觉”行动，换言之，就是冒险。残局和杀王进攻，是我们认识尚不充分的两个领域；同时，它们也是继续探索国际象棋的两个方向，能够把这项古老的游戏推向更高的水平。

text: We have said that there still exist areas in the art of chess where our knowledge is incomplete, and many of our readers may ask whether there are not at least some signposts pointing to where new knowledge might be found. The very attentive reader may also recall that mention was made in the Introduction of Alekhine's and Capablanca's understanding of the attack on the king and that a discussion on this subject was promised at the end of the book. Indeed, this is the right place for such a discussion, since the most difficult and arcane matters should be dealt with at the end, after everything else has been elucidated.
zh: 既然棋艺中仍有我们尚未充分认识的领域，许多读者可能会问：至少有没有一些路标，指示我们到哪里寻找新的知识？非常细心的读者也许还记得，导言曾提到阿廖欣和卡帕布兰卡对杀王进攻的理解，并答应在书末讨论这个问题。现在正是合适的时候，因为最困难、最深奥的问题，应当在其他问题都已阐明之后，留到最后讨论。

text: The discoveries of Alekhine and Capablanca
zh: 阿廖欣与卡帕布兰卡的发现

text: It is a slightly strange thesis that one should go back to the period before the Second World War and look for the culmination of the art of the attack on the king in the play of Alekhine and Capablanca. For have not Botvinnik and Smyslov, Keres and Bronstein, Reshevsky and Gligorić in their rich creativity in the field of chess discovered all that Alekhine and Capablanca knew and also gone on to add something else? It is indeed true that they have proceeded further in many respects, and perhaps even in their knowledge about the attack on the king they are the equals of the great masters of the past; in their actual games, however, they have not so far put it into practice to the full.
zh: 主张回到第二次世界大战之前，在阿廖欣和卡帕布兰卡的对局中寻找杀王艺术的顶峰，似乎有些奇怪。难道鲍特维尼克和斯梅斯洛夫、凯列斯和布龙斯坦、雷舍夫斯基和格利戈里奇，在丰富的国际象棋创作中，不是已经掌握了两位前辈的全部知识，还增添了新的内容吗？确实，他们在许多方面都走得更远；也许就杀王进攻的知识而言，他们也不逊于过去的大师。然而，在实际对局中，他们迄今尚未把这种认识充分付诸实践。

text: If we delve into the whole of chess literature looking for games which serve to illuminate the logical integration of the attack on the castled king and the game in its entirety, then those of Alekhine and Capablanca remain the unsurpassed models; side by side with them may be placed a few of the games of Rubinstein, Keres, and Bronstein, though we shall find scarcely any new discoveries in them: the whole period from Alekhine's death to the present day has not been particularly fruitful in the sphere of the attack on the king. So one is justified in going back to Alekhine and Capablanca as the first to discover knowledge which to this day has been neither refuted nor superseded.
zh: 如果遍览国际象棋文献，寻找能够说明怎样把攻击易位王合乎逻辑地融入整盘棋的对局，阿廖欣和卡帕布兰卡的作品仍是未被超越的典范。鲁宾斯坦、凯列斯和布龙斯坦的少数对局，可以与之并列，但其中几乎没有新的发现。从阿廖欣去世到本书写作时，这整个时期在杀王进攻领域并没有取得特别丰硕的成果。因此，回到阿廖欣和卡帕布兰卡，是有道理的：他们最先发现的那些知识，直到本书写作时仍未被推翻，也未被取代。

text: As far as these actual discoveries by Alekhine and Capablanca are concerned, it can be said that they did not take the form of some new principle but rather depended on a new way of thinking, which proceeded subjectively and therefore in a manner which cannot be expressed or comprehended on a theoretical basis; by these methods they discovered moves which fulfil the chief principle of the attack on the castled king, namely, obtaining the maximum preconditions for an attack with the minimum of commitment.
zh: 至于阿廖欣和卡帕布兰卡究竟发现了什么，可以说，那并不是某条新原则，而是一种新的思维方式。这种思考带有个人特性，因而不能完全用理论表述和理解。他们凭借这种方法发现的走法，体现了攻击易位王的首要原则：以最小限度的投入，创造尽可能充分的进攻条件。

text: This principle in itself is a simple one and can be easily remembered, but playing in accordance with it is extremely difficult. Here two grades of values must be clearly distinguished: the one based on the value of the individual preconditions and the other on that of the successive commitments undertaken. This must then be resolved into a precisely ordered series of moves, while one must also be ready at any moment to convert the attack into some other thematic course of action — all of which requires considerable mastery.
zh: 这条原则本身很简单，也容易记住，但要照着它下棋，却极其困难。这里必须分清两套价值尺度：一套衡量各项先决条件的价值，另一套衡量接连作出的投入。随后，还必须把这些判断落实为次序准确的一连串走法，同时随时准备把进攻转化为其他符合局面主题的行动。这一切都需要很高的棋艺。

text: From a close study of the games of Alekhine and Capablanca one can conclude that they did indeed use a perfected method of thinking in the sense mentioned above; only, in the case of Alekhine this thinking was more analytical and logical, while with Capablanca it was more artistically intuitive. However, the results of this thinking, that is, the actual moves, do not appear to differ greatly to the outside observer.
zh: 仔细研究两人的对局，可以看出，他们确实运用了上述意义上的完善思维方法。只是阿廖欣的思考更富于分析性和逻辑性，卡帕布兰卡则更多依靠艺术家的直觉。不过，旁观者从思考的结果，也就是具体走法来看，两者似乎并没有很大差别。

text: However, Alekhine's discoveries can be somewhat more precisely defined than Capablanca's: Alekhine's output was more abundant, he 'lived chess' more deeply, and he was a more passionate analyser of his own games. A particular characteristic of his commentaries is the frequent use of the idea of commitment (just as with Lasker we get the idea of compensation, with Steinitz that of the balance of the position, and with Nimzowitsch that of centralization). One could say that of all masters Alekhine had the most refined sense of the degree of commitment, even though his temperament sometimes led him to be too eager.
zh: 不过，相较于卡帕布兰卡，阿廖欣的发现可以界定得更准确一些：他的作品更多，对国际象棋的投入更深，对分析自己的对局也更有热情。他的评注有一个显著特点，就是经常运用“投入”这一观念，正如拉斯克强调补偿、斯坦尼茨强调局面的均衡、尼姆佐维奇强调中心化一样。可以说，在所有大师中，阿廖欣对这种投入程度的感觉最为细腻，尽管他的性格有时仍会使他操之过急。

text: When Alekhine, with apparent nonchalance, played, for instance, h4 against the French Defence, this appeared to his contemporaries to be 'the pretentiousness of genius', but a closer analysis today reveals that behind such moves there lay a great deal of mental calculation and hard logic, and that this move h4 belongs exactly when it was played; a move earlier it would have been weak and on the next it would be too late!
zh: 例如，阿廖欣在法兰西防御中看似漫不经心地走出h4，同代人往往把这看成“天才的任性”。但本书写作时更细致的分析表明，这类走法背后有大量计算和严密逻辑，而且h4恰恰应当在实战那个时刻走出：早一步就弱了，晚一步又来不及！

text: Further illustration of all these points will be better obtained by the reader from the actual games which follow.
zh: 下面的实战对局，将更好地说明上述各点。

text:
Alekhine – Asztalos
Kecskemet, 1927
Queen's Gambit Declined
zh:
阿廖欣—阿斯塔洛什
1927年，凯奇凯梅特
后翼弃兵拒弃兵变例

text: 1. Nf3 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. d4 d5 4. Bg5 h6
zh: 1. Nf3 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. d4 d5 4. Bg5 h6

text: A little experiment in the opening — and a dangerous one when Alekhine is on the other side of the board. The spatial advantage now obtained by White is worth more than Black's two bishops.
zh: 这是开局中的一个小试验；当对面坐着阿廖欣时，这种试验是危险的。白方由此得到的空间优势，比黑方的双象更有价值。

text: 5. Bxf6 Qxf6 6. Nc3 c6 7. Qb3 Nd7
zh: 5. Bxf6 Qxf6 6. Nc3 c6 7. Qb3 Nd7

text: Having started experimenting, Black ought to have gone on in like manner, e.g. 7... Qf5 8. e3 Nd7 9. Rd1 Qg6, by which he would have put more difficulties in the way of White's plan to gain space in the centre.
zh: 既然已经开始试验，黑方就应继续沿着这条道路走下去，例如7... Qf5 8. e3 Nd7 9. Rd1 Qg6，给白方扩大中心空间的计划制造更多困难。

text: 8. e4 dxe4 9. Nxe4 Qf4 10. Bd3 Be7 11. O-O O-O 12. Rfe1 Rd8 13. Rad1 Qc7
zh: 8. e4 dxe4 9. Nxe4 Qf4 10. Bd3 Be7 11. O-O O-O 12. Rfe1 Rd8 13. Rad1 Qc7

text: Black cannot complete his development as long as his queen remains on f4, for example 13... Nf6 14. Ne5! Rxd4 15. Nxf6+ Bxf6 16. g3 Qg5 17. Nf3 Qc5 18. Nxd4 Bxd4 19. Bh7+ followed by Qd3+ and Qxd4.
zh: 只要后还留在f4，黑方就无法完成出子。例如13... Nf6 14. Ne5! Rxd4 15. Nxf6+ Bxf6 16. g3 Qg5 17. Nf3 Qc5 18. Nxd4 Bxd4 19. Bh7+，随后Qd3+及Qxd4。
14. Ng3 Nf8 15. Qc3（见图）
caption_zh: 白方走完15. Qc3后的局面

text: A useful move, which is intended, among other things, as a preparation for an eventual Nh5, thereby provoking, by virtue of the threat of d5, a weakness in Black's king position. Black parries this with ...a5 and further moves on the queenside. We shall see at what cost!
zh: 这是有用的一步，其用意之一，是准备在适当时机Nh5，再借助d5的威胁，迫使黑方削弱王的位置。黑方以...a5及后翼的进一步行动应对。我们马上就会看到，他为此付出了什么代价！

text: Now 17. Nh5 can be met by 17... Qa5. However, as a result of Black's advance of the a-pawn, his pawn structure on the queenside has lost its flexibility, which in its turn makes it easier for White to favourably resolve the tension in the centre.
zh: 现在17. Nh5可以用17... Qa5应对。不过，黑方冲起a兵，使后翼兵形失去了灵活性，反而便于白方以有利方式消除中心的紧张局面。

text: This threatens Nc4-b6 and thus induces Black to play ...b5, which leads to a blocked position on the queenside and restricts his counterplay in the event of White's launching an attack on the kingside.
zh: 白方威胁Nc4-b6，诱使黑方走...b5。这样后翼就会封闭；白方一旦在王翼发动进攻，黑方的反击也会受到限制。

caption_zh: 白方走完20. Be4后的局面

text: A series of preconditions for an attack on the king has been created: the weakness represented by the black pawn at h6; the aggressive placing of White's pieces; his control of the centre; and Black's limited resources on the queenside. White, however, is not in a hurry to attack, for he sees that he can use his pressure on c6 to improve the deployment of his own pieces and, at the same time, to constrict his opponent's.
zh: 一系列杀王条件已经形成：黑方h6兵构成弱点；白子位置积极；白方控制中心；黑方在后翼的手段有限。不过，白方并不急于进攻，因为他看到，还可以利用对c6的压力改善己方子力部署，同时进一步压缩对手的活动空间。

text: White is thinking of the square b4.
zh: 白方着眼于b4格。

text: Against the threatening line-up of white knight at b4 and queen at f3 Black has only two expedients, namely, the direct weakening of his king position by ...f6 or an indirect weakening in the form of the exchange of his knight, which defends the square h7. Black decided on the latter course.
zh: 白方准备把马放到b4、后放到f3，组成有力的攻击阵形。黑方只有两种应对：走...f6直接削弱王城，或者兑掉保护h7格的马，间接削弱王城。他选择了后一种。

text: 24. Nxd7 Rxd7 25. Nd3 Rd8 26. Ne5 Bf8
zh: 24. Nxd7 Rxd7 25. Nd3 Rd8 26. Ne5 Bf8

text: Black is sure that the enduring pressure on the diagonal against h7 will oblige him to play ...g6. Logically, therefore, he decides upon a delayed fianchetto as the best means of putting up some resistance.
zh: 黑方知道，沿斜线持续施加于h7的压力，迟早会迫使自己走...g6。因此，他合乎逻辑地决定补走侧翼出象，以此作为组织抵抗的最佳办法。

text: The first move which really commits the attacker; the situation is also ready for it. It is directed against the future weakness on g6.
zh: 这是进攻方第一次作出真正难以收回的投入，而局面也已经为它做好了准备。这步棋针对的是未来的g6弱点。

text: He does not like the idea of 29. Qc2 g6 30. h5.
zh: 黑方不愿见到29. Qc2 g6 30. h5。

text: 29. Qf3 g6 30. g4 hxg4 31. Qxg4 Bg7 32. Ba2!
zh: 29. Qf3 g6 30. g4 hxg4 31. Qxg4 Bg7 32. Ba2!

text: Before proceeding any further, White prevents ...f5, which Black cannot prepare by 32... Qe7 on account of 33. Nxg6 and 34. Rxe6.
zh: 白方在继续行动之前，先防住...f5。黑方也不能以32... Qe7准备这步冲兵，因为有33. Nxg6及34. Rxe6。

text: White prefers to avoid 33. axb4 a3 which would allow Black to obtain counterplay.
zh: 白方避开33. axb4 a3，以免给黑方反击机会。

text: 33... bxa3 34. bxa3 Qa5 35. Qe4 Qc7 36. Qf4 Rab8 37. h5
zh: 33... bxa3 34. bxa3 Qa5 35. Qe4 Qc7 36. Qf4 Rab8 37. h5

text: This must come sooner or later.
zh: 这步棋迟早要走。

text: White cannot count on success without this sacrifice to eliminate the fianchettoed bishop, Black's main line of defence.
zh: 黑方侧翼象是其主要防线；若不通过这次弃子将它消灭，白方就无法指望进攻成功。

caption_zh: 白方走完42. Nxf7后的局面

text: Having played so excellently and — as regards the method of preparing the attack on the king — so instructively, Alekhine concludes the game with a sacrifice that is not fully correct! I say 'concludes', because Asztalos took fright and resigned when he could well have played on. The continuation which Alekhine had in mind and which he expounded in the tournament book contained a loophole giving a draw, and even against White's best play Black would have had drawing chances. Let us first look at Alekhine's line.
zh: 阿廖欣此前下得如此出色，尤其在准备杀王的方法上如此富于启发性，却以一次并不完全正确的弃子结束了对局！我之所以说“结束”，是因为阿斯塔洛什本来完全可以继续下去，却受惊认输了。阿廖欣设想并在比赛专著中给出的变化，存在可以成和的漏洞；即使白方采取最佳走法，黑方也有和棋机会。先来看阿廖欣的分析。

text: If 44. Qg3, Black replies 44... Rg7, while 44. Qf3 can be met by 44... Rd5. Thirdly, 44. Qg5 Qxd3 45. Qg8+ Kh6 46. Qh8+ Qh7 47. Qf8+ Rg7! 48. Rxg7 Rxg7 49. Qf6+ Bg6 50. Qxd8 Be4+ probably results in a draw.
zh: 如果44. Qg3，黑方应44... Rg7；44. Qf3则可用44... Rd5应对。第三种走法44. Qg5 Qxd3 45. Qg8+ Kh6 46. Qh8+ Qh7 47. Qf8+ Rg7! 48. Rxg7 Rxg7 49. Qf6+ Bg6 50. Qxd8 Be4+，大概也以和棋告终。

text: So far this is Alekhine's analysis. However, 45. Qf6! Rg8 46. Qxe6 is stronger and does indeed win, though White still has a hard task ahead¹.
zh: 以上是阿廖欣的分析。不过，45. Qf6! Rg8 46. Qxe6更强，而且确实能够获胜，只是白方接下来仍有艰巨的任务¹。

text: 1 A distinct exaggeration. White has queen and pawn against rook and bishop, Black's remaining pawns are all weak and White has a passed f-pawn — I wouldn't expect many technical problems here!
zh: 编者注1：这显然夸大了困难。白方以一个后和一兵对抗车象，黑方剩下的兵都是弱兵，而白方还有f线通路兵；我不认为这里会有多少技术难题！

text: Here Alekhine concludes his analysis with the remark that Black 'after a few further checks, would inevitably lose one of his rooks.' In fact, he loses after all moves except 47... Kg6 followed by keeping the king on g6 or g7. After 48. Qxe6+ Kg7 49. Qxc6 Rb1+! 50. Kg2 Rxd4 51. Qc7+ Kg6 the checks cease, whereupon Black's rooks begin to deploy themselves for play against the king or the c-pawn. One cannot see how White can win; the position is very likely drawn. Alekhine unintentionally bluffed the unfortunate Asztalos and the jury, who on the basis of his analysis awarded him the Brilliancy Prize.
zh: 阿廖欣的分析到此结束，并说黑方“再遭几次将军之后，必然丢掉一辆车”。实际上，除了47... Kg6并把王保持在g6或g7之外，其他走法确实都输。48. Qxe6+ Kg7 49. Qxc6 Rb1+! 50. Kg2 Rxd4 51. Qc7+ Kg6之后，白方已无将军可用，黑方双车便可以部署攻击白王或c兵。看不出白方怎样取胜；这个局面很可能是和棋。阿廖欣无意间唬住了不幸的阿斯塔洛什，也唬住了依据他的分析颁发精彩对局奖的评委。

text: We must now point out what is objectively the strongest move and the continuation by which White wins. Thus (instead of 42. Nxf7!?) he should have proceeded as follows:
zh: 现在必须指出客观上最强的走法，以及白方的取胜过程。他应当采用以下走法，而不是42. Nxf7!?：

text: 42. Qg3 Qf8 (D)
zh: 42. Qg3 Qf8（见图）
caption_zh: 分析变化中黑方走完42... Qf8后的局面

text: Forced; if 42... f5, then 43. Qg8+ followed by Qh8+ and Qf6+ is decisive, while if 42... Qf6, then 43. Bd3+ wins.
zh: 这是被迫的。如果42... f5，则43. Qg8+，随后Qh8+及Qf6+决定胜负；如果42... Qf6，则43. Bd3+获胜。

text: Both 43... Rd5 44. Ng4 and 43... Rdb8 44. Qf6 Rb3 45. Bxe6 also win for White.
zh: 43... Rd5 44. Ng4，或43... Rdb8 44. Qf6 Rb3 45. Bxe6，也都是白方获胜。

text: 44. Bd3+ Kh8 45. Bg6! Rh7
zh: 44. Bd3+ Kh8 45. Bg6! Rh7

text: Or 45... fxe5 46. Qxh5+ Kg7 47. Bxe8+ and 48. Qg5#.
zh: 或45... fxe5 46. Qxh5+ Kg7 47. Bxe8+，随后48. Qg5#。

text: 46. Bxh7 Kxh7
zh: 46. Bxh7 Kxh7

text: After 46... fxe5 47. Qxd8 Qf3+ 48. Rg2 Black has one more check before White mates him.
zh: 46... fxe5 47. Qxd8 Qf3+ 48. Rg2之后，黑方还可以再将军一次，接着就会被白方将杀。

text: 47. Ng4 Bg6
zh: 47. Ng4 Bg6

text: Or 47... Kh8 48. Nxf6 Bf7 49. Nxh5 and White wins.
zh: 或47... Kh8 48. Nxf6 Bf7 49. Nxh5，白方获胜。

text: 48. Nxf6+ Kg7 49. Nxh5+
zh: 48. Nxf6+ Kg7 49. Nxh5+

text: and Black loses his bishop with check.
zh: 白方接下来吃象，并且带将军。

text:
Capablanca – Schroeder
New York, 1916
Queen's Gambit Declined, Orthodox Defence
zh:
卡帕布兰卡—施罗德
1916年，纽约
后翼弃兵拒弃兵变例，正统防御

text: 1. d4 d5 2. Nf3 e6 3. c4 Nf6 4. Nc3 Nbd7 5. Bg5 Be7 6. e3 O-O 7. Rc1 a6 8. Qc2
zh: 1. d4 d5 2. Nf3 e6 3. c4 Nf6 4. Nc3 Nbd7 5. Bg5 Be7 6. e3 O-O 7. Rc1 a6 8. Qc2

text: This is better than either 8. c5 or 8. a3, which Capablanca played in a number of games of his 1928 match against Alekhine, but best of all is 8. cxd5.
zh: 这比8. c5或8. a3都好；卡帕布兰卡在原书所称的1928年对阿廖欣的对抗赛中，有几盘棋采用了后两种走法。不过，最好的是8. cxd5。

text: 8... Re8 9. Bd3 dxc4 10. Bxc4 b5 11. Bd3 Bb7?
zh: 8... Re8 9. Bd3 dxc4 10. Bxc4 b5 11. Bd3 Bb7?

text: At this point Black cannot spare the time to continue preparing ...c5; he should have played it at once.
zh: 到了这个时刻，黑方已经没有时间继续准备...c5，应当立即走出这步冲兵。

caption_zh: 白方走完12. a4后的局面

text: In order to entice the b-pawn to b4, which is useful for further play against the square c5.
zh: 目的是引诱b兵冲到b4，以便进一步围绕c5格展开行动。

text: This exchange is advantageous in two respects; first, for its 'clearance' of the square c5 and secondly, because it eliminates the possibility of a defence later on by ...Nf8.
zh: 这次兑换有两方面好处：一是“清除”了对c5格的控制，二是消除了黑方以后用...Nf8防守的可能。

text: 13... Nxf6 14. Ne4 Nxe4 15. Bxe4 Bxe4 16. Qxe4 c5
zh: 13... Nxf6 14. Ne4 Nxe4 15. Bxe4 Bxe4 16. Qxe4 c5

text: Sink or swim, Black must play this, for otherwise Qc6 follows, fixing the backward c-pawn.
zh: 无论结果如何，黑方都必须走这步棋；否则白方就会Qc6，把落后的c兵固定下来。

text: 17. dxc5 Qa5 18. b3 Bxc5 19. Ng5! (D)
zh: 17. dxc5 Qa5 18. b3 Bxc5 19. Ng5!（见图）
caption_zh: 白方走完19. Ng5后的局面

text: Can it be that White is justified in switching to an attack on the king after preparations which were clearly directed at the c-file? How does this fit in with our thesis on the need to fulfil a series of preconditions before opening an attack on the king? In fact, there is no contradiction; the preconditions are present, but they have arisen in a different way from those in the Alekhine-Asztalos game.
zh: 白方此前的准备明明都针对c线，现在转而杀王，难道合理吗？这与我们所说的“发动杀王进攻之前必须具备一系列先决条件”，又怎样相容呢？其实没有矛盾：所需条件已经存在，只是它们的形成方式与阿廖欣对阿斯塔洛什一局不同。

text: It is true that the preconditions for the attack on the castled king in this game have come about suddenly and somewhat incidentally; at the same time, this has occurred quite legitimately. The main point is that White's play, starting with 12. a4, serves two purposes: it maintains the pressure on the c-file and simultaneously improves the preconditions for an attack on the king. As a result of 12. a4 b4 and 18. b3 the position on the queenside became blocked, and this has reduced Black's prospects of counterplay, while 17. dxc5 resolved the tension in the centre.
zh: 本局的杀王条件，确实形成得突然，多少像是附带的结果；但它们的形成又完全合乎棋理。关键在于，从12. a4开始，白方的走法同时服务于两个目标：维持c线压力，并改善杀王条件。12. a4 b4及18. b3使后翼封闭，减少了黑方反击的机会；17. dxc5则消除了中心的紧张局面。

text: Furthermore, 13. Bxf6, 15. Bxe4, and 16. Qxe4 represent, in effect, a far-reaching elimination of Black's defending pieces; in the same way, the struggle revolving around the pawns on the c-file has forced Black (in 17... Qa5 and 18... Bxc5) to displace two pieces which are important for the defence of his king position. This is without doubt a full set of preconditions, built up with true Capablanca virtuosity and elan. Now White's knight, a sort of 'equus ex machina', stirs up a whirlwind attack on the king, against which there is hardly an adequate defence.
zh: 此外，13. Bxf6、15. Bxe4和16. Qxe4，实际上大幅削减了黑方的防守子力；围绕c线兵展开的争夺，又迫使黑方以17... Qa5和18... Bxc5，把两枚重要的王城防守棋子调离。这无疑已经是一整套进攻条件，形成过程体现了卡帕布兰卡特有的精湛技艺和洒脱气度。现在，白马如同突然登场的救星一般，掀起一阵杀王旋风，黑方几乎难以抵挡。

text: Although Black has no really sound reply at his disposal, 19... f5 was the lesser evil. Then White does not gain much by 20. Qe5 Bb6 while if 20. Qb7, Black plays 20... Qb6, and after 21. Qf7+ Kh8 22. Qh5 h6 White's attack stops, for example, 23. h4? Bxe3! 24. Qg6 is not sound, since after 24... hxg5 25. hxg5+ Kg8 White cannot give perpetual check, while 26. Rh7 is weak on account of 26... Qd4.
zh: 黑方虽然已经没有真正稳妥的应手，但19... f5相对较好。20. Qe5 Bb6，白方所获不多；如果20. Qb7，黑方应20... Qb6，21. Qf7+ Kh8 22. Qh5 h6之后，白方的进攻便停了下来。例如23. h4? Bxe3! 24. Qg6并不成立，因为24... hxg5 25. hxg5+ Kg8之后，白方没有长将，而26. Rh7又因26... Qd4而无力。

text: The best line is 20. Qc4 Rac8! 21. Nxe6 Bb6 22. Qxc8 Rxc8 23. Rxc8+ Kf7 24. Ng5+ Kg6 25. Nf3 Qd5 26. O-O Bd8 followed by ...Bf6 with some chances of a draw¹. This continuation would have been relatively the best way out for Black.
zh: 最佳变化是20. Qc4 Rac8! 21. Nxe6 Bb6 22. Qxc8 Rxc8 23. Rxc8+ Kf7 24. Ng5+ Kg6 25. Nf3 Qd5 26. O-O Bd8，随后...Bf6，黑方还有一些和棋机会¹。这相对而言是黑方最好的出路。

text: 1 After 27. Rc6+ Bf6 28. Nd4 I see no real chances for a draw; White has two rooks and a pawn for the queen, and Black's king is exposed. One line is 28... Kh5 29. Rc4 Bxd4 30. Rd1, followed by Rdxd4.
zh: 编者注1：27. Rc6+ Bf6 28. Nd4之后，我看不到实际的和棋机会。白方以双车一兵对后，黑王又暴露在外。例如28... Kh5 29. Rc4 Bxd4 30. Rd1，随后Rdxd4。

text: Better than the text move but worse perhaps than 19... f5 is 19... g6. An analysis of this move, which, though it may emanate from Capablanca, needs to be corrected, runs as follows: 19... g6 20. Qf3 Rf8 (everything else is weaker; 20... Ra7 in particular, does not work on account of 21. Qc6) 21. Qh3 h5 22. Nxe6? fxe6 23. Qxe6+ Kh7 24. Qd7+ Kh8 25. Qc6; now the analysis continues with 25... Rac8?, missing the fact that Black can win by 25... Bxe3! 26. fxe3 Qf5² 27. Qf3 (forced) 27... Qd3 28. Qe2 Qxb3, obtaining an attack and, before long, a material advantage as well.
zh: 19... g6比实战好，但也许不如19... f5。下面这段分析即使出自卡帕布兰卡，也仍需订正：19... g6 20. Qf3 Rf8（其他走法都较弱；尤其20... Ra7因21. Qc6而不行）21. Qh3 h5 22. Nxe6? fxe6 23. Qxe6+ Kh7 24. Qd7+ Kh8 25. Qc6。原分析接着给出25... Rac8?，却忽略了黑方可以25... Bxe3! 26. fxe3 Qf5² 27. Qf3（被迫）27... Qd3 28. Qe2 Qxb3，不仅获得进攻，很快还会取得子力优势。

text: 2 This allows a defence by 27. Qc2, but Black can improve by 26... Qg5!, which does indeed win for Black.
zh: 编者注2：这一走法允许白方以27. Qc2防守，但黑方可以改走更强的26... Qg5!，这才确实能够获胜。

text: This analysis can be improved by playing, instead of 21. Qh3, 21. Qf6 (threatening either 22. Rc4 and 23. Nxh7 or at once 22. Nxh7) 21... Rae8 (if 21... h6 then 22. Nxe6 wins, while 21... Rac8 is not good because of 22. Rc4³) 22. Qe5 Bb6 23. Qxa5 Bxa5 24. Rc8 Kg7 25. Ne4, when White has much the better ending, for example if 25... Rfd8, then 26. Nc5 Rc6 27. Nb7 Rxc1 28. Rxc1 Rd5 29. e4.
zh: 这段分析可以改进：不用21. Qh3，而走21. Qf6，威胁22. Rc4后23. Nxh7，或立即22. Nxh7。21... Rae8（21... h6则22. Nxe6获胜；21... Rac8也因22. Rc4³而不好）22. Qe5 Bb6 23. Qxa5 Bxa5 24. Rc8 Kg7 25. Ne4，白方得到明显较好的残局。例如25... Rfd8 26. Nc5 Rc6 27. Nb7 Rxc1 28. Rxc1 Rd5 29. e4。

text: 3 After 21... Rac8 22. Rc4 Black can defend by 22... Rc7!, for example 23. Nxh7 Be7 or 23. Rh4 Be7. Thus it is hard to demonstrate an advantage for White after 19... g6.
zh: 编者注3：21... Rac8 22. Rc4之后，黑方可以22... Rc7!防守，例如23. Nxh7 Be7，或23. Rh4 Be7。因此，在19... g6之后，很难证明白方具有优势。

text: 20. Qh7+ Kf8 21. Qh8+ Ke7 22. Qxg7 hxg5 23. Qxg5+ Kd6 24. Ke2 (D)
zh: 20. Qh7+ Kf8 21. Qh8+ Ke7 22. Qxg7 hxg5 23. Qxg5+ Kd6 24. Ke2（见图）
caption_zh: 白方走完24. Ke2后的局面

text: Two pawns, the exposed position of the black king, Black's commitments at c5, and White's rooks on the c- and d-files — all this is obviously more than sufficient compensation for the sacrificed knight. Capablanca also particularly stresses Black's inability to stop the advance of the h-pawn while White is tying him down on the queenside.
zh: 两个兵、黑王的暴露、黑方在c5受到的牵制，以及白方在c线和d线上发挥作用的车，这些显然足以补偿所弃的马，而且绰绰有余。卡帕布兰卡还特别强调：白方在后翼牵制黑方的同时，黑方无法阻止h兵前进。

text: 24... Rac8 25. Rc4 Kc6 26. Rhc1 Kb6 27. h4 f5
zh: 24... Rac8 25. Rc4 Kc6 26. Rhc1 Kb6 27. h4 f5

text: Capablanca had reckoned on the following transition into a won ending: 27... Rc7 28. h5 Rec8 29. h6 Bd6 30. Qxa5+ Kxa5 31. Rxc7 Rxc7 32. Rxc7 Bxc7 33. f4 Bd8 34. g4 Bf6 35. g5 Bh8 36. e4 Kb6 37. f5 followed by g6-g7.
zh: 卡帕布兰卡已经算到，可以这样转入胜势残局：27... Rc7 28. h5 Rec8 29. h6 Bd6 30. Qxa5+ Kxa5 31. Rxc7 Rxc7 32. Rxc7 Bxc7 33. f4 Bd8 34. g4 Bf6 35. g5 Bh8 36. e4 Kb6 37. f5，随后g6-g7。

text: 28. Qg7 Re7 29. Qe5 Rc6
zh: 28. Qg7 Re7 29. Qe5 Rc6

text: This loses at once, but 29... Rec7 has no future either in view of 30. h5.
zh: 这步棋立即输棋，但29... Rec7也因30. h5而没有希望。

text: For, if 30... Rxc5 then 31. Qd6+ is decisive. Capablanca's virtuosity in integrating all the features of the position into a coherent whole is worthy of close attention.
zh: 因为30... Rxc5会遭到决定性的31. Qd6+。卡帕布兰卡把局面所有特点融为一体的精湛技艺，值得仔细体会。

text:
Alekhine – Kmoch
San Remo, 1930
Nimzo-Indian Defence
zh:
阿廖欣—克莫赫
1930年，圣雷莫
尼姆佐-印度防御

text: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. Bd2
zh: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. Bd2

text: One of the most harmless continuations.
zh: 这是最温和的续着之一。

text: 4... O-O 5. e3 d5 6. Nf3 c5 7. a3 Bxc3 8. Bxc3 Ne4 9. Rc1 Nxc3 10. Rxc3 cxd4 11. exd4 Nc6 12. Be2
zh: 4... O-O 5. e3 d5 6. Nf3 c5 7. a3 Bxc3 8. Bxc3 Ne4 9. Rc1 Nxc3 10. Rxc3 cxd4 11. exd4 Nc6 12. Be2

text: If 12. c5 then Black can immediately play 12... e5.
zh: 如果12. c5，黑方可以立即12... e5。

text: 12... dxc4 13. Bxc4 Qf6
zh: 12... dxc4 13. Bxc4 Qf6

text: White has not achieved very much in the opening. In view of the reduction in material his spatial advantage offers no more than approximate compensation for the isolated pawn.
zh: 白方在开局中所获不多。由于子力已经减少，他的空间优势只能大致补偿孤兵的弱点。

text: 14. O-O Rd8 15. Rd3 Bd7 16. Re1
zh: 14. O-O Rd8 15. Rd3 Bd7 16. Re1

text: By 16. Qd2 White could have prepared to obtain clear equality by d5. However, he does not like the idea of a draw.
zh: 白方本可以16. Qd2准备d5，明确取得均势。不过，他不愿接受和棋。

text: As this threatens 19. Nxe6 fxe6 20. Rxe6, Black does not have time for 18... Bc6 or 18... Nf5.
zh: 这步棋威胁19. Nxe6 fxe6 20. Rxe6，因此黑方没有时间走18... Bc6或18... Nf5。

caption_zh: 黑方走完20... h6后的局面

text: White has proceeded cautiously and prepared the ground for Qd3, with the aim of provoking a weakening of the enemy king position in the shape of ...g6. For this reason Kmoch prefers to go in for ...h6, which weakens him less. White can only obtain results by attacking the king, for Black is the better placed for the endgame.
zh: 白方谨慎行棋，为Qd3做好准备，打算诱使对手走...g6，削弱王的位置。因此，克莫赫宁愿选择削弱程度较小的...h6。由于黑方在残局中更有利，白方只有通过杀王进攻才能取得成果。

text: If 21. Ne4 Black can reply 21... Qh4.
zh: 如果21. Ne4，黑方可以21... Qh4应对。

text: Parrying the threat of Reg4.
zh: 防住Reg4的威胁。

text: 23. Ne5 Nf5 24. Rd3
zh: 23. Ne5 Nf5 24. Rd3

text: White has managed to weaken the enemy king position, but he still lacks the preconditions for a real attack. A little regrouping is therefore needed, and above all the square d4 must be safeguarded. If 24. Rf3 then 24... Bc6 25. Nxc6 bxc6 is quite good for Black. Of the minor pieces the knights are more valuable than the bishops, from the point of view of both the attacker and his opponent.
zh: 白方虽然已经迫使敌王位置变弱，却仍然缺少真正发动进攻的条件。因此还要略作调动，首先必须确保d4格安全。如果24. Rf3，则24... Bc6 25. Nxc6 bxc6，黑方相当好。在轻子中，无论对进攻方还是防守方，马都比象更有价值。

text: Up to this point the author of The Art of Defence has defended correctly and preserved equality. Now, however, he goes astray in playing to exchange off his important knight, which is the main defender of his king position. Correct was 25... Bc6.
zh: 到此为止，《防御的艺术》的作者一直防守正确，保持着均势。但现在他走错了：准备兑掉这匹重要的马，而它恰恰是王城的主要守卫。正确的是25... Bc6。

text: 26. Rf4 Nxc4 27. Nxc4 Qg5 28. Rg3 Qd5 29. Ne3 Qc6 30. Kh2 Qc1 31. Qb4 Qc7 32. d5! (D)
zh: 26. Rf4 Nxc4 27. Nxc4 Qg5 28. Rg3 Qd5 29. Ne3 Qc6 30. Kh2 Qc1 31. Qb4 Qc7 32. d5!（见图）
caption_zh: 白方走完32. d5后的局面

text: Apparently, Black has manoeuvred himself into a new defensive position, one which also affords the possibility of his inconveniencing White's queen further by ...a5. The only weak side of his manoeuvre is that it does not give sufficient attention to centralization. As a result, the alleged pawn weakling on d4 is transformed — ironically — into an aggressor, punishing Black for his neglect of the central squares.
zh: 表面看来，黑方通过调动建立了新的防守阵地，而且还可以...a5继续骚扰白后。问题只在于，这套调动没有充分重视中心化。结果颇具讽刺意味：那个据说软弱的d4孤兵，竟摇身变成进攻者，惩罚黑方对中心格的忽视。

text: After 32... exd5 33. Qd4 g6 (or 33... g5) 34. Nf5 Black would quickly come to grief; equally bad is 32... e5 33. Rfg4 g6 34. Nf5.
zh: 32... exd5 33. Qd4 g6（或33... g5）34. Nf5，黑方会很快遭殃；32... e5 33. Rfg4 g6 34. Nf5同样不好。

text: If 35. Rc4? Black could bring the attack to a halt by 35... Rc6!.
zh: 如果35. Rc4?，黑方就能以35... Rc6!阻止进攻。

text: Or 35... Kh7 36. Ng4! gxh5 37. Nf6+ and mates.
zh: 或35... Kh7 36. Ng4! gxh5 37. Nf6+，随后将杀。

text: 36. Nxd5 exd5 37. Qxh6 Qe5 38. Rh4 Qg7 1-0
zh: 36. Nxd5 exd5 37. Qxh6 Qe5 38. Rh4 Qg7 1-0

text:
Colle – Capablanca
Carlsbad, 1929
Colle System
zh:
科勒—卡帕布兰卡
1929年，卡尔斯巴德
科勒体系

text: 1. d4 Nf6 2. Nf3 b6 3. e3 Bb7 4. Nbd2 e6 5. Bd3 c5 6. O-O Nc6 7. c3
zh: 1. d4 Nf6 2. Nf3 b6 3. e3 Bb7 4. Nbd2 e6 5. Bd3 c5 6. O-O Nc6 7. c3

text: The formation with pawns on c3, d4, and e3, bishop on d3, and knights on d2 and f3 characterizes the Colle System. White's plan is to force through e3-e4 and then exchange his d2-knight for Black's f6-knight on this same square; he thereby creates some of the preconditions for an attack on the king without entailing any commitments. The Colle System, however, lacks positional depth and, consequently, Black does not have any great anxiety as regards the centre.
zh: c3、d4、e3三兵，d3象以及d2、f3双马，是科勒体系的典型阵形。白方计划实现e3-e4，再在e4格用d2马兑掉黑方f6马，从而在不承担额外约束的情况下，创造一些杀王条件。不过，科勒体系在局面棋方面缺乏深度，因此黑方不必过分担心中心。

text: 7... Be7 8. e4 cxd4
zh: 7... Be7 8. e4 cxd4

text: Capablanca's treatment of the opening, adopting a Queen's Indian set-up, is both sound and also suitable for avoiding lines which equalize out to a draw. White's strong point in the centre is now eliminated, for he must recapture the pawn with his knight, otherwise 9. cxd4 Nb4 10. Bb1 Ba6 leaves Black with the better game.
zh: 卡帕布兰卡采用后翼印度式阵形处理开局，既稳健，也便于避开那些简化成和的均势变化。白方的中心强点现在被消除了，因为他必须用马吃回这个兵；否则9. cxd4 Nb4 10. Bb1 Ba6，黑方就更好。

text: 9. Nxd4 O-O 10. Qe2
zh: 9. Nxd4 O-O 10. Qe2

text: First 10. Nxc6 would have been sounder.
zh: 先走10. Nxc6会更稳妥。

text: Preparation for an attack on the king, but also a weakening of the g1-a7 diagonal.
zh: 这既是杀王准备，也削弱了g1-a7斜线。

text: Obviously not 13... Bxf1? on account of 14. fxe5. Moving the bishop to a6 had other points: on the one hand, to drive the white queen back and, on the other, to induce White to play Rf3, whereby he undertakes a commitment to attack before the preconditions for a successful attack have matured.
zh: 显然不能13... Bxf1?，因为有14. fxe5。把象调到a6另有用意：一方面赶退白后，另一方面诱使白方Rf3，在成功进攻的条件尚未成熟之前，就作出发动进攻的投入。

text: Against 14. e5 Black has 14... Nd5 after which 15. Bxh7+ does not work (because of 15... Kxh7 16. Qh5+ Kg8 17. Rf3 f5 18. Rh3 Nxf4) while, given a free move, Black can consolidate his defences by playing 15... f5.
zh: 对14. e5，黑方有14... Nd5；此后15. Bxh7+并不成立，因为15... Kxh7 16. Qh5+ Kg8 17. Rf3 f5 18. Rh3 Nxf4。白方若不采取强制行动，黑方就可以15... f5巩固防守。

text: In the event of other, slower methods of attack Black has a sound defensive plan based on the effective use of the diagonals for his bishops and a centralized knight on d5. This will be seen in the further course of the game.
zh: 白方若采用其他较慢的进攻方法，黑方也有可靠的防守计划：充分利用双象的斜线，并把马集中到d5。这将在后续实战中显现出来。

text: In view of the restricted range of activity of White's dark-squared bishop, this weakness is negligible. It is important for Black to exclude short-term dangers on the kingside, since he needs time to increase his pressure on the central squares.
zh: 白方黑格象的活动范围受限，因此这一削弱可以忽略。黑方需要时间加强对中心格的压力，所以眼下首先应当排除王翼的直接危险。

text: 15. N2b3 Nxd4 16. Nxd4 Bb7 17. Qe2 Bc5 18. Rh3 Qc6!
zh: 15. N2b3 Nxd4 16. Nxd4 Bb7 17. Qe2 Bc5 18. Rh3 Qc6!

text: Black forces e5 in order to gain the d5-square for his knight and open up the diagonal.
zh: 黑方迫使白方e5，为己方马争得d5格，同时打开斜线。

caption_zh: 白方走完20. Qf2后的局面

text: Up to this point Colle's play has been a little pretentious but not really incorrect, for his commitments have not been decisive ones. Still, he should now have admitted that it was pointless to continue playing for an attack and striven, by paying careful attention to the central squares, to keep the game within the well-known 'margin of a draw'; for example, 20. Be3 Bxd4 21. cxd4 Rac8 22. Bb3! when Black, after 22... Nxe3 23. Rxe3 clearly has nothing either in the centre or on the c-file; nor does 22... b5 or the like offer anything very much.
zh: 到此为止，科勒的行棋虽然有些勉强，却还谈不上真正错误，因为他的投入尚未达到决定性的程度。但现在他应当承认，继续谋求进攻已无意义，转而认真照看中心格，努力把局面维持在大家熟知的“和棋余地”之内。例如20. Be3 Bxd4 21. cxd4 Rac8 22. Bb3!，22... Nxe3 23. Rxe3之后，黑方无论在中心还是c线上，都显然没有什么成果；22... b5等走法也提供不了多少机会。

text: (In Golombek's book Capablanca's Hundred Best Games of Chess, instead of 22. Bb3!, the erroneous 22. Rc1? is given; then Black does indeed get the upper hand by 22... Nxe3 23. Rxe3 Qc4.)
zh: （戈隆贝克的《卡帕布兰卡百局名局选》没有给出22. Bb3!，而是误列22. Rc1?；这样黑方确实可以22... Nxe3 23. Rxe3 Qc4取得上风。）

text: Satisfied with the centralization he has achieved, Black too now becomes rather presumptuous and opens up the c-file prematurely. 20... f5 followed by a quiet positional plan based on ...b5-b4 was probably best. In that event simplification by 21. Nxc6 Bxf2+ 22. Kxf2 Bxc6 would give Black the better ending, while if 21. Be3, then 21... Bxd4 22. cxd4 Nb4 would be perfectly agreeable.
zh: 黑方对自己已经实现的中心化感到满意，也有些自负，过早打开了c线。最好大概是20... f5，再以...b5-b4为基础，采取安静的局面棋计划。这时21. Nxc6 Bxf2+ 22. Kxf2 Bxc6的简化会使黑方得到较好残局；21. Be3 Bxd4 22. cxd4 Nb4也完全令人满意。

text: The move suggested, 20... f5, signifies that Black is satisfied with a small advantage, whereas Capablanca's idea aspires to dynamic play on the c- and f-files. However, the preconditions for this are insufficient, for counterattacks too demand preconditions and entail commitments just as attacks on the king do. The laws which determine the connection between the two types of action dictate the form, timing, and tempo of the counterattack in accordance with the state of the attack. Thus, the degree to which the attacking units have been diverted conditions the extent and force of the counterattack. In this case, therefore, direct defence by 20... f5 would have been better than 20... Bxd4.
zh: 建议的20... f5表示黑方满足于小优，而卡帕布兰卡的构思，则着眼于在c线和f线上展开动态行动。但是，所需条件尚不充分，因为反击与杀王进攻一样，也需要先决条件，也会带来投入。两类行动之间的联系有其规律：反击的形式、时机和速度，都必须适应进攻的实际状况。进攻子力偏离原位的程度，制约着反击的范围与力量。因此，本局直接以20... f5防守，比20... Bxd4更好。

text: 21. cxd4 Rac8
zh: 21. cxd4 Rac8

text: The immediate 21... f6 did not work on account of 22. Qh4 Rf7 23. Bxg6.
zh: 立即21... f6不行，因为22. Qh4 Rf7 23. Bxg6。

text: Other moves by the bishop are defeated by 22... Qxc1+. 22. Qh4 is also inadequate; for example, 22... Nf6! 23. Rg3 Qxc2 24. Be3 (to prevent ...Qd1+) 24... Ne4 25. Rh3 h5 and Black wins.
zh: 象的其他走法都会遭到22... Qxc1+。22. Qh4也不够，例如22... Nf6! 23. Rg3 Qxc2 24. Be3（防...Qd1+）24... Ne4 25. Rh3 h5，黑方获胜。

caption_zh: 黑方走完22... f6后的局面

text: This much-praised move of Capablanca's is very economical in that it both attacks and defends in equal measure; it is probably Black's best, now that he has embarked on 20... Bxd4. It is also true that an attack generally collapses when the pawns in front of the king begin to 'bite', but in this case the question is no longer one of attack but of the overall state of the position. Black has in fact awoken possibilities for White on the c-file, and in the event of the game being opened up White's two bishops could come into their own.
zh: 卡帕布兰卡这步备受称赞的棋，确实十分经济，攻防兼顾；既然黑方已经走了20... Bxd4，它大概就是现在最好的选择。通常，当王前兵开始“咬住”进攻子力时，进攻就会瓦解；但在本局，问题已经超出单纯的进攻，而涉及整个局面的状况。黑方实际上也为白方激活了c线的机会；一旦局面打开，白方双象就可能充分发挥力量。

text: This gains a tempo for Bf3 but neglects the development of his c1-bishop and a1-rook. The correct move was 23. Bd2!. Capablanca's intention in that case was 23... Nxf4!? 24. Bxf4 fxe5 25. Bf3 e4 but the combination has a flaw: White does not play 26. Be2? (when 26... e3! wins) but 26. Qh4!, and Black finds himself in difficulties.
zh: 这为Bf3争得一个先手，却忽略了c1象和a1车的出子。正确的是23. Bd2!。卡帕布兰卡准备以23... Nxf4!? 24. Bxf4 fxe5 25. Bf3 e4应对，但这个组合存在漏洞：白方不走26. Be2?（26... e3!获胜），而走26. Qh4!，黑方反倒陷入困难。

text: Moreover, 23. Bd2! cannot be met by 23... fxe5, e.g. 24. Rc1 Qb5 (24... Qxc1 would not succeed against correct play by White) 25. Rxc8 Bxc8 26. Qh4, whereupon 26... Rf7 27. Qd8+ leads to a draw, 26... h5 is not good due to 27. Qg5, while the complications following 26... Nf6 27. fxe5 Ba6 28. Rf3 seem full of uncertainty.
zh: 此外，23. Bd2!也不能用23... fxe5应对。例如24. Rc1 Qb5（对白方的正确走法，24... Qxc1也不能成功）25. Rxc8 Bxc8 26. Qh4，此后26... Rf7 27. Qd8+成和；26... h5因27. Qg5而不好；26... Nf6 27. fxe5 Ba6 28. Rf3所产生的复杂局面，则看来充满不确定性。

text: Against 23. Bd2! Black would probably have to play 23... d6 24. Rc1 Qd7, when 25. Rxc8 Bxc8 26. Rf3 results in a complex struggle in which White's dark-squared bishop derives pleasure from every exchange on e5. This represents an analytical proof of the assertions made in the note to the twentieth move.
zh: 对23. Bd2!，黑方大概必须23... d6 24. Rc1 Qd7；25. Rxc8 Bxc8 26. Rf3之后，双方进入复杂的争斗，而e5上的每一次兑换，都会使白方黑格象更加活跃。这些分析印证了第20回合评注中的论点。

text: Since 25. Qf2 does not work (because of 25... Qxc1+) White is now lost.
zh: 由于25. Qf2不能走（有25... Qxc1+），白方现在已经败势。

text: 25. Be3 Nxe3 26. Bxb7 Nf5 27. Qe1 Rc7 28. Be4 Qxd4+ 29. Kh1 fxe5 30. Bxf5 exf5 31. fxe5 Re7 32. Re3 Qxb2 33. e6 dxe6 34. Rxe6 Kf7 0-1
zh: 25. Be3 Nxe3 26. Bxb7 Nf5 27. Qe1 Rc7 28. Be4 Qxd4+ 29. Kh1 fxe5 30. Bxf5 exf5 31. fxe5 Re7 32. Re3 Qxb2 33. e6 dxe6 34. Rxe6 Kf7 0-1

text: This game is very instructive for the purpose of studying the complex connection between attack and indirect defence; the decisive points illustrating this were shown in their correct light only by a thorough revision of the commentary.
zh: 这盘棋对于研究进攻与间接防守之间的复杂联系，极有启发性。只有彻底修订评注之后，那些能够说明问题的关键之处，才得到了正确的揭示。
